title: Major Lamar Jackson Injury Update And 4 Key Takeaways From Ravens Third Straight Defeat
full_text:
It’s November, the Ravens have two AFC victories, their feckless general manager has been exposed for the utter failure that he is once again, and his offensive line is truly a remarkable disaster which can’t stop getting quarterbacks hurt.
Welcome to the midpoint of the 2026 season; it’s even worse than 2025.
When you fire a future Hall of Fane head coach and over-empower Eric DeCosta, the huckster who can’t evaluate players or negotiate contracts with a modicum of acumen or professionalism, you can torpedo a season almost before it starts. This qualifies - another year of Lamar Jackson missing more time than he plays and more unsightly football in all three phases and Sunday’s 36-10 debacle at Buffalo may just have been the last truly meaningful game this fading team (4-4) plays.
Jackson was smashed in the hand by Bills edge rusher Greg Rousseau on his first snap back from a high-ankle sprain that Ravens overmatched rookie coach Jesse Minter insisted was day-to-day for nearly three weeks (allegedly Ravens $30M “closer” Trey Hendrickson was active for this game; another DeCosta scam gone wrong ). Backup Snoop Huntley was immediately under assault and he was gone before the midpoint of the second quarter with a toe injury and so undrafted rookie Joe Faganao took the rest of this beating in his NFL debut behind a line that was shameful in its approach and execution (Fagnano was receiving regular medical attention by the third quarter).
Minter said Jackson will head to Injured Reserve and when asked if it could be season-enning he said, "potentially." It's also potentially his final game as a Raven, in that case. Even a four-week absence means garbage time in the season for Baltimore and with no real contract moving forward, it would be stupid - even by DeCosta standards (super low bar) - for Jackson to play again. Baltimore has no tie-breaking hope as it's two conference wins are against teams a combined 3-11 (Colts and Titans).
"Things happen," Minter offered, "but it's how you respond."
DeCosta better get real about an always-necessary rebuild that should have started with his firing in January. And with the trade deadline now nine days away and his roster overloaded with horrible contracts for bad football players, a loss to the Jaguars should trigger a natural resetting of this organization that will beg major questions of the owner, Steve Bisciotti, and DeCosta for charting this path in the first place.
The fools in charge of this franchise better get another QB (or two) in here, but good luck finding one who had much experience with a coaching staff full of novices. This is dire, and it could definitely get worse. They face a stout Jacksonville team at home Thursday and the only other QB who was around them this summer for any period of time, Skyler Thompson, was put on IR before Fagnano for his chance to make the team.
A toe problem for Huntley can be a very big deal, and certainly more than enough to keep him from playing on a short week after being unable to play a half of football with the injury. Executing a trade and getting a player in Baltimore in time to know the offense and be able to serve even as a back-up with only one real day of practice this week is impossible. Will have to be a free agent or someone off a practice squad I figure, but either way this is quite a bleak scenario for the first few days of November. Fagnano will clearly be ailing after all the huge shots he took, and he too could miss what little practice time there is this week.
"We have to make sure Joe came through the game okay," Minter said, acknowledging more transactions might come with Huntley under review, too.
Jackson can call his shot next season given how he took DeCosta to school on his contract and why would want to sign on for more of this, you have to start to wonder. Miami will make a push, among others.
I don’t want to hear about injuries to centers who aren’t even starting centers and were never going to be starting centers. Danny Pinter and Jovaughn Gwyn were silly vanity plays by a loser GM, he always needed a real center and the desperate, panic overpay for Cam Jurgens – very likely about to be benched in Philly – has already backfired, badly.
Jurgens missed two games with a concussion, offered nothing in the ground game in Week 7 and was totally exposed in Week 8. Somehow first-round pick Vega Ioane is the only competent lineman on this team, and he was hurt. Jurgens got abused on simple stints, the interior got abused and Baltimore had 52 yards in the first – even on three QBs that’s a joke. They were destroyed at the line of scrimmage. Rousseau undressed right tackle Roger Rosengarten whenever he wanted, or Ronnie Stanley on the other side.
Buffalo blitzed with abandon, and produced 9 QB hits, four hurries and four sacks on 17 dropbacks in the first half. Stanley is not a starting-caliber left tackle, DeCosta lit $10M on fire signing John Simpson and they continued to commit crushing penalties when they did move the ball, with Stanley’s hold negating Derrick Henry’s TD on the opening drive of the second half (Baltimore settled for a field goal).
"It's honestly a tough eval (evaluation) right now," Minter said, deferring to a tape study that is going to be ugly for all involved.
And while Mark Andrews is not an OL, he must be mentioned for being a total no show yet again. He is there to help the linemen, and it is beyond ridiculous how little he has to offer as a football player and how unthinkable it is that DeCosta is paying his buddy $13.5M a year to do nothing while letting Iasiah Likely walk.
But hey, "genius" coordinator Declan Doyle didn't get shutout for the third straight week after halftime. He put up a field goal.
All the tough talk about kicker Tyler Loop, now’s the time to make the move to Jake Moody. Full disclosure – this team is no good, the GM is a mega fraud and they should be selling everyone they can before the deadline and playing the kids. But given the talking points DeCosta has been giving his puppet coach about this kicker – I believe this is it and Moody will get his shot (careful what you ask for).
Loop’s opening kickoff went out of bounds, setting up the Bills with great field position on what became a scoring drive. With the QBs under duress, every point would matter, and Loop missed a 27-yard field goal on a perfect day that would have tied the game at 10; Buffalo scored off what amounted to that turnover and the Ravens wouldn’t get any closer.
DeCosta is desperate for scapegoats and his greatest (only) strength as an NFL exec is convincing the glazed over billionaire he works for that it’s always someone else’s fault. The kid kicker will pay for this.
Stop me if you’ve heard this before – the defense was awesome in the first half and then gave up a 50-yard explosive and a TD on the first drive of the second half and showed their true colors after the half? Yeah, that’s who they have been under DeCosta for years, and the half-field shot to DJ Moore, beating Marlon Humphrey, after Buffalo just missed on one late in the first half, told you all you need to know.
Good on the defense for bowing up after a terrible first drive and they showed some badly-missing determination and gumption on repeated short-yardage situations to stay in the game into the second half despite the QB injuries, but you knew the levy would start to break in the second half.
While Buffalo couldn’t finish drives and Josh Allen was off in the first half, they ran 44 plays in the first 30 minutes and the volume was going to catch up to this awful defense as the game went on,, when Minter gets utterly thrashed week after week as a head coach and play caller.
And Minter got destroyed in the second half again. He is worse than Zach Orr, folks. Allen produced 20 points in the second half, rolling up 219 yards on a ridiculous 7.5 yards/play before he made way for the back-up. Minter stinks at being a head coach and coordinator at the same time and…

title: Lamar Jackson Suffers Potentially Significant Thumb Injury At Buffalo
full_text:
Lamar Jackson came back to the Ravens from a three-week absence and suffered what appeared to be a significant thumb injury on his first snap, casting further doubt on a season already on the brink.
Jackson dropped back to pass under immediate pressure, with Bills EDGE Greg Rousseau following through on a pass rush and hitting Jackson’s right hand with some velocity as he released an incomplete pass. Jackson immediately grabbed his hand, began moving to the sidelines with great pace and was whisked back to the locker room for immediate medical attention. The CBS cameras picked up a shot of the hand in which there was clearly damage around the thumb and Jackson appeared to be in great pain.
The Ravens ruled out Jackson for the rest of the game before the first quarter had concluded. Backup Snoop Huntley suffered a foot injury shortly after entering the game and undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano made his NFL debut midway through the second quarter and he has to play the rest of the game (running back Justice Hill would replace Fagnano if he got hurt). Jackson came back to the field in the second half with a large cast/splint on his right hand.; by the end of the third quarter Fagnano was receiving attention on his foot and ankle.
Thumb injuries on a quarterback’s throwing hand tend to be very difficult to navigate, and will beg questions about the position not just with a quick turnaround against Jacksonville on Thursday, but llikely beyond that.
A former NFL head coach was I was texting with during the game immediately commented that it looked serious to him, he has seen multiple quarterbacks take hits like that and it tends to be problematic with the tendons and ligaments around the thumb and all the torque needed to deliver the ball with velocity and accuracy
Back-up quarterback Snoop Huntley was thrust back into the game after successive games in which he and the offense failed to score a point in the second half with rookie offensive coordinator Declan Doyle calling plays for the first time this year. The Ravens were hopeful that Jackson could reignite their failing run game with Derrick Henry looking his age at 32 behind a bad offensive line, but Huntley has not activated his legs and he cannot push the ball downfield.
The Ravens win 70% of their regular season games that Jackson starts and are 7-14 without him, with general manger Eric DeCosta a fraudulent roster builder and talent evaluator. Decosta has also repeatedly failed to extend Jackson like a normal front office would, putting themselves in  a massive hole now, with Jackson a de-facto free agent in 2027 , with a no-trade clause and no-franchise tag clause and $85M cap hit, and Baltimore a team in serious decline liking having to gut the roster next year with a $370M payroll heavy on bloated contracts and short on blue chip players.
There is a growing drumbeat in NFL personnel circles that the Miami Dolphins will make a serious push for Jackson, who is a native of that area and spends his offseasons there. The Ravens maintained Jackson was “day-to-day” while missing three weeks with the high-ankle sprain, during which time he could barely run or practice for the most part. DeCosta made Jackson play out his entire rookie deal, and endure a potential collusion case while on a non-exclusive tag to get a fair-market deal the first time; all highly unusual but that's how this suspect front office operates.
As for the game, Huntley was getting attention on the sidelines after the Ravens cut the deficit to 10-7 early on, and Fagnano (UCONN) soon entered as the emergency third QB. The Ravens came into Buffalo with just one AFC win, and losses to the Bills and Jaguars in the span of five days would effectively end their season and perhaps prompt selling veterans at the trade deadline.

title: Four Pivotal Ravens Matchups to Watch vs. Bills
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens' Week 8 bout against the Buffalo Bills could ultimately be decided by battles between specific position groups or individual players outperforming their counterparts on the other side of the ball.
In the team's first game with two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson back under center after he missed the last three games with an ankle sprain, they're entering this matchup as slight road underdogs.
If the Ravens prevail, they will improve to 5-3 and will likely still be in last place in the AFC North standings since they're the only team without a division win, and even if the other three lose on Sunday, they'd all be tied with the same number of losses. Here are the four matchups that can either make or break this game:
The Ravens' two-time Pro Bowl wideout ranks seventh in the league in receiving yards with a team-leading 608 yards and is one of only two pass catchers averaging over 100 receiving yards per game with his 101.3, trailing only the reigning Offensive Player of the Year, Jaxon Smith-Njigba. An area where Flowers has feasted the most this year, no matter who has been under center, is over the middle of the field.
First-year offensive coordinator Declan Doyle has consistently found ways to get him matched up against off-ball linebackers in space, which is a mismatch in favor of the Ravens every time. With Jackson back in the lineup, Flowers can get back to stretching the field vertically, as the two of them were routinely linking up for 20-plus yard plays through the air to begin the season before injuries interrupted their lethal connection.
With Buffalo's elite blocking unit at full strength in this game, Baltimore is going to need to play to its full potential in the trenches both along the interior and on the edge. In order to slow down James Cook and a Bills' rushing attack, which ranks fifth in the league in yards, second in yards per attempt (5.1) and first in expected points added by the ground game (31.71), they'll need to win at the point of attack and own the line of scrimmage. With a quarterback like Josh Allen who can plow his way for a first down in just about any short-to-medium yardage situation, limiting their gains on early downs will be paramount, as will maintaining rush-lane integrity to limit and prevent scrambles.
Some specific individual matchups to keep an eye on will be the Ravens' four-time Pro Bowl edge rusher Trey Hendrickson against Bills' left tackle Dion Dawkins, two-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike against guards O'Cyrus Torrence and Alec Anderson and outside linebacker Mike Green against backup right tackle Tylan Grable, who is filling in for injured veteran Spencer Brown .
On the flip side, the Ravens also need to dictate terms in the trenches on offense against a talented Buffalo front in order to have success in Jackson's long-awaited return to the lineup. It won't be easy along the interior, especially without stud first-round rookie Vega Ioane, who is out with a knee injury . It means that they'll have to face the defensive tackle duo of veteran Ed Oliver and second-year breakout Deone Walker with yet another different configuration, as this will mark the second game for two-time Pro Bowl center Cam Jurgens since being acquired via trade and the second start of the season for Andrew Vorhees.
On the edge, the only player who's been consistently generating pressure for the Bills is defensive end Gregory Rousseau. He leads the team with six sacks but hasn't recorded one in their last three games, and since he lines up on the defense's left side, he'll be seeing a lot of Ravens right tackle Roger Rosengarten, who has had a nice bounce-back campaign as one of the team's most consistent offensive linemen.
The Ravens have struggled to limit the impact of the opposing team's wideouts for all four quarters this season, and their corners are the primary culprits, allowing the third-most receiving yards to the receiver position with 1,271. While the Bills haven't gotten much prolific production from their wideouts, with none over 300 receiving yards entering this game, they tend to make key plays in high-leverage moments, and veteran D.J. Moore will be back in action for the first time since Week 4. After horrendous showings in last week's loss to the Cincinnati Bengals, Baltimore will need a big bounce-back game from their starting outside duo of Marlon Humphrey and Nate Wiggins in this one if they hope to avoid getting in a shootout.

title: Ravens Week 8 Inactives, With Lamar Jackson Returning
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens may be a few more AFC losses from being out of contending more and into player-development mode with another season in the balance, but they are leaning into their experience Sunday at Buffalo.
With the return of Lamar Jackson from a three-week absence with a high-ankle sprain, Baltimore badly needs to beat the Bills to turn the tide after blowing double-digit leads in the second half two straight weeks in losses to the division rival Bengals and Browns. With that in mind, general manager Eric DeCosta is leaning into his highest-paid players at Buffalo – despite their historic struggles – and the inactives for this game speak to that dynamic.
The Ravens also knew their top pick, guard Vega Ioane (14th overall and the best center on the team as well) was out with a knee injury. Perhaps he can get back for Thursday’s game bit this is obviously a short week. Rookie receiver Elijah Sarratt (fourth round) was also inactive and the Baltimore native has yet to find his way in this offense.
Rookie slot corner Chandler Rivers (fifth-round) has strong instincts attack the ball on screens in front of him but has been picked on badly in coverage – Baltimore’s slot defense has been atrocious - and has plenty to do with them getting DeCosta-ed week after week – and he is not playing in this game, either.
Young guard Emery Jones has been battling injury which means a sixth new offensive line combination in eight games, with struggling Andrew Vorhees likely thrust back into that role. Aeneas Peebles – the only defensive tackle DeCosta took in a historically significant 2025 DT draft despite it being a big need – still cannot see the field and he was scratched again. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano is again the emergency third QB.
Starting safety Jaylinn Hawkins was ruled out with injury on Friday.
Jackson’s return gives this team a chance to reverse the course of its season, but it carries almost identical warts and serious personnel concerns as the pathetic product DeCosta fielded in 2025, when he won a power struggle with potential Hall of Fame head coach John Harbaugh, gutting that staff that included offensive coordinator Todd Monken, now head coach of the Browns and a top midseason candidate for NFL Coach of the Year, along with Harbaugh (Giants).
DeCosta and team president Sashi Brown branded this a Super Bowl contender when they hired novice head coach Jesse Minter and built one of only two staffs in the entire NFL without a former NFL head coach on the roster . Yet about 20 percent of the Week 1 roster was compromised of players without an NFL snap, while at the same time the bulk of the team-record $370M payroll was going to veterans decidedly on the decline with ridiculously bloated contracts (Roquan Smith, Marlon Humphrey, Mark Andrews, John Simpson).
The coming weeks will be critical to determining how much longer they can afford to prop up some of them, as we discussed recently with longtime NFL GM Marty Hurney on "The Daily Flock."
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Predicting What Lamar Jackson Will Do Vs. Bills In First Game Back From Injury
full_text:
It’s been a month since we were able to forecast what Lamar Jackson was about to do to an NFL defense.
Man, have we missed doing the research and, especially, watching him play. We were quite on point about what to expect from him in each of the first four games, and unfortunately Jackson suffered a high-ankle sprain at the end of the first half in Week 4 and the Ravens spiraled without him (7-14 all time when he can’t start). He covers up the repeated failures of general manager Eric DeCosta , and he is the genius – not rookie offensive coordinator Declan Doyle who has been getting exposed lately – and he has carved up the Bills in the regular season throughout his career and this Bills defense is particularly vulnerable.
So what do we expect on Sunday afternoon with Jackson just back from injury? Well, after being able to practice fully all week, and given the magnitude of this game (it’s must-win for Baltimore, one could argue), and given the Ravens’ proclivity for getting DeCosta-ed every week without him ( blowing a double-digit lead in the second half and losing ), I believe we are going to see the two-time MVP in do-it-all mode from the onset, whether that’s how Doyle is calling the game or not.
Jackson knows best. And the Ravens best operate accordingly
The Ravens should get over their projected team total here and 30 points feels right (of course, that’s unlikely to be enough to win given the state of Baltimore’s defense, which needs changes before the trade deadline) . Jackson has faced Buffalo five times in the regular season, and they average 33.2 points/game when he does. Buffalo will likely move the ball at will , so pressure will be on to score.
The Bills rely on a few pass rushers to get them off the field, but the secondary is among the worst in the NFL and we doubt they figured out how to overcome their talent limitations in the bye week. Doyle’s early-game scripts have been remarkable, Zay Flowers has been featured in those looks, and that won’t change against these defensive backs.
Flowers, despite missing time to injury and despite Jackson missing half the season, leads the NFL in receptions per game in the first half (27 in 6 games), and first-half receiving yards (486) at an astounding 18 yards/reception. Doyle will go after this group – Buffalo has allowed 26 passes of 20 yards or more (third in NFL despite already having their bye) and 15 of 25 yards or more (fifth-most) and they don’t have anyone who can handle Flowers with a two-way go in the slot.
Buffalo’s slot defense is even worse than Jesse Minter’s – which is saying something – ranking 28th in allowing a 122.2 rating and 9.2 yards/attempt (26th). We anticipate explosives with YAC and air yards and could see Jackson having a 50-yard pass and 25-yard run.
Jackson tends to prove a point when people doubt his physical ability and playing against Josh Allen, the rare running QB who can rival him, tends to get Jackson’s wheels going, too. He’s never had a 20 yard run against Buffalo in the regular season but he tends to extend drives repeatedly with his legs.
Jackson averages 8 runs for 55 yards against these guys and he has at least six carries in every meeting with them in the regular season and this defense, while 15th in Defensive Expected Points Added vs QB runs, is allowing 5.5 yards/carry to them but has not really been tested in ways that Jackson’s can challenge them.
Doyle’s run scheme is failing with Derrick Henry starting to show his age at 32 – and leading the NFL in carries, while averaging just 3.9 yards/rush (gulp) – and this offensive line is not good. Jackson is going to have to scoot and make things happen himself outside the pocket to revive a dormant attack. We believe he will do just that and believe he has to run for 3-5 first downs and 65 or more yards if he’s going to keep pace with what Baltimore’s defense is going to yield to Allen (Ravens are 30th in EPA vs QB runs despite not facing anyone who really wants to run this season).
Jackson was a top five QB in the redzone before his injury. Doyle has defaulted to the failing run game without him – as he should with Snoop Huntley in charge – but that’s over now. And handing it off to Henry in short-yardage situations has been a disaster. Jackson will finish multiple drives with redzone TD passes and we suspect rookie tight ends Josh Cuevas and Matthew Hibner to get chances to hit pay dirt.
The Ravens need Jackson's genius most in the RZ, and there is no reason to doubt it.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Ravens Red Zone Report: What’s Working And Failing And What Must Change in Week 8
full_text:
There is so much going on with the Ravens at a macro level right now between coaches and general managers getting exposed and all the second-half collapses and blaming fans for not being loud enough and with team legends excoriating this current edition on social media, it’s easy to gloss over specific micro issues.
And, with two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson coming back from a three-week absence due to a high-ankle sprain, it’s also easy to fall into the trap that he’s going to just solve everything. Indeed, he is the ultimate deodorant that covers up Eric DeCosta’s nasty work as an evaluator and negotiator and “steward” of the franchise, and they need him desperately. They need him to save the offense and therefore provide an even greater safety net to a defense that’s on fraud alert.
The Ravens especially need him to find ways to finish drives in the second half of games after Baltimore has failed to score after the half in two straight games with “genius” offensive coordinator Declan Doyle at the helm, stalling out in the redzone when they manage to get there. Jackson can’t do much to help the Ravens defensive redzone woes, but the more points the better ahead of what could be a shootout with the Bills in Buffalo on Sunday.
The Ravens rank 20th in the NFL in redzone TD% differential (-4.2%) and 25th in redzone scoring differential (-8.3%) and no one in the media is even bringing it up because of all the other chaos and noise. But if they don’t fix it soon, this season will spiral into the abyss like last year’s and they’ll keep getting Decosta-ed (blowing second-half, double-digit leads to lose) week after week.
RedZone TD Efficiency : 62.5% (13th) 3rd-and-1/4th-and-1 Rush Conv : 25% (27th)
Total Pass EPA/Game : 0.50 (14th) Total Run EPA/G : -.27 (21st)
The issues with the offensive line are getting compounded as the field compresses and the play book constricts, and as the rookie play caller gets into clutch situations in the second half of games. Doyle spoke about wanting to script even more of the game as he explained his self-scout this week; um, yeah I am not sure thinking you can have even more of the game called a day before it starts is the answer, but whatever.
“I would say I probably haven't stuck to that second-half script enough,”’ Doyle offered this week, “and I probably have to stick with my guns a little more at times, and that would be kind of my own self-evaluation of that.”
I would say Jackson is the only thing keeping this from being a bottom-eight offense, and you’d best defer to his true genius in the redzone and let him do what he wants and follow what he sees. Stay out of the way. And lean into him doing what he wants at the line of scrimmage.
The best offensive lineman on the team – rookie Vega Ioane – is out with a knee injury it will be yet another new offensive line combination (the sixth unique one to start a game). Doyle also needs to change his play calling trends now that Snoop Huntley is making way for Jackson. The Ravens are throwing the ball just 39% of the time in the RZ – 30th in the NFL – and with tight end Mark Andrews fully cooked and this team’s only big-play threat quite small to go real damage in the redzone (Zay Flowers) Doyle better start flooding this area with his rookie tight ends.
The short-yardage game with Derrick Henry (who looks like a 32-year old back and needs help in the backfield by the deadline ) hasn’t been good for over a year now, this line stinks inside (paying a ridiculous ransom of a struggling offensive lineman will go down as another DeCosta FAIL , and Doyle better lean into the option game and RPOs in this part of the field.
RedZone TD Efficiency: 66.7% (T-20th) Opposing Passer Rating : 111.7 (25th)
Pressure Rate: 30% (20th) Third Down Conv: 46.3% (T-20th)
Total Pass D EPA: -1.61 (23rd)                                 T otal Rush D EPA : -0.84 (29th)
Rookie head coach in Jesse Minter, no former head coaches on staff ( just the way DeCosta designed it ), trying to manage a defense through an entire game and run a sideline and coach an entire team for the first time on an alleged Super Bowl contender, was a big ask. Of course it’s manifesting more profoundly in the second half of games as injuries mount and adjustments are demanded in all three phases. And of course that nativity shows up most in special situations: RZ is everything in this modern game (with defensive coordinator often willing to bleed out yards between the 20s playing soft zone – and that’s all Minter does).
His defensive backs are a tragedy right now, they don’t seem connected or comfortable with his zone assignments and longtime head coach Marvin Lewis pointed out on “The Daily Flock” the obvious communication issues and bad fits in key moments. Minter best get that fixed first.
“It just starts with us putting them in a better position,” Minter said Monday. “Always starts with the coaching, in my opinion, and I'll leave it at that."
As always, we have suggestions (and they read everything, trust me).
Start with what Wink Martindale, the guy who created this defense with some help from Minter and Seahawks Super Bowl winning coach Mike McDonald, who agreed with me that Minter “needs to blitz more.” Let’s start there. DeCosta’s secondary lacks anything close to a play maker on the back end (Kyle Hamilton is a linebacker).
He also needs to get Marlon Humphrey into the slot in these tight-field situations, he should have him blitzing more from the slot and getting Roquan Smith off the field in some of these dime looks – yeah I get it he wears the green dot – is something I called for way back in the summer when defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver guaranteed an impact season.
This chart would say otherwise .
The sooner DeCosta’s made men start seeing more of the bench , the better the chances of actually keeping this from being another total disaster.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Four Winners & One Loser From Bills Lopsided Win Against Ravens in Week 8
full_text:
Once again, the Buffalo Bills proved to be one of the top teams in the league after a bye week as they defeated the Baltimore Ravens easily in Week 8.
It might not have been the prettiest game throughout, but Buffalo still won 36-10, thanks in large part to the Ravens dealing with multiple injuries at quarterback . Lamar Jackson was lost to a thumb injury on the first play of the game, and not long after that, backup Tyler Huntley went down with a foot injury.
Undrafted free agent Joe Fagnano was no match for Josh Allen and the Bills, who remain the top team in the AFC East. With this one in the books, let's see who stood out as both winners and losers for the Bills this weekend.
Nursing a 10-7 lead, the Bills needed a play from their defense in the second quarter, and Cole Bishop delivered. The safety went after Tyler Huntley on a blitz and lit him up, forcing a fumble in the process. The loose ball was recovered by linebacker Kaleb Elarms-Orr, and even though Buffalo was kept out of the end zone, Bishop set them up close enough that Tyler Bass knocked in a field goal to make it a 13-7 lead for the Bills.
2025 third-round pick Landon Jackson recorded his first career sack on Sunday, and did so at a great time. Baltimore had to turn to emergency third-quarterback Joe Fagnano, and he completed a couple of passes to move the Ravens to the Buffalo seven.
That's when Jackson broke free and sacked the rookie for a nine-yard loss. A couple of plays later, Tyler Loop missed a 34-yard field goal as things fell off the rails for Baltimore following Jackson's play.
Geno Stone was given a chance to prove himself on Sunday and was facing his old team. He stepped up near the end of the first half after DJ Moore fumbled the ball away. Baltimore was attempting to cut the lead going into the half, but Stone broke up a pass from quarterback Joe Fagnano.
He was unable to come up with the pick himself, but he batted the ball in the air, and rookie Davison Igbinosun ended up corraling it for his first career interception. That set up the Bills for a late field goal, sending them into the half with a nine-point lead.
Buffalo was up 10-0, but allowed the Ravens some life late in the first quarter with a costly turnover. Josh Allen threw the ball to Jackson Hawes, and while it was slightly behind the second-year tight end, Hawes had both hands on the ball.
He was unable to bring it in, however, and the ball bounced into the arms of Broderick Washington Jr. Baltimore responded with a Derrick Henry touchdown as Hawes' sophomore slump continues.
Josh Allen wasn't sharp throughout, but he threw for 289 yards with two touchdown passes and a touchdown run. His two passes put him atop the franchise leaderboard as he surpassed Jim Kelly for the most touchdown passes in team history.
Josh Allen becomes the Bills all-time leader in TD passes (259) with Jim Kelly in attendance 👏 BALvsBUF on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/k62VFqausS
Allen and the Bills' offense continue to rack up points, and they just improved to 6-1 this season. Now, they turn their attention to the Minnesota Vikings, whom they will face on Monday Night Football in Week 9.

title: Josh Allen Leaps Bills Hall of Famer, Sets Another Team Record vs. Ravens
full_text:
Josh Allen may go down as the greatest Buffalo Bills player of all time. And the team record he just set will be a major addition to his resume.
The Bills took care of business off of their bye week, handling the Baltimore Ravens , 36-10, after the team lost both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley to injury in the game.
Allen looked like he had become the franchise's all-time passing-touchdown leader (including the playoffs) when he found Khalil Shakir on a first-quarter throw in the red zone. That only set up his first touchdown of the day: a 1-yard quarterback sneak, pushing his rushing TD total for the year to nine.
But it was D.J. Moore who hauled in the record-setting pass. Which was fitting, as Buffalo's new No. 1 wide receiver returned to the lineup for the first time since Week 4 . Shout-out to the CBS camera crew too for immediately cutting to Jim Kelly, the previous Bills' record-holder.
Adding in is connection with Dalton Kincaid in the fourth quarter, Allen is now up to 260 TD passes in his career.
Josh Allen becomes the Bills all-time leader in TD passes (259) with Jim Kelly in attendance 👏 BALvsBUF on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/k62VFqausS
Allen has become the franchise's leader in several categories, including rushing touchdowns and total touchdowns scored. Next on his radar could be regular-season TD passes (237), passing yards  (35,467), and wins by a QB (101), all held by Kelly.
Kelly and Allen's mutual admiration has been shared over the years. The Hall of Fame QB joined Good Morning Football in June to discuss Allen being named the NFL's top QB in a poll run by ESPN specificallly with coaches and executives throughout the league.
"Josh is Josh. That's what he does. He runs, he makes the big plays with his legs," said Kelly in an iterview with WWE star Seth Rollins. "And yeah, you want him to protect himself a little bit more, because he does take chances. But the thing is, that's him. That's the way he plays football, and I love it."
With Allen's league-leading ninth rushing TD of the year coming in the win over Baltimore, he extended his career rushing scores to 88. He and Cam Newton are the only players in NFL history to lead their respective franchises in both passing and rushing TDs.
It is hard to quantify how diverse Allen's dual-threat skills are. Once he gets to 90 rushing TDs, he'll be tied for 14th all-time with Eric Dickerson and Curtis Martin, two Hall of Fame running backs.
That's what makes what he does through the air even more impressive. It will only be a matter of time before Allen's name is attached to more of Buffalo's all-time passing ranks when it's all said and done.
Josh Allen. Dalton Kincaid. All Buffalo in this one. BALvsBUF on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/StHo4EOPvC

title: Biggest Takeaways From Buffalo Bills Week 8 Win Against Ravens
full_text:
Leading up to the showdown between the Buffalo Bills and Baltimore Ravens, there was a lot of news surrounding the health of Lamar Jackson . He had been dealing with a high ankle sprain, which kept him out for three games, but he was back in action in Week 8 . At least for one play.
Jackson was injured on the first snap of the game when his hand hit Greg Rousseau's while attempting a pass to Zay Flowers. Jackson was quickly taken to the locker room , and Tyler Huntley took over under center. Huntley couldn't finish the first half either, as he suffered a toe injury. Baltimore turned to undrafted rookie free agent Joe Fagnano, who was the emergency third quarterback.
Despite being down to their third quarterback, the Ravens hung with the Bills much longer than expected. Eventually, the Bills pulled out in front, winning 36-10. Considering they were coming off a bye week, it was a rather sloppy performance from Buffalo, as they had far too many penalties and left points on the board.
Still, they're 6-1 and looking ahead to their big showdown with the Minnesota Vikings next week. Before we turn our attention to that game, let's look back at their latest win with the biggest takeaways from Week 8.
The Bills have one of the top offenses in the NFL, and part of that is due to Joe Brady's aggressiveness. That was on display on Sunday as he attempted four fourth-down conversions in the first quarter.
His first was a fourth-and-goal, which ended in a touchdown run from Josh Allen. They failed to convert on a fourth-and-four in the second quarter, but made up for it on fourth-and-one from the 11 on the next drive. Allen pitched the ball to James Cook, who extended the ball and converted the first down, although they needed the assistance of replay.
Brady and the Bills should have been able to score another touchdown there, but a questionable third-down run led to a loss of yards, forcing them to settle for a field goal from Tyler Bass. His final fourth-down attempt in the first half was a short pass to Ty Johnson, which moved the ball to the Baltimore 18 at the two-minute warning.
Even with the Ravens going to their third quarterback by the second quarter, this game was closer than it should have been for much of the first half. That wasn't necessarily due to the Ravens, but more so to the continued sloppy play from Buffalo.
There was a first-half interception from Josh Allen, which went off the hands of backup tight end Jackson Hawes. Shortly after the two-minute warning, there was another turnover; this time, DJ Moore fumbled it away after catching a pass at the Baltimore 20. That ended an impressive six-play, 61-yard drive and took points off the board for the home team.
An interception allowed Buffalo to score right before the half, giving them a 16-7 lead, but this game should have been a blowout going into the break.
After recording six sacks over the first three games of the season, Greg Rousseau was getting plenty of attention as a potential Defensive Player of the Year candidate . Since then, he's been quiet . That changed against the Ravens, as Rousseau impacted the game on the opening play.
While no one wants to see an opponent injured, it was a good play from Rousseau to get a hand in the way and force an incomplete pass from Jackson. He continued to create pressure and picked up his seventh sack of the season. In all, Buffalo had four sacks on the day, including the first of Landon Jackson's career.
Penalties have been a concern throughout the season, and that was the case once again in Week 8. Buffalo was flagged 10 times for 87 yards, giving the Ravens far too many free yards in the process.
They take on one of the elite defenses in Week 9 in the Minnesota Vikings. It will be a tough contest on the road and the Bills are going to have a tough time coming out with a win if they don't clean up the discipline issues.
Congratulations are in order for Josh Allen, who hit DJ Moore for a touchdown early in the fourth quarter, which was the 259th of his career. That moved him ahead of Jim Kelly for the most in franchise history.
Josh Allen becomes the Bills all-time leader in TD passes (259) with Jim Kelly in attendance 👏 BALvsBUF on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/k62VFqausS
He threw another one to Dalton Kincaid shortly afterward, putting the game away in the process.

title: James Cook Injury Update: Buffalo Bills RB Status Following Scary Hit
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills and Baltimore Ravens are playing in a game full of injuries .
Most have been on the Ravens' side, but the Bills might have just been dealt a major blow. While driving for a score early in the fourth quarter, running back James Cook ran for a first down but landed awkwardly while being tackled.
Cook's head hit the turf , and his upper body seemed to roll over the top of him. It was scary enough that left guard Alec Anderson was seen waving the training staff onto the field to check on the star running back.
After lying on the ground for a moment, Cook was able to pop up, which was an excellent sign. He then entered the blue medical tent for further evaluation.
Cook was evaluated for a head injury and has been cleared to play . He returned to the sideline with his teammates and will be able to get back on the field.
Before going to the sideline, Cook had been a huge part of the offense. He had 20 rushing attempts for 76 yards with a touchdown. He also had two receptions for 21 yards, helping Buffalo take a commanding lead into the final quarter.
With the Bills up by multiple touchdowns, it would probably be wise to allow Cook to rest for the remainder of this game and focus on their big showdown in Week 9 as the Bills will visit the Minnesota Vikings on Monday Night Football. Minnesota boasts one of the league's elite defenses and Buffalo will need Cook as close to 100 percent as possible to pull off a win.
Baltimore lost their starting quarterback on the opening drive, with Lamar Jackson suffering a thumb injury when his hand hit Greg Rousseau's arm. His backup, Tyler Huntley, also went down as he suffered a foot injury.
For Jackson, it was a frustrating turn of events after he missed the previous three games with a high ankle sprain. He was excited to return to action against the Bills, but finished just 0-1 passing.
Huntley was also sidelined after suffering a foot injury, leaving the Ravens with their emergency quarterback Joe Fagnano. The undrafted rookie out of UConn was also banged up during the game, suffering an ankle injury. He stayed in the game, but this has been a tough one for both sides of the ball.

title: Will Dalton Kincaid Play for Bills Today? TE Fantasy Advice
full_text:
Dalton Kincaid started the season on fire for the Buffalo Bills, but has since slowed down some. Still, he remains one of the more intriguing fantasy options, especially in a high-octane offense.
Even during their Week 7 outing against the Las Vegas Raiders , Kincaid managed double-digit points, hauling in seven passes for 38 yards. His day could have been even better as he had a touchdown called back due to penalty.
Not everything was great for Kincaid, even though that game was on his birthday. The tight end had to leave briefly when he suffered a chest injury. He was able to return and had the week to rest up with the Bills off in Week 7.
Now as the Bills prepare to play the Baltimore Ravens in Week 8 , the question is whether he will suit up. Kincaid was limited during the week, but said he felt good entering the weekend.
“Feeling good. Just how football goes. Some weeks will be worse than others, and then some weeks will feel great. But lucky and grateful enough to be able to go out there and practice," said Kincaid after Wednesday's practice (via WGR's Sal Capaccio ).
Entering the weekend, Kincaid is one of the Bills listed as questionable , but the belief is that he will be able to play. The next question, is how much of an impact can he make against Baltimore. He's been hopeful, although the team will make the determination after warmups.
From @SportsCenter over weekend on Bills: -Dalton Kincaid optimistic about playing. Bills to determine but he’s been hopeful -D.J. Moore could be back for the first time in about a month pic.twitter.com/t00nd6ApGo
Overall, the Ravens have been strong against tight ends this season, although they did surrender two touchdowns last weekend as Mike Gesicki and Drew Sample of the Cincinnati Bengals both found their way to the end zone.
That said, Kincaid hasn't been ultra reliable. He had 130 yards in Week 1 followed by 95 yards in Week 2. Since then, he has yet to record more than 38 yards in a game. Oddly enough, he hit that number twice and has just seven yards in his two other appearances since his breakout.
As for the last time he faced the Ravens, he did finish with four receptions for 48 yards and a touchdown. That's a solid fantasy performance, but at this point, Kincaid is a touchdown-reliant player. Until he proves he's back to running routes the way he did to start the season, fantasy owners should exercise caution.

title: Will DJ Moore Play Today? Injury Update, Fantasy Advice for Bills' WR in Week 8
full_text:
UPDATE: Buffalo Bills wide receiver DJ Moore is officially active for Week 8 .
Here we are once again with uncertainty surrounding Buffalo Bills wide receiver DJ Moore ahead of the Week 8 game against the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday afternoon.
Moore has unfortunately been dealing with a shoulder injury for much of the 2026 season and hasn't played in what seems like forever.
After his impressive debut in Week 1, Moore suffered an AC joint sprain in Week 2 and then re-aggravated the injury in Week 4 and has not appeared in a game since then.
Now, coming out of the Week 7 bye, Moore practiced on a limited basis all three days in the lead up to the Week 8 contest against the Ravens and has drawn the questionable tag .
Here's what we know about Moore's chances of suiting up in what is a huge AFC showdown with the Ravens.
UPDATE: He's back: Moore is officially active for Week 8 .
UPDATE: To further confirm Moore's status, ESPN's Adam Schefter reports he is expected to play .
"Bills WR D.J. Moore, who has missed the past two games due to a shoulder injury, is expected to play today vs. the Ravens," Schefter wrote.
Despite having the questionable tag he has failed to beat the last two games, Moore is indeed expected to suit up in Week 8, according to NFL Network's Cameron Wolfe .
"WR DJ Moore is listed as questionable but to he expects to play Sunday barring any setback. Obvious boost for Josh Allen," he reported.
With the Bills and Ravens kicking off a 1 p.m. ET on Sunday, both teams will drop their inactives at 11:30 a.m. ET, so make sure to confirm Moore's status then.
It's a tough call with Moore this week.
In the two games he has finished, Moore has recorded 11 catches for 167 yards and a touchdown. However, he has also exited two games early because of his shoulder injury.
The fact that he didn't practice in full this week and was wearing a red non-contact jersey tells us he still isn't 100%, which means there is added risk of another early exit.
But, here's the thing: it's possible he may not be 100% for weeks, if not for the rest of the season, so this is something fantasy owners may just have to live with and roll the dice on each and every week.
As far as the matchup is concerned, it's a good one, as the Ravens are ceding the eighth-most fantasy points per game to wideouts this season, according to CBS Sports .
We're putting Moore in lineups this week and hoping he makes it through the game in one piece.

title: NFL Prediction Panel's Consensus Pick for Bills' Return to Action vs. Ravens
full_text:
There are multiple intangibles that favor the Buffalo Bills in their Week 8 home game against the Baltimore Ravens, but the same can be said from the other side.
Yes, the Bills have home-field advantage along with the benefit of extra rest and recovery from the Week 7 bye .
"Extra week's great. Great for everybody, honestly. Just mental, physical reset," said tight end Dalton Kincaid, who is questionable to play due to a rib issue.
The Bills can move one step closer to NFL history by winning again immediately following their bye week. Buffalo is 11-0 over its last 11 games after a bye. The Philadelphia Eagles set the record with 13 consecutive wins from 1999 through 2011.
In addition to the historical trend ebeing in the Bills' side, there's  the fact that Buffalo leads the NFL in scoring offense while Baltimore was forced for 35 points last time out.
It seems as if that is enough to convince Sports Illustrated's weekly prediction panel to back the Bills over the Ravens on November 1.
All eight experts, including senior reporter Albert Breer, picked Buffalo to take care of business in Orchard Park and move to 6-1 overall. As always, SI's selections are straight up. When it comes to the official wagering line, the Bills are a 3.0-point home favorite ( per DraftKings ).
There is, however, reason for caution amongst Bills' backers. On the other sideline, the heavily-criticized Ravens should be a hungry, desperate bunch having lost their last two games.
Furthermore, they should receive a noticeable boost from quarterback Lamar Jackson's return to the lineup after missing three consecutive contests.
"I'm excited. I'm always excited when I'm able to be back on the field with my guys. Put us in the win column, help us get another dub," said Jackson on Friday.
Buffalo not only has to account for the explosive dual threat that Jackson presents. Ravens' primary running back Derrick Henry is on the back end of a Hall-of-Fame career.
"They're two dimensional in everything that can do. It's gonna be a huge task for our defense, but it's a great opportunity for us as well," said Brady.
In his last two regular season games against the Bills, Henry has rushed for a remarkable 368 yards on a combined 42 carries.
Making for an even greater challenge, Buffalo is shorthanded in the defensive secondary. Safety CJ Gardner-Johnson is suspended for the game while slot cornerback Dee Alford will likely be unavailable due to an ankle injury.
Veteran Damar Hamlin will start in Gardner-Johnson's place, and Buffalo added three reinforcements to the defensive backfield on Saturday.
On the plus side, the Bills are expected to welcome back defensive tackle Ed Oliver to the front for the first time since Week 4.

title: Analyzing Three Trade Deadline Targets Linked to Bills
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills need help on defense.
That's probably why NFL analyst Bucky Brooks linked the team to three defenders potentially on the trade block when analyzing the best fits for them at the deadline.
But are any of these players actually realistic options for Brandon Beane?
How he could help: Terrel Bernard and Dorian Williams have not been playing their best football this season. The former has surrendered 22 receptions for 233 yards and a 98.8 passer rating when targeted (per PFF), and has missed five tackles in six games. The latter has given up 17 receptions for 146 yards and three TDs, along with a 116.3 passer rating against (per PFF).
Brooks writes, "His instincts, awareness and disruptiveness make him a perfect addition for any roster that lacks an alpha dog in the middle."
Why it won't happen: Aside from the Dolphins likely avoiding trading one of their best players to another AFC East team, Brooks recently signed an extension keeping him in Miami until 2029 as one of the highest paid linebackers in the NFL. The Bills would need to prepare to take on his $17 million cap hit next season, with the two seasons after costing even more.
How he could help: The Bills need help on the back end too. CJ Gardner-Johnson has been wildly inconsistent and is now serving a one-game suspension , and Cole Bishop likely needs more stability in a safety partner in order to take the next step as an emerging player.
Why it might work: Arizona likely won't be a serious contender this year, and already traded away Marvin Harrison Jr. Baker has just one year remaining on his deal, with $0 guaranteed after this season. The Bills would need to take on roughly $8 million of Baker's contract this season, meaning Brandon Beane would need to pull some levers or negotiate salary retention for Arizona to help the Bills stay under the cap.
How he could help: Despite playing in his age-35 season, Mack is still a viable edge rusher. Per PFF, his 10.1% win rate is nearly identical to TJ Watt and ahead of players like Josh Hines-Allen and Brian Burns. In fact, Greg Rousseau is the only Bill with a higher win rate.
Why it shouldn't happen: I would love to see Mack return to Buffalo, but the Bills have already poured too many assets into the edge rusher position and need to spread the wealth. Beane signed Bradley Chubb to a three-year $43.5 million contract and drafted TJ Parker with their first selection in the 2026 NFL Draft. That was with Greg Rousseau and Michael Hoecht already on the roster. The Bills would need to give up a draft pick and roughly $4.5 million in cap space in order to obtain Mack, who would crowd an edge rusher room full of capable bodies already.

title: Panthers Mock Draft: Trenches, Trenches, and More Trenches
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers are still in first place, but based on the last few weeks of football, it's hard to predict that they'll stay there. The competent, capable team that beat the Detroit Lions is seemingly nowhere to be found now.
Regardless of whether they can stay afloat in a bad division, they should have eyes on the future. There are still way too many holes on this roster, and we suspect plenty of current starters or key contributors won't be around next year.
So, without further ado, here's our first mock draft of the season.
Note: Draft order changes constantly with virtually every single game played.
The offensive line has to be a priority, and ironically, the Panthers have good options at tackle moving forward. They don't have good options on the interior. The jury's out on center Sam Hecht, Luke Fortner won't stick around, Robert Hunt has been bad, and Damien Lewis is hurt. Enter Iowa interior lineman Kade Pieper, who can play guard and center.
The other side of the line isn't in good shape, either. Tershawn Wharton has been bad and could be cut, and aside from Derrick Brown, not much is working to stop the run. Kentucky defensive lineman Tavion Gadson would provide the Panthers with a much-needed body up front to help fix the defense's biggest issue.
The Panthers still can't really rush the passer. Nic Scourton will be back and Jaelan Phillips will hopefully be healthier, but the Panthers are likely to lose Pat Jones. Since Phillips has sadly been underwhelming, EDGE isn't a spot the Panthers can totally ignore in the draft.
Apparently, you can't actually have too many cornerbacks. Mike Jackson may or may not be on the team, and relying on Jaycee Horn and Will Lee to play 17 games each is a risk. The position has to be addressed again, and going back to the fourth-round CB well here with Jalen Mayo is smart.
It's true that tackle is in a better spot (assuming Ikem Ekwonu gets re-signed and can play again), but it's still not good. Who knows what Taylor Moton's future looks like? Rasheed Walker should honestly never play a down for the Panthers after his contract is up, and Monroe Freeling, at best, is very raw right now. The Panthers can add some developmental depth in Niki Prongos.
At this point, the Panthers should be more than happy loading up on the trenches. That is clearly the weakness of this team despite the investments, so the need is still there. Adding Santana Hopper gives the Panthers another shot at someone up front being able to stop the run.
Sure, a seventh-rounder faces long odds of ever even playing in the NFL, but if the Panthers are taking a swing, it should be at a position they need depth at, and this year has revealed exactly where that is. Adding cornerback Dezz Ricks gives them one more bullet in the chamber.
The same logic above applies. On offense, the position that's been crushed the hardest is tackle, so adding more players there makes the most sense. They need better blocking, so why not take a chance on Tyree Adams?

title: Panthers Urged to Swap Bryce Young for Lamar Jackson in Ill-Fated Proposal
full_text:
Could the Carolina Panthers move on from Bryce Young? It's possible, although it seems like they're smart enough to understand that what's gone wrong over the last two weeks has less to do with Young and more to do with his surroundings.
Jason McIntyre and Colin Cowherd of FOX Sports, however, don't agree with that assessment. They're wrong, and their proposal for how the Panthers should proceed at the quarterback position is not a good one.
McIntyre said that this makes "back-to-back weeks" that Young "did not look like a starting quarterback," which is immediately a misinformed take on what's been going on with the Panthers.
Cowherd interjected that he simply couldn't extend Young if he were the Panthers based on these last two weeks. McIntyre added that during the offseason, head coach Dave Canales said Young was the franchise player "for now."
Because the door was technically left open with that comment (nevermind the fact that Young has played the best football of his NFL career, last two weeks included, this season), McIntyre and Cowherd began to speculate on who the Panthers could get, and a two-time MVP came up.
"Lamar Jackson wanted a contract, has not gotten it," McIntyre said. "Does he want to head south, perhaps? Is there a world where Carolina makes a move on Lamar Jackson? I'm just speculating because Bryce Young just does not look like the guy."
Cowherd added that Young is "too good to be a backup," calling him a high-level bridge quarterback. It's as if these two haven't watched a snap of the Panthers this year. Young has faced the highest pressure rate in the NFL and has been dealing with a knee injury since Week 3 that has sapped his mobility.
Those are untenable circumstances for virtually all NFL quarterbacks. The protection has fallen off a cliff (and it was bad to begin with), and Young isn't healthy enough to offset it at the moment. But enough about Young being way better than these two understand.
Jackson is obviously an upgrade. He's a two-time MVP, and when he's playing, there are one or two quarterbacks better than him. He is nearly unrivaled, and his prime is still going on. So yes, the reductive take that Jackson improves the Panthers is true, but it's not that simple.
The Panthers are on the hook for Young's fifth-year option regardless of an extension. That complicates an addition. The cost to acquire Jackson would be astronomical. If they were to pull off a trade, it would cost them a boatload of valuable picks.
That's before signing Jackson to a long-term deal. Now, Jackson is significantly better than Young, but it's probably not worth skipping a potential $40 million salary for Young to add a $60 million salary for Jackson.
Plus, say what you want about Young, but he is durable. Jackson, lately, has not been. Is there any hope that a different, more injury-prone slender QB would hold up better behind this porous offensive line?
Young might not be Jackson, but simply swapping them out just doesn't make sense for the Panthers in any way, shape, or form.

title: Eagles Defender Pitched as Panthers Trade Acquisition & It Makes Too Much Sense
full_text:
I wasn't really looking for Riq Woolen's name when I started checking out some of the trade talk around the Panthers. I knew Carolina needed another corner, but I figured most of the names being thrown around would either cost too much or wouldn't be much better than what the Panthers already have.
Woolen made me stop for a minute. I remember him from Seattle more than anything, especially his rookie year when he had six interceptions and made the Pro Bowl. He's 6-foot-4, can run and has 12 interceptions in his career. Now he's in Philadelphia on a one-year deal and his name is starting to come up with the trade deadline getting closer.
I wouldn't mind seeing Carolina take a chance on him.
I already thought the Panthers were thin at corner before the Green Bay game. Then I watched Will Lee III leave with a hamstring injury and started wondering who Carolina had left.
It wasn't a long list. Chau Smith-Wade and Marco Wilson were out there, and Malcolm DeWalt IV ended up playing in his first NFL game just days after joining the Panthers. Akayleb Evans had already gone on injured reserve, while Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson weren't available.
I don't know when all of those guys are coming back. Maybe Horn and Jackson return soon and things start looking a lot better. After watching Thursday night, I'd rather not wait around and find out.
That's why Woolen makes more sense to me now than he probably would've a couple of weeks ago. Carolina doesn't need him to come in and be its No. 1 corner. The Panthers need another guy who has actually played a lot of NFL football.
Woolen isn't playing like the guy I remember from Seattle right now. He had a rough game against Dallas on Monday, and I'm not going to ignore that just because I like the idea of Carolina trading for him.
But I do remember what he looked like early in his career. Six interceptions as a rookie will get your attention , and he followed that with two more the next year and three in 2024. He's had 12 in four-plus seasons, which is more than enough for me to wonder if there's still something there.
Maybe there isn't. Philadelphia signed him for one year, and if everything was going great I doubt we'd be talking about whether the Eagles might trade him a few months later.
I still think I'd take the chance if the price wasn't much.
I've seen Woolen mentioned in several trade ideas lately, and Carolina keeps coming up as a possible fit. That isn't surprising after watching what has happened to the Panthers at corner over the last month.
I wouldn't give Philadelphia anything close to a premium pick. If the conversation starts getting into the first three rounds, I'm out. Carolina has too many other needs and I'm not giving away an important draft pick for a player who could leave after the season.
If we're talking about a late-round pick, I'm listening.
Maybe Horn and Jackson both come back and a month from now Carolina suddenly has plenty of corners. I'd be fine with that problem. It sounds a lot better than what I watched Thursday night, when the Panthers were trying to finish a game at Lambeau Field with three healthy guys left at the position.
I don't know what Philadelphia would actually want for Woolen or whether Dan Morgan has any interest in him. I just know this is one of the trade ideas I've seen where I wouldn't need much convincing.

title: Panthers Not Trading for Quenton Nelson Aged Like Milk Within Days
full_text:
I saw the Quenton Nelson trade Tuesday and immediately thought about the Panthers. A few days ago I wouldn't have said that. Nelson was available and Carolina apparently wasn't interested, and I didn't have much of a problem with it. He's 30, his contract is almost up and I wasn't interested in seeing the Panthers give away a bunch of draft picks for a guard.
Then I saw Seattle got him for a third-round pick in 2027 and a fifth in 2028 . That wasn't nearly as much as I thought Indianapolis would get for him, especially considering the kind of player we're talking about. Throw in everything that's happened with Carolina's offensive line over the last few days and I started looking at it differently.
I probably would've made that trade.
I wasn't thinking much about Nelson when the Panthers played Tampa Bay. I was thinking about Taylor Moton finally being back and hoping Carolina could get through a game without something else happening up front. Instead, Moton broke his fibula and now he's done for the year . That's a pretty lousy way for his season to end after he had just gotten back.
That's also when the Nelson stuff started bothering me more. Ikem Ekwonu hasn't played yet, and now Carolina is going back to Monroe Freeling at right tackle. Rasheed Walker has been handling the other side, so this isn't exactly an offensive line where I'd look around and say they're good enough and don't need anybody else.
I know Nelson wouldn't have taken Moton's spot. If Carolina traded for him, he was going to play guard and Moton's injury still would've been a problem. But I would've felt a whole lot better about the line with Nelson somewhere in the middle of it, especially once I found out Seattle didn't have to give Indianapolis a first or second-round pick to get him.
Maybe I wouldn't be thinking this way if Moton hadn't gotten hurt. That's why I didn't care much when the Panthers weren't involved with Nelson in the first place. A week later I'm looking at who's available up front and what Seattle paid, and it doesn't sound like such a bad idea anymore.
A future third and fifth isn't nothing, but those aren't picks that would've scared me away. Carolina would've kept its first and second-round picks, and the third wouldn't have been until 2027. When I first heard Nelson's name around the deadline, I figured Indianapolis would want considerably more than that.
Maybe the Colts would've asked Carolina for something different. I have no idea what those conversations would've looked like, or if the Panthers even called. All I can go by is what Nelson actually cost Seattle, and I would've been comfortable with Carolina paying that price.
The contract would've been the part I'd worry about. Nelson is going to want to get paid, and I understand not wanting to spend a ton of money on a guard in his 30s. But that's something Carolina could've figured out later, and I think I'd rather have that decision to make with Nelson already on the roster.
If you asked me about Nelson before Moton got hurt, I probably would've told you to keep the picks. I didn't think this was the kind of move Carolina needed to make, and I definitely didn't want to see them overpay for an older player. A lot changed once Moton went down and I saw what Seattle actually gave up.
I don't know if Nelson would've changed much about this season. The Panthers are 3-4, they've lost two straight and putting one great guard on the offensive line isn't fixing everything we've watched go wrong. I can understand why Carolina might've looked at the age, contract and draft picks and decided it wasn't worth it.
I'm just not sure I agree anymore.
A 2027 third and a 2028 fifth for Quenton Nelson is a deal I would've made.

title: The Panthers Aren't Playing Sunday, But There's One Team They Need to Win
full_text:
I'm not used to the Panthers already being done for the week when Sunday gets here. After watching them lose to Green Bay on Thursday night , I guess the good part is I can sit back today and watch everybody else.
There is one game I'll be paying attention to more than the others.
Atlanta plays Tampa Bay, and as much as I hate to say it, I'm pulling for the Falcons.
I probably wouldn't care much about this game if Tampa hadn't just embarrassed Carolina. The Bucs came into Charlotte with one win and left with a 43-13 win . I didn't see that coming at all.
What bothers me now is Tampa is sitting at 2-5 and still isn't buried. That's crazy when you think about it. Carolina and Atlanta only have one more win, and New Orleans is sitting there with two as well .
So I'm looking at Tampa a little differently than I was a week ago. I thought the Panthers would beat them. Instead, Tampa beat Carolina by 30 and now gets another NFC South game at home.
Let Atlanta handle them today.
I'm not thrilled about the Falcons getting to four wins either. I just don't care about that as much today.
Carolina gets Atlanta again later this season . If that game matters when we get there, the Panthers can do something about it themselves. Right now I'd rather see Tampa take another loss.
Maybe I'm putting too much into what happened last week. A 30-point loss will do that to you. I just watched Tampa look a whole lot better than its record against Carolina, and I'm not interested in seeing whether it can start putting a few wins together.
The Panthers can't do anything about their 3-4 record today. They already played their game this week and lost it. All they can do now is watch the rest of the division play out.
If Tampa loses, I'll take it. The Bucs stay at two wins, Carolina gets a few extra days to get itself together and we move on to next week.
It might feel strange pulling for Atlanta for three hours.

title: Panthers Given Mandate to Make 1 Crucial Trade to Salvage Season
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers have to make a trade. After another debacle , this time on national television, Thursday night, the Panthers clearly don't have the guns to keep up with actual NFC contenders. They may not have the guns to keep up with NFC South contenders.
Injuries are probably the main reason why. It is hard to say this team wouldn't be pretty good if at least some of Xavier Legette, Taylor Moton, Damien Lewis, Ikem Ekwonu, Will Lee III, Nic Scourton, Chris Brazzell, Jaycee Horn, Mike Jackson, Jonathon Brooks, and Jaelan Phillips were out on the field.
The Panthers have to do something if they really want to try to contend this year, and their offseason spending spree suggests that they do. And if that's the case, FOX Sports' Greg Auman has a clear target in mind.
The last two weeks (or five days) have been absolutely brutal to the Panthers. Not only did more injuries pop up, but every facet of this team came crashing back down to earth as the Panthers slipped from 3-2 to 3-4. It has been ugly.
Bad performance has played a part, but a complete lack of healthy players has, too. And that is nowhere felt more than at cornerback. It's been weeks since Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson went on IR, and Dan Morgan has sat idly by. The injuries at corner haven't gotten better.
Akayleb Evans, who was outmatched as a starting corner, is on IR now. Will Lee III went down on Thursday, and it doesn't look good. They're trotting practice squad players out and running out of options at the same time.
A trade just has to happen, and according to Greg Auman of FOX Sports, it needs to be Philadelphia Eagles cornerback Riq Woolen.
"There’s so much of a Seattle presence in Carolina between head coach Dave Canales and general manager Dan Morgan, both longtime Seahawks guys and where Tariq Woolen began his career," he wrote, highlighting the obvious connection.
"Backups aren’t likely going to get them a repeat division title, so upgrading the secondary would be a priority if they were to be active at the trade deadline," Auman concluded.
The Panthers can't survive with the corner situation as it is. They also can't survive the offensive line situation, but Woolen is available, and starting-caliber offensive linemen just aren't. Cornerbacks are also cheaper.
The Panthers may or may not make a move, but this is one that has to be on the radar. We simply cannot go on like this unless Carolina is content struggling all year.

title: Ejiro Evero's Firing Just Put More Pressure on Dave Canales
full_text:
I wasn't surprised when the Panthers fired Ejiro Evero on Friday. I probably would've been more surprised if they kept him after what we've watched the last couple of weeks. My first thought when I saw it wasn't really about Evero though. It was about Dave Canales.
Evero is gone now. Jonathan Cooley is gone too. Todd Wash gets the defense, and we'll find out soon enough if any of that makes a difference. I went back and forth on Evero for a while this season, but after the last two games I understood why Carolina finally did it.
The Tampa Bay game was probably where I had enough. I watched the Buccaneers come into Charlotte and score 43 points, then Green Bay put up another 30 four days later. It's hard to defend a defensive coordinator after giving up 73 points in five days.
Here's the thing I kept thinking about after Evero was fired. Carolina scored 13 against Tampa Bay and 19 against Green Bay. I actually went back and added it up because it didn't seem like they had scored that much. Thirty-two points in two games isn't exactly helping anybody.
I've had questions about the offense for a while anyway. Some weeks I like what Carolina is doing and then the next week I'm wondering where it went. I've wondered why Chuba Hubbard wasn't getting the ball more, and there have been play calls where I've just sat there trying to figure out what Canales saw that I didn't.
That's the stuff I'm watching now. Evero can't take the blame for any of it.
I had forgotten Evero was already in Carolina when Canales got the job until I started thinking about all of this. Canales kept him, which made sense to me at the time. Evero was getting head-coaching interviews and there were years when I wondered why somebody hadn't hired him yet.
Funny how quickly that changed.
Now Wash gets his shot. I don't know if he's going to make the defense any better, and I'm definitely not expecting everything to suddenly look different because one coach is gone. I mostly want to see if there are things I notice right away.
I'm going to be doing the same thing with the offense. Canales came to Carolina with an offensive background, and that's the side of the ball where I expected him to make the biggest difference. Lately I haven't seen enough of it.
I'm not there. I don't think that's where this conversation needs to go seven games into the season.
But I do think Friday changed things for him. One of his coordinators is already gone, Carolina has lost two straight and the Panthers are sitting at 3-4. Canales has a few extra days now to look at all of it.
I'm curious what he changes.

title: Rookie Defender Has Been Bright Spot in Panthers' Latest Rollercoaster Season
full_text:
On Thursday night at Lambeau Field, the Carolina Panthers fell below the .500 mark with a 27-19 loss to the Green Bay Packers. Dave Canales’s club couldn’t slow down Matt LaFleur’s one-dimensional offense. While the worst ground game in the league was held under 100 yards for the eighth time in as many games, the Panthers had no answers for Packers’ quarterback Jordan Love.
Green Bay’s signal-caller hit on 30-of 41 throws for 288 yards and three touchdowns, with one interception. Carolina’s pass rush finished with zero sacks and zero quarterback hits, and defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero was fired by the team on Friday.
Intercepted by Zakee Wheatley ‼️ CARvsGB on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/vOUDlt94xC
As for that one interception, it was the first of his NFL career for Panthers’ rookie safety Zakee Wheatley. Per Pro Football Focus, only Green Bay’s Evan Williams (90.6) has a higher grade at the position than Carolina’s second pick (89.8) in the fifth round of the 2026 NFL draft. The former Nittany Lion has excelled in pass coverage and is PFF’s No. 3 safety in this facet with an 83.4 grade, behind only Williams (90.1) and Seattle’s Julian Love (85.4).
Although Wheatley was inactive for the season-opener against the Bears, he has played in each of the past six games and made four starts. He ranks sixth on the club with 25 defensive stops (18 solo), one forced fumble, Thursday night’s interception of Jordan Love, and four passes defensed. He also recorded a solo tackle on special teams.
In the loss to the Packers, the five starting members of Carolina’s secondary were cornerbacks Marco Wilson (his first game with the team) and rookie Will Lee III, as well as safeties Wheatley, Nick Scott, and Tre’von Moehrig.
Wilson led the club with eight tackles, while Wheatley and linebacker Devin Lloyd were tied for second with seven stops. It marked the fifth time in six games that the 24-year-old rookie totaled at least four defensive stops in a contest.
There are certain aspects of Carolina’s defense that have improved from a year ago. Of course, the back end of this unit has certainly been hamstrung by the absences of veteran cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson. And with pass-rusher Jaelan Phillips out the last two games, the Panthers failed to come up with a sack in each of those contests.
Still, Wheatley has stood out this season and looks like a Day 3 steal, which may not be a total surprise considering some post-draft evaluations of Dan Morgan’s 2026 draft class.
