title: Ikem Ekwonu's Value Keeps Rising While Panthers Wait for Return
full_text:
Ikem Ekwonu hasn't played a snap for the Panthers this season, and I think I've appreciated him a little more every week he's been out. I definitely did after watching Carolina's offensive line against Tampa Bay and Green Bay.
Ekwonu is still working his way back from the torn patellar tendon he suffered against the Los Angeles Rams in January. Carolina signed Rasheed Walker after four seasons in Green Bay and put him at left tackle while Ekwonu recovered. So far, that hasn't gone very well.
Tampa Bay was probably the worst of it. Walker gave up three sacks and seven pressures, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. Young didn't have much time to get comfortable that afternoon, and the Panthers ended up losing 43-13.
Four days later, Young was running around again. Green Bay pressured him on 48.9% of his dropbacks and sacked him six times. Walker was out there for all 73 offensive snaps against his old team.
Through seven games, Walker has allowed 30 pressures and four sacks, according to Core Football Labs. He's also been called for six penalties. I've seen enough to know Carolina needs better play at left tackle.
I'm not putting all of the problems up front on Walker. Taylor Moton is out for the season, Damien Lewis didn't play Thursday and Corey Bullock hurt his quad during the game. This line looks a lot different from the one Carolina expected to have, but Walker hasn't helped much either.
Dave Canales gave an update this week and said Ekwonu is “trending in the right direction.” He's doing more individual work now, which is good to hear considering the injury he's coming back from.
Canales isn't ready to have somebody go at him full speed yet, and I'm fine with that. A torn patellar tendon isn't something I'd mess around with just because the offensive line has struggled for a couple of weeks. The Panthers have already gone this long without Ekwonu.
Carolina also has some extra time before Denver comes to Charlotte on Nov. 8. Maybe Ekwonu is ready by then and maybe he isn't. I sure wouldn't mind seeing No. 79 again soon, but there's no reason to put him out there before he's ready.
Ekwonu has frustrated me plenty since Carolina took him sixth overall in 2022. His pass protection hasn't always been where it needs to be, and I've wondered at times whether the Panthers had their long-term answer at left tackle. I haven't wondered nearly as much lately.
Young has been under pressure on half of his dropbacks over the last two games. That number was 39.4% before this stretch, and his yards per attempt under pressure has fallen from 6.2 to 3.2. Watching Young deal with that much pressure has made Ekwonu's absence pretty noticeable.
Putting Ekwonu back at left tackle isn't going to fix the entire offensive line. Moton isn't walking back through the door this season, and we don't know what the group will look like by the time Denver gets here. I just know I'd rather have Ekwonu protecting Young's blind side right now.
Seven games without him have changed my mind quite a bit.

title: Overreaction? The Panthers' Season May Already Be Over
full_text:
Five days ago, the Panthers were 3-2 and had Tampa Bay coming to Charlotte. The Buccaneers had won one game, and I thought Carolina had a pretty good chance to get to 4-2 before heading to Green Bay four days later.
Well, that went about as bad as it could've gone. Tampa Bay beat Carolina 43-13, and the Panthers followed that with a 27-19 loss at Green Bay. They're 3-4 now, and I'll admit I'm looking at the rest of this season a lot differently than I was a week ago.
The Green Bay loss isn't the one that gets me. Carolina was on the road four days after getting beat up by Tampa Bay, and the Packers are a good football team. The Panthers actually did some things I liked in that game.
They held Josh Jacobs to 39 yards on 21 carries. That was nice to see after Tampa Bay ran for 258 yards Sunday. Chuba Hubbard had another good night with 119 yards from scrimmage, and Carolina took the ball away three times.
Getting three points off those turnovers is what hurts. Carolina had the ball three extra times and couldn't turn any of them into a touchdown. Young also took six sacks, and Green Bay eventually put the game away.
Tampa Bay is harder for me to explain. The Panthers were at home against a 1-5 team and got beat by 30. If Carolina ends up a game short of winning the division or getting into the playoffs, I have a feeling we're going to remember that one.
I've watched Young throw for 329 yards against Detroit this season. He had 287 against Atlanta, and a few weeks later he threw for 281 against Philadelphia. We haven't seen much of that lately.
Thursday was rough. Young threw for 209 yards and took plenty of hits while trying to get the ball out. Six of those plays ended with him on the ground.
Carolina doesn't have its normal offensive line out there right now. Taylor Moton is on injured reserve. Damien Lewis wasn't available against Green Bay, and then Corey Bullock hurt his quad during the game.
I had the offensive line on my list after Thursday's loss . The Panthers have more than a week before Denver, so we'll see who they can get back by then.
Hubbard hasn't been the problem. He ran for 81 yards and a touchdown Thursday and added 38 more through the air. I'd keep throwing it to him too, especially if Young is going to have defenders in his face that often.
Denver is up first on Nov. 8. Carolina gets New Orleans after that before Baltimore comes to Charlotte. The Panthers will see Tampa Bay again at the end of November.
December isn't exactly empty either. Minnesota and Pittsburgh are both on there, and Seattle comes to Charlotte a few days before Christmas.
Maybe I'm putting too much into two bad games. Carolina has played well this season, and I've seen enough from this team to know Thursday night isn't necessarily what we're going to get every week.
But 3-4 doesn't leave much room to keep finding out.
The Panthers still have their division games, which is probably the best thing they have going for them right now. They'll get another shot at Tampa Bay, and they haven't played New Orleans yet. Atlanta comes at the end of the season.
I'm looking at Denver first. Get that one and you're 4-4 with New Orleans coming up. Lose it and you're sitting at 3-5.
I'm not ready to call the season over.

title: Will Jeffery Simmons Play Tonight? Workload Expectations for New Bears DT vs. Seahawks
full_text:
The Chicago Bears made a massive addition — both literally and figuratively — to their defense this past week when they acquired Jeffery Simmons in a trade with the Tennessee Titans.
General manager Ryan Poles showed he's really going for it this season after giving up two first-round picks and a fourth-round selection in exchange for Simmons and a fifth-rounder.
The blockbuster deal marked the first time in the common draft era that a team has traded multiple first-rounders for a defensive tackle, so that goes to show you how serious Poles is about 2026.
But with that trade going down just days ago and Simmons having such a short time to get acclimated and ready to play in a new defense, many are wondering if he will make his debut versus Seattle.
The expectation is that Simmons will indeed suit up for his Bears debut on Monday night against the Seahawks.
First, Poles said he believed that Simmons would go , although he did say the ultimate decision will rest on the coaching staff.
Then, when he first addressed the media on Friday, Big Jeff told reporters that he's ready to go.
"At this point, I'm still trying to catch up with the playbook, get this game plan down and just trust the process, especially with this first week" he said . "But at the same time, I'm ready to roll. I'm ready to help this team win football games."
Head coach Ben Johnson also made it sound like Simmons will play.
“He’s played a lot of football, he’s been in a few different defensive schemes, and I think (Dennis Allen) is going to be able to find a spot to do what he does best,” Johnson said . “We don’t want him thinking out there, and that’s what you’re conscious of coming into a new team, but he’s a smart guy and we’ve been encouraged by what we’ve seen so far.”
As far as how much Simmons will play, we can't say for sure. One would assume he probably won't see a full workload in his first game with the Bears, which is something Johnson said would likely be the case.
“He might not be quite that high Week 1 for us, but he certainly has shown the ability to carry a load,” he said of Simmons' expected workload in his first game with the Bears.
The only real roadblock is how much of the defense Simmons can grasp in such a short time. It's not like he's coming off the couch to play, so conditioning isn't an issue at all.
One of the Bears' starters along the interior of the defensive line, Grady Jarrett, has been playing 72% of snaps this season. We could see Simmons playing around 50% in Week 8.

title: Everything Chicago Bears Have to Fear About Seattle Seahawks in Week 8
full_text:
The Chicago Bears have an opportunity to show just how for real they are in a Week 8 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks .
The Bears have looked like true contenders through seven games of the 2026 campaign, but knocking off the reigning Super Bowl champs would go a long way toward furthering the notion the Bears can compete for big things this season.
The Seahawks have seen their fair share of struggles, but they are also coming off a game in which they completely dismantled the previously unbeaten Kansas City Chiefs and showed they might be rounding into form.
It goes without saying this is not going to be an easy matchup for the Bears, and the following three concerns Chicago should have ahead of the contest with Seattle show why.
It might be tough sledding for the Bears' offense this week as it faces off with an elite Seahawks defense that is loaded with a bunch of talent at every level of the unit.
There really is nothing this Seahawks' defense doesn't do well. The unit ranks first in total yards allowed per game, first in passing yards and sixth in rushing yards.
While Seattle's 17 sacks ranks in the middle of the pack in the NFL, the reigning Super Bowl champs are also ranked third in pressures with 77.
Seattle also turns the ball over at an impressive rate, with 12 in seven games, ranking fifth in the league.
As if all of that wasn't enough, Ben Johnson will meet his match in Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald, who has proven to be one of the best defensive minds in the NFL.
Now you know why this is a measuring stick game for Caleb Williams and the Bears' offense.
Smith-Njigba is having another phenomenal season for Seattle in 2026, with the superstar wideout ranking first in receiving yards and touchdowns through seven games.
He's a problem in and of himself, no matter who is guarding him, but there is even more concern for Chicago because of the lackluster cornerback play on the boundary this season.
Jaylon Johnson has been a shell of the guy who used to be considered an elite cornerback and Tyrique Stevenson isn't stopping anyone, either.
Chicago's best corner, rookie Malik Muhammad, may not even play, as the fourth-round pick is questionable because of a toe injury.
All of this sets the stage for a huge night for Smith-Njigba, which is obviously going to make securing a win over Seattle more difficult for the Bears.
The Seahawks are widely known to have one of the best home-field advantages in the NFL and that has remained the case the last season-plus.
Since 2025, Seattle has gone 9-3 at Lumen Field with the help of their "12th man," including 3-1 this season.
As if squaring off against an elite defense wasn't difficult enough, the Bears are also going to have to battle crowd noise in what will be their most difficult challenge of the 2026 campaign.

title: Bears Target Khalil Mack Discusses Trade Rumors Ahead of NFL Deadline
full_text:
The Chicago Bears are in the market for an edge rusher and their old friend, Khalil Mack, has constantly been tied to them over the past few weeks.
Mack's name has regularly come up in trade rumors across the NFL and the Bears' fan base isn't the only one that wants to see their team acquire the future Hall of Famer.
As the Chargers lost yet another game on Sunday to push them to 0-7 and a step closer to selling at the trade deadline, Mack was asked about all the noise surrounding him and the team.
"You’ve got to be where your feet are man, ultimately. That can be the most difficult thing when you’re dealing with a lot of outside noise and stuff. Just trying to be where your feet are at all time. That’s kind of been my thing in years past," Mack said, per Eric Williams of FOX Sports .
We didn't sense any "I don't want to be traded" vibes in the comment
FOX's Jay Glazer really kicked off the Mack to Bears trade rumors a few weeks ago when he revealed that the Bears had already called the Chargers about the veteran EDGE .
"I know they've already talked to, you know, the Chargers, saying, 'Hey, what about a guy like Khalil Mack?' I think they're going to be very aggressive. Ryan Poles, that's what he does. More aggressive than the other teams in that division," Glazer said.
More recently, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported that Chicago is still calling around for an edge rusher and he said he wouldn't be surprised if Mack ended up with the Bears.
"Meanwhile, the Bears may not actually be done," Rapoport said on Sunday morning. "I'm told they are still calling around, still looking on the edges of their defense."
"Wouldn't be surprised if a Khalil Mack trade was in the offer here. A possible reunion for Mack and the Bears," he added.
The Athletic's Jonathan Jones reported on Saturday that Los Angeles has been the roadblock to a Mack trade because the team insists it won't sell off pieces at the trade deadline.
But we're simply not buying it. The Chargers' season was over at 0-6, and it's now even more over at 0-7.
We don't expect a fire sale, but we do expect the Chargers to unload players who are on the final year of their deals, and Mr. Mack is in that group.
There is no reason for the Chargers to hold on to him and they should do the merciful thing and trade Mack to give him an opportunity to compete for a Super Bowl.
The Bears give him that, as well as a familiar landing spot that Mack has made clear he loved.

title: Jeffery Simmons Headlines Bears' Week 8 Keys to Victory vs Seahawks
full_text:
A monumental Week 8 showdown awaits the Chicago Bears on Monday Night Football. They're set to face the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field in what could be an NFC Championship preview. But that's for January. For now, the Bears need a win to stay in the thick of the playoff race.
If the Bears win, they remain in second place in the NFC North and just half a game back from the Minnesota Vikings, who saw their perfect season end in a loss to the Detroit Lions on Sunday. A loss, however, would drop the Bears to last place in the division and No. 8 overall in the NFC. Obviously there would remain plenty of time to get back in the playoff picture before January, but stealing this win on the road would give the Bears a cushion to fall back on.
But how can the Bears beat the Seahawks? It's easier said than done, but if they can hit on these three keys, they should emerge victorious.
When the Bears pulled off a blockbuster trade for superstar defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons , they did so with the expectation that he could turn them into a legit Super Bowl contender, and he needs to provide proof of concept right from the jump. The Seahawks are a great team, but Simmons is arguably the best defensive tackle in all of football right now.
If the Bears get a signature performance from their newest acquisition, then the Seahawks are going to find it extraordinarily difficult to move the ball through the air or on the ground, even with Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet finally being cleared to play.
The Seahawks are 4-0 when they turn the ball over two or fewer times. They're 0-3 if they turn the ball over at least three times. It doesn't get more simple than this. Dennis Allen's defense needs a throwback performance to the 2025 version of themselves and get takeaways in bunches.
Luckily for the Bears, their recent reinforcements on defense give them the horses to make that happen. Aside from the aforementioned acquisition of Simmons, they're also getting linebacker T.J. Edwards back from injury, and he's proven to have a nose for the football. Kyler Gordon has forced two fumbles since returning from injury, and it feels like he's due for an interception.
With Kyle Monangai ruled out for Week 8, I expect the Bears to lean on their passing game. And for the first time in decades, that won't be a problem. Caleb Williams has been playing at an MVP level since he returned from his hamstring injury , putting up back-to-back games with over 300 passing yards. To beat the Seahawks, however, he's going to have to make it three in a row.
Seattle boasts a ferocious defensive front, and without the hard-charging, heavy-hitting Monangai, I can't see Chicago's ground game making much headway. They're going to need Williams to deliver another statement performance. That means taking what the defense gives him on 90% of dropbacks, punctuated by several explosive passing plays.
I see a low-scoring game for these two squads, an old-fashioned, bare-knuckle fistfight of a football game. Both teams will struggle to move the ball consistently until the fourth quarter, at which point Caleb Williams will lead the Bears on a touchdown drive that gives them a one-point lead with just a few minutes left in the game.
That's when things fall apart for the Bears. The reigning champions will lock in and march down the field in a punishing drive that keeps the clock running despite the Bears using all three timeouts in the final minute. Sam Darnold then takes a knee at the 15-yard line, setting up a short field goal attempt, and Jason Myers boots it through the uprights as time expires.
Unfortunately for the Bears, they're no longer at a place where they can boast about moral victories. A loss to the Seahawks does them no good, and they'll be desperate to avoid the trap game waiting for them in Week 9 against the feisty Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

title: Bears Rumored to Be Top QB Trade Target for Ravens, But Would Chicago Make the Deal?
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens are in dire straits at the quarterback position and they might be eyeing the Chicago Bears for help.
The Ravens lost not one but two quarterbacks in Week 8, with Lamar Jackson and backup Tyler Huntley sustaining injuries during the loss to the Buffalo Bills on Sunday.
Making matters worse for the Ravens, Jackson, who suffered a thumb injury, needs surgery and is slated to go on injured reserve , head coach Jesse Minter said. There is also a chance that Jackson could miss the remainder of the season.
Meanwhile, Huntley reportedly may have turf toe , which Bears fans know can be a multi-week injury after running back Kyle Monangai has missed four games with the same issue .
Now, the Ravens are faced with starting rookie Joe Fagnano and that will almost certainly spell the end of their season, hence the Ravens' need for a trade.
According to On SI's Jason La Canfora , the Ravens have called the Bears already to inquire about quarterback Tyson Bagent, who La Canfora says is Baltimore's top target.
"The Ravens top pursuit is Bears back-up quarterback Tyson Bagent, according to multiple high-ranking NFL personnel execs," La Canfora said before adding that the Ravens "have reached out to Chicago" in the wake of losing Jackson and Huntley.
“Chicago doesn’t have to trade him,” an NFL GM said of Bagent to La Canfora. “They like him … Wonder how hard they squeeze DeCosta?”
The fact that the Ravens appear to have already reached out to the Bears just goes to show how desperate Baltimore is, but they have to be because time is of the essence. Baltimore will play its next game on Thursday against the Jacksonville Jaguars.
As we saw with the Jeffery Simmons trade , just about anyone in the NFL can be had for the right price.
Bagent certainly isn't a blue-chip player like Simmons is, but the Bears do have a high opinion of Bagent and may not be keen on trading him for anything less than an overpay.
It's hard to imagine the Ravens coming up with that kind offer. They would have to believe that Bagent can save their season and there has been no indication he's capable of doing such a thing. In fact, his stock is probably at an all-time low after he stunk it up in place of an injured Caleb Williams in Chicago's Week 5 loss .
Making it even less likely is the fact that Bagent will have to learn a new offense on the fly and that takes time. Bagent did play under Ravens offensive coordinator Declan Doyle for a season, but it was still Ben Johnson's offense.
We aren't scoffing at the rumor that the Ravens put in a call to the Bears to check on Bagent's availability given the dire situation Baltimore finds itself in, but we find it very hard to believe the Ravens are going to come up with the kind of offer to make it worth it for the Bears to subtract from their quarterbacks room.

title: Could Ravens' QB Disaster Open Door For Bears to Trade Tyson Bagent or Case Keenum?
full_text:
A nuclear bomb went off in the Baltimore Ravens quarterback room in their 36-10 blowout loss against the Buffalo Bills on Sunday.
Lamar Jackson suffered a thumb injury in the first quarter. Netflix NFL reporter Tom Pelissero reported that he will land on injured reserve. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter confirmed he might even miss the remainder of the season when speaking to reporters after the contest.
Meanwhile, backup Tyler Huntley also went down with a toe injury (the same ailment that has sidelined Kyle Monangai over the past month) shortly thereafter. NFL insider Adam Schefter reported that he's believed to have suffered a turf toe injury and will undergo further testing tomorrow to determine the severity.
Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano took over as the emergency third QB, and he completed only 10 of 21 attempts for 91 yards and an interception. The Ravens are still 4-4 and don't want to throw in the towel on the season, but they're about to be desperate for stable play at quarterback.
The Ravens poached former Bears offensive coordinator Declan Doyle to fill the same role (with added play-calling duties) for Baltimore. That might create a logical connection if they can find common ground for one of Chicago's two (occasionally) promising backup QBs.
Doyle might've only been with the Bears for one season, but Tyson Bagent still made a positive impression on him during his time in the Windy City.
“Tyson is very businesslike,” Doyle said ahead of training camp last season. “Football is really important to him. He’s excellent in the position room. And out on the field he’s constantly communicating what he sees and where he needs to go with the football when he comes back, and what the problems might be. He sees the game pretty clearly and that’s because he takes it really seriously and he studies.”
Now, I know Bagent might've tarnished his trade value in the team's Week 5 blowout loss against the Packers, but he was previously considered one of the league's best backups . That's why they handed him a two-year, $10 million contract ahead of the 2025 campaign. Everyone inside Halas Hall has also consistently spoken highly of him, including Doyle.
Sure, the Green Bay game was a bad look for Bagent, but the bar is the floor for Baltimore right now. Fagnono doesn't instill confidence, and Doyle's offense features similar wrinkles to Ben Johnson's in Chicago.
If they need someone to come in and grasp the scheme relatively quickly (they host the Jaguars on Thursday night), Bagent might be their best bet. Even if Thursday night is too ambitious (which it very well might be), he'd be able to play after the Ravens mini-bye if Doyle gives the stamp of approval.
Alternatively, they could try to poach Case Keenum if they prefer a higher-floor option. Unlike Bagent, his most recent showing (completing 24 of 34 attempts for 247 yards and 2 passing TDs in their Week 3 blowout win over Philadelphia) was the best game we've seen from a backup QB in recent memory , and he was the third-string.
Chicago would prefer to keep Keenum around thanks to his leadership and experience, but they'd at least listen to Baltimore's offer if it helped them recoup some of the draft capital they lost in the Jeffery Simmons trade.
With the Ravens still in the thick of the AFC playoff picture, they'll be desperate to make a move. Desperate teams often create one-sided trades, and a third- or fourth-round pick wouldn't be out of the realm of expectations if Doyle's praise for Bagent wasn't hyperbolic.

title: Seahawks' Quenton Nelson Trade Gives Bears Unexpected Advantage in Week 8
full_text:
Three NFC contenders made big acquisitions via trade last week, and two of them are set to face off in Week 8 on Monday Night Football. The Chicago Bears pulled off a blockbuster trade for superstar defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons while the Seattle Seahawks acquired six-time All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson in a trade with the Indianapolis Colts .
Nelson is arguably the best guard in the league and will have a solid case for a spot in the Pro Football Hall of Fame one day. However, by adding Nelson to their offensive line, the Seahawks have inadvertently created a massive liability in their offensive line, and that's something that the Bears can exploit with ruthless efficiency thanks to their acquisition of Simmons.
After making the trade for Nelson, the Seahawks announced that he would slot in at left guard on their offensive line, which has been his position for his entire NFL career. However, the Seahawks already had a committed left guard in second-year player Gray Zabel. Zabel will now move to right guard, a position he hasn't played since college, and even then, that was not his full-time position.
Zabel has said that this move to right guard will be "such a growing experience" for him as a player, and maybe it will pay off in his future. However, learning an entirely new way of blocking in just a handful of practice sessions is a tall order, and his first test will come against the newest member of the Bears' defense, three-time All-Pro Jeffery Simmons.
While it might make sense to some fans to put Simmons against Nelson during this game in a match of strength against strength, the Bears would be wide to heed the words of Sun Tzu. The famous Chinese general and philosopher in fact urged the opposite of this strategy, advising instead to concentrate one's strength against enemy weak points.
In this case, the Seahawks' biggest weakness on the offensive line is likely to be the second-year player starting at a brand new position. By lining Simmons up across from Zabel consistently, the Bears should be able to get constant, immediate pressure on quarterback Sam Darnold, and also stop the run game from getting any traction.
Jeffery Simmons should make an immediate impact against the Seattle Seahawks despite only having a few days with the Bears' defensive playbook. Like Nelson, he's the kind of player who's good enough to excel wherever he goes. However, if the Bears want to maximize his impact and knock off the defending Super Bowl champs, they'll send Simmons at Zabel as many times as possible.
Nelson is going to do what he does best, and that's stonewall just about anyone who comes his way. Let him do that to Grady Jarrett or Kentavius Street. They're not likely to cause the Seahawks much trouble, anyway.

title: What Jeffery Simmons Trade Can Mean for the Future of Bears Roster
full_text:
The future of the Bears in terms of the salary cap after their trade for Jeffery Simmons is more of alteration than overhaul. Adding a $105 million deal to the payroll can things, but it's all relative in a league that keeps making gobs of money.
Some could look at their cap situation for coming years and wonder what they're doing when they have to pay Caleb Williams an extension, but his deal is always under consideration and their contract negotiator, Matt Feinstein has weighed this out in planning.
“All of those things we started a while ago, just researching what does that look like and how does it impact this?" GM Ryan Poles said. "Because you do have to work both directions.
"We’ve got a ways to go and get through the season before we get to that, but we're always forecasting how do these different things and events and contracts fit together. I have an unbelievable analytics program. I have an unbelievable guy in Matt Feinstein, who does really good work helping us understand the impact that all of those things have on us.”
The reason it means alterations is it is going to mean some players who may have been back, won't be in the future. Then again, some of these players may not have figured into their future. It's all open to speculation now, but based on their performances it is easy to see what could happen.
Feinstein and Poles are not the only ones who can forecast.
Mahomes cap hits the next 3 years: 2027: $90M 2028: $86M 2029: $83M Remember this when everyone is throwing around these pipe dreams of signing big name players.
The Bears could actually add someone still this year but it would need to be at a low rate. They have $1.8 million left in cap space, according to Overthecap.com. Adding anyone else of significance now would mean more contract restructuring for some players.
As for the future, the Bears now are over the 2027 salary cap by $23.6 million, but it's $32.8 million in terms of effective cap space. This is a more relevant figure becuae it includes what they would have after signing at least 51 players and a projected rookie class. There are only four teams in bigger salary cap holes for 2027 than the Bears.

Cutting Montez Sweat, Jaylon Johnson, Cole Kmet, Grady Jarrett, T.J. Edwards, Dayo Odeyingbo, and Tyson Bagent would get them well below, largely because Sweat gives them $21 million in cap savings and would now only stick them with $4.8 million in dead cap space. Plenty of cash exists but it will create a drastically altered roster. Then again, some would look at the production some of these players have had and would expect some sort of roster move.
The important year is 2028 because this is the cap more affected by Caleb Williams' deal. They've been planning for this as they have the third-most cap space in the league available even after Simmons' contract is weighed into all of it.

In 2028, they only have 12 starters under contract, assuming Willams' fifth-year option is picked up. Kyler Gordon, Darnell Wright, Simmons, Colston Loveland, Coby Bryant, D'Andre Swift, Devin Bush, Dillon Thieneman, Luther Burden III, Ozzy Trapilo, Trapilo and possible future starting center Logan Jones would be those players besides Williams.
None of those players whose departure would provide relief next year are among players who would be back in 2028, unless they got extensions.
NFL revenue keeps climbing — $301.2M cap is up ~7.9% from last year. Players cashing in big time.📊
Adding a top defensive lineman did not really change much in that respect. What has to be done in the future is filling the spots that will be vacated when these players are no longer part of the picture.
They'll have plenty of cash to find many of those, but the draft will need to produce plenty. At least, the draft picks they'll have available after trading away two first-rounders and fourth-rounder will need to be good enough to fill those vacated spots.
Williams is going to command a ridiculous contract, but the key here is that salary cap is only going to keep increasing. That's all it ever does, except during the pandemic.

title: NFC North Standings: Where Bears Sit After Packers, Lions & Vikings Games in Week 8
full_text:
The Chicago Bears are right in the thick of things in the NFC North going into their Week 8 contest against the Seattle Sehawks on Monday night.
After beating the New England Patriots last week and seeing the Green Bay Packers lose to the Detroit Lions, the Bears improved their positioning to second place in the division.
However, they did not gain any ground on the Minnesota Vikings, who managed to defeat the Indianapolis Colts to stay unbeaten, and they remained the only unbeaten team in the NFL going into this week.
Now that the Vikings have played their Week 8 contest against the Lions and the Packers took part in their game against the Carolina Panthers on Thursday night, here's how the NFC North shakes out going into Chicago's Monday night game against the Seahawks.
1. Vikings (6-1) 2. Detroit Lions (5-2) 3. Chicago Bears (5-2) 4. Green Bay Packers (5-3)
The NFC North remains one of two divisions in the league to see every team sporting a .500 or better record. Safe to say, this is once again one of the best divisions in football.
The Packers notched their fifth victory of the season on Thursday over the Panthers in a bounce-back showing after last week's loss to the Lions.
The Vikings are undefeated no longer after they dropped their contest to the Lions on Sunday. And, with that, there are no undefeated teams left in the NFL.
Despite the loss, the Vikings hold on to first place for at least another week, although both the Packers and Lions did gain ground, and the Bears will, also, if they beat Seattle.
Detroit moves up to second place past Chicago for now because of their better divisional record. If the Bears win, they move back into second place because of a superior win percentage.
If the Bears lose, they will fall into last place in the division. In that scenario, the Packers jump ahead of them because of the head-to-head advantage following Green Bay's Week 5 win over Chicago.
In order for the Bears to get into first place, they have to beat both the Seahawks and Tampa Bay Buccaneers in their next two games and the Vikings have to lose next week to the Buffalo Bills.
Because the Vikings beat the Bears in Week 2, Minnesota owns the head-to-head tie-breaker for now, hence Chicago's need to sport a better win percentage in order to leapfrog Minnesota.
Next week, the Bears host the Bucs and the Vikings host the Bills. Meanwhile, the Packers draw a road matchup against the Patriots and the Lions square off against the Miami Dolphins in South Beach.

title: Bengals' Offensive Shootout Victory Over Titans Made Franchise History
full_text:
Not many people predicted the Cincinnati Bengals to get in an offensive slugfest with the Tennessee Titans on Sunday. If anything, the majority of folks following both teams probably felt the Bengals should handle the 1-6 Titans fairly easily.
Instead of the Bengals having a smooth outing before their trip to Spain, the team had to go to overtime to take down the Titans 43-36. There were struggles on both sides of the ball, which included Joe Burrow throwing three interceptions.
Still, allowing 36 points is normally the recipe for a loss. Taking a closer look at the Bengals' history, it's really a miracle they won on Sunday.
John Sheeran of AtoZ Sports shared a stat that almost sounds made up. The Bengals' win on Sunday was the first time in franchise history that the team has won a game while allowing 36 points and turning the ball over at least four times.
Coming into Sunday, the Bengals were 0-20 in such cases.
What can be said about Burrow's performance? The three interceptions were obviously brutal, yet the Bengals quarterback accounted for six touchdowns on the day, which included five through the air and one rushing touchdown.
Burrow finished the game with a passer rating of 115.5, and the Bengals quarterback is not taking this win for granted in his postgame press conference.
"We lose that game the last three years," Burrow said . "Like I said, it's hard to win. Obviously you want to be great, snap in and snap out. It's not the reality of it. All we can do is keep working hard and try to get better."
No one should ever feel sorry for winning a game in the NFL. Sunday's game against the Titans proved that winning is hard in this league. One could look around the rest of the league and see that from the results on Sunday.
This is a game that can be put in the rearview quickly and move the focus to the next week. Next week will be a tricky matchup with the Atlanta Falcons, given the nature of the crazy travel. A fast turnaround may be what this team needs to keep their momentum.

title: Joe Burrow WOWS With Elite Titans Pro Football Focus Grade Despite Turnovers
full_text:
The Bengals didn't play a clean game by any means in Sunday's 43-36 win over the Tennessee Titans, but they still tallied some stellar Pro Football Focus grades from the outing.
The team posted a season-high 87.6 grade overall and had two players grade out at 93 or higher, starting with Joe Burrow on offense (93.1 overall).
The league's highest-graded passer this season continued playing elite football with 450-plus total yards, six touchdowns and three interceptions on Sunday. He committed three turnover-worthy plays on Sunday after entering the game with four total, but he was so clutch and sound on the other 71 snaps to wash it all away.
According to ESPN, Burrow is the second QB in NFL history with 450 passing yards, five pass TDs, and one rushing TD in a single game, and first in 75 years. The other was Norm Van Brocklin in 1951, who set the NFL record with 554 passing yards in that game.
Following Burrow, Tee Higgins (90.8) continued his career-best season with another 90-plus outing after leading all Bengals with a 91.6 mark last week. The rest of the top-five on offense went in this order: Dalton Risner (80), Ja'Marr Chase (78), and Amarius Mims (75.3).
The bottom-five offensive grades went in this order (min. 15 snaps): Drew Sample (49.6), Chase Brown (57.1), Colbie Young (61.1), Mike Gesicki (64.9), and Samaje Perine (68.9). It was a very strong day for the offense with low-end grades this high.
On defense, Cincinnati is really hoping to not have DJ Turner II (93.3) on the mend for long. The fourth-year corner is playing the best football of his career and peaking at the right time for a major payday in one way or another this offseason.
He got ruled out with a lower-body injury after posting the best grade of the game across 58 snaps. Turner has a career-best 74.3 PFF grade this season. Four other Bengals graded 67 or better on Cincinnati's defense: B.J. Hill (91.8), Jordan Battle (76), Dexter Lawrence (70.6), and Myles Murphy (67.9).
The bottom-five on defense went in this order (min. 15 snaps): Josh Newton (39.6), Bryan Cook (40.6), Dax Hill (44.9), Demetrius Knight Jr. (47.7), Barrett Carter (54.4). The middle of the Bengals defense struggled in a big way at the second and third levels.
They have to get that cleaned up before facing the Falcons in Spain on Sunday morning.

title: 7 Winners and 3 Losers From Bengals' Wild OT Win Over Titans
full_text:
In nail-biting fashion, the Bengals emerged victorious in Paycor Stadium on Sunday 43-36 over Tennessee.
Here are seven winners and three losers from Sunday's win.
Higgins just continues to add to his career-best campaign. He consistently beat his coverage and created easy options for Joe Burrow in the middle of the field and on the boundary. His best grab happened on the offense's first play following a Boye Mafe strip-sack turnover where he and Burrow connected for a 17-yard touchdown. Burrow then found Higgins later for the game-tying touchdown at the end of the fourth quarter.
Higgins has continuosly exceeded expectations this season, and is comfortably on pace for his first 1,500 yard receiving season. He finished Sunday with 10 catches for 155 yards and two touchdowns.
Both Demetrius Knight Jr. and Barrett Carter continue to miss tackles, and this time it played a large part in Tony Pollard gashing the defense for a 41-yard score. They were not alone however as Jordan Battle, Bryan Cook, and D.J. Turner failed to bring Pollard down as well.
To make matters worse, there is absolutely no awareness when it comes to covering tight ends. The Titans have failed to generate production from their tight ends all season, yet on Sunday both Gunnar Helm and Daniel Bellinger combined for eight catches, 112 yards and a touchdown. The lack of performing a basic task on defense is inexcusable at this point.
That is another reason you trade for Dexter Lawrence. Lawrence showed up on the stat sheet with seven total tackles, a sack, and a fumble recovery that he almost scored on. He saved his best play for the most dire moment however.
Cam Ward and the Titans needed to gain only 12 yards to setup a possible game-winning field goal with 32 seconds left. Lawrence then took matters into his own hands, and on 3rd and 3 chased down Ward for a crucial 13-yard sack to force overtime. He is the star that this Bengals defense has missed on the interior of the D-line.
Holding penalties are now officially a problem for Fairchild at this point. He committed a terrible holding penalty on a play where Burrow found Chase Brown in the end zone. He also jumped early for a false start penalty at the end of the third quarter.
Fairchild has maintained a solid level of play at left guard all season, but he has to clean up the penalties.
Mafe showed more dominance on Sunday and added another sack to his total with 5.5 sacks now on the year. It did not stop at the sack however as Mafe knocked the ball out of Cam Ward's hands as well for a fumble that Dexter Lawrence recovered. He has proven himself as one of the best playmakers on the team.
On a day where the defense seeming did all that it could to keep the Titans in the game, one drive stood out more than the rest. The defense committed three different penalties while up 21-13 in the third quarter to extend the Titans drive where they ultimately tied the game.
Josh Newton committed the first of two pass-interference penalties against Gunnar Helm for a thirteen yard penalty.
After a Cashius Howell offsides call, Bryan Cook got to Helm too early at the goal line for a four-yard penalty that placed the ball at the one-yard line. Tony Pollard scored his second touchdown of the day on the next play. These undisciplined mistakes have plagued the defense all year, and cannot continue if they hope to make a deep playoff run.
Chase finished with eleven catches for 141 yards, but his best grab happened on a third down where he and Burrow connected deep over the middle for a touchdown.
That play essentially woke the Bengals offense up for the rest of the game, and like Higgins he showed up on outside as a consistent option for Burrow.
The argument is there for Burrow to not make the winners list after he tossed three interceptions to Amani Hooker. However, the way Burrow continued to launch accurate passes afterwards is the main reason the Bengals avoided an upset in their stadium.
Burrow proved all of the doubters wrong when it comes to his ability as a clutch quarterback. After having an even ratio of three touchdowns to three interceptions, he threw two more touchdowns and ran for the game-winning score in overtime. He could have thrown five interceptions, and he would still make the winners list this week as he set a career high in total touchdowns in a game with six.
Burrow finished Sunday with a statline of 38 for 48 passing, for 472 total yards, and six total touchdowns.
Gesicki has finally become involved in the offense outside of the red zone and still kept his touchdown streak intact.
He finished the day with four catches for 76 yards and a 25-yard touchdown.
Burrow found two of his tight ends for touchdowns today, with Jack Endries hauling in one for what also was his first NFL reception. This is the best first impression Endries could have possibly had after the team placed Erick All Jr. on Injured Reserve with another torn ACL.
Endries should continue to see his role within the offense develop.

title: Bengals Narrow Betting Favorites in Spain Battle Against Falcons
full_text:
Cincinnati is headed to Europe as betting favorites over the Atlanta Falcons this week. The team opened as three-point favorites Monday morning on DraftKings Sportsbook with a point total set at 51.5 points overall.
Both teams are struggling to beat the number this season as Cincinnati failed to cover as 13.5-point favorites on Sunday. They sit at 3-4 against the spread in 2026, while Atlanta is 3-5.
The Bengals just beat the Titans 43-36 to get to 5-2 on the 2026 season.
"We found a way to win. We talked all week about playing a complete game. We talked about all those things. That's obviously our intent," Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said on Sunday. "Today didn't go that way for us, but I'm not going to lose sight of the fact that our guys stepped up at the end of the game, kept it together, and believed we were going to find a way to win. I don't care what their (the Titans') record is. They have been in a lot of games this year.
"So, our guys, in all phases, stepped up and found a way to walk off a winner. I get the chance after a win to clean things up. We need to clean up, go on the road to Spain, and find a way to get another one."
Cincinnati has won its past three games against the Falcons, last losing to them in the 2010 season, 39-32.
The Bengals have played two international games in their history, both in London last decade. In their last trip across the pond, Cincinnati took on a 24-10 loss to the Rams at Wembley Stadium during Taylor's first season in 2019.
"It's an unbelievable opportunity to grow the game internationally. That's an important part of what we do," Taylor said this past offseason about the contest. "I think it's awesome the brand of the Bengals gets extended internationally. We've got a lot of great players on the team that the world will get to watch on center stage."
Cincinnati kicks off against Atlanta at 9:30 AM ET on Sunday.

title: Cashius Howell Posts Video of Injured Wrist Following Bengals Win Over Titans
full_text:
The Bengals look like they won't have Cashius Howell for a while.
Cincinnati's 2026 second-round pick suffered a wrist injury in the 43-36 win over Tennessee. He posted a video from the hospital on his Instagram showing a big cast on his arm.
We will learn more from Zac Taylor this week. If he is put on injured reserve, expect the Bengals to add a name to its practice squad before leaving for Spain this week.
"Cashius, we'll see. I think it was his wrist. He (trainer) just told me about DJ Turner, and I forgot. I'll get you an update tomorrow or Wednesday," Taylor said on Sunday.
Howell has six tackles and one sack in seven games played this season.
Cincinnati won a wild game that was much closer than expected.
Joe Burrow had to pull off two clutch touchdown drives in the fourth quarter and overtime.
"We won. I want a complete game, and I want to start the first quarter faster — those are things we are going to continue to talk about," Taylor noted. "But there is something to finding a way to win. You guys have watched us play the last two years, and some of these games have gone the other direction. So for our guys, particularly late in the fourth quarter and overtime, to step up and seal the game, I'm not going to dismiss that. I'm proud of the guys for fighting through the whole time and finding ways for each guy to step up and make some plays so we could walk out a winner — to get to 5-2 and now go on the road, and reset and go do it again."
Taylor was impressed with how Tennessee kept so much pressure on his team.
"Those guys fought. They had a great plan. They attacked us," Taylor noted. "I give Tennessee a lot of credit. We'll watch the tape to see the things we need to clean up. There are certainly a lot of things. How many turnovers did we have? Four? Four turnovers are going to keep a team in the game. There are just things we're going to watch and clean up, but I am proud of the guys for finding a way to win the game."
Cincinnati travels to Spain early this week.

title: Bengals' Lawrence-Mafe Duo Emerging as Defense's Version of Chase-Higgins
full_text:
Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow threw for at least 450 yards and five touchdowns while also rushing for a score, something no NFL quarterback had done in 75 years.
Wide receivers Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins became the second duo in team annals – and sixth in NFL history – to each record at least 140 receiving yards, 10 receptions and a touchdown.
Mike Gesicki became the first tight end in franchise history to catch a TD pass in five consecutive games.
Chase Brown ripped off his first explosive run of the season and topped 100 scrimmage yards for the first time in 2026.
And the Cincinnati offense as a whole put up 510 yards, its most in 67 games.
But maybe the single most important play in Sunday’s 43-36 overtime victory against the Tennessee Titans at Paycor Stadium was a single tackle.
With Tennessee on the edge of game-winning field goal range and just 32 seconds left in regulation, Bengals defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence burst into the backfield, chased down Titans quarterback Cam Ward from behind and slammed him to the turf for a game-saving sack.
Asked to put recency bias aside and rank where that one ranks among his 35.5 career sacks in terms of impact, Lawrence didn’t hesitate.
“That was pretty big,” he said. “As of today, No. 1.”
The sack took the Titans from the Cincinnati 45 to the Tennessee 42, forcing the Titans to punt.
The game-saving element obviously was the most important aspect, but Lawrence relished the way it came about, adding an unofficial assist to teammate Boye Mafe.
“Working with Boye has been good for me,” Lawrence said. “We worked together on that play to get that, and then the moment of the of the sack and how I threw him down, it felt pretty good.
“We saw something on the field that we liked, so we just called it and, and it so happened to work.”
Mafe said he and Lawrence didn’t actually call it; they just gave each other a knowing look.
Which is pretty impressive for a pair of guys who have only played seven games together, with Mafe arriving in free agency in March and Lawrence via trade in April.
Mafe was lined up to Lawrence’s left at the snap, but instead of rushing wide to the right tackle’s outside, Mafe cut inside, resulting in a forced double team that freed Lawrence to pursue Ward as he rolled to his right.
“I looked at Dex, Dex looked at me and we kind of have that situation where we look at each other and we know what we mean,” Mafe said. “We wanted to run something, and I looked at him and he agreed, we confirmed.
“We just said, ‘All right, let's run it.’ And that situation worked out perfectly,” he added. “You couldn't write it better.”
Mafe entered the game as the team leader in sacks with 4.5, a half sack more than Lawrence.
The stunt they pulled meant Mafe would have no chance of getting to Ward in that situation, but Lawrence would have an enhanced one.
“It was one of those situations where if I do my thing and then Dex helps me out, covers my back,” Mafe said. “I think the best thing about it is that we're willing and able to play off of one another. There is no selfishness on this D line right now, and it doesn't matter who gets the sack, who gets the glory. We do not care about that.
“At the end of the day, we are just trying to get the man down.”
It was one of two big plays the two hooked up on in the win.
Early in the third quarter with the Bengals clinging to a 14-13 lead, Mafe sacked Ward at the Tennessee 29 and forced a fumble. Lawrence scooped up the ball and had nothing but space between him and the goal line, but Titans right guard Atonio Mafi got a hand on Lawrence’s ankle and brought him down.
“I did think it was gonna happen,” Lawrence grinned. “I didn’t know somebody was that close. I guess I have to have better awareness. Or ask somebody to pick up a block for me or something.”
Mafe was injured on the play, but the vision of Lawrence rumbling gave him some quick pain relief.
“I kind of poked my head up, looked over,” Mafe said. “Once I saw he had the ball in his hands, I went back down. As long as he had the ball, it didn’t matter to me.”
Like Lawrence, Mafe thought the big man was going to score.
“I did for a second. I’m not gonna lie,” he said. “I saw him pick up his feet. One thing y’all don’t know, Dex is actually kind of fast.”
Mafe spent a few minutes in the blue injury tent but returned to the field a short time later.
One play after Mafe’s sack and Lawrence’s recovery, Burrow hit Higgins for a 17-yard touchdown pass, upping the Cincinnati lead to 21-13.
If either one of the Lawrence-Mafe plays doesn’t happen, the Bengals likely lose that game as a 13.5-point favorite, regardless of all of the other offensive fireworks.
The Mafe-Lawrence tandem is becoming every bit as potent as Chase-Higgins on offense, and Sunday was their coming out party.
But the fact remains the Bengals defense gave up 36 points and 440 yards to what had been a stagnant Tennessee offense.
"I think this game was just, you know, showing us that we can be mentally strong through the ups and downs of the game due to change of possessions, change of leads, going into overtime," Lawrence said. "Just allowing us to just understand who we can be.
"Most of the games in the NFL are close," he added. "So to win games like this is big."
Mafe said it's great to not only know Lawrence has his back, but also that Burrow and the offense do as well.
"It's amazing," he said. "This is the first time being on a team where you just never know what's going to happen and just being able to watch and trust in that takes a lot of pressure off the defense, knowing that we can trust our offense to go out there and do what they gotta do.
"As long as we give them a drive, they'll show up," Mafe added. "And that's what our mentality is -- we've just got to give the offense a drive. And as long as we can do that, we can trust them to make sure they do their job."

title: 'A Lot Of Good And A Lot Of Bad Today' - Joe Burrow Reacts to Historic Rollercoaster Titans Performance
full_text:
Joe Burrow had plenty to be happy about and plenty to be upset about after a rollercoaster 43-36 win for his Bengals team. Cincinnati's passer notched a historic outing that hasn't happened in a long time after passing for 462 yards, five TDs (one rushing), and three picks.
According to ESPN, Burrow is the second QB in NFL history with 450 passing yards, 5 pass TDs, and 1 rushing TD in a single game, and first in 75 years. The other was Norm Van Brocklin in 1951, who set the NFL record with 554 passing yards in that game.
"Yeah, a lot of good and a lot of bad today," Burrow said about the historic mark.
He had a short reaction to that stat history. The leader more worried about how Cincinnati can execute better and not commit four turnovers overall.
"Yeah, that's always the difficult part of games in this league," Burrow said. "It's never going to be a perfect game, and certainly going to enjoy it today. And then we'll come in tomorrow and learn from our mistakes and try to get better. Then get back to it and we'll fly to Madrid and get back to practice on Tuesday and try to get better."
Ja'Marr Chase had a big day with 11 catches for 141 yards and a score, but still showed a lot of frustration with how Cincinnati executed.
"I don't know," Chase said to The Enquirer about the team's slow starts of late. "Ask Zac (Taylor). That's not my job, ask Zac."
Burrow isn't worried about his top wide receiver as everybody gets ready to hit the road to Madrid in a couple of days.
"I don't think I need to make sure about that. You know, he's a pro, and guys get emotional sometimes. That's how it is. I like when he gets emotional like that. That usually means that I need to do a better job of throwing the ball, and sometimes that's a good reminder," Burrow said about Chase.
Burrow is leading a contender and should be right in the thick of the MVP race still, even with his third career game featuring three interceptions. He did more than enough to win and showed the clutch factor on not one but two drives in the fourth quarter/overtime.
He finally got a defense to steel up in the right moment this time as the whole team looks to clean things up before facing the Falcons next Sunday morning.
Joe Burrow is the second QB in NFL history with 450 passing yards, 5 pass TD and 1 rush TD in a single game, and first in 75 years! The other was Norm Van Brocklin in 1951, who set the NFL record with 554 passing yards in that game. pic.twitter.com/R7rArOTIXm
Ja’Marr Chase said “Ask Zac” when asked about how the #Bengals can avoid slow starts. Chase was still encouraged about the team getting the W in a wild OT win over the 1-win Titans. pic.twitter.com/R9nyr52SKL
Elite status. pic.twitter.com/TLRRh8fpBn

title: 'Why You Trade For A Guy Like That' - Zac Taylor Relishes in Dexter Lawrence's Game-Changing Titans Plays
full_text:
The Bengals snuck out a close win over the 1-6 Titans at home on Sunday.
The high-scoring 43-36 victory featured Dexter Lawrence (seven tackles, one sack) helping seal things in the final minutes. The Titans could've kicked a game-winning field goal in regulation facing a huge third down at midfield, but Lawrence sacked QB Cam Ward to end their chance.
It was another massive Lawrence play in a season that's featuring them weekly. He's been everything and more Cincinnati could ask for.
Lawrence made sure Joe Burrow's massively clutch showing down the stretch in the face of three interceptions didn't get wasted.
"In that moment right there, we've kind of seen that situation before," Taylor told the media. "Two-minute drive, a field goal wins it for them. They could probably kick it at that point from 45 or beyond. They might have attempted that thing, so we're right there on the fringe, and Dexter can win: get him on the ground, not let him out of his grasp, not let him throw the ball away, and see if they can't try something really long. Gets him on the ground and finishes the game for the defense. That's why you trade for a guy like that, and he stepped up and has been the impact player we hoped he would be."
Sometimes you just got to find a way to win in the NFL as Cincinnati now gets ready for a days-long trip to Spain this week.
5-2 is a huge next step, especially as things look like a potential two-team race in the AFC North with the 6-2 Steelers.
Cincinnati is rowing forward across the pond.
"Gotta take a deep breath," Tayor said. "I wish we played 17 perfect regular season games, but those guys are getting paid a lot of money too on the other side of the ball on the other team, and so they made some plays today too that made things difficult for us. And again, it's just about finding a way."
Cincinnati won in the clutch after blowing out the Ravens, now an NFC foe awaiting the Falcons.

title: Instant Takeaways: Joe Burrow Leads Bengals to Wild OT Win Over Titans
full_text:
The Bengals were supposed to dominate on Sunday against the Titans. Instead, they escaped with a win. Joe Burrow delivered in the clutch, leading the Bengals on 3-straight touchdown drives in the fourth quarter and overtime to secure the 43-36 win.
Burrow ran for a 9-yard touchdown in overtime to give Cincinnati the lead for good. The Bengals are 5-2 on the season. It was ugly, but they found a way to secure the victory. It's their third-straight win.
Here are our postgame observations:
Joe Burrow put up big numbers, but the turnovers will be a talking point this week. He completed 38-of-48 passes for 462 yards, five touchdowns and three interceptions.
Burrow did lead the Bengals on back-to-back touchdown drives in the fourth quarter to force overtime.
His third interception was brutal. He had Ja'Marr Chase wide open in what should've been the go-ahead touchdown. Instead, Amani Hooker snagged the late and underthrown ball for his third pick of the day.
Burrow threw three interceptions in total, including two in the second half. Hooker is the first NFL player to have three interceptions in a game since Jets safety Jordan Whitehead did it in 2023 against the Bills.
The Bengals' defense stepped up, forcing three turnovers of their own. First, DJ Turner knocked the ball away from Wan'Dale Robinson. Josh Newton recovered the fumble.
In the second half, Dexter Lawrence recovered a Cam Ward fumble after Boye Mafe knocked the ball away. Lawrence and Mafe have been game changing additions to the defensive line room. They also forced a safety following Burrow's third interception of the day that gave Cincinnati a 23-21 lead.
It wasn't all pretty for the defense. Ward completed 25-of-38 passes for a career-high 298 yards. He also ran for 33 yards.
Tony Pollard led the Titans with 117 rushing yards and two touchdowns. He also had three receptions for 20 yards.
The defense had a chance to end the game in the fourth quarter, but allowed the Titans to go on back-to-back toucdown drives, including an 8-play, 68-yard drive that ended with a Wan'Dale Robinson touchdown.
Lawrence came up big with a sack on Ward to force overtime.
Despite not being in a rhythm for most of the day, Burrow led Cincinnati on a go-ahead touchdown drive in the fourth quarter. Burrow found Mike Gesicki for a 25-yard score to give the Bengals a 29-28 lead with 7:08 left in the fourth quarter. He led a second touchdown drive, this time finding Tee Higgins for a score.
Tee Higgins led the way with 10 catches for 155 yards and two touchdowns. Ja'Marr Chase had 11 receptions for 141 yards and a score. Gesicki finished with four catches for 76 yards, including the go-ahead touchdown in the fourth quarter.
Chase Brown ran for 48 yards. He also had seven catches for 39 yards.
Cincinnati's offense never fully got into a rhythm on Sunday. Burrow was sacked three times. Despite that, they took the lead late in the game when Burrow found Gesicki for the go-ahead score.
The Bengals started slow for a second-straight week. The Titans scored on their first three possessions to take a 13-0 first quarter lead. Cincinnati rallied to take a 14-13 lead at halftime, but this is the second-straight 13-0 deficit they've faced in the past two games.
The Bengals hit the road. They play the Falcons in Madrid, Spain on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 9:30 AM ET.

title: DJ Turner II, Other Bengals Defenders Injured Against Titans
full_text:
Cincinnati is dealing with a few injuries at the defensive end position during Sunday's game against Tennessee, along with a problem for DJ Turner. Rookie Cashius Howell is out with a right wrist injury as well, and Cedric Johnson is questionable to return to the game with an ankle injury (now out).
Turner headed to the locker room in the fourth quarter and is out.
"Cedric Johnson has a left ankle injury. His return is questionable. DE Cashius Howell has a right wrist injury. He has been declared out," The Bengals posted on X.
The Bengals are trailing 28-23 as of this writing after forcing a safety late in the third quarter and then fumbling away possession a few plays later. Cincinnati is trying to get to 5-2 in the 2026 season and keep their momentum rolling from the past few weeks.
They entered this game as giant favorites to win but haven't lived up to that. A bunch of defensive injuries would be tough to swallow, having already gone through the bye week this season.
Joe Burrow is going to have to step up through these injuries; alas, he's thrown three interceptions in this game, marking just the third time in his career that's happened.
"I've never been around that detailed of a guy. It's not just a rep in practice or the game," Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said this week. "It's all the things around those reps that he does to prepare himself. He could probably articulate it 1,000 times better than I can. I'm just observing what I see from him. I don't talk to him about it that much.
"It's just that I've just, from a distance, always sat there and watched him in all sorts of areas and tried to prove my own quarterback knowledge, because it's really impressive watching how he goes about putting himself in a position to make the plays he does and be as accurate as he is. Because he's the most accurate in the world. He is the most accurate. It's really impressive."
Cincinnati is trying to avoid a huge upset loss at home.

title: Steelers Players Clap Back At Browns' Jared Verse Following Disappointing Performance
full_text:
Things can't get much worse for the Cleveland Browns right now.
On Sunday, Nov. 1, the Browns lost to the Pittsburgh Steelers on the road from Acrisure Stadium in an abysmal 27- 6 showing. Not only did the offense fail to score a touchdown, but the defense was getting beat left and right as running backs Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle combined for nearly 200 yards on the deck with two touchdowns.
Leading up to the game, just weeks after beating the Steelers at home, Browns defensive end Jared Verse spoke up about how he had been waiting for the rematch. He said the Steelers' antics in the first meeting were "garbage" and "dirty."
Browns vs. Steelers recently Jared Verse: "I don’t got no respect for anybody that plays too dirty, and that does too much extra shit after the game. ... I can’t wait to get my hands on them again." Cam Heyward: "The AFC North is on fire and I’m glad I’m in the kitchen because…
Well, unfortunately, not only were the Browns not able to back him up, but his play wasn't able to either.
The 25-year-old finished the game with practically nothing on the stat sheet, posting just a single assisted tackle.
Following the win, Steelers defensive back Jaquan Brisker clapped back at Verse, saying he should have kept quiet.
“He should have kept his mouth shut," Brisker said. "All that talk, and then to come out with 0 tackles? You didn't stand on business. He gotta look at himself in the mirror and get better."
#Steelers S Jaquan Brisker calls out Jared Verse: “He should have kept his mouth shut. All that talk, and then to come out with 0 tackles? You didn't stand on business. He gotta look at himself in the mirror and get better." (📽️ @AshleyWenskTV ) pic.twitter.com/0dA7tduHdQ https://t.co/8eKpqrPMSr
Verse's time in the Orange and Brown hasn't been too hot, with Sunday's performance just adding fuel to the fire that is the narrative that he has lost his touch.
Through the first eight games of the year, he has a whopping 10 solo tackles and eight assisted tackles for 18 total . He also has zero sacks, forced fumbles, fumble recoveries and pass deflections, all areas he at least recorded a single statistic in previous years.
Following in Brisker's words, Steelers offensive lineman Max Iheanachor also shot a diss in Verse's direction.
On X, he posted, "Like I said, Talk is cheap," followed by a talking emoji.
Like I said, Talk is cheap 🗣️
Verse didn't just have a tough time in the stat column either on Sunday, as he was seen being ragdoll-tossed down to the ground by Steelers offensive guard Mason McCormick on a field goal attempt. Verse went crashing down to the ground, landing right on his head.
The circumstances warranted a 15-yard penalty.
After the game, Verse spoke out and said that he doesn't have any respect for McCormick's moves on the play.
In response, McCormick said that he had no idea it was even Verse jumping towards him on the play, seemingly downplaying the situation.
I asked #Steelers G Mason McCormick on dumping #Browns DE Jared Verse during a PAT — you’ve probably seen it by now, I don’t really need to explain: pic.twitter.com/PaeBLlXtxP
Either way, Verse has dove head first into the Browns-Steelers rivalry, getting a front row seat to just how crazy it can get.
While antics, lackluster performances and postgame quotes are going to steal the show, that could have all been avoided if the Browns had won on Sunday.
But for the third time this season, Cleveland ended up on the bad end of a result.
If Verse and the Browns want to chat back and forth with the opposition leading up to a Sunday showdown, next time, they better be able to back it up.

title: Steelers Expose Browns' Biggest Weakness in Frustrating Cleveland Loss
full_text:
There was plenty of back-and-forth between the Cleveland Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers throughout the past week.
The latter ended up being the team to live up to all the talk.
The Steelers took an early 10-0 lead that proved to be insurmountable as Deshaun Watson and the Browns offense failed to reach the end zone on Sunday.
Cleveland's first two drives ended in fumbles, setting the tone for an ugly Sunday in Pittsburgh.
The Browns couldn't do much of anything right in the loss. A quick glimpse at the box score shows how the Browns finished with 34 rushing yards, while the Steelers had 200. Jaylen Warren led the way with a dominant 17 carries for 143 yards.
The Browns defense had no answer for Warren and company, while the Browns offense struggled for each and every yard on the ground. That made passing the focus and resulted in Watson taking eight sacks, as he was under constant pressure with every single dropback.
#Browns DE Jared Verse has been talking plenty of trash about the #Steelers .... Well, Steelers G Mason McCormick just did this to him.  😳😳 pic.twitter.com/OP1iknS4JP
The score may have been even worse if the Steelers capped off two early drives with touchdowns instead of field goals, and if DK Metcalf didn't bobble a potential big catch right into the arms of Denzel Ward.
Watson and the Browns have been comeback specialists in 2026, with the latest coming last week against the Tennessee Titans. Yet the Steelers are on an entirely different level, improving to 6-2 with the win.
Sunday's game also involved a rare Shedeur Sanders sighting in 2026. He came on for a series and completed two short passes while Watson was getting checked out on the sideline and ultimately cleared to return.
Fans seeking a positive from the loss can look to the big day from Harold Fannin Jr. The tight end finished with 10 catches for 154 yards, representing a new career-best in yards. Yes, some of the yardage did come near the end of the game. But there's still no denying his game-changing abilities when properly involved in the offense.
Next up is a road game against the 2-5 New Orleans Saints, currently resting up on a bye week. That is a team with a total of 602 rushing yards through seven games, so all eyes will be on the Browns defense to see if the unit can end this current trend of getting destroyed in the running game.
This loss was an ugly one, however, the Browns do get the split with the Steelers in 2026. Winning in Pittsburgh has been nearly impossible for the post-1999 Browns, so Sunday's loss was nothing too surprising.
