title: 3 Biggest Takeaways From Browns Week 8 Loss to Rival Pittsburgh Steelers
full_text:
Well, the Cleveland Browns just embarrassed themselves.
After talking big all week leading up to the final regular season meeting with the Pittsburgh Steelers this year, the Browns took the field at Acrisure Stadium and put up a disappointing performance.
On Sunday, Nov. 1, the Browns lost to the Steelers, 27-6, with multiple glaring issues leading to the team's downfall. From a lackluster start to the game from the offense to countless penalties and issues with self-control, the Browns suffered loss No. 3 of the season.
Fortunately, there is still plenty of season left to make corrections, but this one stung a bit.
Here are the three biggest takeaways from the Browns' Week 8 loss to the Steelers on the road:
Yet again, the offense looked slow out of the gates.
Across the first three drives of the game, the Deshaun Watson-led offense managed to muster a whopping 14 yards off of 11 players. The Browns would leave each with zero points, as two fumbles and a punt stole the show.
Watson was responsible with one fumble, with tight end Harold Fannin Jr. being the other.
The Browns would finish the first quarter trailing by seven points, before two field goals helped to lessen the blow in the second. By the time the opening half concluded, Cleveland was down by 14 points, 20-6.
While Watson did end up finishing the game with 27 completions for 324 yards passing , his lackluster start to the game set the tone.
Deshaun Watson may have finished with 27 completions for 324 yards... but the slow start to Sunday's game set the tone for the Browns' offense... They have to stop turning it on so late. Final: 27-6. #DawgPound
If the Browns want to start putting themselves in more favorable positions to win, getting on the board within the first drive or two is going to have to become a priority.
The Browns hurt themselves... a lot.
By the end of Sunday's game, penalties had taken away 80 yards from them. For a team already going up against a loud fanbase at Acrisure Stadium, putting yourself in increasingly difficult situations with self-inflicted penalties makes things much worse.
Heading into Week 8, the Browns had a whopping 63 penalties across seven games, bringing them to an average of nine per game. While pre-snap issues have been a big part, the offense has just been all-around sloppy.
Head coach Todd Monken will likely harp on the team's penalty issues behind closed doors, which is the correct thing to do, but things have got to start changing.
The Browns just can't keep beating themselves.
Among the 80 yards of penalties on Sunday were a few taunting calls, something that seemed shocking considering they came with Cleveland trailing by multiple scores.
If the Browns are going to talk the talk, they better be able to walk the walk.
On Sunday, they just simply didn't.
Two takeaways: 1) how are you taunting down 21 points? 2) how are you throwing flags like that in a rivalry game? Either way, gotta keep your emotions in check… #DawgPound
Before they started to lose control of their emotions later in the game, the Browns looked asleep. From start to finish, the entire game felt all over the place in the emotional department. Jared Verse, one of the Browns' leaders on the defensive side of the ball, yet again fell short after a week of talking smack to the Steelers.
It's always nice to see players hype up an outing, especially when the rivalry runs so deep, but if you are going to, you have to back it up.
Looking to put Week 8 behind them, the Browns return to the gridiron on Sunday, Nov. 8, at 1:00 p.m. EST from Caesars Superdome in New Orleans to take on the Saints.
Cade Cracas is a sports media professional with experience in play-by-play, broadcasting and digital storytelling. He is a recent graduate of Ashland University with degrees in digital media production and journalism.

title: Week 8 Browns vs. Steelers: What To Expect, Injury Report, How To Watch and More
full_text:
It's another rendition of a rivalry that runs deep.
Following a 27-24 victory at Huntington Bank Field for the Cleveland Browns just a few weeks ago, the Pittsburgh Steelers will be searching for revenge in the second meeting of the 2026 NFL regular season.
On Sunday, Nov. 1, the Browns and Steelers will face one another at Acrisure Stadium in Pittsburgh for a Week 8 showdown. The two sides will renew the storied rivalry in the 151st all-time meeting. This time around, though, the narrative is centered on the Steelers' long winning streak at home and the Browns' opportunity to sweep the Steelers for the first time since 1988.
The Browns last won in Pittsburgh on Oct. 5, 2003, when then-quarterback Tim Couch threw for over 200 yards and two touchdowns, while the defense forced two interceptions in a 33-13 victory.
Looking to repeat such efforts, the Browns will need to come locked in and ready to go against an experienced, veteran-led Steelers squad.
From the jump, Sunday's game is going to be a fiery one.
Throughout the week, the two sides had been throwing little jabs at one another, with defensive linemen Jared Verse and Cam Heyward being at the center of the attention.
"I'm not worried about Cam [Heyward]," Verse said earlier in the week. "I'm not worried about their O-line. I'm not worried about nobody they got on their team. We out there to go dominate."
He went on to say that he has been waiting for the rematch, and that last time's meeting left a bad taste in his mouth due to some "dirty" plays.
In response, Heyward clapped back at Verse, pretty much calling him a baby.
"Double-teaming, sliding, chipping, are those not allowed in our game? Yeah, I got the bruises to prove it," Heyward said. "But we don’t whine about it, baby. It’s part of the game. And so, I’m looking forward to this game. It’s gonna be a fun game..."
But this isn't something unexpected.
In seasons past, the rivalry has run deep, with tensions never really running low. However, that isn't necessarily a bad thing, as a blood-boiling rivalry makes things entertaining for everyone involved.
Fortunately, things are looking clear for Sunday's meeting.
From 1pm through 5 pm, the temperature is expected to sit between 67 degrees and 69 degrees, with somewhat cloudy skies. The precipitation is at 10%, while the Humidity comes in at 53%. There are no expected storms.
While Browns Stadium always sees a good amount of wind, Acrisure will not.
The air quality is a strong 44, with the wind coming in at just three miles per hour. If there are any gusts, they are expected to be roughly eight miles per hour.
Date and Time: Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026 at 1:00 p.m. EST
The game can be watched on television on CBS, with streaming options such as YouTube TV, Fubo, DirecTV and Paramount+ available as well.
The last time the Browns and Steelers clashed, multiple players went down with injuries.
For the Browns, the two standouts were defensive tackles Mason Graham and Mike Hall Jr., who left the game at different points with lower-body injuries. Although Hall Jr. ended up finishing the game, both he and Graham would miss future games.
Heading into Sunday, both players are healthy.
Here is the rest of the injury reports as of the early morning hours on Sunday:
CB Echols (Hamstring) - Out LB Highsmith (Groin) - Cleared CB Ramsey (Wrist) - Cleared WR Skowronek (Calf) - Questionable DB Slaughter (Hamstring) - Out
S Delpit (Neck) - Cleared DT Graham (Ankle) - Cleared DT Hall Jr. (Ankle) - Cleared CB Harden (Hamstring) - Questionable OT Howard (Concussion) - Cleared LB Schwesinger (Ankle) - Cleared DE Verse (Knee) - Cleared DB Thomas (Ankle) - Questionable
Kickoff between the two sides is set for 1:00 p.m. EST, with the winner taking the top spot in the AFC North in a crucial part of the season.
Cade Cracas is a sports media professional with experience in play-by-play, broadcasting and digital storytelling. He is a recent graduate of Ashland University with degrees in digital media production and journalism.

title: Can the Browns Beat the Steelers? Traveling to Pittsburgh is No Easy Task
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns have already weathered the storm that is the Pittsburgh Steelers once this season.
But that doesn't mean the second meeting is going to be any easier.
On Sunday, Nov. 1, the Browns will travel to Acrisure Stadium to take on the Steelers for the second matchup between the two sides during the 2026 NFL regular season. The Browns won the first meeting, 27-24, but since then, the Steelers have made many changes and improvements.
They head into Sunday's outing with a three-game winning streak in hand, a mark the Browns sit just a game behind.
When these two sides meet, though, records and successes that season are thrown out the window.
It is simply a good ol' fashioned rivalry, and anything can happen.
What is going to make the biggest difference on the first day of November will likely be confidence, especially in the way of the Browns.
As a young squad, they won't just face one of the league's most experienced, veteran-led teams, but also a team that has called their number time and time again in Pittsburgh. The Steelers have held onto a narrative for 22 straight regular-season games: not losing at home to the Browns.
The Browns have lost 22 straight regular-season games in Pittsburgh, and have not won a regular-season game there since Oct. 5, 2003 -- 8,248 days ago. They are one loss today shy of tying the NFL record for most consecutive road regular-season losses vs. a team in NFL history… pic.twitter.com/10avzSmShS
The Browns have not won a game in Pittsburgh since Oct. 5, 2003.
At that time, Tim Couch was the Browns' signal caller, throwing for two touchdowns and one interception in a 33-13 victory. The Browns would go on to win just five games that season, losing 11, but as the rivalry has shown in the past, sometimes that is one of the most important games on the schedule.
Browns defensive end Jared Verse sparked the fire up a bit earlier in the week, putting more weight on a good performance from Cleveland on Sunday.
"I'm not worried about Cam [Heyward]," he began. "I'm not worried about their o-line, I'm not worried about nobody they've got on their team. We're out there to go dominate."
Verse has yet to record a sack this season, but that doesn't mean he hasn't been impactful. On film review, the 25-year-old has been seen taking assignments away from other offensive linemen, freeing up his teammates to get into the backfield and go to work.
As a defense, the Browns rank 12th in points allowed this season, while the line itself ranks fifth in pressure rate. Even with Verse not putting any sacks on the board, the group is finding a way to disrupt opposing quarterbacks.
But in front of the Steelers faithful, Verse and the rest of the defense will certainly get an earful. They will have to show they can cut out the fans and trash talk and put veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers on his backside.
Browns head coach Todd Monken understands that the rivalry runs deep, but he is making it known that this new group of players has nothing to do with the long-winded losing streak.
Instead, he has been trying to set the stage for a new opportunity for the current squad to show the rest of the league how good they are, as a win against the Steelers would put them in sole control of the AFC North.
"Whether it's where we're at record-wise, comparing the past or the history against the Steelers—it's a divisional game," Monken said. "Fastest way to get in the playoffs is win your division. That's the fastest way to get in the playoffs. I mean, you're guaranteed in the tournament and we're a long ways away from that.
"That's not what I'm saying. That's why the game is what it is. And rivalries are made up of good teams playing each other and we're fighting like hell to be a really good team."
The Browns will look to snap a losing streak that has lasted longer than many players on the active roster have been alive.
Even with that, though, rookie wideout Denzel Boston understands just how important a win would be.
"We know coming into this game it’s going to be chippy considering what happened last game," he said. "...I had a conversation yesterday with people [about the losing streak]... which we aren't paying attention to any of those stats going into the game, but I can tell it is huge for the city of Cleveland."
Sunday will be the 151st installment of such a storied rivalry, with the two sides set to square away at 1:00 p.m. EST.
Cade Cracas is a sports media professional with experience in play-by-play, broadcasting and digital storytelling. He is a recent graduate of Ashland University with degrees in digital media production and journalism.

title: Eye-Opening Stat Shows What the Browns Need WR Jerry Jeudy to Rediscover
full_text:
A season where the Cleveland Browns won just three games and lost a whopping 14.
But although there were many, and I mean many, negatives following that season, one big-time positive was the breakout of wide receiver Jerry Jeudy.
The then-25-year-old went out and led the offense with 90 receptions, 1,229 yards and four touchdowns . He averaged 13.7 yards per reception and 72.3 yards per game. That type of productivity gave a glimpse into Jeudy's true potential.
Posted on X by Gridiron Stats and Info on Saturday, Oct. 31, the last time the Browns had a 150-yard receiver was Jeudy, back during the 2024 season. In a late-season Dec. 2 matchup with the Denver Broncos, he hauled in nine of 13 targets for 235 yards and one touchdown.
Last time each NFL team had a 150-yard receiver pic.twitter.com/gOIl3DRSHK
Even with such production, somehow, someway, the Browns would lose 42-31. But Jeudy still put a positive light on the game as he joined the record books, becoming the fourth player in franchise history to surpass 200 receiving yards in a game, trailing just Josh Gordon and Amari Cooper for the top spots.
However, just a few years later, now at age 27, Jeudy has seemingly fallen completely out of the Browns' offensive plans.
And looking back at 2024 and comparing his play to that of 2026 begs the question: can he ever return to that form?
Just three seasons ago, Jeudy was catching passes from a combination of Jameis Winston, Deshaun Watson, Dorian Thompson-Robinson and Bailey Zappe.
Now, in 2026, he has Watson as his starting signal caller.
Building chemistry has been difficult, especially with Watson missing the last two seasons. When Jeudy joined the Browns from the Denver Broncos, the controversial quarterback was already dealing with off-field issues and injuries, limiting the time they could spend developing a connection.
As long as Watson can stay healthy this season, the bond will gradually form.
Since getting just five targets for two catches and 26 yards across the first three weeks of the season, his involvement in the offense has shot up tremendously over the last four weeks. From Week 4 through Week 7, he has made 14 catches on 18 targets for 145 yards.
While at times he doesn't get the rock thrown his way until late, Watson has turned to him in critical moments, where Jeudy has then delivered.
The Browns know it, Watson knows it and Jeudy knows it: when the Browns need a play, they go his way. He has the experience and the resume to prove that he can be an elite weapon, especially downfield; that connection just needs a chance to fully grow.
I asked #Browns WR Jerry Jeudy about Cleveland’s fourth-quarter grit and ability to find a way to win: "We're just motivated. We're determined to win each and every week. We come with the mindset to win the game, no matter what the score is. We focus on each play." pic.twitter.com/d7mPzimahA
And fortunately, it seems that he will have every opportunity to make up for lost time.
Over the course of the last few weeks, rumors have swirled about whether or not the Browns' front office would start shopping him. While the Browns will at least listen to an offer if it is substantial enoug h, which makes total sense, they do not plan to actively look to move him elsewhere.
It seems that the 27-year-old will have a chance to remain in Cleveland and form a deeper bond with the young offense.
"With Cleveland in the postseason mix and Jeudy maintaining a good attitude despite the emergence of rookies KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston at wide receiver, sources say his chances of being traded is viewed as less likely," Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter recently wrote. "The Browns aren't shopping Jeudy at all, and the price is high. It would take a premium deal to get Cleveland to move on -- even if general manager Andrew Berry is open to discussing any deal.
"But as of right now, a Jeudy deal seems unlikely."
It sounds like Jerry Jeudy is locked into the Browns roster unless a team comes with a wild offer (which isn’t happening). Ian Rapoport ( @RapSheet ) and Adam Schefter ( @AdamSchefter ) reporting the Browns aren’t shopping the veteran receiver and "the price is too high." Browns… pic.twitter.com/qV98g4Ce6b
Jeudy's next opportunity to slowly start regaining that dominant form he displayed in 2024 will be this weekend on Sunday, Nov. 1, when the Browns travel to Pittsburgh to take on the Steelers.
The two sides will matchup at 1:00 p.m. EST at Acrisure Stadium for the second meeting of the season.
Cade Cracas is a sports media professional with experience in play-by-play, broadcasting and digital storytelling. He is a recent graduate of Ashland University with degrees in digital media production and journalism.

title: 8 Players that Need to Step Up in Week 8 Against the Steelers
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns head into Pittsburgh to take on the Steelers, looking to fortify their first-place standing in the AFC North and put the league on notice. ESPN ranked the Browns last in the AFC North in their power rankings and the league is not buying their early success due to having to rely on game-winning drives.
The Browns are 2-0 within their division in the first half of the season and have beaten the Steelers in Week 4 in primetime. Their struggles in the Steel City have been well documented, but they do not apply to this new roster and coaching staff.
The Browns will need several of their young players to step up on Sunday to change history.
Graham started the season looking like a completely new defensive tackle with four sacks in the first four games. He got injured in the first matchup against the Steelers and missed a couple of weeks, returning last week and recording no sacks .
The defense got gashed last week in the running game and Jaylen Warren has been one of the NFL’s best recently. Graham needs to be able to limit their running game and force Aaron Rodgers to have throw in obvious passing situations. Graham needs to then do what he did best to start the season and get pressure from the middle of the pocket.
The offense became unlocked when the Browns forced the ball to Concepcion last week and he had over 150 yards of total offense. Todd Monken and Deshaun Watson have to put an emphasis on getting him the ball in space and letting his speed and elusiveness take over.
The Steelers’ pass rush will be looking to unsettle Watson and he has to get the ball out of his hands fast. Concepcion is the perfect outlet for Watson in the slot being around the line of scrimmage to turn a short pass into a big yard gain.
Fano has been a solid left tackle in his rookie season and he will be tasked with blocking TJ Watt and Alex Highsmith. They have to provide a clean pocket for Watson to be able to read the secondary and make good decisions with the ball.
They did a nice job in the first half of their Week 4 meeting, but the second half was a different story and the offense stalled with turnovers.
Howard got the clearance to start after not practicing all week with a concussion. The edges are going to test these tackles, and they have to come ready to play.
The veteran quarterback finally got his first 300-yard passing game last week and he did that by being decisive with the ball, taking the shots downfield when he could, and leading his receivers for yards after the catch.
The Steelers will try anything to get him off his game, and he cannot let the atmosphere get too big for him. Watson must have a plan at the line of scrimmage for where the ball needs to go in the face of pressure and not solely rely on his legs to bail him out.
Verse does not have a sack this season and at times gets lost in the shuffle of the line of scrimmage. He has been close on making big plays and has helped the line in general, make game-changing plays.
He needs to be effective against the run and make Warren try and beat them on the inside. If he can control the perimeter, then it will allow Grand Delpit and Emmanuel McNeil-Warren to play in the secondary and ball hawk. The first meeting ended with an interception by Delpit.
The offense looked completely different last week, with Judkins exploding for his best game of the season. They ran the ball with Watson under center more than they had in previous weeks and there were bigger holes for Judkins to hit.
The Browns have to stay out of third-and-long situations and Judkins has to build on last week and forget about the first handful of games.
The Browns are considerably better on offense when Fannin is involved. They have gone away from him in a couple of games, and the offense struggled. They made an effort to get him the ball last week, and he helped them on the last drive by breaking tackles and setting them up with a chip-shot field goal.
The task is tough, but the Browns have not seemed to care about the situation they have been put in so far this season. If these players perform to their capabilities, then the Browns can leave Pittsburgh with their stamp on the division and the rest of the NFL will take notice .
Graduated from Bowling Green State University with a Journalism degree. Written and contributed to numerous media outlets. Cleveland sports victim.

title: Browns Final Injury Report Reveals a Few Key Concerns Against Steelers
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns have one of their biggest tests of the season coming up this Sunday when they take on the Pittsburgh Steelers.
With both teams battling for the top spot in the AFC North, it’ll be crucial for the Browns to be as prepared as they can be heading into this contest. The most important thing for Cleveland will be the availability of their players.
A few names popped up on the injury report over the course of the week that were alarming, but some have since been cleared and will play. That won’t be the case for every player that was listed.
Friday #Browns @ #Steelers injury report pic.twitter.com/SDoQKuljwn
Whether it’s a starter or a depth player, everyone will matter in this game, as it can be a brutally physical game anytime the Browns face off against the Steelers.
Cleveland got the best of Pittsburgh a couple of weeks ago on Thursday Night Football, but this is a new week with new stakes. Here are a few names from the injury report to watch out for in this divisional duel:
In Cleveland’s last game against Pittsburgh, Graham suffered a lower leg injury that looked a lot worse , but he was ruled week-to-week following the game. Now, Graham looks primed to play against the team that took him out once again.
Graham hasn’t recorded any stats in their previous two games, but has been making progress over the weeks, even appearing in last week’s win over the Titans. Graham looked to have reaggravated his injury but was held out as more of a precautionary decision.
The Browns will have to do their best to stop the Steelers’ red hot run game, and Graham could be at the forefront of making that happen. Having their top defensive tackle back alongside the recently extended Maliek Collins will be key to beating Pittsburgh.
A hamstring injury has been limiting Harden this past week, which means he likely tweaked it during their game last Sunday. Harden is one of three Browns players carrying a questionable status heading into Sunday.
Harden has been seeing plenty of playing time for the Browns this season as their third string cornerback and would play a big role in the secondary if he’s available to play.
It’s never an easy task limiting future Hall of Fame quarterback Aaron Rodgers, but if Harden can play, he’ll be responsible for making it tough on Pittsburgh’s offense to throw the ball downfield.
As of today, it’s expected that Howard could miss this week’s game after suffering a concussion last week. He didn’t log a single practice this week and now is in jeopardy of missing this massive game.
His duties would be to block Pittsburgh’s all-pro linebacker TJ Watt on the outside, but that may be the job of Dawand Jones this week if he’s ruled out . Jones has done well when facing Watt in the past, which should give the Browns confidence in his abilities once again.
In the Browns’ last game against the Steelers, Hall Jr. stepped in for the injured Mason Graham and also got injured in that game. He’s done his best to get back on the field lately but hasn’t been cleared since.
It was also a lower leg injury that Hall Jr. suffered, which sparked Jared Verse’s comments regarding Pittsburgh’s dirty playstyle on defense. Regardless of how the team plays, Hall isn’t officially cleared to seek his revenge.
He carries a questionable status heading into Sunday as well, but if he’s good to go, it’s expected he’ll play an important role in limiting the Steelers’ offense.
Dominic Pagura is from Medina, Ohio and a graduate from Kent State University.

title: Way-Too-Early Veteran QB Options for Browns To Start in Week 1 of 2027 Season
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns have shocked the football world, starting the season with a 5-2 record, but one thing still hangs over their heads: what they'll do at quarterback next season.
Cleveland will face a difficult decision about whether to re-sign Deshaun Watson to a new contract next spring and let him start in 2027. However, the Browns also have a handful of veteran options they could explore next year.
Cleveland will likely be in the mix to draft a rookie quarterback in the 2027 NFL Draft, but it might end up selecting one in the middle of the first round rather than at the beginning. If that's the case, the Browns could use the 2027 season to let the rookie quarterback learn as much as possible behind the veteran they bring in to start next season. Here are some names to consider.
Deshaun Watson: Let's revisit the Watson situation. Coming into the season, the Browns had no intention of offering Watson a new contract after this year. But winning is crucial in the NFL, and securing five wins in the first seven games is significant. Watson will need to continue performing well over the next ten games for Cleveland to even consider re-signing him. If he does, he wouldn't be a bad option for the Browns as a bridge quarterback for a rookie next season. Spotrac listed his market value at $20 million over two years, or $10 million per season, so the Browns could get behind it.
Shedeur Sanders: The Browns still have Sanders on the roster, and head coach Todd Monken could use this season to prepare him to start in 2027. Cleveland drafted Sanders in the fifth round of the 2025 NFL Draft, and he started seven games last season. He was not ready to be a starting quarterback in his rookie season. Sanders was in a quarterback competition all offseason with Watson, and if Watson had performed poorly in the Week 2 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, there was a chance the Browns would bench Watson and move on to Sanders.
Just because Sanders is unlikely to start this season doesn’t mean the Browns have given up on him starting games down the road.
Mac Jones: It was a little surprising that the San Francisco 49ers didn't consider trading Jones this offseason, especially after he performed well backing up Brock Purdy last season. He appeared in 11 games, started eight, and finished with a record of 5-3. Jones threw for 2,151 yards, 13 touchdowns and eight interceptions. However, he will be a free agent this offseason and could be looking for an opportunity to start somewhere.
Sam Darnold was on a similar path to Jones, bouncing around a few teams before landing with the 49ers as Purdy's backup. Darnold found his footing by signing a one-year deal with the Minnesota Vikings in 2024, where he started 17 games and went 14-3. He then signed a three-year, $100.5 million deal with the Seahawks in March 2025, and just 11 months later, he won the Super Bowl.
Jones could follow a similar trajectory to Darnold: start for the Browns for a season, perform well, and then secure a big payday from another team, especially since Cleveland could transition to a rookie it drafts in 2027 and let them start in 2028.
Davis Mills: Mills has been with the Houston Texans for the last five seasons and is set to enter the free agent market. He has appeared in 44 games, starting 29, with eight wins, 19 losses, and one tie. With C.J. Stroud expected to sign a long-term extension with the Texans soon, Mills will be looking for a new team, and Cleveland could be an option.
Stetson Bennett : Bennett and Monken go back to college football at Georgia from 2020 to 2022. Moken served as the Bulldogs' offensive coordinator for three seasons, while Bennett was the starting quarterback in 2021 and 2022, helping Georgia win back-to-back national titles. Bennett has been with the Rams the last four seasons and will be a free agent this offseason. He has appeared in only two games, throwing two passes for 13 yards, but if the Browns sign him, he could start for a few games until the rookie is ready.
Justin Herbert: Herbert may be looking at playing for a new team next season, as the Chargers are currently 0-6 and might be considering a total rebuild. If the Chargers identify a rookie quarterback they like at the top of next year's draft, they could trade Herbert to regain draft capital to build around the new quarterback. Cleveland has gone down this road before, trading three first-round picks for Watson, and it has backfired. But Herbert would likely get only two first-round picks and a little more capital since he turns 29 in March.
Cam Ward: The Browns almost had the opportunity to select Ward in the 2025 NFL Draft if they had lost one more game and secured the No. 1 pick instead of No. 2. The Titans chose Ward with the No. 1 pick, and he has been a disaster. Ward has started 24 games over the past two seasons, throwing for 4,348 yards and 19 touchdowns to 12 interceptions, and has only four wins to show for it.
Ward didn't find himself in the best situation when he arrived in Tennessee, as the Titans fired head coach Brian Callahan six weeks into last season. The Titans demonstrated how little they believe in Ward by trading their star defensive tackle, Jeffery Simmons, to the Chicago Bears on Thursday for two first-round picks. Perhaps a change of scenery could help Ward, and he wouldn’t cost much, as failed first-round picks usually don’t command high draft capital.
Bryce Young: There is a very low chance—about 1%—that the Panthers will move on from Bryce Young this offseason. The Panthers are currently 3-4. If this record doesn’t improve much and they're in a position to take a quarterback early in the first round, Carolina could move on from Young.
Young is in the last year of his rookie contract, but Carolina has picked up his fifth-year option for 2027. If the Panthers are not interested in extending Young long-term, he could become a trade candidate. A similar situation occurred in 2022 with the Browns and Baker Mayfield, who was also a No. 1 pick. The Browns decided not to pay him as he approached his fifth-year option, which led them to trade for Watson.
Daniel is a sports writer from Northeast Ohio. He has followed the Browns, Cavs, Guardians, and Buckeyes for years and loves sharing his thoughts on the team.

title: Can the Browns Break the Losing Streak? A Look at the Numbers Ahead of Rivalry Matchup
full_text:
After a historic 5-2 start to the season, the Cleveland Browns are once again looking to rewrite the history books this week.
Since their last win in 2003, the Cleveland Browns have not defeated the Steelers on the road in a regular season game. The last time they did it? Tim Couch led the Browns to a 33-13 win.
Let's look at the numbers to see if the Browns have a real chance to sweep their biggest rival.
Sixteen players on the Browns’ 53-man roster were not yet born the last time the Browns won a regular season game in Pittsburgh.
The Browns, led by Deshaun Watson , currently have five game-winning drives through the first seven weeks of the NFL season. This number leads the league.
However, there are some glaring numbers that stick out. Pittsburgh may go after some of these gaps and expose the current AFC North leader .
Looking at the Steelers, their games have been won primarily by their defense getting stops, with their offense narrowly getting the job done.
#Browns Jared Verse responds to Cam Heyward’s comments saying that they are going to address his comments after the last Steelers game. Verse called the #Steelers dirty and that he can’t wait to see them again after their Thursday Night win. pic.twitter.com/ZCQK4ILUuM
Despite the historic losing streak, this may be the best chance the Browns have of getting their long sought after win.
If the Browns can come out early, find a consistant source of offense, and simply score, they can look to control the game with a lead.
However, Pittsburgh's defense is one of the NFL's best. Especially when playing divisional games at home, they will be one of the toughest units Cleveland will face all season.
For Pittsburgh, they need to shut down Deshaun Watson and force him to turn the ball over.
The Biggest mistake teams have been making is letting Watson get comfortable. It isn't a coincidence that Watson is the best fourth-quarter quarterback in the NFL right now. Once he gets going, it is hard to stop him.
In the same breath, we have seen Watson get himself into holes many times before. That is why the first half will be a lot more important than people think.
The game will be decided between the Browns' offense and the Steelers' defense. On the opposite side, with Cleveland facing Aaron Rodgers, we pretty much already know what we are going to get.
Louis Timura is a student sports broadcaster and content creator. He currently attends Ashland University while pursuing a degree in Digital Media Production.

title: Dak Prescott Misses the Mark in Attempt to Deflect Blame off Schottenheimer Amid Cowboys' Woes
full_text:
When a team is struggling as badly as the Dallas Cowboys are this season, it's only natural to blame the head coach.
And that's especially true when it comes to Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer, who hasn't done a good job, both in a lead role and as the offensive play-caller.
After the Cowboys' latest debacle against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 8, quarterback Dak Prescott tried to deflect the mountain of blame that has come Schottenheimer's way.
He said placing all of the blame on Schottenheimer for the Cowboys' struggles is "cowardice."
“It’s all of us,” Prescott said, per the team’s website . “Don’t put the blame on one person. Simple as that. I think that’s weak. I think that’s cowardice."
"This game is about all 11 that touch the field and every person that has a part in it coaches and support staff. It’s never just one person’s fault," Prescott added. "Even if I go out there and throw a bunch of interceptions, it’s never just truly one person’s fault. And so, don’t take the easy and cheap way out. This is about us and it’s about us backing him up and backing one another up and we’ll have to show it.”
The problem with what Dak is saying is that nobody is placing all of the blame on Schottenheimer's shoulders. There is plenty to go around for the players and for defensive coordinator Christian Parker, who is simply inadequate , at best, at his job.
But the buck stops with Schottenheimer, who has failed miserably at leading this team and calling the offense.
We saw another example of Schotty's poor decision-making at the end of the first half on Sunday, when, with one timeout in his pocket, he decided to call a run play with 11 seconds left rather than throwing a pass to get Brandon Aubrey closer.
The result was a four-yard gain and a 61-yard attempt for Aubrey that the Cowboys kicker missed. Had Aubrey made the field goal, Dallas would have won the game, plain and simple. Now, it never should have come to that, but the point stands.
There may also be a culture issue in Dallas, and if so, that's yet another stain on Schottenheimer's tenure.
Multiple former Cowboys have questioned the players' effort , and even Schottenheimer has called out George Pickens for not doing enough as a run-blocker, for example.
Effort problems equal culture problems and it's Schottenheimer who is responsible for setting the tone in that department. He's clearly not doing a good enough job on that front.
There are no two ways about it. The Cowboys don't have the right man for the job and no amount of support from Prescott is going to convince us otherwise. Until Schottenheimer is let go, there's zero hope for Dallas.
Unfortunately, owner Jerry Jones continues to show no desire to make a much-needed change , whether that's at head coach or defensive coordinator.

title: Cowboys Insider Believes Brian Schottenheimer’s Ego Holding Him Back
full_text:
Despite going 7-9-1 during his first season as the head coach of the Dallas Cowboys, there was still a lot of positive energy around Brian Schottenheimer entering the new year.
His offense was among the best in the league and the Cowboys spent the offseason working to improve their defense . Now after a 3-5 start and yet another fourth-quarter meltdown, Schottenheimer is feeling the heat . The calls for his job are growing and every week, he says he’s going to put in the work to get things fixed.
Schottenheimer has done his best to remain confident, but one insider thinks the way he sees himself might be the problem. Following the loss to the Arizona Cardinals, Bryan Broaddus said that Schottenheimer’s ego is getting in the way as he’s trying too hard to be something he’s not.
"Schotty called himself an elite play caller. And you know what I think Schotty's biggest issue is? I think Schotty wants to be compared to (Sean) McVay, and I think he wants to be compared to (Kyle) Shanahan, or Ben Johnson. I think he wants to be compared to those guys,” Broaddus said.
“And I think his ego doesn't allow him to just be Brian Schottenheimer. Just to go and call a game where it's for the best of what he's got on the field that day. I think his ego doesn't allow him to be that way. I think he wants to be recognized as McVay and all those top play callers right now. You know, (Liam) Coen. But you don't have the creativity of those guys. You don't have the way that they have – The forward thinking."
@BryanBroaddus says Schotty’s EGO is what’s holding him back @1053thefan @ZachWolchuk pic.twitter.com/REYLarNeFp
Broaddus also discussed how those elite play-callers he mentioned have plays ready to go for certain situations. He said they know what to do with a four-minute offense and how to move the ball when they need to, where as Schottenheimer falls flat when it’s time to rely on scheme and game management.
Nothing summarizes that better than an unbelievable stat shared by Bobby Belt of 105.3 The Fan. Belt pointed out that the Cowboys had 34 yards of offense on their final 27 plays. During that same span, Arizona had 267 yards on 31 plays.
Dallas gained 34 yards of offense on its final 27 plays from scrimmage. The Cardinals picked up 267 yards on its final 31 plays in that same time frame.
Schottenheimer had the better players, there’s no denying that. But even with Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens, and Javonte Williams, the Cowboys were unable to move the ball. Yet the Cardinals did whatever they wanted with Gardner Minshew, Michael Wilson, Trey McBride, and Tyler Allgeier.
That comes down to coaching and once again, the better coach won.

title: Checked Out George Pickens Wasted No Time Leaving Field After Cowboys' Week 8 Loss
full_text:
George Pickens looks like he's checked out after the Dallas Cowboys' Week 8 loss to the Arizona Cardinals .
Well, maybe we should say he was checked out before the Cowboys' Week 8 loss because Pickens appeared to be quite convinced that Arizona kicker Chad Ryland's game-winning field goal in overtime would go through before it actually did.
Thanks to video shared by FOX Sports via WFAA's Mike Leslie, Pickens was seen running through the tunnel and to the locker room just seconds after Ryland's field goal went through.
It would appear that Pickens had already made his way to the back while the ball was in the air, at the latest. He clearly had no desire for postgame handshakes.
How did he get there so fast? (via @MikeLeslieWFAA ) pic.twitter.com/gUZKSxzM5q
Pickens got there so fast, it's like he hopped in a time machine. If that doesn't show a player who is checked out, we don't know what does.
Pickens' early exit from the field came after a game in which he was targeted just four times and reeled in two catches for 48 yards. Pickens also played 42 snaps, which was fewer than CeeDee Lamb (56) and Ryan Flournoy (50).
The Cowboys wideout isn't having a terrible season, but he also isn't putting up the numbers he did in 2025, which isn't totally surprising because Lamb has stayed healthy.
Let's be realistic here: Dallas isn't going anywhere in 2026 and it's time to seriously consider trading Pickens at the deadline, when teams will be most desperate to add to their rosters.
There is just no future for Pickens in Dallas. We've been hit with another stark reminder that having two great receivers doesn't mean anything if a team can't play defense at a competent level, something the Cowboys have been incapable of all season.
Dallas cannot extend Pickens under any circumstances because of the hinderance that would have on the Cowboys' ability to improve the rest of the roster, and especially the defense.
The same rule applies with franchise-tagging Pickens in 2027, and there is also a good chance he won't fall in line with that again like he did this year, which could lead to a holdout.
Furthermore, we're seeing the relationship between Pickens and the Cowboys deteriorate in real time. It started with head coach Brian Schottenheimer calling Pickens out for his lackluster run blocking, and his rapid exit from the Week 8 game was another shining example of how things are moving in a bad direction.
The Cowboys could certainly use a replenishment of draft capital after trading away so much of it in recent years. Dallas is sitting with just 10 picks in the next two drafts, including only four in 2027.
Pickens can get the Cowboys at least one pick back, and maybe two if there is enough competition to acquire his services.
It's more worth it to do that than to hold on to him in what is looking like another lost season for the Cowboys.

title: Cowboys Injury Updates After Week 8 Loss: Joey Porter Jr., Jake Ferguson, Caleb Downs
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys saw three key players deal with injuries during the Week 8 loss to the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday afternoon.
First, tight end Jake Ferguson suffered an ankle injury in the first quarter, and while he did get back into the game after that, Ferguson exited again later on and did not return.
On the defensive side of the ball, safety Caleb Downs suffered a concussion that forced his early exit and cornerback Joey Porter Jr. was in and out of the game throughout with an ankle issue.
Here's what we know about all three players following the game on Sunday.
According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , Ferguson suffered a low-ankle sprain.
"Cowboys TE Jake Ferguson suffered a low ankle sprain Sunday in Arizona, per source," Fowler reported.
That's obviously better than the high-ankle variety, but Ferguson could still miss time depending on the severity. That's not an ideal situation for a Cowboys team that already has an injury at the position with Luke Schoonmaker, who didn't play in Week 8 .
James Mitchell replaced the injured Schoonmaker on Sunday and he now has a chance to see more action next week. If both players are ruled out, we could see highly-touted rookie Michael Trigg get his first game action of 2026.
We don't know the severity of Porter's ankle issue yet, but we do know it's something he has been battling since he joined the Cowboys.
Porter spoke on the injury after the game.
""It's been going on since I got here in the first game against Houston," he said . "It's very frustrating. Today, I just wasn't on a good leg. It's very frustrating to not be able to move how I want to."
Despite his ankle injury, Porter continues to be very effective in coverage after giving up just one reception on two targets for nine yards, per Pro Football Focus . He was limited to just 36 snaps.
There was no update on Downs' concussion after the game.
He'll now begin this coming week in the concussion protocol and that leaves his status up in the air for Week 9.
It goes without saying the Cowboys can ill-afford to lose a player who has been one of the best on the defense this season. If he doesn't play, we might see Cobie Durant in the slot next week.

title: Former Cowboys QB Calls Dallas An Embarrassment After Shocking Loss
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys were the laughing stock of the NFL during Week 8's slate of games. But that's a spot the franchise should be all too familiar with by this point.
The Cowboys suffered an epic collapse in Sunday's 33-30 overtime loss to the Arizona Cardinals at home, falling to 3-5 in the process. Despite leading 27-17 with 2:16 left to play and the Cardinals having just one timeout, the Cowboys found a way to throw the game away in typical fashion.
Even when Arizona's missed extra point at the end of regulation gave Dallas a lifeline and sent the game to overtime, the Cowboys still couldn't win the game after being handed an opportunity on a silver platter. Perhaps a loss was for the best, though, as it puts head coach Brian Schottenheimer one step closer toward being fired , though we can only hope.
Add former Cowboys quarterback Ben DiNucci to the list of people who are dumbfounded by Dallas' consistent incompetence, especially after watching what unfolded in Week 8.
During a TV hit with CBS Sports Network on Sunday, DiNucci ripped into his former team, repeatedly calling Week 8's loss to Arizona "embarrassing."
"This was absolutely embarrassing today. They stink," DiNucci said. "This was, I'm lost for words. Honestly, they have so much talent on both sides of the ball, and year after year, week after week, always see just letdowns from them. And I'm not sure what needs to change."
DiNucci, a former seventh-round pick by the Cowboys in the 2020 NFL Draft, appeared in just three games with Dallas, including one start. He went 23-of-43 passing for 219 yards, no touchdowns and no picks.
He understands the woeful lows that the franchise has been through over the past 30 years and wants to see change immediately.
"This was absolutely EMBARRASSING! They STIINK!" 😳 @B_DiNucci6 reacts to the Cowboys' OT loss to the Cardinals. #scoreboard pic.twitter.com/D6qvPKb6X7
"At some point, the same old, same old in Dallas for the Cowboys, it's not cutting it," DiNucci said. "Something needs to change. Somebody needs to look themselves in the mirror. I don't know who it is, but that was an embarrassing loss for them. They had a 10-point lead with a couple minutes left. They let Arizona drive the length of the field a couple times, tie that thing up. Should have lost in regulation. Ended up losing in overtime, but. But this is embarrassing for the Cowboys. It was embarrassing."
Though some fans have often pointed to DiNucci's lack of NFL production as a reason to ignore any comments he has about the game, a toddler would recognize how much of an embarrassment Dallas has become this season.
Unlike his pro career, DiNucci hit this take right on the money.

title: Brian Schottenheimer Reaches New Level of Delusion With Comment After Cowboys' Week 8 Loss
full_text:
After his team reached a new level of stink after the Week 8 loss to the Arizona Cardinals, head coach Brian Schottenheimer reached a new level of delusion with one postgame comment.
The Cowboys suffered one of the ugliest losses in franchise history on Sunday after blowing a two-touchdown lead in the fourth quarter to one of the worst teams in the NFL.
Saying the defeat was one of the ugliest in franchise history isn't hyperbole, either. According to ESPN's Todd Archer , the 14-point lead the Cowboys coughed up in the fourth quarter was tied for the largest in team history.
It has been clear for quite some time now that Schottenheimer is not the right man for this job , and he's especially not the right guy to get the Cowboys out of the Grand Canyon-sized hole they are currently in.
But Schottenheimer doesn't see it that way. In fact, he had the gall to label himself a "problem solver" after the game.
“There’s only one thing I know how to do, and that’s work. I’m a problem solver," Schottenheimer said.
Schottenheimer's head-scratching comment comes a few weeks after he called himself a "great coach," which was also laughable.
Schottenheimer is a great guy, so this isn't personal, but he just is not a good coach and the numbers prove that. Whether it's Dallas' 10-13-1 record in Schottenheimer's 24 games as head coach or his routinely bad play-calling, the proof is in the pudding.
All of the problems we have seen this team have over the last year-plus never get fixed, so Schottenheimer is anything but a problem solver. Instead, he is very much part of the problem.
Now, it's fair to point out that the defense is the biggest issue the Cowboys have right now and that's not Schottenheimer's side of the ball, but the offense has had plenty of issues, also.
Week in and week out we're watching a unit that has to scratch and claw to put points on the board. Nothing ever looks easy, no matter how many points Dallas scores.
Despite it being abundantly clear to anyone who watches this team play that Schottenheimer should be fired, Jerry Jones continues to stick by Schotty, even after Sunday's loss.
“I made a change, and I don't want to mention it because I'm not proud of it. But I made a change with Wade Phillips there in the middle of the season, and I don't see that here at all," Jones explained after the game, per Ed Werder.
At this point, it's hard to even blame Schottenheimer any longer because it's Jones who is allowing this you-know-what show to continue.
I hate to be the bearer of bad news, but fans know this already, anyway: there is no hope for the 2026 season as long as both Christian Parker and Schottenheimer remain employed.

title: Former NFL Player Calls for Cowboys to Fire Entire Coaching Staff
full_text:
Sunday was a chance for the Dallas Cowboys to get back into the mix for the NFC East title. After winning on the road in Week 7 against the Philadelphia Eagles , the Cowboys hosted the Arizona Cardinals who were just 2-5.
Dallas knew it wouldn't be easy even with Arizona entering this game struggling as the Cardinals were 8-1 against them over the past nine games. They seemed up to the challenge, going into the half with a 17-3 lead and then going up 24-10 in the fourth quarter.
Then, the Cowboys completely imploded and lost 33-30 in overtime . Immediately following the game, there were calls for Jerry Jones to end the experiment with Brian Schottenheimer . However, it's not just Dallas fans who have seen enough. Former NFL wide receiver Jarvis Landry posted on social media following the loss, saying he wants to see every coach in Dallas fired tonight.
I want every coach in Dallas Fired by the time I lay my head on a pillow TONIGHT!!
Landry spent nine years in the NFL after a stellar career at LSU. He played for the Miami Dolphins, Cleveland Browns, and New Orleans Saints. He was never connected to the Cowboys, making his comments incredibly interesting.
It's also rare for players who understand how cruel the business can be to openly call for firings. Landry, who was one of the more cerebral route runners during his time, is clearly unhappy watching what is going on in Dallas.
As soon as the game ended, Jerry Jones was asked about the status of his head coach. He was quick to defend Schottenheimer, saying he has no intention of making a change at this point.
As for Schottenheimer, he says he's disappointed in the way things played out, but he has just one focus which is getting back to work and solving the problems .
“Disappointed. Disappointed in the way we played  in the second half. But I only know how to do it one way, and that’s to work. I’m a worker, I’m a problem solver.”
If we're being honest, it sounds like a broken record at this point. Dallas is just 3-5 this season and is now 10-14-1 in his career. He has an offense full of Pro Bowl players and a defense that was completely remade in the offseason but they continue to go backward.
It's difficult to defend anyone on the staff at this point, but it's not as if there's a better option either. That said, it woud be a real shocker to see Schottenheimer return for a third season.

title: 2 Winners & 5 Losers During Cowboys Ridiculous Loss to Cardinals in Week 8
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys are now 1-9 in their last 10 meetings with the Arizona Cardinals , but this one might have been the most inexcusable loss of the series.
Dallas had a 17-3 lead going into halftime and extended that to 24-10 early in the fourth quarter. Then, they suddenly forgot how to play. They allowed the Cardinals to score 20 points in the final quarter and even failed to capitalize after their defense forced a three-and-out in overtime. In the end, the Cardinals hit a late field goal, escaping with a shocking 33-30 victory .
While the front office wrestles with whether this 3-5 team is salvageable , we can look back at this ridiculous loss and see who stood out as both winners and losers for the Cowboys.
Over the past couple of weeks, Shemar James Sr. has been a more prominent figure in the Dallas defense, and he continues to take advantage. The new green-dot linebacker has been making his presence known and came up with a big turnover on Sunday when he picked off a pass from Jacoby Brissett.
The ball was intended for Elijah Higgins, but was low. As Higgins attempted to make a play, the ball bounced off his hands and landed in the arms of James, who returned it to the Arizona five, setting up the first touchdown of the game.
Luke Schoonmaker wasn't able to play in Week 8, and that allowed James Mitchell to play his first game of the year. He was asked to do more when Jake Ferguson had to leave early due to injury. Mitchell made an impact play when Javonte Williams fumbled the ball at the goal line, which was almost a disaster. They were saved by Mitchell, who landed on the loose ball in the end zone, scoring a touchdown in the process.
George Pickens was held without a catch in the first half and seemed ready to change that on the opening drive in the third quarter in a major way. Pickens took a pass from Prescott 59 yards for a touchdown, but the play didn't count. Tyler Booker was called for holding, which negated the big play. Overall, Booker played well, but this is a play he will want back.
Even with Joey Porter Jr. on this roster, the Cowboys' highest-paid cornerback is DaRon Bland, but he continues to let them down. Arizona was dead in the water in this one until Gardner Minshew began targeting Bland on one play after another.
While Bland wasn't the one to give up the touchdown to Michael Wilson at the end of the fourth quarter, Bland was beaten multiple times by Wilson. His inability to come up with a stop allowed Arizona to force overtime in a game that should have been an easy win for Dallas.
Christian Parker seemed to find something early in this game as the Cowboys were up 17-3. Then, everything fell apart.
Arizona scored 27 points in the second half before hitting the game-winning field goal in overtime. There was no excuse to lose this one and much of the loss falls on Parker, who had no answers for Gardner Minshew and Tyler Allgeier, which isn't exactly an offensive powerhouse.
As bad as Parker was in this game, the Cowboys had a chance to win it in overtime. After forcing a three-and-out, the offense had the ball at their own 29 yard line. Brian Schottenheimer, who boldly called himself a great play-caller recently, managed to lose five yards on three plays before punting it away.
That was the second time the high-powered Dallas offense had a chance to win the game and lost yards. They also recovered an onside kick in the fourth quarter, but went backward and had to settle for a field goal, making it a 30-24 game. Schottenheimer is supposed to be a great offensive mind, but he couldn't pull this one out, despite having multiple opportunities to do so.
While his coaching staff did nothing to help him, this was another game where Dak Prescott was unable to come up with a clutch play at the end. While things weren't going their way, the $60 million quarterback had the ball in his hands in overtime and only needed a field goal to win.
He couldn't pick up any yardage, however, throwing an incompletion on second down followed by a sack on third down. The best quarterbacks in the game make plays when it matters most, which is something Prescott hasn't done consistently this season.

title: Will Cowboys Fire Schottenheimer, Parker? Jerry Jones Weighs in on Possible Coaching Changes
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys sunk to a brand new low in Week 8 by losing to the Arizona Cardinals, 33-30, in overtime.
It's not that the Cowboys lost to the lowly Cardinals because, as we know, that's nothing new , no matter how bad Arizona is. Rather, Dallas sunk to a new low because of how ugly the loss was.
The Cowboys were cruising in the first half of the contest and we actually saw a promising performance from the defense in that span.
But, unfortunately, the Cowboys had to play two halves of football and the second went much differently. The defense reverted back to the pathetic mess it has been all season and the offense just couldn't finish drives to put the game away.
The end result was one of the ugliest losses we've ever seen from the Cowboys — and that's a sky-high bar.
If a loss like the one on Sunday afternoon wasn't enough to get Brian Schottenheimer and Christian Parker fired, no loss will be enough.
When asked about Schottenheimer's job after the game, owner Jerry Jones said he is not going to fire Schottenheimer and instead still has faith in him.
“I made a change, and I don't want to mention it because I'm not proud of it. But I made a change with Wade Phillips there in the middle of the season, and I don't see that here at all," Jones explained , per Ed Werder.
Jerry Jones said he is not considering any kind of coaching changes and said he still has confidence in Brian Schottenheimer.
The plural with "changes" in Archer's tweet suggests that Parker's job is safe, also, which just makes you want to hit your head against the wall.
“None of us are getting it done, and that should be my concern," Jones told reporters .
In a quote that feels straight out of the Twilight Zone, Jones told reporters that "a lot of people let Brian Schottenheimer down" during the game against the Cardinals.
"I will say that a lot of people let Brian (Schottenheimer) down today," Jones said . "And so, for whatever criticism we want to have of Brian, we can all get in line and that was a total, to use a cliche, that was a total team effort out there for us. We have to be, for our fans, better than that when we have our hands on a win and then drop the ball."
That is true because of the pathetic performance of the players in the second half, but Schottenheimer has been letting this team down all season long, and he did so again on Sunday.
As long as Jones continues to cling to two terrible coaches in Parker and Schottenheimer, there is no hope for this team to improve.
And if Jones thinks that some trade is going to be the answer to this team's problems, he's kidding himself. The Cowboys are much more than just one player away from getting on track.
Truth be told, a coaching change probably won't even save this team, but that's really all that's left to try because absolutely nothing else has worked.

title: It's Time for The Dallas Cowboys to Fire Brian Schottenheimer & Christian Parker
full_text:
Thanks for the memories, Schotty.
Not really. Just trying to practice our goodbye message.
The Dallas Cowboys somehow found a way to hit a new low in Week 8's 33-30 overtime loss to the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday, choking away a late lead against -- you guessed it -- backup quarterback Gardner Minshew, who rallied his team to a thrilling victory while Dallas stood there and did nothing about it.
As a result of one of the more embarrassing finishes for the Cowboys in recent memory, it's simply time for Dallas to fire head coach Brian Schottenheimer and defensive coordinator Christian Parker. Forget about potentially sneaking into the playoffs at this point. The New York Giants will win the NFC East anyways since they don't have Schottenheimer leading the way.
Losing games is one thing, but the fashion in which Dallas has routinely come up short this season is beyond comprehension. There's been multiple collapses against less-talented teams.
It's clearly not a talent problem; the Cowboys have a roster full of elite players. The coaching staff is not NFL caliber, and it starts with Schottenheimer and Parker. If Dallas was losing games with a bad roster, there would be more reason for patience, but that's simply not the case.
Jerry Jones loves to hear himself talk. He's the only owner/general manager/team president that routinely meets with the media to spit out word-salad nonsense.
He met with reporters right after Sunday's loss and said that changes to the coaching staff are "not on his mind" and that there's confidence in Schottenheimer.
“We’re not going to get into anything. That’s not on my mind at this time," Jones said, per Jon Machota of The Athletic. " ... I will say that a lot of people let Brian down today."
What exactly have Schottenheimer and Parker shown that makes you feel confident that they need to stay on staff the rest of the season? The offense has not come close to living up to its potential and the defense, well, has been a nightmare.
Dak Prescott deserves better. CeeDee Lamb deserves better. George Pickens deserves better.
If there's one positive, the Cowboys have done a good job of building a roster to get fans excited. Not being able to do anything with it because of an inept coaching staff is football malpractice.
The Cowboys visit a lowly 2-6 Indianapolis Colts team that's coming off a 42-7 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday after cleaning house in the front office last week. If Schottenheimer is still the head coach by kickoff time, the matchup with Dallas will be a good opportunity for the Colts to get right.

title: Sean Payton Reveals Broncos Loved Two Other RBs in Draft Besides Jonah Coleman
full_text:
Jonah Coleman has arrived.
The Denver Broncos' rookie running back has only been active for four games this season. He's actually touched the ball in three of those contests and in each one, he's been a difference-maker.
In his second game since returning from injured reserve, Coleman posted a season-high 104 yards from scrimmage and scored the Broncos' go-ahead touchdown to vanquish the Kansas City Chiefs 28-24. Once again, the rookie out-earned J.K. Dobbins in snap share and touches.
Coleman has momentum, and the spark he has provided the Broncos' offense has been palpable. One play before his touchdown, late in the fourth quarter, the rookie caught a Bo Nix pass and rumbled 51 yards downfield to set the Broncos up on the 5-yard line.
JONAH COLEMAN DOWN TO THE 4 KCvsDEN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/nRd1e0xIhC
It was a huge, explosive play that electrified the Mile High faithful at Empower Field. Suffice it to say, Broncos Country loves its rookie running back.
On the other side of the field, Kansas City's rookie running back also had himself a day, totaling north of 100 scrimmage yards, almost all of which came as a receiver. Johnson scored a 73-yard touchdown on a play where Patrick Mahomes beat the Broncos' blitz, lofting the ball over everyone's heads and into the rookie's hands, who then turned on the jets and rumbled to the house.
With a running back like Kenneth Walker III at the top of the depth chart, Johnson doesn't get many carries, but the Chiefs find creative ways to utilize him. The Broncos met with Johnson as a prospect, but ultimately chose to draft Coleman about a round-and-a-half before Kansas City selected the former Nebraska star.
The Broncos' interest in Johnson during draft season was public, but Payton confirmed it after Sunday's game, complimenting the running back class in the 2026 draft.
“Yes, that’s right... Emmett was one [of the running backs Denver liked]," Payton said post-game. "We just didn’t like two [running backs], but we loved Emmett."
Payton said the Broncos also liked Indiana's Kaelon Black, whom the San Francisco 49ers drafted late in the third round.
"The 49ers drafted one (Black) that we really liked," Payton said. "We felt this was a good running back draft, and I’m not even talking about those guys that went early. The kid from Indiana (Black), the player that Kansas City took, all of those guys have good tape and [are] different type runners, right? Exciting backs that are going to play a long time in this league.”
For what it's worth, Coleman has rushed for 134 yards and two touchdowns in the four games he's been active, with nine receptions for 97 yards. Black has touched the ball in all seven of San Francisco's games, and with the 49ers on bye, he's sitting with 233 rushing yards and one touchdown, with three receptions for four yards.
Johnson has touched the ball in all seven of Kansas City's games, totaling 77 rushing yards, with 14 receptions for 237 yards and one touchdown. Coleman is on pace to obliterate the numbers of Black and Johnson, but both of those rookies are playing behind two of the best running backs in the NFL.
What's so exciting about what the future of Coleman's rookie campaign could hold is that he's become the de facto No. 1 running back in Denver. There's always the chance that Dobbins could wrest back the RB1 duties because Payton likes to ride the hot hand, but the arrow is pointing straight up for Coleman.
Coleman's football IQ and make-up are very unique for a rookie. Crediting his offensive line and teammates for helping to spur his big day and secure a tough win over the Chiefs is only the latest example of the intangible traits that drew the Broncos to him.
Coleman has already caught the clutch-time bug. He's been part of two big fourth-quarter comebacks and without his contributions in those games, including Sunday vs. the Chiefs, the Broncos don't come back to win.
From the locker room after the final gun, Coleman showed his appreciation to Broncos Country and talked about the team's mindset that head coach Sean Payton helped cultivate this past week.
“Coach [Payton] said it was going to be a fourth-quarter game and it’s hard to play at [Empower Field at] Mile High when they got the crowd rocking like how they [were]," Coleman said. "Broncos Country showed up today. It helped us get that win."
Of course, without the Broncos' defense stopping Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs from racing down the field and scoring a touchdown in the closing 1:48 of the game, this one would have shaken out differently. It was another complementary win for the now 6-2 Broncos, and Coleman was thrilled to contribute to it in such a big way .
"It was good to just go out there and punch in the game winner and rely on the defense and allow them to dominate like they’ve been doing all year," Coleman said.
The rookie garnered rave reviews from his head coach and veteran teammates, including Nix. Like Payton, Nix complimented Coleman's explosiveness, burst, and ability to create big plays for a Broncos offense that's — let's face it — still finding its way.
“Jonah played great, ran the ball really tough. He’s explosive when he gets the football," Nix said. "He runs hard, hard to tackle, very quick to the hole and through it. I thought he did a really good job of... He just made the plays that were there. He didn’t let the moment get too big."
The rookie was even doing his part to motivate his veteran teammates and keep their eye on the prize as the fourth quarter approached.
"I just got to give a shoutout to my O-line and my teammates for keeping the confidence up the whole game," Coleman said. "The game didn’t go our way the whole entire game until the fourth quarter. I went up to all the O-linemen and the receivers and the defense [saying],  ‘It’s going to be a four-quarter game,’ like Coach [Payton] said, just to remind them it’s not over. So when the fourth quarter hit, that’s when the spark just lit up in the whole team.”
With how well this kid is playing, it makes you wonder how serious the latest rumors are of Denver's interest in the running back market ahead of the NFL trade deadline, especially Jonathan Taylor in Indy. If the Broncos traded for a player like Taylor, Coleman would take a back seat, and it might affect his development.
For this reason and many others, when it comes to the rumors of Denver's interest in Taylor and other backs on the trade block, I'll believe a move when I see it. The NFL trade deadline is November 10, and the Broncos have one more game until then — a road trip next week to face the Carolina Panthers.

title: Broncos QB Bo Nix Makes NFL History in Week 8 Win Over Chiefs
full_text:
Despite trailing by 11 points in the fourth quarter... despite quarterbacking an offense that converted just 2-of-11 third-down attempts, Nix led the Denver Broncos to a massive 28-24 comeback victory over the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday that shifted the balance of power in the AFC West.
Few Broncos quarterbacks have been able to conjure Mile High Magic with the potency that Nix does. With each week that passes , another record falls, and it was no different in the Broncos' win over the Chiefs that gave them sole possession of first place in the AFC West.
In Sunday's win over the Chiefs, Nix completed his 15th game-winning drive and his 12th fourth-quarter comeback since entering the league in 2024. Both stats lead the NFL over that span.
Nix's 15 game-winning drives and 12 fourth-quarter comebacks are tied for the most by any quarterback in his first three seasons in NFL history. And if the best predictor of future outcomes is past outcomes, he's likely to get at least one more of each before this season is over, pulling into sole possession of those records.
Since Week 7, Nix's confidence has seemingly returned. The Broncos' offense was frustratingly inefficient at times against the Chiefs, but he totaled four explosive passing plays, all to different receivers.
Again, it wasn't always pretty, but Nix did a good job of walking the razor's edge of pushing the ball when there were opportunities while also avoiding turnovers. Against the Chiefs, he went 20-of-32 for 222 yards and two touchdowns.
Nix has been criticized as being too conservative this season, but he has begun to loosen up over the past two weeks. Despite the Broncos' offensive inconsistencies, they've been able to hang in games due to excellent, timely defensive play, and Nix's discretion as a passer.
This was Nix's fifth straight game without an interception. What makes it more impressive, though, is that he's attempted at least 20 passes in each of those games without being picked off.
Now, given how often he passes the ball horizontally or behind the line of scrimmage, we shouldn't be too surprised, but he has been pushing the ball downfield more over the past two weeks. Five straight games without a pick is tied for the second-longest streak in team history, and it's the longest since Case Keenum back in 2018.
Nix has now attempted 164 consecutive passes without being picked off. It's the sixth-longest streak in Broncos history, and it's the second time in his career he's recorded a passing streak of more than 160 straight attempts without an interception.
Overall, Nix is more than satisfied with the win, given how hard they are to come by in the NFL, especially against the Chiefs, but he knows there's plenty of room for improvement.
“I thought the first two quarters were pretty good," Nix said post-game. "We hung in there; we got three scoring drives. Then the third quarter, where we had three three-and-outs, we just didn’t do too well on first and second down. We had too many third downs."
The better the Broncos can start doing on first down, the more proficient they'll become on third down. As rookie running back Jonah Coleman continues to build momentum, perhaps that worm will soon turn; otherwise, it wouldn't be a shock to see the Broncos swing for the fences and trade for a running back — like Jonathan Taylor — they could rely on to create on his own on first and second down.
The most important thing was getting the win, though, especially with the magnitude of Sunday's stakes. The Broncos dethroned the Chiefs as AFC West champions last year, and they're now in the driver's seat when it comes to repeating.
“It means a lot," Nix said of the victory. "That’s a big divisional win for us, obviously—one of our toughest opponents in the division, one of our rivals. They played us really well again, and we just responded this time. That’s just a good football team, and they’re going to give us their best every time, and so we just have to respond well.”
