title: Broncos Had Some Big Winners & Losers in 28-24 Victory Over Chiefs
full_text:
Sean Payton and Bo Nix are undefeated at home against the Kansas City Chiefs, after the Denver Broncos stormed back in the fourth quarter to vanquish their rival and avenge their Week 1 loss.
The Broncos were down 24-13 in the fourth quarter, but once again, they were able to conjure some Mile High Magic and prevail 28-24.
The 6-2 Broncos now take the lead in the AFC West, and their schedule opens up for the next several weeks. The Chiefs still have a couple of not-so-tough games coming out of Week 8, but then they’ll face the worst of their schedule.
The Broncos are poised to run away with the division and repeat as AFC West champions, if they can keep the pedal to the metal from here on out. There’s still a lot of football left to be played this season.
As we romp through the aftermath of this huge divisional victory, let’s break down the Broncos’ biggest winners and losers.
Once again, Nix didn’t play all that well through the first three quarters, but as is his way, he turned it on when it mattered most and came through with some big plays when the chips were down.
Nix fed his playmakers in the fourth quarter, and the Broncos galvanized around him, with several players contributing to this team’s fourth fourth-quarter comeback of the season. Fans can get frustrated with the conservative play and relative inconsistencies, but Nix has now won 20 of his last 23 games.
Does it matter how the sausage gets made, so long as it does? After Nix took some big steps forward last week against the Arizona Cardinals, he played with much-improved confidence against the Chiefs — rising to the occasion given the stakes — and delivered another signature win.
Nix finished 20-of-32 for 222 passing yards and two touchdowns. He also converted a two-point attempt with his arm, connecting with Jaylen Waddle, and rushed three times, though it was for just four yards.
Now that the Broncos are truly through the worst of their hellish first-half-of-the-season gauntlet, look for Nix to take his game to the next level. It’s time to start padding the stats along with the wins in the standings.
Comeback complete for Bo Nix and the @Broncos pic.twitter.com/C0Vc6UtMtW
After returning last week from injured reserve to ignite the Broncos’ ground attack , Coleman once again served as this offense’s spark plug. He didn’t have the most efficient day rushing against the Chiefs’ tough front seven, toting it nine times for 41 yards, but like his quarterback, the rookie saved his best play for when it mattered most.
In the fourth quarter, the Chiefs failed to extend their lead to six points with 2:36 left in the game when Harrison Butker missed a 53-yard field-goal attempt. On the ensuing play, Nix hit Coleman underneath, and the rookie turned on the jets, rumbling 51 yards to the Chiefs’ 5-yard line.
JONAH COLEMAN DOWN TO THE 4 KCvsDEN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/nRd1e0xIhC
Coleman punched it on the next play for the Broncos’ go-ahead touchdown. The rookie just gives the Broncos’ offense an element that J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey haven’t been able to provide.
Coleman’s burst is palpable, as are his want-to and intensity. Coach Payton is going to continue riding the hot hand.
Now, it wasn’t all great, as Coleman did get stuffed several times on the goal line on two different possessions that forced the Broncos to go for it on 4th-&-Goal, but they were the collective plays of the offense and the line, and Nix punched it in with his arm both times.
With the NFL trade deadline coming up on November 10, the Broncos don’t need to make a move for Jonathan Taylor . However, it would be nice to have another weapon in the backfield who can create on his own.
This was only the third game of Coleman’s career in which he touched the ball, and he’s just gaining a head of steam. For that reason and others, I have my doubts that Denver will make a move.
It’s obvious, given what I just wrote and what we all witnessed on Sunday, but Dobbins comes out of this game as a big loser. He said last week that he cares most about winning, but the Broncos signaled a lack of trust in him to make plays and move the chains against the Chiefs.
Dobbins finished with just seven carries for 13 yards, and although he was already being usurped by Coleman before it happened, we didn’t see the veteran much after his brutal eight-yard loss in the second quarter, where he ran backward and paid the price. That cost the Broncos, killing a drive.
With RJ Harvey out on injured reserve for at least the next three games, the Broncos are going to need Dobbins for their running back committee, but Coleman is clearly the guy Payton and company are now counting on to spark the offense. Dobbins simply hasn’t looked the same since returning from his season-ending foot injury last year.
So long as Dobbins can keep his cool and not cause problems as his snap and touch share erode in the face of Coleman’s rise, the Broncos could opt to hold onto the valuable draft capital required to land the likes of Taylor, even though they’ve been linked to him in the rumor mill. I’ll put it this way: I’ll believe a Taylor-to-Denver trade when I see it.
Surtain returned to the field for the first time since Week 4, and boy was it good to see him out there. He finished with eight tackles (seven solo), tied for the second-most on the team, and he defended four passes, allowing three completions for just 20 yards.
Surtain saved a touchdown with an absolutely beautiful diving pass break-up. It would have been nice to see him come away with the near-interception he was close to nabbing, but given that he hasn’t played football for a month, it was a strong return performance.
Outside of a couple of explosive completions to running back Emmett Johnson out of the backfield, the Chiefs’ passing offense was lackluster. Take away Johnson’s 119 receiving yards on three catches, and Patric Mahomes would have passed for just 193 yards.
I don’t know what it is or why, but Engram can’t seem to get on the same page with Nix. The veteran tight end was targeted three times on Sunday, but he was held without a catch.
Engram has kept a strong attitude, focused on all the winning he’s done since joining the Broncos last year, but he’s certainly disappointed with his lack of statistical production. The Broncos have involved him much more in the run game as a blocker, so he’s making his contributions, but the receiving stats aren’t there.
Usually, they’re not there for any other tight end, but against the Chiefs, Nix connected with Adam Trautman for a big 22-yard gain and Nate Adkins for a one-yard touchdown. That’s got to be tough for Engram, but hey, the Broncos won the game, and if he wants it to change, he’s got to step his game up.
Waddle played this game hurt. He’s dealt with a chest injury for several weeks and aggravated it last Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals, but he was a trooper and dressed against the Chiefs .
Waddle was Nix’s most-targeted receiver once again, earning six. He caught three of them for 39 yards and a touchdown, the bulk of which came on a big 35-yard strike over the middle.
Bo Nix scrambles and finds Jaylen Waddle for 35 yards! KCvsDEN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/twsyio2RAC
Nix missed a wide-open Waddle in the third quarter, throwing the ball in the dirt at his feet, just a bit short. But Waddle saw plenty of action, scored a touchdown, and caught a two-point conversion.
Props to the veteran wideout for battling through a painful chest injury to help the Broncos knock the Chiefs down a peg or two and take the divisional lead.

title: 3 Wild Takeaways From Broncos' 28-24 Comeback Win Over Chiefs
full_text:
You simply cannot make this up.
In a thrilling game, the Denver Broncos outlasted the Kansas City Chiefs in the most improbable fashion. Down by 11 points to start the fourth quarter, Bo Nix and the Broncos' offense scored two touchdowns, and the defense came away with a massive sack of Patrick Mahomes on fourth down to seal a 28-24 victory and take sole possession of first place in the AFC West.
My heart is still pounding. My blood pressure is through the roof. And I still cannot believe what we just witnessed.
What did we learn, though? Let's break down this week's key takeaways.
It was frustrating in the second half. Denver's offense went three-and-out on three consecutive drives as the Chiefs started to pull away. But as quickly as the weather changed to start the fourth quarter, so did Bo and the offense.
Nix's performance in the fourth quarter over the course of his career has been nothing but magical. The throw he made to Adam Trautman on the first scoring drive in crunch time was absolutely insane.
This might be the second-best fourth-quarter comeback of Nix's career, behind only the 33-point display he had against the New York Giants last year. The stakes in this Broncos-Chiefs game meant so much more, making it one of the best finishes I have personally witnessed.
Nix finished the game 20-of-32 for 222 yards and a pair of 4th-&-Goal touchdown passes from the 1-yard line.
You may doubt the guy. But don't ever count him out.
The ending of that game was made even more insane due to a couple of explosive gains following the game-winning touchdown run by Jonah Coleman.
But those explosive gains weren't the only ones.
Chiefs rookie running back Emmett Johnson absolutely destroyed the Broncos on Sunday. He had a 73-yard touchdown catch and run on a blown coverage, as well as another 38-yard reception in the second quarter, where he slipped a Justin Strnad tackle.
Johnson was also responsible for the 44-yard kickoff return that set the Chiefs on the last drive of the game.
It wasn't just Johnson. Known Bronco assassin Travis Kelce had a 27-yard reception on the final drive as well.
Denver's defense did a much better job in the tackling department this week against Kenneth Walker III and company, but they nearly lost the game by allowing as many explosives as they did.
Overall, the Broncos' defensive performance was rather impressive. Kansas City finished with 399 total yards, but over 100 of those yards came on two Johnson explosives. The Chiefs only ran the ball for 90 yards as a team, which was a triumph given what they did to Denver in Week 1.
Rumors have been swirling about the Broncos looking to make a move at the running back position heading into the November 10 trade deadline, and it's not hard to see the shift in focus in the running back room as it stands.
Dobbins lost his starting job to Coleman, and it's blatantly obvious. Dobbins only ran the ball seven times for a paltry 13 yards and rarely saw the field in the second half.
Coleman out-carried Dobbins by four totes, looked more explosive in doing so, and the rookie's 51-yard reception to set up his second career rushing touchdown was incredible.
Given the remaining schedule and being in first place in the West, this is the time to make a move. Adding an explosive playmaker who can create for himself should be a key focus this week, and there are more than a few options on the table with Jonathan Taylor , Tony Pollard, and Breece Hall reportedly on the trade block.

title: Broncos vs. Chiefs: 5 Bold Predictions for AFC West Showdown
full_text:
In a day's time, the Denver Broncos could be sitting atop the AFC West . To do that, the Broncos have to beat the Kansas City Chiefs .
If my bold predictions this week are realized, pulling ahead of the Chiefs in the division race is a given. These predictions won't be easy, some more than others, but they're bold for a reason.
Let's grab the crystal ball and dive in.
Nix has only broken 200 yards passing three times this season, and he's thrown for two touchdowns in just one game. He's yet to break 200 yards and throw for more than one touchdown in a single game this season.
Nix gets over that hump against the Chiefs by pushing the ball and hitting some explosive plays . He gets picked off once, early in the game, but bounces back instead of retreating into his safe shell.
Coleman has only played in three games, but he only saw three snaps and no touches in one of them, so it's only really been two games. In both games, the Broncos' coaches trusted the rookie to run out the clock, finishing with 69 yards and 58 yards from scrimmage.
In Coleman's third game of real action, he continues his takeover of the top running back spot and breaks 100 yards from scrimmage.
Patrick Mahomes is currently the least-sacked quarterback in the NFL this season, with only seven. The Chiefs are surrendering the seventh-lowest pressure rate on Mahomes.
He's difficult to sack because of how he moves the pocket and escapes, and quickly gets rid of the ball. Now, Jacoby Brissett was hard to sack for the same reasons, and Denver walked out with three sacks, and his time to throw was faster than Mahomes.
However, at Mile High, Bonitto, Allen, and Roach combine for five sacks on Mahomes, keeping the streak alive.
In his first game back from injury, Surtain nets an interception. I'm not predicting he takes it to the house, but given how he plays, it's possible.
Surtain is due for an interception, and it comes in a huge game with the division lead at stake.
Vance Joseph should start every defensive meeting with 29.8%, as that was the Broncos' missed-tackle rate in the season opener at Arrowhead Stadium. The Broncos had eight players with at least two missed tackles, and both starting linebackers combined for nine.
Suffice it to say, the Broncos' tackling won't be that bad again. They vastly improve it with the home crowd at their back.

title: Potential Fallout of Broncos Placing RB RJ Harvey on Injured Reserve
full_text:
The curious case of Denver Broncos running back RJ Harvey has reached its climax.
Harvey, who reportedly suffered a knee injury during Thursday's practice, has been placed on short-term injured reserve and will miss at least the next four games, the team announced Saturday .
The second-year back had already been ruled out for Week 8 against the Kansas CIty Chiefs.
In corresponding transactions, the Broncos promoted safety Taylor Rapp from the practice squad to the active roster, while also elevating running back Cody Schrader and offensive lineman Gavin Ortega from the taxi squad.
As mentioned, Harvey popped up on the injury report earlier this week with a knee issue; he was limited in practice on Thursday and did not practice Friday. The injury is not considered to be abnormally long-term or season-ending, though severe enough to warrant placement on IR.
Speaking Friday, Broncos head coach Sean Payton failed to disclose an update on Harvey's outlook, saying only, "No status now."
First, the obvious: this further thins out a running back room that previously lost RB Tyler Badie to short-term IR -- a room now presumably led by rookie Jonah Coleman, with fading veteran J.K. Dobbins also slated for a significant workload.
Coleman and Dobbins (and, to a much lesser extent, Schrader) must pick up the slack after Harvey rushed for 87 yards and a touchdown while ranking second on the team in receiving with 25 catches for 217 yards and another score across six games thus far.
“I think I’ve been a broken record just relative to a lot of things offensively and us improving," Payton said Wednesday concerning the run game. "There was obviously a step last week. We have to continue to build on it, different type [of] defense in this game. I think it’s shifting the focus to the technique of where these ends play, the type of front we see. It’s different than the last couple of games.”
Second, there were conspiracy-level theories floating around social media that Harvey wasn't really injured and instead was being kept healthy as part of a pending trade for Colts RB Jonathan Taylor. Those ... can be put to rest.
The Broncos continue to be linked to a blockbuster Taylor acquisition, though if Indianapolis insists on a back being included in the deal, they'll need to settle for Dobbins or Coleman, provided the latter is made available.

title: Broncos' Jonathan Taylor Trade Pursuit May Be Heating Up, Insider Claims
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts have officially put Jonathan Taylor on the trading block, per Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport .
The Denver Broncos are among a handful of teams that have "expressed interest" in Taylor and talks are "active and ongoing," per the report.
Schefter linked the Broncos to Taylor last Sunday morning, and on Friday, NFL On Prime 's James Palmer reported that Denver is " monitoring " the situation in Indy. It now sounds like the Broncos' interest could be much more active.
According to Schefter and Rapoport, the Colts have already received an offer that includes a second-round draft pick and additional compensation. The precedent Indy will surely point to is Christian McCaffrey back in 2022, when the San Francisco 49ers traded a second-, third-, fourth-, and fifth-round pick to the Carolina Panthers to acquire the star running back.
McCaffrey was two years younger — nearly three — than Taylor is now, though. Taylor is older and arguably has far more wear-and-tear on his NFL tires.
But there's no question Taylor still has juice. He's already rushed for 587 yards and eight touchdowns this season, though he's on pace for a career-low 4.2 yards per carry.
Taylor is under contract next year for $15 million and in 2028 for $9.46 million, though his cap numbers for those years is larger, due to the signing bonus the Colts gave him when he agreed to the two-year, $44 million extension they offered before this season started.
That definitely makes the Pro Bowl running back a bit more attractive. The rub certainly wouldn't be Taylor's salary — it would be the compensation required to get him in Denver.
Meanwhile, the Broncos are hoping to see continued signs of life from their running game. There are two games left to go until the November 10 trade deadline, so the team wants to see whether rookie Jonah Coleman can continue to spark the offense as he did last week, and whether veteran J.K. Dobbins can kick things into gear now that he's past the brutal six-game gauntlet of defenses he faced to start this season.
The Broncos recently invested in Dobbins, but they're not tied to him beyond the 2026 season, so if they were to acquire Taylor, they have the flexibility to move on. Plus, the Broncos have made running-back investments in each of the past two drafts, selecting RJ Harvey in the second round last year and Coleman in the fourth round this past spring.
Both Harvey and Coleman have shown flashes of greatness, but if either of them has true RB1 upside, it's the rookie. Coleman has only taking carries in two games this season, but he was impressive in both games and showcased a complete skill set.
If talks are active and ongoing, the Broncos may not have the luxury of waiting until after Week 9 to make a decision on Taylor. The Colts are big-time sellers right now, but it would likely take an extreme turning of events to get the Broncos to spend what it would take to land Taylor.
More likely, the Broncos end up erring on the side of patience with their running backs and ground game. The schedule opens up dramatically in Week 9, and this ground attack could go on a run.
But where there's smoke, there's fire. So we can't rule out the possibility of a Taylor-to-Denver trade. Stay tuned.

title: Broncos Week 8 Injury Report: Final Decisions on Harvey, Waddle
full_text:
The Denver Broncos unveiled their final injury report and game designations for Sunday's first-place home meeting with the Kansas City Chiefs.
Denver will officially be without safety Talanoa Hufanga for another game as he tends to a weeks-long ankle issue. The team also ruled out running back RJ Harvey, who suffered a knee injury during Thursday's practice and was considered limited . Speaking Friday, head coach Sean Payton failed to elaborate on Harvey's status.
Rookie RB Jonah Coleman is slated to see an increased workload aside -- or perhaps ahead of -- veteran starter J.K. Dobbins. Former practice-squad S Taylor Rapp will continue filling in for Hufanga, who could be back for Week 9 at Carolina.
The Broncos listed wide receiver Jaylen Waddle ( chest ), safety Brandon Jones (hamstring), left tackle Garett Bolles (hip), and defensive end Zach Allen (hamstring) as questionable to suit up against the Chiefs. Each player was limited in practice Friday; Jones' injury first popped up Thursday, while Waddle and Allen were upgraded from DNP (Did Not Practice) earlier in the week.
Sai'vion Jones would likely start if Allen were forced to sit. Should Waddle miss Sunday's contest or be limited in any capacity, the Broncos should make a concerted effort to get WR Marvin Mims more involved .
“Sometimes it’s coverage and then it’s trying to find those personnel groupings where we’ve got a number of guys that are healthy and playing well. So hopefully we can find those opportunities," Payton said of Mims on Wednesday.
The team will make a final decision on the questionables at least 90 minutes prior to kickoff on Sunday, when inactives are due.
Denver also listed Mims (ankle), inside linebacker Karene Reid (elbow), defensive tackle Malcolm Roach (neck), and cornerback Patrick Surtain II (ankle) as full participants. None of these players carry designations and will play at Empower Field at Mile High. Surtain is making his return following a three-game absence.
On the other side, Kansas City ruled out defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott, and listed cornerbacks L'Jarius Sneed and Mansoor Delane and defensive end R Mason Thomas as questionable. Wide receiver Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) is expected to play after sitting the last two games.
One of the aforementioned players is quietly an anchor on a defense that's arguably playing the best ball in the league over the last month. That player is Malcolm Roach, who's recorded 20 total tackles, (12 solo stops), 2.5 sacks, and four passes defensed across the first seven games of the season.
Roach, who's in his first year with the Broncos, currently ranks as the 42nd-best interior defensive linemen among 126 qualifiers, according to Pro Football Focus. His 69.4 pass-rush grade is good for 25th.
Payton knows the importance of Roach to his elite defensive unit -- especially so with Allen now nursing his hammy.
“I think I would say this: he does a lot of things well," he said Wednesday. "The other thing as an NFL player, you know exactly what you’re getting that’s very helpful then when you’re putting a gameplan together. Then all the other things with his personality and you guys have been around him, he’s consistent. I think that’s important to find those type of players in your front.”

title: J.K. Dobbins Sets Record Straight on Broncos RB Controversy
full_text:
J.K. Dobbins and the Denver Broncos have obviously heard to rumors over the past week.
Dobbins's body language in the Broncos' 30-16 win over the Arizona Cardinals last week was curious, and after a handful of early carries, the veteran's role gave way to rookie Jonah Coleman in the second half. Dobbins did get a goal-line carry in the second half, which he punched in from the 1-yard line, but aside from that, the Broncos mostly kept him on the bench while protecting a sizable lead.
Dobbins said there was a good reason for that, though. And he clearly doesn't appreciate the rumors that he's unhappy or that there's something greater at work to explain his diminished role last week. We've questioned it here at Denver Broncos On SI , too. We've also noted the rising trade rumors linking the Broncos to Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor.
"We were winning pretty good, right? Weren't we?" Dobbins asked 9NEWS ' Mike Klis on Thursday in a curious exchange from his locker. "Everybody wants me to play 17 games, correct? So can you take that into account before you start saying stuff like that? Because the coaches have a plan."
Dobbins referenced his " pinky promise " with the local press this past summer, a sacred covenant vowing to appear in all 17 games this season. He played the first 10 games of last year before suffering a foot injury in Week 10 that ended his first year as a Bronco.
The Broncos not only re-signed Dobbins, but they also gave him a 4x raise on a two-year, $16 million deal this past spring. What he's saying about the coaches' plan for him holds water; the Broncos want to get a good return on their investment, so in games where they're blowing out an opponent, there's not much reason to expose him to unnecessary wear and tear.
Dobbins still takes pride in coaching the young running backs behind him on the depth chart. Dobbins has looked out for RJ Harvey, and he says that veteran leadership applies to Coleman this year, too.
"This organization has a plan for me, and I'm always there to coach my young guys," Dobbins said. "I've said this from the beginning: RJ is my rookie. And we've got another rookie in Jonah. I'm coaching them to make their plays because I want to see them succeed."
Dobbins assured local reporters that his primary motivation is to win games.
"We were up by a lot," Dobbins said. "I want to win the game, and I also want to win in the playoffs and eventually get to the Super Bowl. So, to say... No, we're winning the game."
If the Broncos were losing games and Dobbins wasn't getting starter touches, it might be a different story, he said. But the Broncos are 5-2 and coming off a brutal initial six-game gauntlet to start this season, and that high level of defensive competition goes a long way toward explaining why he's averaged a career-low 3.3 yards per carry.
"I like to consider myself a pro," Dobbins said. "Now, if we're losing, and I'm not getting the carries, s**t, I'm going to be mad as f***. Sorry, excuse my language. But if we're winning and it's working,"
All three of Denver's top running backs contributed their fair share to last week's road win over the Cardinals. Harvey took a screen pass 52 yards to the house. Coleman led the team with nine rushes for 54 yards, closing the game out with some strong running to keep the clock running, while Dobbins scored his third straight touchdown of the season.
The Broncos have a talented backfield, which is one of the reasons why their rushing offense being ranked 24th entering Week 8 is so mystifying. However, Dobbins said there's a reason for that: the quality of opposing defenses the offensive line and backs have faced.
"I mean, shoot, we've got good running backs," Dobbins said. "When I get out there—I know you guys want to bring up the numbers and me having a lower average than normal, because I always have five yards a carry—like, I just played six great defenses, all in a row."
Dobbins believes that the familiarity that Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike Macdaniel and the Los Angeles Chargers have with him only intensified his struggles against those two defenses. Plus, the Jacksonville Jaguars were interested in signing Dobbins this past offseason, so as a matter of pride, they were focused on not letting him have a big day, in his opinion.
"To think that an NFL coach—the Seahawks coach, I was with him in Baltimore, so he knows me well," Dobbins said. "The Chargers know me well. The Jacksonville Jaguars, they wanted me in the offseason. You think they're just going to let me run it up their tails? No."
Dobbins believes the noise surrounding him and the Broncos' ground game has been "blown out of proportion." As the Broncos' schedule opens up a little bit, his theory about the strength of schedule will be put to the test.
Dobbins gets a Kansas City Chiefs defense this week that's currently ranked 13th against the run, allowing just 99.5 yards per game on the ground. Then he draws the Carolina Panthers, whose defense is in shambles after firing coordinator Ejiro Evero on Friday .
The NFL trade deadline is two days after the Panthers game. Time will tell whether these Taylor trade rumors are smoke or fire, but if Dobbins wants to keep the Broncos from leaning in that direction, he'll have to make some hay over the next two games.
He's healthy, though, and with Coleman helping to shoulder some of the between-the-tackles load, Dobbins has a great opportunity to start turning the ship around. The veteran back believes there's still plenty of season left to get his numbers back up, and while that's true, the Broncos will likely be looking for assurances on that front over the next two weeks because after November 10, they won't have the freedom to make an in-season trade.
"We'll get it back above five (yards per carry)," Dobbins said. "It's a long season. I'm feeling great. The coaches are doing everything to keep me healthy, and when I'm healthy, I think I'm dangerous."
There's a reason the Broncos made Dobbins available at his locker on Thursday. The team may indeed be considering making a move ahead of the deadline, but they apparently wanted to nip the rumors surrounding Dobbins's purported dissatisfaction in the bud.
Dobbins is going to continue to start, but as I wrote earlier this week, if the efficiency isn't there, the Broncos have to be willing to lean on Coleman because the rookie's burst and twitchiness have given the rushing offense an explosive edge that has been completely lacking this season. That's been the case in the two games Coleman has received carries, anyway.
Harvey popped up on Thursday's practice report with a knee injury , so don't be surprised if Coleman again out-earns Dobbins in snap share because he's a more proficient receiver and pass protector. The Broncos have the horses in the backfield, but it's time to get more consistent production out of the group of talented players.
Dobbins may end up with more carries on Sunday against the Chiefs, but if Harvey can't go or is limited because of his injury, look for the Broncos to again rely on their fourth-round rookie.
At the very least, it'll be interesting to see how Dobbins responds against Kansas City after an awkward week. Iron always sharpens iron, but now he has something to prove.
What better way to do that than by having a big day in a game that will decide the AFC West leader at the midway point of the season?

title: Mile High Roundtable Drops its Predictions & Picks for Broncos-Chiefs Rematch
full_text:
The Denver Broncos entered the 2026 with a few prime objectives, the first of which is winning the AFC West.
The Broncos started on the wrong foot in that endeavor, getting blown out by the Kansas City Chiefs in the season opener on national television. However, seven weeks later, the Broncos have been through a gauntlet to open the season, and they've built up a sizable callus through seven weeks of brutal resistance training.
Meanwhile, after starting the season 5-0, the Chiefs just suffered their first loss of the season to the Seattle Seahawks last week — a team the Broncos defeated the week prior. Now, the Chiefs head to Mile High to try to get back on the horse and avoid a two-game losing streak.
The 5-2 Broncos have won three in a row, and after sweeping the Chiefs last year, they're looking to balance the scales this season . A win would give the Broncos the lead in the AFC West and put them on a path to repeating as division champs, especially given Kansas City's remaining schedule.
How will this Broncos-Chiefs rematch shake out? Let's go around the table to see how the Mile High Huddle / Denver Broncos On SI staff envisions this one unfolding at Mile High.
Keith Cummings ( @KeithC_NFL ) 5-2 : After falling flat on their face against the Chiefs in Week 1, the Broncos' revenge mission is timely. Coming off a lopsided defeat against the Seahawks, the Chiefs run into a Broncos' offense that's finally showing signs of life, with quarterback Bo Nix getting loose. On Sunday, the Denver D stuffs the Chiefs' run game, and Nix finds Marvin Mims Jr. to put the game away late. Pick : Broncos 27, Chiefs 21
Chad Jensen ( @ChadNJensen ) 5-2 : The Broncos haven't lost to the Chiefs at Mile High since Sean Payton became head coach. Nix is 2-0 at home against Kansas City, and with his confidence flooding back on the heels of his historic game last week, he takes another step forward in Week 8. With the exception of that Week 1 performance at Arrowhead, Nix usually saves his best play for the Chiefs. In this game, J.K. Dobbins turns in his best performance of the season, alongside Jonah Coleman, as the Broncos' offense galvanizes around its defense. A Wil Lutz field goal seals the win as time expires.
Pick : Broncos 26, Chiefs 24
Zack Kelberman ( @KelbermanNFL ) 5-2 : Last week's game was fairly easy to predict if you've watched this team long enough. For the same reason, however, this week's game is much less so. Will the Broncos avenge their Week 1 blowout or suffer a season sweep to their nemesis in Kansas City? Which squad will show up, the Good Broncos or the Bad Broncos? The angel on my shoulder says the former; the devil says the latter. But I've touched the proverbial hot stove and gotten burned enough over the years, so what's one more time?
Pick : Broncos 20, Chiefs 19
Nick Kendell ( @NickKendellMHH ) 5-2 : It’s hard to predict what the Broncos will do this week with Zach Allen, Jaylen Waddle, and Talanoa Hufanga all injured . This game may come down to which team is healthier. However, I expect a redemptive effort by the Broncos' defense after the embarrassment Kenneth Walker III and the Chiefs put on them in Week 1. It was also against the Chiefs at Mile High when Nix turned the corner last season. Ultimately, it's an ugly one, but a win for Denver against the Chiefs, who lack pop offensively outside of Walker
Pick : Broncos 20, Chiefs 17
Bob Morris ( @BobMorrisSports ) 5-2 : The Broncos were not good in Week 1 but have played better since. Meanwhile, the Chiefs are still a quality team but not a dominant one. I think the Broncos' defense has put its season-opening issues behind them, and the offense is showing improvement. Here's to hoping Nix plays with more confidence, Jonah Coleman makes an impact, and Marvin Mims Jr. steps up again, with the Broncos finding a way to win at home . Pick : Broncos 23, Chiefs 20
Carl Dumler ( @CarlDumlerMHH ) 4-3 : I can't remember the last time a Week 8 game had so much on the line. The winner leads the division and has a very clear path to home-field advantage, in wildcard weekend, at least. Thankfully, this game is in Denver, and that home crowd will be alive and making life very difficult. The Broncos' defense will hold up its end, forcing a couple of turnovers, and making up for Week 1's lackluster showing. The Broncos' offense gets the run game going with Coleman back, and the play-action boot game finally yields some positive plays. The Broncos win a close one on a last-minute field goal. Pick : Broncos 24, Chiefs 21
Lance Sanderson ( @LanceS_MHH ) 4-3 : The Seahawks proved that if you stop Walker, you almost completely neuter the Chiefs' offense. The Chiefs don't have the skill-position players to make you pay on a consistent basis. Denver did a fairly good job of bottling up the Chiefs' run game at the line of scrimmage in Week 1, but couldn't get Walker to the ground due to poor tackling. That won't be the case this time around. Bolstered by arguably the best home-field advantage in the league, I fully expect a rambunctious defensive performance and the Broncos to be in first place in the AFC West on Sunday night. Pick : Broncos 23, Chiefs 16
James Campbell ( @JamesC_MHH ) 3-4 : If the Broncos want to repeat as division champs, this is the game to make it so. The Broncos have been playing better football of late, and Nix certainly looks healthier, but they have fundamental flaws, and the Chiefs are one of the teams best primed to expose them. Moving to Coleman is a welcome change and should provide a shot in the arm for the running game, but the performance of Travis Kelce and Walker against Denver's linebackers key a Chiefs win, as Kansas City finds a way to generate the explosive plays the Broncos do not. Pick : Chiefs 31, Broncos 14
Erick Trickel ( @ErickTrickel ) 3-4 : Nix bounced back against a terrible Arizona Cardinals defense, and the Chiefs are next. Kansas City's defense has struggled this season, so the opening is there for Nix to keep up his play. There's a chance to take the division lead in this one, but can the offense do enough, and can the defense tackle Walker and company? Denver wants to send a message that the first game was a fluke, with a 29.8% missed-tackle rate among other statistical outliers. However, Denver wins thanks to some big-time decisions from Sean Payton late, including going for a two-point conversion after a touchdown.
Pick : Broncos 32, Chiefs 24
Dylan Von Arx ( @DylanVonArxMHH ) 3-4 : The Broncos handled the Cardinals but now must turn their attention to the Chiefs, who embarrassed them to open the season. The Broncos showed more life on offense last week, but Waddle's likely absence means Mims has to step up and contribute. The game being played in Denver may be the difference-maker, and I'm going with the Broncos to take the AFC West lead from the Chiefs' clutches. Pick : Broncos 20, Chiefs 17

title: Lions Provide Jack Campbell Update After Scary Injury
full_text:
The Detroit Lions earned a bittersweet win over the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday, moving their record to 5-2 on the young season.
While it was big for the team to earn a win over a previously unbeaten division rival, many of the players' thoughts after the game were not with the magnitude of the victory but rather the demoralizing injury to linebacker Jack Campbell.
A defensive captain in his fourth season with the team, Campbell is one of the group's biggest leaders. On Sunday, he left the game after suffering a serious injury . He was worked on for several minutes without moving on the Ford Field turf before being placed on a backboard and carted off the field.
Campbell was transported to a local hospital and evaluated for a neck injury. The latest updated was provided late Sunday evening by the organization.
"Jack Campbell is resting and will remain in a local hospital tonight, for continued evaluation and monitoring," a statement from the team read. "The team will provide further updates as we have them."
The injury to the linebacker preceded a massive fourth-down in Sunday's game. On the first snap out of the injury break, defensive end Aidan Hutchinson led the charge in pressuring Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray into an incomplete pass.
Hutchinson was observed bringing his teammates together on the game's TV broadcast, and appeared to share words of motivation for his teammates before the key fourth-down stop.
"I was just, man, it was just a lot of emotions. I got a good rush on that fourth-down. I mean, we're in the huddle, we were more united than we've ever been before that play," Hutchinson said in a postgame interview with Brad Galli. "You go out, and it's a weird dynamic between football being a game and then you snap out of it to see a dude getting carted off and then you're right back in it. Riding that roller coaster, it's a little foreign for sure."
Campbell signed a four-year contract extension that will keep him in Detroit for the foreseeable future  this offseason after an All-Pro season last year. A first-round pick in the 2023 NFL Draft, Campbell has asserted himself as one of the team's biggest defensive stars.
He was one of several players to depart Sunday's game with an injury, as the group also included DJ Wonnum (Concussion protocol), Brian Branch (Concussion protocol), Cade Mays (ankle), D.J. Reed (hip) and linebacker Jimmy Rolder (hamstring).
Detroit continues its season with a trip to Miami to take on the Dolphins next week, followed by a trip to Munich, Germany to play the New England Patriots.
Sports journalist who has covered the Detroit Lions the past three NFL seasons. Christian brings expert analysis, insights and an ability to fairly assess how the team is performing in a tough NFC North division.

title: 6 Winners, 3 Losers From Lions Win Over Vikings
full_text:
On Sunday, the Detroit Lions squared off in their second straight divisional contest, taking on the undefeated Minnesota Vikings.
The Lions faced early issues with discipline and blocking, allowing three sacks alongside two unsportsmanlike conduct penalties in the first quarter alone.
The Lions wore down the Vikings, with the run game taking over the second half and bleeding the clock out to win 19-15.
Here are the winners and losers from the contest.
Reed started the day as a player with a tough assignment , but built on his solid outing against Green Bay with another strong showing against the Vikings.
Reed was whistled for a defensive pass interference on the day, but got the last laugh in the first half by intercepting Kyler Murray.
Unfortunately, his solid stretch came to a screeching halt with a third quarter injury.
Anytime there is a mobile quarterback in the backfield, there is extra stress on the defense. Sure enough, Murray had the capability to escape pressure, and the Lions found themself allowing scrambles.
Gill-Howard was able to net his first full sack of the season, showcasing his speed, something that he has been flashing since the preseason. Gill-Howard’s sack was the sole Lions’ sack of the first half.
Rolder finally got more time on the field Sunday, and he immediately made the most of it with a sack on Kyler Murray on third down, forcing a punt.
That sack came at a crucial time after Jake Bates missed a go-ahead field goal attempt off the upright. Any momentum was destroyed with a two-sack effort on the drive by the defense.
It was a slow start for Gibbs, as was the case for most of the Lions offense. The back was a focal point of the Vikings defense, forcing many of his runs parallel to the line of scrimmage with no running room.
However, in the second half, Gibbs and the Lions came alive, with the back accounting for 53 rushing yards in the first two drives of the third quarter alone. Both put the Lions in scoring position, with one missed field goal followed by Gibbs taking one in for 30 yards. His two-point conversion did not get through the Vikings line, however.
In his first rush of the fourth quarter, Gibbs had a 17-yard burst, making it another 100-yard game.
Gibbs was not the only back making the Vikings pay, as Sione Vaki flexed his muscle in the second half as the Lions run game dominated.
Vaki put together multiple crucial runs, including a pair of 10-or-more yard gains to finish with 65 yards on the day, alongside 5 yards receiving.
McNeill continues to showcase his 2024 form, adding another sack from the middle of the defensive line.
It was a statement game from the defensive line with star Aidan Hutchinson held in check and DJ Wonnum getting carted off in the first half. The interior stood strong and held the Vikings to 81 yards on 18 carries, too.
Anytime the starting assignment opposite a corner is Justin Jefferson, it is a rough outing. On Sunday, McCreary was among the corners facing off with Jefferson, and the corner got bested by the wideout for the Vikings’ opening touchdown.
To be fair to the corner, it was a spectacular catch deflected by Jefferson to himself. That said, the rest of his body of work does not make up for the day he had.
In a surprise twist Penei Sewell finds himself among the losers on the day after an outing that is one to forget. The Vikings pass rush had a prolific day, with early sacks and Andrew Van Ginkel disrupting Detroit at any moment.
Sewell in particular finds himself on the losers bracket after a series with back-to-back false starts securing him a spot in the negatives this week. Sewell was not done for the day on the penalty sheet, being whistled twice more including a holding in the second half.
St. Brown was held in check on Sunday, with only 46 yards on 7 catches, along with a rush for 10 yards.
The receiver could not get separation and it helped make Sunday’s contest into a close one that needed the run game to carry the slack from the passing. St. Brown’s 56 total yards look even worse when a 15-yard first quarter taunting is factored in.
Sports writer since 2022. Emmett Matasovsky started covering the Detroit Lions in 2025. He has extensive experience covering Michigan State Spartans athletics, including MSU basketball and football. Has demonstrated passionate, in-depth coverage of college athletics.

title: Dan Campbell: No New Update on Jack Campbell’s Neck Injury
full_text:
The Lions had a rough day on the injury front Sunday against the Vikings, losing multiple players to physical ailments.
Center Cade Mays, in just his second game of the season, exited the NFC North divisional clash early with an ankle injury. Backup Juice Scruggs, who started the first five games of the season for Detroit, replaced Mays for the remainder of the game.
In addition, DJ Wonnum and Brian Branch collided on a tackle attempt of Vikings wideout Justin Jefferson with 2:57 remaining in the opening half. Wonnum was carted off the field following the collision and failed to return to the game.
Just like Wonnum, Branch did not play another snap following the injury, as he was ruled out for the second half with a concussion. In Branch's absence, rookie Keith Abney II received a healthy dose of reps at safety.
On Sunday, Branch was suiting up for just his second game of the 2026 campaign. In his season debut against the Packers the previous week, he secured an interception on a Jordan Love pass intended for receiver Christian Watson. Plus, he recorded the highest Pro Football Focus overall grade of any Lions defender for the week.
That wasn't the last of the injuries for Dan Campbell's team on Sunday, either.
On the opening play of the fourth quarter, Pro Bowl linebacker Jack Campbell fell straight to the Ford Field turf on a tackle attempt of Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson. Campbell laid motionless on the field for several minutes after the injury, and needed the assistance of multiple medical staff members prior to being loaded on a stretcher and carted off the field.
Per the Lions , the fourth-year linebacker was eventually transported to a local hospital to be evaluated for a neck injury. In his postgame presser, Dan Campbell did not have any additional info regarding the status of the linebacker.
Linebacker Jimmy Rolder, a fourth-round pick of the organization this past April, also suffered an injury on the same play. It came just one down after Rolder dropped Minnesota running back Jordan Mason for a five-yard loss on a second-down run.
Then on the following defensive series, Detroit lost its No. 1 cornerback, D.J. Reed, to a hip injury. The Vikings ended up exploiting the Lions’ banged-up secondary during the series, with Kyler Murray connecting with Jordan Addison on a 51-yard bomb. And Minnesota capped off the possession with an 8-yard TD strike from Murray to Hockenson.
Altogether, the Lions lost five defensive players in the divisional affair.
Additionally, Jacob Saylors suffered a neck injury in the first half and sat out the rest of the Week 8 contest .

title: Key Takeaways From Detroit Lions 19-15 Victory Against Vikings
full_text:
The Detroit Lions were hoping this week to avoid allowing Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores to wreak havoc on the offense.
Entering Week 8, Detroit's division rival had the No. 1 scoring defense in the NFL.
"These offenses are cracking significantly," Dan Campbell said during the week leading up to the Vikings game. "Turnovers, massive turnovers so, it's third-and-32. And that's where they want you, way behind the sticks. So, poise is going to be big for us. Poise, patience. And then our defense has got to step up. We've done a hell of a job these last two weeks. We're going to have to continue to do that because they're problematic on offense as we know. (Kyler) Murray, they brought him in to be the captain of that ship over there, get them in the right play, be steady, reliable, facilitator of the football. And then he certainly still has all that mobility that he's had before.
"You can do everything right for a full game and then just like last week, it's a third-and-8 or whatever, he takes off and it's 30 yards and you're down on the four-yard line. So, he can extend plays, he can extend drives. He's very dangerous that way. (Justin Jefferson) 18, as we all know, is a massive factor. He's a hell of a receiver, highly competitive range, ball skills, it's tough, the whole thing. Nothing new there. I mean, he's just an outstanding football player. (T.J.) Hockenson, his uptick in production here and Murray has found him quite a bit. He's separating, getting open for him."
It was a tough game for the Lions health-wise, as numerous key defenders were injured and departed the contest, prior to the conclusion of the game.
After 60 minutes of action, the Lions advanced their record to 5-2, as they avenged two losses last year to a division rival.
Here are the main takeaways from the Lions' 19-15 win at Ford Field.
After the Lions won the toss and elected to defer, Kelvin Sheppard's defense held firm on the Vikings opening drive.
Will Reichard missed a 57-yard field goal, keeping the game scoreless.
Detroit was able to gain a little momentum on their opening drive , but a taunting call on wideout Amon-Ra St. Brown derailed the drive.
On 3rd-and-13, the Vikings dialed up the pressure and sacked quarterback Jared Goff.
The third-down blitz design dialed up by Brian Flores featured an eight-man that had Jahmyr Gibbs being taken away from a late dropper, Sam LaPorta and Sione Vaki found themselves blocking the same Vikings defender, causing the breakdown and a sack.
Early in the game, the Vikings were quickly able to record three sacks on Goff.
Detroit opened the scoring on their second-drive, as Jake Bates connected on a 25-year-yard field goal.
Detroit landed on the scoreboard first. Jameson Williams was also called for taunting after a 46-yard reception from Goff.
St. Brown secured a 24-yard reception that appeared to be a touchdown, but a review overturned the call, forcing the Lions to settle for a Jake Bates 25-yard field goal.
The former fourth-down pick quickly left the game and headed to the locker room, but was back on the sideline prior to Detroit's next offensive possession.
The Vikings were able to answer quickly, as Kyler Murray led the Vikings on a seven-play, 74-yard scoring drive that took just under three minutes.
On Detroit's next offensive possession, Williams unfortunately slipped, resulting in the veteran signal-caller tossing his first interception of the 2026 season. Vikings cornerback James Pierre was the beneficiary of the first-half gift.
The former No. 1 overall pick did not throw an interception in his previous 231 tosses to start the season. Detroit's defense held the Vikings to a three-and-out.
D.J. Reed picks off Kyler Murray! 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/pfHjURqCbO
After entering the game with the roster fully healthy, the injury bug came for the Lions in the second quarter. Center Cade Mays (ankle), safety Brian Branch (concussion protocol) and defensive end DJ Wonnum (concussion protocol) all exited throughout the quarter.
Wonnum was eventually ruled out for the game at halftime.
The Lions were able to shift some of the momentum working against them, however. Cornerback D.J. Reed pulled in a diving interception with under two minutes to play, giving him nine career interceptions with three coming with the Lions.
Detroit was able to overcome a holding penalty against Penei Sewell to drive into Minnesota territory and cut their deficit to 7-6 at halftime thanks to a 37-yard field goal by Jake Bates.
A scary scene occurred early in the fourth-quarter, as linebacker Jack Campbell was carted off the field after a scary collision with Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson.
In a defensive battle, the third-quarter also saw both teams struggling to move the football.
Following a missed field goal, the Vikings were not able to capitalize. Rookie linebacker Jimmy Rolder earned his first career sack, as Detroit's defense continuously pressured Murray.
On Detroit's next possession, Gibbs was able to scamper to the end zone on a 30-yard run, evading multiple Vikings' defenders.
Unfortunately, the two-point attempt was chaotic and unsuccessful. Gibbs was celebrating on the sideline, but was the intended target on a poorly designed pitch play. After the failed attempt, the Lions took a 12-7 lead in the third-quarter.
Mr. Jahmyr Gibbs pic.twitter.com/48QhRTUVaL
In the fourth-quarter and trailing 15-12, Sione Vaki was able to secure valuable rushing yards in relief of Gibbs.
The inexperienced running back secured 11 rushing attempts for 65 yards (5.9 yards per rush) against a  staunch Vikings' defense.
Goff led the Lions on a seven-play, 69-yard scoring rive after the Vikings briefly took the lead on a Hockenson eight-yard touchdown reception.
Williams capped off the drive with a seven-yard touchdown toss.
1.) It was announced before the game Wu-Tang Clan would be the halftime performance during The Thanksgiving Day Classic this year.
2.) Kicker Jake Bates had his first missed field goal try of the season. Early in the third quarter, Bates missed from 46-yards out after directly hitting the upright.
3.) Rookie defensive lineman Skyler Gill-Howard recorded his first career solo NFL sack against the Vikings.

title: Detroit Lions LB Jack Campbell Carted Off After Scary Collision
full_text:
The Detroit Lions had a roster full of healthy players heading into their Week 8 game against the Minnesota Vikings. However, throughout the game things took a turn for the worst.
After losing four players to injuries in the first half, two more Detroit Lions exited the game early in the fourth quarter. Linebackers Jack Campbell and Jimmy Rolder collided while attempting to make a tackle, and both players remained on the turf.
At the time, the Lions led their division rival Vikings 12-7 early in the fourth quarter. Minnesota would score on their next drive to take a 15-12 lead.
Rolder was helped to the sideline, while Campbell remained down and was being worked on by a number of medical personnel. Medical staff worked on him for a lengthy period of time before he was eventually carted off the field. Lions PR reported that Campbell was being transported to a local hospital to be evaluated for a neck injury.
Meanwhile, Rolder was ruled questionable to return with a hamstring injury. Cornerback D.J. Reed suffered an injury on the following play, and was ruled questionable to return with a hip injury.
Many players on both sides of the field appeared emotional upon Campbell being taken off the field, with defensive captain Aidan Hutchinson calling his teammates together and providing some words in a huddle.
Immediately following the injury, the Lions forced a turnover on downs as they hurried Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray into an incomplete pass on fourth-down. After getting the stop, the Lions' entire defensive unit huddled together on the sideline in support of their injured teammate.
Behind Campbell and Rolder, the Lions have Derrick Barnes, Trevor Nowaske, Malcolm Rodriguez and Amen Ogbongbemiga on the roster at linebacker.
Detroit lost safety Brian Branch (Concussion protocol), defensive end DJ Wonnum (Concussion protocol), center Cade Mays (ankle) and running back Jacob Saylors (neck) all to injuries in the first half of Sunday's game.
Branch and Wonnum both exited after a helmet-to-helmet collision in the second quarter, with Branch walking to the sideline and Wonnum needing to be carted off.
The Lions got off to a slow start in Sunday's game, trailing 7-6 at halftime with their only scoring being a pair of Jake Bates field goal. They did have a touchdown pass from Jared Goff to Amon-Ra St. Brown nullified due to St. Brown being unable to control the ball through landing on the ground.
In the second half, Detroit was able to retake the lead on a 30-yard touchdown run by running back Jahmyr Gibbs.

title: Lions Branch, Wonnum Evaluated For Head Injuries, Mays Leaves With Ankle
full_text:
Detroit Lions center Cade Mays did not take the field with the offense for their second series of the second quarter Sunday against the Minnesota Vikings.
Mays was ruled questionable to return after suffering an ankle injury, according to the team. The Lions trailed the Vikings, 7-3, at the time of his departure. Juice Scruggs, who started the first five games of the season at center, replaced Mays upon his injury.
Later in the first half, safety Brian Branch and defensive end DJ Wonnum had a helmet-to-helmet collision that resulted in both players leaving the game. Branch was able to walk to the locker room, while Wonnum had to be carted off.
Both Branch and Wonnum were downgraded to out prior to the start of the second half. Mays and running back Jacob Saylors would also be downgraded to out in the third quarter.
Rookie Keith Abney II replaced Branch at safety while defensive end Tyler Lacy was the first of Detroit's rotation to enter the game in Wonnum's place. Both players are being evaluated in concussion protocol.
Mays, who signed a three-year contract to join the Lions in free agency, was carted to the locker room after being evaluated in the blue injury tent.
Sunday marked Mays' second game with the Lions, as he suffered a wrist injury in training camp which sent him to injured reserve for the first five battles of the 2026 season.
"Cade Mays, he is questionable to return with an ankle injury," FOX sideline reporter Erin Andrews said during the broadcast. "He made his debut last week against Green Bay, Jared Goff telling us that second week of practice with Mays, he was really helping out with the communication. It felt like the line was jelling, now they're making another change."
In place of Mays, Scruggs had played at a high level manning the pivot position. He earned a Pro Football Focus overall offensive grade of 75.5 in his first five games, along with an 83.7 run-blocking grade.
Detroit got off to a slow start offensively, due in part to some self-inflicted obstacles. A taunting penalty on Amon-Ra St. Brown derailed a positive start to their first drive, while the second drive was interrupted by a touchdown catch by St. Brown being overturned to an incompletion.
The Lions were able to get points on the second drive with a field goal from Jake Bates, but the Vikings answered with a 1-yard touchdown from Kyler Murray to Justin Jefferson.
Lions backup running back Jacob Saylors also suffered an injury in the first half, as he was ruled questionable with a neck injury.
Detroit's offensive line struggled early to contain the aggressive blitzing Vikings defense, as Jared Goff was sacked four times including three times by linebacker Andrew Van Ginkel through their first five possessions.

title: Key Matchup Detroit Lions Must Win Against Minnesota Vikings
full_text:
Jared Goff will face one of his stiffest tests of the 2026 season when he takes on the Minnesota Vikings Sunday.
The Vikings’ defense has been the best unit in the entire NFL in 2026, and especially stout against the pass. In fact, the Brian Flores-coordinated unit has permitted the second-fewest yards through the air (930) and the fewest passing touchdowns (three) through seven weeks. Plus, Minnesota has secured the second-most interceptions (seven), spearheaded by Byron Murphy's league-high three picks.
Murphy should play a pivotal role in the Vikings’ efforts to stymie Goff and the Lions’ air attack in this Week 8 divisional clash.
Murphy, a Pro Bowler in 2024, has been rock solid in coverage this season. He's allowed a passer rating of just 53.5 on balls thrown his way, and for his efforts, he's earned a 69.3 pass coverage grade from Pro Football Focus . It not only ranks as the 20th-best mark among 97 qualified cornerbacks this season, but it also is the second-best PFF coverage grade of his eight-year career.
He and fellow Vikings CB Isaiah Rodgers are expected to receive the lion's share of one-on-one reps with Detroit's dynamic pass-catching tandem of Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams.
Rodgers has been the epitome of a shutdown corner thus far in 2026. The 28-year-old has permitted a passer rating of only 46.3 when targeted by opposing quarterbacks, as well as a measly 4.9 yards per reception. It's a large reason why he's currently PFF's second-highest graded corner when it comes to defending the pass (88.7).
Simply, Rodgers and Murphy have both excelled in coverage through the first half of the 2026 campaign. Yet, it hardly means they're going to be able to shut down St. Brown and Williams on Sunday.
St. Brown is one of the most prolific wideouts in the game today, possessing the ability to beat defenders both over the middle of the field and deep. He's caught 46 balls for 525 yards on the season, and is coming off a monstrous nine-catch, 153-yard receiving game against the Green Bay Packers.
Meanwhile, Williams is one of the league's biggest vertical threats, with the ability to slip past defenders with his game-changing speed . He also had a big day against the Packers last week, with nine catches for 91 yards and two touchdowns.
It wouldn't be surprising to see both St. Brown and Williams end up with a long catch or two going up against Flores’ blitz-heavy scheme .
Subsequently, this matchup between St. Brown and Williams and the aforementioned Vikings CB duo likely favors the Lions – at least slightly.
And all the while, Minnesota will need to do its best to contain Goff. The veteran signal-caller is off to an MVP-caliber start to the season, and has been extremely proficient against the blitz. In fact, he's thrown for 32 first downs, and has accounted for zero giveaways when blitzed in 2026.
Flores, for one, is well aware of the challenge that lies ahead with facing Goff and the Lions’ potent passing game.
“Statistically, he’s been one of the best quarterbacks, not even statistically, period. He’s been one of the best quarterbacks in the National Football League over a good amount of time,” the Minnesota defensive coordinator said of Goff. “And so, yes, he’s grown quite a bit. And that’s what you expect as guys get more time on their belt, see more coverages, see more fronts, see more blitzes. He’s seen all the blitzes. He’s seen them all.
“And so he’s really, I think he’s one of the best in the league. And they’ve got a great skill group, and he knows how to distribute the ball to all of them. And this is a major challenge, (which) certainly (kept) me up (the) last couple nights.”
At this present juncture, I'm willing to predict that St. Brown and Williams both end up with five catches and combine for 125 yards and a score in Sunday's pivotal divisional tilt .

title: Detroit Lions Week 8 Inactives List: Will CB Play Against Vikings?
full_text:
The Detroit Lions have officially released their list of players who will not suit up against the Minnesota Vikings at Ford Field.
Detroit already ruled out safety Kerby Joseph, who was limited at practice all throughout his first week back in action.
Cornerback Roger McCreary is active this week, after being ruled as questionable on the injury designation report on Friday afternoon.
Among those ruled inactive in Week 8 include defensive end Ahmed Hassanein, defensive lineman Mekhi Wingo, safety Bishop Fitzgerald, offensive lineman Seth McLaughlin and tight end Jackson Meeks.
This week, the decision was made not to elevate any players from the practice squad.
Lions head man Dan Campbell expressed his thoughts about the Vikings in the lead up to the NFC North divisional contest.
"Minnesota, playing outstanding football. Kevin (O'Connell)'s doing a hell of a job. (Vikings defensive coordinator) Brian (Flores)'s doing a hell of a job. This thing, they play very complementary football. Everything is fueled by this defense," said Campbell. "That's the starting point. This defense is as good as it gets. They fly around the football. They're smart. I think eight out of these 11 starters for the most part are veteran guys, they're seven years or older and they've been in this system with Flores."
The Vikings have been adept at creating chaos for opposing offensive linemen. As a result, Flores is likely in line to be a head coach again soon.
"The versatility between (Linebacker Blake) Cashman and (Outside linebacker Andrew) Van Ginkel and (Safety Joshua) Metellus and (Safety) Harrison (Smith) and (Linebacker Eric) Wilson just allow them to do a lot. (Outside linebacker) Dallas Turner on the perimeter, (Defensive lineman Jalen) Redmond in the middle among others, they work well together," said Campbell. "And obviously the corner's outside there, (Byron) Murphy (Jr.) and (Isaiah) Rodgers and they roll those other ones. But they understand the system.
"They understand where they're going to exploit you at and then where you're trying to, 'Okay, this is where my outlet is.' They take that away too," Campbell added. "They exploit you and then take away your outlet. They're very good at it and they just create havoc and chaos. And inevitably what they want, and have done consistently, is they force you to make massive errors . It's one thing to get stops. They're forcing offenses, at the end of the day, it gets late. This is a tight game and it's just wave after wave."

title: Setting Lions Fans Expectations for Gibbs, Goff Against Vikings
full_text:
The Detroit Lions ' offense will face its toughest test of the season Sunday against the vaunted Minnesota Vikings defense.
The Vikings will roll into Ford Field with an unblemished 6-0 record, and Sunday's game could have massive divisional ramifications on both sides. A Lions win puts them one game out of first with a leg up currently due to the head-to-head tiebreaker, while a Vikings win puts them three games ahead of Detroit in the loss column.
As a result, there is a legitimate sense of urgency for Detroit to handle business and defeat the Vikings. A big key to that will be the performances of quarterback Jared Goff and running back Jahmyr Gibbs.
Against Brian Flores' defense, which features plenty of blitzes, the Lions could utilize the screen game as one way to get the running back going. Sports Betting Dime's Drew Ellis believes Gibbs is a good pick to go over his projected total of receptions, which is currently set at 4.5.
"The Lions are up against a blitz-heavy defense, so that means Jared Goff is going to have to get the ball out quickly," Ellis told Lions OnSI. "With that in mind, I expect quite a few screens and slants while getting Gibbs lined up in the slot. We’ve seen Gibbs carve up linebackers in the past with his route-running ability and Goff trusts him as a receiver. This season, Gibbs has had at least five receptions in all but one game."
Additionally, he believes that Flores' defensive pressures could get to Goff. The veteran has had some success against Flores in his career, but struggled in the two meetings between these teams last year including on Christmas Day when the Lions turned the ball over five times.
Goff is currently playing some of the best football he's played in his career, and has thrown 14 touchdowns against zero interceptions through six games. Ellis believes that could change Sunday, picking Goff to throw his first pick of the season and go over 0.5 interceptions.
"Jared Goff has been good at avoiding turnovers this season with 14 touchdown passes to 0 interceptions. The law of averages says that has to end at some point," Ellis explained. "Against this blitz-heavy defense, Goff will have to react quick and throw decisively. I think Minnesota will manage to fool him a time or two, which will lead to his first interception of the season."

title: 3 Yards And Cloud of Dust Would Be Dream for Packers’ Worst-Ever Run Game
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The phrase “3 yards and a cloud of dust” to describe a rushing attack goes back at least 70 years. It’s a fitting sentence to lead off a story about the Green Bay Packers’ rushing attack.
One, the Packers’ rushing attack isn’t just bad. It’s historically bad. And, two, coach Matt LaFleur might let his eyebrows grow out of control for a 3-yard rushing average given how the first half of this season went.
The Packers’ ground game is impossibly horrible. With Week 8 almost complete, they’re the worst in the league with 60.6 rushing yards per game and 2.85 rushing yards per carry. The Raiders are next-to-last in both categories with 77.3 yards per game and 2.99 yards per carry.
Packers are averaging 60.6 yards rushing/game and 2.85 yards/carry. That's lowest per carry thru 8 games since 2016 Vikings at 2.71 and lowest per game since 2019 Bengals were at 59.5 The only team in last 80 seasons to be that low in both thru 8 games was Washington in 1961…
It’s not as if they’ve faced a series of powerhouse defenses. On Thursday night, the Packers rushed for 66 yards and averaged 2.54 yards per carry against the Panthers, who were last in the league against the run at the time. A couple weeks earlier, they rushed for 57 yards and averaged 2.19 yards per carry against the Cowboys, who were last in the league against the run at the time and are again after giving up 202 rushing yards against Arizona on Sunday.
Against Carolina, after 13 of their 26 carries gained 1 yard or less, LaFleur was asked if he’d seen anything to make him optimistic about the rushing attack.
“I mean, if I’m being honest, not a lot right now,” he said, “and that’s our job as coaches. We got to figure it out, because it’s not good enough.”
The Packers have gained a league-worst 485 rushing yards in eight games. That’s 77 yards behind Cincinnati, which has played seven games.
Green Bay’s 60.625-yard average equates to 1,031 yards for the season. Unbelievably, that would be the lowest season-ending number for any team since 1961, when the NFL moved to a 14-game season.
And if that’s not enough, going back to 1947 – the year in which the NFL stopped subtracting sack yardage from rushing totals – Green Bay’s 17-game pace would be the second-lowest season-ending number behind the 1947 Boston Patriots, who rushed for 973 yards in 12 games.
The lowest per-game average since 1947 belongs to the 2000 San Diego Chargers, who went 1-15 while averaging 66.4 yards per game. The Packers would have to average 71.6 rushing yards the rest of the season to not set that dubious record.
The Packers’ best rushing game of the season was 86 yards against Tampa Bay in Week 4. That was the debut of a new offensive line, which led to some optimism. So much for that. They haven’t gotten past 70 yards since. In two games with Josh Jacobs, they rushed for 60 yards with a 3.2-yard average against Detroit and 66 yards with a 2.5-yard average against Carolina.
Their eight-game streak of failing to reach 90 rushing yards in a game ranks as the sixth-longest single-season streak since the historically significant 1947 season. The Falcons in 1994 and the Colts in 1990 hold the record with 10. Only the Cols have a longer streak to start a season.
Since 1947, the Packers’ 485 rushing yards are the seventh-fewest for any team in the first eight games of a season. The Packers have a 5-3 record. Those other teams were a combined 6-42; the 2005 Eagles had four wins and four teams had zero wins.
The Packers’ best rushing game this season in terms of yards per carry was their 3.50-yard average against the Jets in Week 2. If that best game represented their season average, they’d be 30th in the league behind the aforementioned Raiders and Packers.
Those are all big-picture numbers. How about from an individual play perspective?
A “run stuff” is a running play tackled at or behind the line of scrimmage. For Green Bay, 24.7 percent of its running plays have been stuffed; only the Raiders (28.0 percent) have been worse. On the other hand, they also have a league-low 11 runs of 10-plus yards; the league median is 20.
On first-and-10, the league average is 4.27 yards per carry. The Packers are last with a 2.39-yard average – an incredible half-yard worse than any other team and 1.14 yards worse than 29 teams. Green Bay averaged 2.64 yards per carry on first down against Carolina, highlighted by Savion Williams’ 18-yarder on an end-around. Otherwise, the other 13 carries gained 19 yards.
From an EPA standpoint, the Packers are 32nd in expected points per carry and 31st in success rate, according to Sumer Sports.
Would the return of Josh Jacobs help save the running game? His eye for the smallest creases and his pile-pushing history suggested that, yes, he would at least get the running game out of neutral.
That definitely has not been the case.
Jacobs carried the ball 21 times for 39 yards against Carolina with a long run of just 6 yards. During the LaFleur era, which started in 2019, it was the fourth-fewest yards in the league by a back with at least 21 carries. (Also, and semi-related, Jacobs caught six passes for 13 yards, giving him 27 touches for 52 yards. It was the fewest scrimmage yards with 27-plus touches in three decades.)
“It wasn’t a lot out there,” he said after the game.
Still, the Packers are 5-3. Dating to the advent of a 16-game season in 1978, only four of the 36 teams that finished with less than 80 rushing yards per game posted a winning record. So, the Packers have been beating the odds.
“I honestly don't know,” Jacobs said if the team’s success without a running game is sustainable. “I've never been in this situation. But I mean it's a lot of hope. I would say that.
“I see the way that these guys work, the way that they’re intentional. We'll go have meetings without no coaches, just the O-line and the running backs, and we go over what we see and what they're thinking and what I'm thinking and the design of the play and little things like that. So, I think it’s only a matter of time before it gets cleaned up.”
Eight games is a large sample size. The Packers’ run game was terrible in Week 1, it was terrible in Week 8 and it was terrible in every game in between.
It was terrible with MarShawn Lloyd and it’s been terrible with Josh Jacobs. It was terrible with Brian Gutekunst’s hand-picked offensive line and it’s been terrible with his veteran additions. There have been six starting offensive line combinations and 11 individual starters. Nothing has made a difference.
With an opportunity to run out the clock against Carolina, the Packers failed. Against a quality opponent in a do-or-die game late in the season, that could end their season. With a stretch of late-season home games, the elements might dictate that the Packers have to run the ball.
Now, with Jacobs’ future perhaps in limbo again , there are additional questions about the state of the rushing attack.
The trade deadline is set for Nov. 10. Trading for Jonathan Taylor , especially with the new uncertainty surrounding Jacobs, could help, but probably not as much as landing a people-moving offensive lineman.
If it’s not the personnel, it must be the coaching. Fortunately for LaFleur, he had three extra days to sort through all the issues. Then again, he had three extra days after the Atlanta game and it didn’t help a bit.
The legendary Vince Lombardi famously said: "Gentlemen, we are going to relentlessly chase perfection, knowing full well we will not catch it, because nothing is perfect. But we are going to relentlessly chase it, because in the process we will catch excellence. I am not remotely interested in just being good.”
At this point, catching mediocrity would be a huge win.
