title: Rams Sunday Morning Notebook: Optimism Grows for Myles Garrett Return, Trade Buzz Heats Up
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are set to play the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 8 at SoFi Stadium. With the Chargers entering with an 0-6 record, it’s an opportunity for the Rams to earn their first back-to-back wins of the season.
Sunday will also be unconventional in the sense that both teams share SoFi Stadium. However, not too much will change for either team. Both teams will remain on their typical sideline and use their own team locker rooms. The only difference is that Chargers coaches who typically sit in the booth will use the visiting team's boxes.
With the trade deadline quickly approaching and Myles Garrett’s injury situation ever-changing, there’s a lot to discuss before Sunday’s game. Let’s get into this week’s Sunday Morning Notebook.
A story that continues to drag on for the Rams is when edge rusher Myles Garrett will finally return to the field. Garrett has been on injured reserve since before Week 2, and the timeline for his return continues to get pushed back. However, on Sunday, NFL Media’s Ian Rapoport reported that the Rams are optimistic Garrett will return to practice for Week 9.
“Once again, there is optimism that Myles Garrett will return to practice this week. I know there was optimism last week, much more this week,” said Rapoport. “He should practice and should be on the field playing relatively quickly.”
From @NFLGameDay Morning: The NFL continues to review #Packers RB Josh Jacobs, as more allegations come to light; Plus, the latest on when Micah Parsons and Myles Garrett could return. pic.twitter.com/KKQp1BWAsS
It’s worth noting that Rapoport reported last week that Garrett would return to practice. There is also a key distinction with this report. Rapoport simply reported that there is optimism for Garrett to return to practice. With Garrett on injured reserve, the Rams have the ability to open his 21-day practice window. That allows Garrett to practice for up to 21 days until the team has to decide to elevate him to the roster.
With that being said, even if the Rams activate Garrett’s practice window, that doesn’t mean he would play next week. Given how safe the Rams have played it with Garrett, they could activate his practice window, see how his knee responds to being back in action, and then proceed from there. That’s not to say that Garrett won’t play next week, but a return after the bye remains more realistic. If the Rams open his 21-day practice window this week, they could wait until ahead of their Week 12 matchup with the Green Bay Packers to activate him.
There is some thought that the Rams could try to trade for a wide receiver. However, things have remained quiet on that front as Les Snead waits for the market to shake out. One name who has been connected to the Rams is Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Josh Downs .
Downs requested a trade from the Colts this week, but according to ESPN’s Stephen Holder , the team would prefer to keep him. While Downs is in the final year of his deal, he is also one of the few healthy targets in the passing game. Alec Pierce has been hurt. If the team deals Jonathan Taylor, Downs would be one of the only playmakers remaining on offense.
Now, that doesn’t mean Downs can’t be had. ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported on Sunday NFL Countdown that the Colts want a third-round pick. Now, that might mean they would take a fourth-round pick, but they don’t appear to be in a rush to trade him.
Also on the wide receiver market, the Jacksonville Jaguars are open to trading Brian Thomas Jr. Thomas is also a player who the Rams have been connected to. There is ongoing belief that the Jaguars will move Thomas by the deadline as his role in the offense continues to decrease.
On Saturday, the Rams elevated kicker Joshua Karty from the practice squad to the active roster, meaning he will play on Sunday against the Chargers. That would give the Rams two kickers active , which is certainly unconventional.
However, given the Rams’ struggles in kickoff coverage, the Rams may use Karty solely on kickoffs. Karty found success with a “knuckleball” kickoff last season, making it difficult for opposing teams to handle kickoffs. With Karty, the Rams allowed a league-best 17.7 yards per return.
The Rams won't want to activate two kickers on gameday all season. Karty only has three eligible practice squad elevations. Ideally, the Rams can activate Karty for the next three games and become comfortable enough with him to eventually take over field goal duties as well. This is certainly going to be a situation to watch, especially as the Rams get healthier going forward and roster spots get more limited. Once that happens, it would be very difficult for the Rams to have two kickers active.
The Carolina Panthers fired defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero on Friday following their loss to the Green Bay Packers. Evero spent five years with the Rams as their safeties coach before being promoted to secondary coach and passing game coordinator.
Evero will be a name to watch for the Rams, especially if Chris Shula ends up getting hired somewhere as a head coach. Shula has led a Rams defense without Myles Garrett to rank 11th in EPA per play and an impressive sixth in EPA per pass allowed. The Rams rank fifth in total defense and sixth in defensive DVOA.
Over the past two years, Shula has garnered head coach interest around the league, and that will likely be the case again this year. If Shula does get hired, Evero will be a top candidate to replace him. It wouldn’t be surprising if the Rams brought Evero back at some point this season as a consultant of some sort.

title: Rams Injury Report: Multiple Key Starters Questionable vs. Chargers in Week 8
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams could be managing several injuries in Week 8 as they take on the Los Angeles Charger s. Center Coleman Shelton, tight end Colby Parkinson, wide receiver Jordan Whittington, and cornerback Trent McDuffie were all listed as questionable for Sunday’s game while long snapper Joe Cardona was listed as doubtful.
Shelton is one of the bigger names on that list given his role as the starting center on the offensive line. Shelton was a non-participant in practice on Wednesday and Thursday, but was upgraded to a limited participant on Friday.
If the Rams are without Shelton, they will turn to backup Dylan McMahon. McMahon has been in the system for the past two years, developing on the practice squad. This is the first year he’s spent most of his time on the active roster.
“What's been good is Dylan McMahon has done a great job this week. He's had a lot of work,” said head coach Sean McVay. “Dylan's had a lot of work this week because of the approach we've taken with Coleman. I think he's handled it really well. He's been here for a handful of years so he would be the guy that would step up.”
Another player the Rams will be closely watching heading into Sunday's game is McDuffie, who has missed the last two weeks with a groin injury. While McDuffie was a limited participant in practice all week, he will be listed as questionable against the Chargers. McVay was hopeful about McDuffie going into Sunday, but the Rams can feel confident with the players behind him as Josh Wallace and Emmanuel Forbes have each played well.
Additionally, Parkinson didn’t participate in practice all week. If Parkinson is out, it would likely leave the Rams with just Tyler Higbee, Davis Allen, and Max Klare at tight end and limit what the offense could do out of 13 personnel. Parkinson is extremely valuable in those formations, especially with his ability as a blocker in the run game.
“He brings a lot,” said offensive coordinator Nate Scheelhaase. “I think he's as good as anybody in the league right now at the point of attack on the line of scrimmage. I think his ability to impact in the pass game has been tremendous. He gives you more than what I think anybody even realizes or expects.”
Popping up on the injury report on Friday was Whittington. McVay noted that Whittington’s back locked up in practice, which is why he’ll be listed as questionable.
On the Chargers’ side, they’ll be without guard Kayode Awosika, safety Derwin James Jr., defensive back Deane Leonard, and wide receiver Brenan Thompson. All four players have been ruled out. Additionally, cornerbacks Donte Jackson and Rodney Shelley will be questionable with hamstring injuries.
The Rams have been managing injuries all season and Sunday will be no different. If the Rams are going to win back-to-back games for the first time this season, they’ll be relying on their depth to get by. Going up against the 0-6 Chargers, the Rams will hope that they can get by another week with key starters injured.

title: Jeffery Simmons Trade Exposes the Biggest Risk Rams Took With Myles Garrett
full_text:
This week, the NFL trade market has heated up significantly. While the Los Angeles Rams made their big moves in the offseason , the Seattle Seahawks traded for Quenton Nelson on Tuesday while the San Francisco 49ers added DeForest Buckner. A day later, the Chicago Bears made one of the biggest trades of the season when they acquired defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons from the Tennessee Titans.
As those teams get the benefit of seeing their big acquisitions take the field immediately, the Rams continue to wait on Myles Garrett. Garrett has spent the last six weeks on injured reserve. After reports surfaced that Garrett would return to practice this week, the Rams declined to activate his 21-day practice window.
Through every passing week, the timeline of when Garrett will actually return only seems to get further away . While Garrett initially had a reported six-week timeline, it now seems unlikely that he will return before the bye week. The Rams are traveling to the east coast next week to play on a grass field in Washington that has historically been lower quality, although upgrades have been made in recent years. The following week, the Rams have a rematch with the Cardinals. It’s possible the Rams may feel they can beat the Cardinals without Garrett.
When the Rams acquired Garrett, they gave up a future first-round pick in 2027, a star edge rusher in Jared Verse, a 2028 second-round pick, and a 2029 third-round pick. That’s a huge haul for a player that has yet to take a healthy snap for the team.
That haul also became the baseline for the Bears’ deal with the Titans for Simmons on Wednesday. Simmons has been an elite defensive tackle in the NFL over the past several seasons, but has been overshadowed on a struggling Titans team.
Detailing how the trade for Simmons went down, Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer looked into previous trades that the Rams had made for Matthew Stafford and Garrett.
“Borgonzi’s research into the Watson, Stafford, Wilson and Hunter deals, had put a ballpark price in his head for what it might take to actually part with Simmons. He told Poles he’d need the Browns’ equivalent they got from the Rams in the Myles Garrett trade,” wrote Breer. “The Rams gave up a 2027 first-round pick, a 2028 second-round pick, a 2029 third-round pick and star rusher Jared Verse for Garrett. Verse’s inclusion, as Borgonzi saw it, is why the 2028 pick was a second-rounder rather than a first. And the third-rounder Cleveland got was two and a half years off, devaluing it a bit.”
The Bears ended up giving away 2027 and 2028 first-round picks in addition to a 2027 fourth-round pick to acquire Simmons. While the Bears gave up a similar package for Simmons that the Rams gave up for Garrett, there is still a big difference in the deals.
On Monday, the Bears will take the field with Simmons as part of their defense. Meanwhile, the Rams are still waiting for Garrett to take a healthy snap after placing him on injured reserve before Week 2,
This isn’t to say that the Rams should have done a trade for Simmons instead of Garrett. For starters, Simmons and Garrett don’t play the same position. The Rams were already good on the defensive line with Kobie Turner,  Braden Fiske, and Poona Ford. Additionally, Simmons had just signed an extension with the Titans in June and likely wasn’t available.
With that said, it does emphasize the risk that the Rams took with Garrett. Over the past few years, when the Rams have made these types of blockbuster trades, they’ve mostly worked out. The trade for Stafford resulted in a Super Bowl win. Jalen Ramsey was an integral part of the secondary. The trade for Brandin Cooks may not have worked out as well, but he played well in 2018.
When the Rams traded for Garrett, they couldn’t have anticipated that seven games into the season, he would have played just once. However, an argument can be made that the Rams got greedy in a sense when they traded for Garrett. The Rams didn’t have a need for a pass rusher, but saw Garrett as an upgrade over Verse . It was a calculated risk, but right now, they are paying the price.
The Rams currently rank 17th in pressure rate at 39 percent and their four percent sack rate ranks 28th. That’s also while blitzing at a 28.1 percent rate, which ranks 15th. Last season, the Rams ranked second in pressure rate and ninth in sack rate with the lowest blitz rate in the NFL.
It’s hard to blame the Rams for making the trade for Garrett. However, given that they didn’t have a need at that spot to begin with, waiting until the season to make a splash might have made more sense.
By trading for Garrett in the offseason, the Rams sacrificed both future draft capital and a young pass rusher who could have continued making an impact on the defense. Instead of having the flexibility to address their needs at the trade deadline, they have been left waiting and hoping that Garrett returns to the field at some point. Right now, that doesn’t seem like a guarantee.
The Bears traded for a healthy Simmons, hoping that he can push them over the hump in a competitive NFC. However, the Bears will have an opportunity to see the impact of their investment immediately while the Rams continue to wait. The Rams took a risk trading for Garrett when they did, and right now, it has yet to pay dividends.

title: Les Snead's Trade Deadline History Reveals When Rams Could Make a Move
full_text:
As the Los Angeles Rams get closer to the NFL trade deadline, the anticipation of whether or not they will make a deal continues to grow. There have been some rumors that the Rams could be interested in a wide receiver. However, after the flurry of moves this week, including trades by three teams in the NFC, two of which were in the NFC West, the Rams stood pat .
It’s possible that the Rams are waiting for the market to take shape and for things to cool down. Les Snead is typically good about waiting for the right opportunity. With exactly 11 days until the trade deadline, Snead has made three trades within that time period. Given his past history, if the Rams make a trade, next week or deadline day appears to be when a move will most likely happen.
Throughout the Les Snead era, the Rams have made four trades on deadline day. However, he’s also made two trades eight days ahead of the deadline and one trade the day ahead of the deadline.
When the Rams traded for Austin Corbett and Jalen Ramsey in 2019, both of those trades landed outside of the 12-day window. In 2021, Snead’s trade for Von Miller happened on the day before the deadline. Meanwhile, when the Rams traded for Roger McCreary last year, it happened eight days ahead of the deadline.
Snead has undoubtedly been one of the more active general managers when it comes to trades ahead of the deadline. Only four general managers have made more trades than Snead and only two have made more trades on deadline day.
If the Rams do make a trade next week, Monday seems like the most realistic scenario. This is typically when the Rams evaluate their roster for the upcoming week. Outside of actual deadline day, which typically takes place on a Tuesday, Snead hasn’t made a trade within the 12-day window later in the week. While the Chicago Bears traded for Jeffrey Simmons on Thursday, that isn't typically when Snead has made his moves. It’s more realistic that he’ll wait until after the game on Sunday.
The Rams will certainly have options at the trade deadline, especially if they are looking at wide receivers . Josh Downs requested a trade from the Indianapolis Colts last week and is expected to get moved. Brian Thomas Jr. is an option as well as he continues to fall out of favor with the Jacksonville Jaguars.
With the wide receiver market as hot as it is, Snead and the Rams may opt to wait to see how things shake out and for the market to cool down. While the lack of a trade this week during the NFC arms race may have been frustrating, it doesn’t mean they won’t still be buyers at the deadline. Snead may simply be waiting for the right opportunity. If the Rams don’t make a trade early next week, they may be waiting until the final days of the deadline given Snead’s history.

title: The Real Reason The Rams Are Keeping Two Kickers on Their Roster
full_text:
Earlier this week, the Los Angeles Rams brought back kicker Joshua Karty after cutting him last season. Karty was just 10-of-15 on field goals last year and 23-of-26 on extra points. He also had four kicks that were blocked.
It’s not a bad idea for the Rams to add a younger kicker on the practice squad. Brandon McManus should help add some stability to the kicking operation as a veteran. However, heading into next season, the Rams would be right back at square one in their search for a kicker.
If nothing else, Karty gives the Rams a young, promising kicker that they can hope to develop. The presence of McManus, a different long snapper, and a new special teams coordinator could be beneficial to Karty. At one point, Karty was a talented kicker. From the end of his rookie season until his two blocked kicks against the Philadelphia Eagles, Karty had made 21 consecutive field goals and was 5-for-5 on kicks of 50 yards or more. If the Rams can get that out of Karty again, it could work out.
For the time being, where Karty may provide some value is on the kickoff unit. The Rams currently rank 31st in average kickoff yards allowed per return. The Rams have allowed an average of 29.7 yards per return, which is only ahead of the Miami Dolphins. Last week, the Rams allowed returns of 36 and 42 yards on their first two kickoffs of the game. It’s something that is continuously eating at head coach Sean McVay.
“We've talked about this a lot and it has to get fixed. It's not good enough and we cannot allow ourselves to do that,” said McVay earlier this week. “I have to figure that out. It's one of those deals that’s driving me crazy. We have to figure it out and we haven't yet.”
At this point, it seems as if McVay is willing to try anything to fix the kickoff coverage unit, which may be partially why the Rams brought back Karty. Last year, Karty led all kickers in fewest yards allowed via kickoff with 17.7. That’s over 10 yards better than where the Rams are currently.
A big reason for Karty’s success on kickoff was his ability to execute a ‘knuckleball’-type kick that made it difficult for the returner to handle. This allowed the Rams’ coverage unit time to get downfield as the returner struggled to handle the ball.
these knuckleball kickoffs are leading to some comical moments of NFL returners looking like the kids in the outfield during the home run derby. pic.twitter.com/G0TeqFjpru
The knuckleball kickoff is something that the Rams executed very well last season. The Rams currently rank last in kickoff DVOA at -8.6 percent. The Rams had the fourth-best kickoff unit last year, ranking fourth. With the overall lack of speed on the coverage unit, the knuckleball kickoff could be a benefit.
Ideally, the Rams would only want to have one kicker activated on gameday. It’s not at all customary for teams to have two kickers active on gamedays. However, until the Rams can trust Karty enough in the field goal operation, it may be their only choice.
“We'll work through those things and just see how the week goes,” said McVay on Wednesday. “When you have 48 bodies and the different guys that are filling in, you have to really ask yourself, 'Okay, does that really make sense? Does it fit?' There are a lot of layers to it.”
A knuckleball kickoff from the LA Rams to start their game against the 49ers 😅 pic.twitter.com/FdLGp9dPO0
Given some of the Rams’ injuries, they do have some flexibility to create space on the 48-man roster. There is a scenario where it could work. Here’s how the gameday roster could look on Sunday against the Chargers:
Quarterback (2): Matthew Stafford, Stetson Bennett Running Back (3): Kyren Williams, Blake Corum, Dean Connors Wide Receiver (6): Puka Nacua, Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, Jordan Whittington, Alex Bachman, CJ Daniels Tight End (3): Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson, Davis Allen Offensive Line (7): Alaric Jackson, Steve Avila, Dylan McMahon, Kevin Dotson, Warren McClendon, David Quessenberry, Beaux Limmer Defensive Line (5): Aaron Donald, Braden Fiske, Tyler Davis, Ty Hamilton, Larrell Murchison EDGE Rusher (5): Byron Young, Josaiah Stewart, Wesley Bailey, Desjuan Johnson, Darryl Peterson III Linebacker (4): Nate Landman, Omar Speights, Shaun Dolac, Grant Stuard Cornerback (4): Trent McDuffie, Jaylen Watson, Josh Wallace, Emmanuel Forbes Safety (5): Quentin Lake, Kam Curl, Kam Kinchens, Jaylen McCollough, Maximus Pulley Special Teams (4): Brandon McManus, Josh Karty, Ethan Evans, Jake McQuaide. Inactives (5): Ty Simpson (Emergency QB), Max Klare, Coleman Shelton (Injured), Bill Murray, Joe Cardona (Injured)
It’s very possible that the Rams wanted Jon Rhattigan to be active for special teams this week after signing him. However, with the injury to Cardona, they’ll need to use one of their two practice squad elevations on McQuaide, leaving the other available for Karty.
While unconventional, it is doable for the Rams to have two kickers active on gameday. Desperate times call for desperate measures, and for the past month, it’s been easy to hear the desperation in McVay’s voice .
The Rams have lost several games this season in which special teams have played a significant role. It’s not something the Rams can just sit back and not do anything in hopes that it gets better. Through seven weeks of the season, that hasn’t been the case. The Rams may not activate two kickers on gameday and simply keep Karty available on the practice squad. However, they have reached a point where they at least have to consider it.

title: Rams Midweek Report: Biggest Trade Deadline Need Has Become Painfully Obvious
full_text:
As the Los Angeles Rams near the trade deadline , it has become increasingly clear that the team needs a WR3. While they primarily operate out of 13 personnel, the Rams still use three wide receiver sets at a 55.9 percent rate. It’s true that they are set to get Davante Adams back in approximately six weeks. However, they still lack depth behind Puka Nacua should he miss more time due to injury.
There comes a point when the Rams have to stop living in the fallacy that Tutu Atwell and Konata Mumpfield are good enough. Last season, the Rams entered the trade deadline with an obvious need at cornerback. In the NFC Championship game against the Seattle Seahawks, the Rams allowed Sam Darnold to throw for 346 yards and three touchdowns.
Throughout the season, it was painfully obvious that the Rams had a need at cornerback. However, the Rams did nothing and it cost them. That’s not a mistake that the Rams can afford to make twice, let alone in back-to-back years.
We can certainly point to times in which Atwell has stepped up. When the Rams were without Cooper Kupp in 2023, Atwell stepped up along with Nacua and played well. Atwell stepped up again in 2024 when his number was called.
However, we can’t keep living in a world from two years ago. The Rams and head coach Sean McVay have let everyone know what they think of Atwell and it isn’t as a WR2 or WR3 in the offense. Despite paying Atwell $10 million that was fully guaranteed, Atwell had six receptions total last season. This year, he has three. It’s clear that the Rams see Atwell as nothing more than a vertical clear-out player. That has value in an offense, but it’s also replaceable.
It’s fine to be hopeful for what Konata Mumpfield can be. However, right now, the Rams have to live in the reality of what he is. Despite being the de facto WR2 last week, Mumpfield had one reception for 15 yards. He has nine receptions for 142 yards on the season with a 42.1 percent targeted success rate.
Jordan Whittington is a great special teams player. With that said, the idea that he’s a Puka Nacua-lite is simply not the reality. Whittington has had opportunities. He has two receptions this season. Whittington has 42 career receptions and 38 percent of those all came during a three-game stretch in his rookie season.
Even prior to Adams getting hurt, the Rams needed a WR3 in the offense that they can rely on consistently to win over the middle. Mumpfield is averaging -0.07 EPA per target and Whittington is averaging -0.24 EPA per target. They are actively detrimental to the offense.
Among 131 wide receivers to run at least 50 routes this season, Whittington’s targeted success rate ranks 119th. Mumpfield’s 42.1 percent ranks 96th. Whittington and Atwell each have 0.05 targets per route, which ranks 130th. Mumpfield’s 0.14 ranks 99th. In yards per route run, Atwell and Whittington both rank inside the bottom-10 while Mumpfield is 95th.
It simply isn’t good enough and won’t be good enough come December and January when the games matter more. The Rams have a clear need at WR3 and if they want to properly compete for a Super Bowl, they’d be right to address it at the trade deadline.
Last week, it was reported that the Rams were exploring options at wide receiver. According to 1st and Tuna , the Rams are expected to be among the teams to make an offer for Jaguars wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr.
It’s unclear exactly what Thomas would cost in a trade. Given his draft status as a former first-round pick and previous production, a second-round pick seems likely. At the same time, if the Jaguars simply want to move on from Thomas and don’t want to bench him, they could be willing to move off of him for less. It’s certainly a situation to keep an eye on over the next week.
Additionally, the Rams are reported to have interest in Josh Downs according to Josh Taylor.
The Raiders, Jags, Patriots, Chiefs, Rams, and 49ers are all interested in Josh Downs per sources.
While Thomas would fit the need as the Rams’ “X” receiver when Adams is out, his fit becomes a lot more complicated after that. Meanwhile, Downs would fit in the offense alongside Adams and Nacua and may only cost a fourth- or fifth-round pick. Downs may have more of a market as teams look to add a wide receiver. We’ll see if the Rams get involved. For now, the interest appears to exist.
There’s no doubt that the Rams have dealt with their share of injuries this season. Their biggest offseason addition hasn’t played since Week 1 and their other big offseason acquisition has missed the last two games. However, it can be easy to get sucked into an echo chamber during the NFL season.
RotoWire recently put together an impact index score to quantify how hard teams have been hit with injuries. The Rams ended up with a moderate score of 4.56, ranking ninth in the NFL in injury impact. However, the Rams have had $67.3 million in cap space out due to injury, which is the fifth-most. Davante Adams and Poona Ford have been the biggest contributors to that with Adams’ $28 million cap-hit and Ford’s $11.4 million.
The Rams can certainly point to injuries as being a reason they are 3-4, but not the sole reason. Every team deals with injuries. The Rams have made enough mistakes independent of injuries that have hurt their record more.
Former Rams running backs coach Ra’Shaad Samples was in municipal court this week in Eugene, Oregon, as he faces charges of DUII and reckless driving stemming from an incident in April. In the incident, Samples hit a parked car and fled the scene. During the court hearing, an added charge of failure to perform your duties as a driver was added as well.
University of Oregon Football Assistant Head Coach Rashaad Samples is currently in Eugene Municipal Court facing DUII & Reckless Driving charges in relation to an April incident where he hit the parked car of local man, Steven Young, and fled the scene.
According to news reports of the hearing, the other driver claimed that Samples was blaring music and eating chips before the incident. The driver also alleged that Samples offered him $1,000 and initially refused to provide his name and insurance information before giving the fake name DeSean Jackson.
A decision was not made, but another court date of December 3 has been set. At that point, the court will decide whether Samples is eligible for DUII Diversion. If Samples were to enter and complete the program, the DUII charge would be dismissed and there would be no criminal conviction.
Samples was the Rams’ running backs coach in 2022 and left before the end of the season. Since 2024, he has been the assistant head coach and running backs coach at Oregon.
To be clear, this is only me speculating. While there had been reports that Garrett would return to practice this week, the Rams opted not to open his practice window . Given that the Rams are in Washington next week, it seems unlikely that Garrett will test his knee on that field. The Rams then play the Arizona Cardinals the following week. The Rams are likely to continue playing it safe. At this point, it’s hard to see Garrett coming back before the bye.
This isn’t to say that I’d be upset if the Rams traded for Thomas or another wide receiver. However, I do believe Downs is the best fit for what the Rams need at the position right now. They don’t have a shifty player that can be used in a variety of ways or create from the slot. In an offensive system with a better quarterback, Downs has the ability to thrive . If the Rams make a move, this is the one they need to make.
The Rams’ run game is at its best when both Blake Corum and Kyren Williams are involved . A big reason the run game got going last week was because of the mixed usage of Corum and Williams. In the weeks prior, it had been mostly Williams. Corum had 17 carries just last week. He had 19 carries in the previous three weeks combined. The Rams need to keep finding ways to get both players involved. Corum’s burst and creativity as a runner add…

title: 3 NFL Trade Deadline Deals the Rams Should Explore Right Now
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are a team who could be buyers at the NFL trade deadline . They have been rumored to be exploring options at wide receiver, but there are certainly other positions where the Rams have needs as well. It seems unlikely at this point that the Rams would make a trade until next week. However, here are three NFL trade deadline deals that the Rams should explore immediately.
Brian Thomas Jr. could certainly be mentioned here as well. Thomas would give the Rams an “X” receiver while Davante Adams is injured. However, Downs wouldn’t cost as much as Thomas and would fit into the Rams’ offense once Adams does return. The Rams are missing a reliable WR3 in the offense who they can trust when they are in 11 personnel. Tutu Atwell and Konata Mumpfield have shown flashes, but they haven’t been consistent. Downs gives the Rams some speed, but more importantly, someone who can create after the catch and create separation with his route-running. With the Colts in a fire-sale situation and Downs requesting a trade, this is a name the Rams should be exploring. Price: 2027 fourth-round pick
Trading for a defensive lineman may not be the preferred move, but it would be a smart one. The Rams do have some depth at the position and will be asking a lot of that depth with the absences of Kobie Turner and Poona Ford. It is expected that the Rams will get Turner back at some point, but Ford is out for the remainder of the season. The Rams are going to miss Ford’s presence in the middle of their defensive line. A’Shawn Robinson is familiar with the Rams and would provide the veteran run-stopping presence that they need. Price: 2028 late-round pick
It’s hard to see the Rams exploring positions outside of wide receiver and defensive line. With that said, it may not be a bad idea to explore edge rusher , and Khalil Mack makes sense. Mack is at a stage of his career in which he wants to play for a contender. The Rams have lacked consistent pressure off the edge without Myles Garrett. While Garrett is set to return within the next few weeks, Mack would still fit the rotation with Josaiah Stewart. Adding Mack would also provide some insurance if Garrett's recovery takes longer than expected. The Rams can't afford to continue struggling to generate pressure off the edge. Price: 2028 late-round pick swap

title: Encouraging, Discouraging Signs for Raiders in Week 8 Win
full_text:
For the first time since Sept. 27, the Las Vegas Raiders have won a game.
In Week 8, the Raiders defeated the New York Jets, 38-33, ending their four-game losing streak. With the trade deadline on Nov. 10, Las Vegas was in danger of being forced into tough conversations about considering selling off pieces. However, this result puts those concerns to rest, for the time being. That said, here are encouraging and discouraging narratives emerging from Sunday's win.
No one has claimed Las Vegas' offense has been the issue during the four-game skid, but there were certainly discussions about swapping Kirk Cousins for Fernando Mendoza. The 38-year-old quarterback quieted those doubts, completing 19-of-26 passes for 247 yards and three touchdowns in the barnburner win.
The rushing attack continues to slog along, as the Raiders took 33 carries for 95 yards (2.9 yards per attempt) and one touchdown. We'll talk about that department in a second.
The second-year running back was usurped by Mike Washington Jr. in Week 8. Washington Jr. outcarried Jeanty 25-2, demoting the former No. 6 overall pick to solely a receiving-down back.
While it's good that Kubiak can rely on the rookie running back, nobody foresaw this situation unfolding the way it has. For the Raiders' offense to reach its potential, Jeanty has to be much better as a runner.
Las Vegas' defense has been an issue all season, failing to contain opposing offenses. That was apparent on Sunday, as the Jets scored 33 points while tallying 290 passing yards and 166 rushing yards.
Right now, the Raiders' only path to victory is to outscore their opponents in shootout environments. As much as Cousins has impressed, this probably isn't how Kubiak wanted this team to operate. Additionally, the front office invested a surplus of resources into the defense through free agency and the draft, and it clearly hasn't paid off yet.
While the offense has been a well-oiled machine, the wide receiver corps has left much to be desired, and the Raiders still lack a true WR1. On Sunday, Jalen Nailor was the only wideout with a single reception, catching four passes for 38 yards and one touchdown.
Las Vegas' passing attack has been heavily dependent on Brock Bowers, Michael Mayer, and Jeanty. Other than them, it's been a revolving door of which wide receiver will produce. Tre Tucker has had a few explosive games, but he failed to record a single reception this week. Assuming Las Vegas doesn't acquire a wideout at the deadline, that position will be one of the top needs this upcoming offseason.

title: Grading Each Raiders Position Group Following Week 8 Win
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders snapped their four-game losing streak with a road win over the New York Jets in Week 8.
Below are the grades for each position group.
Kirk Cousins played a masterful second half against the Jets on Sunday. Cousins finished the first half with 79 passing yards, while completing six of his seven passes. The Raiders entered the half down 23-14.
Then, Cousins and the Raiders' offense rode their best third quarter of the season to victory. In the second half, Cousins completed 13 of his 19 passes for 168 yards and two touchdowns.
That is the type of impactful stats the Raiders need from Cousins while they are still truly competitive in games, not when they are down two or three possessions entering the fourth quarter. Sunday proved that not all stats are the same— timing and context matter greatly.
The Raiders needed more from their ground game, since it had contributed little over the previous four weeks. Starting Mike Washington at running back threw a curveball for the Jets that they could not figure out for four quarters, as Washington paced Las Vegas' offense.
The Raiders leaned on the ground in the second half, running the ball 22 times for 68 yards, compared with 19 passes. Washington's strong second half took a decent part of the workload off of Cousins, allowing him to manage the game properly.
Ashton Jeanty finished the first half with one run and one reception on one target.
However, the burst he displayed on his 45-yard reception in the fourth quarter, which was mostly yards after the catch, showed that giving Jeanty some time off, as they did in the first half, was probably a move worth trying before Week 8 .
Connor Heyward is a chess piece.
Jalen Nailor was the only receiver to catch a pass against the Jets. Nailor and Tre Tucker combined for four catches on five targets. One of those receptions was a touchdown.
It would be a mistake to judge the unit's impact by stats, since Nailor did not have stats when the Raiders signed him this offseason. Instead, notice that Nailor and Tucker open up the offense, especially for the team's tight ends.
Las Vegas' first offensive drive displayed what the Raiders' brass has in mind for the unit long term.
Las Vegas' offensive line only allowed one sack on the day. Through Week 8, the unit has allowed the third-fewest sacks per game in the league. Last season, the unit allowed the most sacks in the league.
The unit also paved the way for a productive day running the ball.
Best group of tight ends in the league.
It was far from pretty, but Las Vegas' defensive line quietly proved it can be effective enough against the run when the team is actually competitive enough in games that opposing offenses cannot run the ball an inflated number of times. In the first half, Las Vegas' defense allowed 140 rushing yards.
Las Vegas entered halftime down 23-14. Then, the Raiders' offense woke up early in the second half, instead of at the start of the fourth quarter, and produced its best third quarter of the season. Las Vegas scored points on its first offensive drive of the second half for the first time this season.
The Raiders' offense also scored more points in the third quarter than it had this season. After scoring three points in the past four third quarters combined, Las Vegas' offense scored 14 points in the third quarter on Sunday.
After allowing an eye-popping 140 rushing yards in the first half, Las Vegas' defense held the Jets to an equally eye-popping 26 rushing yards total in the second half. The Raiders' defense showed what it can do when its offense does its part.
It's almost as if the Raiders' offense scoring points helps the defense, mentally and physically.
Las Vegas' defensive line's improvement against the run allowed Nakobe Dean and Quay Walker to be used properly in ways that fit their respective skill sets.
Sunday's win over the Jets clarified the specific issues plaguing the Raiders' defense. Stopping the run has been an issue, but they've struggled because of the running backs and quarterbacks they have faced in the weeks leading up to Week 8.
With Geno Smith not being nearly as much of a running threat as Patrick Mahomes, Drake Maye, or Josh Allen, Las Vegas' defense eventually focused on stopping running backs out of the backfield rather than a mobile quarterback who is accurate and a talented runner.
Holding the Jets to 26 rushing yards in the second half forced Smith to throw the ball even more. Still, Las Vegas' defensive backfield also tightened up in the second half. Smith finished the first half with a 131 rating. His rating dropped to 64.3 in the second half.
It was far from pretty, but the Raiders' young defensive backfield figured it out just in time. They even sealed the win with an interception.
Dylan Laube's kickoff return for a touchdown was the Raiders' first in 15 years. It was the first time a kickoff had been returned for a touchdown this season in the entire league. That should explain how big of a deal it was. At halftime, Laube had as many points as the Raiders' offense.
Throughout this season, Laube's success, or lack thereof, has directly impacted the Raiders' offense. When he has a productive day returning the ball, Las Vegas' offense generally does well. When he does not have a good day returning kicks, the Raiders' offense struggles.
Kicker Matt Gay also had another strong outing, converting all five extra-point attempts and converting a 53-yard field goal with 31 seconds left, with Las Vegas up by only two points. His field goal forced the Jets' hand, as they needed a touchdown to win.
Without Gay's field goal, the Jets would have been in field-goal range with less than 30 seconds left, only down by two. Gay's eight points were the difference in Las Vegas' five-point win.
Punter AJ Cole continued to prove himself as one of the league's best at his position. Cole averaged over 50 yards per punt against the Jets.
Las Vegas' special teams unit accounted for a chunk of the Raiders' 38 points on Sunday. Hats off to special teams coordinator Joe DeCamillis' unit on a stellar outing.
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: 3 Overreactions to Raiders Ending Winless Skid vs. Jets
full_text:
It wasn't pretty, but the Las Vegas Raiders are back in the win column for the first time since September, ending a streak of 11 consecutive losses in November and a four-game losing streak that lasted all of October.
For the last four weeks, it looked like this week would be the week the Raiders could get back into the win column. Now, they sit at 4-4, still in the thick of things, and may have to win in high-scoring games to have a chance this season. With that in mind, here are some overreactions to Sunday's win against the New York Jets.
Kubiak effectively made rookie Mike Washington Jr. the early-down running back, carrying the ball 25 times for 83 yards, while Ashton Jeanty got most of his work done on third down in pass protection and the receiving game. Instead of Caleb Rogers or Jackson Powers-Johnson, the Raiders started rookie Trey Zuhn III at right guard for the first time.
These moves have made Washington the effective No. 1 running back for the Raiders' offense, regardless of the talent that Jeanty possesses. It's unclear whether Jeanty will get going at any point this season, but for now, Washington is the one to carry the load.
This is the reality of a team committing to a rebuild. If the Raiders were 6-2 fighting for the AFC West lead, I'd be on board with them making a move for a defensive tackle, edge rusher, or defensive back. Yet I don't see this happening, and defensive coordinator Rob Leonard will have to make do with what he has.
There is too much inconsistency in the secondary; the linebackers can find a clear lane to the ball carrier because the defensive tackles are being pushed off the ball and combo-blocked; and the edge rushers opposite Maxx Crosby remain ineffective. No one is saving this defense anytime soon, and Raiders fans will have to deal with it.
This isn't a question for me, no matter how good Trey McBride is in Arizona; Brock Bowers is the best tight end in the game and easily one of the most ridiculous receiving threats in the NFL.
This is a player who missed two games to start the year and is continuing to dominate any linebacker or defensive back covering him, as he added seven catches for 92 yards and two touchdowns against the Jets.
He is impossible to beat at the catch point and is a dangerous threat in the open field. With the way Kubiak deploys Bowers in the passing game, he is a force multiplier on offense.

title: Winners & Losers: Resilient Raiders Refuse To Lose vs. Jets
full_text:
EAST RUTHERFORD, NJ.—The Las Vegas Raiders (4-4) came to Gotham and tamed the New York Jets (2-6) 38-33. 2026 has been nothing short of an overachieving season.
When I made my final regular-season record prediction , I had the Silver and Black pegged at 3-5.
To say this franchise is ahead of schedule under the leadership of Klint Kubiak would be an understatement.
As I sit here in the press box, a lot from this game is percolating in my head, and like I do each night after the game, I'll offer you my winners and losers beyond the score.
Coming into the game, Cousins led the NFL in touchdown passes and ranked third in passing yards.
He was nothing short of sensational today with three more touchdown passes, 247 yards through the air, no interceptions, and, oh, by the way, he ran for another. His QB rating was 141, and he was sensational.
The NFL world so desperately wants to see the No. 1 overall pick that NFL executives ranked as the best QB prospect in the last four drafts, Fernando Mendoza, but Cousins' play won’t allow it.
Kubiak praised his play: “That's who he's been all year. He's been a leader, he's been a playmaker for us, and that's been the story of the season so far. We have a lot of season to go, so we need to clean up the mistakes.”
For Cousins, it wasn’t about his stats; he only wanted to talk about the team snapping a four-game losing skid.
“It’s tough to lose in this league. I think only one other time was I a part of losing four games in a row. It’s hard. It happens, but it’s hard. We’ve played some good football teams, and it took everything we had today. It’s great to get a win, to be .500 in November now and to be playing meaningful football is important. It doesn’t get any easier from here, and we understand the challenge ahead.”
Every week, the rookie Arkansas Razorback Mike Washington Jr. (MWJ) continues to reward the staff for their trust, and he does more and more.
With Ashton Jeanty and the running game struggling lately, he took the lead and didn’t disappoint.
He ran 25 times for 83 difficult yards and looked comfortable and in command, pounding the ball when there was no way to go. Like Steph Curry of the Golden State Warriors, famous for creating his own shot, MWJ created something out of nothing when there wasn’t a hole.
Kubiak was happy for him, but he wasn’t satisfied. “I thought Mike did a good job. He ran hard. I think we took a step forward in that aspect of our game, but it's something that's not a finished product.“
Cousins waxed a little more loquacious for his teammate, and his joy for him was tangible.
“He’s from New York, so he had a ton of family here and friends, and I was really happy for him. He did today what he’s shown us in practice and through camp with the way he ran. We’re going to have to lean on him moving forward a lot, and Ashton as well. Mike did a great job for us today.”
Dylan Laube, the Raiders “Dog,” went wild in front of his family and friends with a kickoff return for a touchdown, an incredible play on a kick out of bounds, a superb special-teams play, and nearly blocking a kick. He may not be that large, but the way he played today makes me wonder if he is the Raiders equivalent of Clark Kent, with a big S under his uniform.
Laube said of his performance, “He’s from New York, so he had a ton of family here and friends, and I was really happy for him. He did today what he’s shown us in practice and through camp with the way he ran. We’re going to have to lean on him moving forward a lot, and Ashton as well. Mike did a great job for us today.”
I asked Kubiak about his special teams weapon, and he was more than willing to praise his performance.
“He's back home, you know, a lot of family here, so it was cool for him to have that moment. Dylan is a stud player for us. He continues to make plays, and as you continue to make plays the expectations continue to rise and he's earned that.”
Cousins was even more verbose. This team loves Laube, and you can count their QB as a fan.
“It’s complementary football. Especially when you go on the road, to be able to have that seven-point gift given to your offense and get the wind at your back makes a big difference. It’s what winning football teams do. There are so many different ways to win in this league. I was really happy for Dylan, like you mentioned, coming back to where he grew up. He had so many people here as well, like Mike, and that had to be a special moment for his family, too.”
The Georgia Bulldog and the best TE in the NFL had seven catches for 92 yards and two touchdowns. He made catches that defied gravity and looked like the superstar that the NFL already knows he is.
Cousins' description of how he played was almost comical, because it sounds so absurd and it is 100% true.
“I think what’s hard is when you play with Pierre Garçon, DeSean Jackson or Justin Jefferson, you’re used to throwing to guys who are really open. There were times, even when they would get doubled and I would progress off of them, and Kevin O’Connell would say to me, ’Still throw it to Justin when he’s covered.' I was like, 'I don’t like throwing to covered guys. I like throwing to open guys.'"
"The coaching point with Brock has been like it was with Justin, where it’s like, when he’s covered, you still need to throw it. That kind of breaks my instincts.”
Cousins continued to explain, “My instincts are to progress and throw to open guys. I think you can see there are moments this year where I can be better, and then there are moments where I’m starting to figure that out. He’s made me right, if you will.”
Even Kubiak, who isn’t usually funny, was in awe. “It surprises me when he doesn't catch it (laughter). That's the truth.”
The Raiders are 4-4. The defense struggled, and we will dissect that and dig into it this week before they head to San Francisco this weekend, but for now, we focus on these four winners.
I will get into some tough discussion on the defense with my report card later in the week, but this team, behind the iron jaw of their first-year coach, didn’t quit. That defense is under the microscope for what is sure to be a less-than-stellar prognosis, but one fact stands out: when it had to, it got key stops. No quit. They may not be great, but they got grit.
Al Davis would have been proud of this win, and that is saying a lot.
Hondo S. Carpenter Sr. is an award-winning sports journalist with decades of experience. He serves as the Senior Writer for NFL and College sports, and is the beat writer covering the Las Vegas Raiders. Additionally, he is the editor and publisher for several sites On SI. Carpenter is a member of the Pro Football Writers Association (PFWA), the Football Writers Association of America (FWAA), and the United States Basketball Writers Association (USBWA).

title: Raiders Stock Report: Risers & Fallers After Thrilling Win Over Jets
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders entered their Week 8 matchup against the New York Jets desperately needing a win. After four straight games against the league's top teams, the Jets were, on paper, the team Las Vegas needed to get back on track after a tough few weeks.
Week 8 was supposed to be a manageable game for a Raiders team that has one of the league's toughest schedules. Las Vegas' road slate against the Jets is sandwiched between games against multiple teams with Super Bowl aspirations.
Las Vegas' offense woke up just in time to pull out a thrilling victory against the Jets on Sunday. Their defense played a solid second half, holding New York to 10 second-half points.
Falling behind early and trying their hardest to come back in the second half is becoming the Raiders' identity. Below are the players who are rising and falling after the Raiders' Week 8 loss to the Jets, their fifth straight loss.
Despite many narratives, Las Vegas' offensive line entered Week 8 in the top 10-15 in several statistical categories. The unit excelled significantly more in pass-blocking than in run-blocking. On Sunday, the unit excelled in both, helping Las Vegas jump out to an early lead.
The unit has its deficiencies, but when it comes to giving the quarterback enough time to throw the ball or escape the pocket and make a play, Las Vegas' offensive line plays well. Las Vegas' ground game was its most efficient in weeks because the line played well overall on Sunday.
Nailor's numbers have not shown the true impact he has on the Raiders' offense. However, Nailor's absence noticeably strained the unit in Week 6. His return made a subtle but significant difference for Las Vegas' offense in Week 7, opening things up, despite his lack of stats.
His impact was even more noticeable on Las Vegas' opening drive, as he registered two catches for 24 yards, which were pivotal in the Raiders' 10-play, 60-yard touchdown drive.
Bowers continues to prove he is the best tight end in the league. The price keeps rising weekly, as Bowers shows he is arguably just as much of a wide receiver as a tight end.
Laube entered Week 8 among the league leaders in kickoff return yards. This forced the Jets into a mistake. On the kickoff following their opening-drive field goal, the Jets kicked the ball out of bounds. This gave Las Vegas the ball at their own 40-yard line. This is the type of starting position the unit needs.
Las Vegas' offense capitalized on the good field position, scoring a touchdown on their first drive. Laube's solid kickoff returns this season immediately impacted the game. Laube helped the Raiders score their first touchdown without even touching the ball.
Then, Laube directly impacted the game by returning a kickoff 95 yards for a touchdown. It was the Raiders' first kickoff return for a touchdown in 248 games. Laube's is a valuable weapon for Las Vegas. The Raiders would not have snapped their losing streak without Laube.
Stokes made two big third-down plays to hold the Jets to a field goal, including on a drive when the Jets had a first-and-goal on the Raiders' five-yard line. Aside from those two plays, the Jets repeatedly targeted Stokes, especially on third-and-short situations.
The Raiders focused first on stopping that aspect of the Jets' offense. However, that left several of Las Vegas' questionable defensive backs in one-on-one situations. Instead of letting their opponent choose, the Raiders picked their poison. It was the passing game.
This was still better than struggling against both the run and the pass, as Las Vegas' defense had done in the previous four games. However, the improvement against the run cost the Raiders through the air, especially Stokes. It simply was not a good outing for the Raiders' best cornerback.
Still, it made more sense for the Raiders to depend on Stokes to figure it out than to switch their defense back into a schematically unfavorable situation.
The rookie looked lost on the Jets' first touchdown. He also could have played better against the run on the Jets' first touchdown after halftime.
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: 4 Instant Observations From Raiders' Comeback Win vs. Jets
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders snapped their four-game losing streak with an impressive comeback win against the New York Jets on Sunday. After falling behind early, as has been the case, Las Vegas used an uncharacteristically productive third quarter on offense to beat the Jets.
Below are my instant observations from the Raiders' outing on Sunday.
Starting rookie running back Mike Washington and making him the team's primary back gave Las Vegas' offense more of a presence on the ground than it had in recent weeks. However, even that was minimal statistically early on, as Washington finished the first half with seven carries for 24 yards.
Las Vegas' offense scored one touchdown in the first half. The Raiders had 97 total yards in the first half.
Still, using Washington as the team's primary back threw the Jets off, as there was no way to prepare. Las Vegas has barely used Washington this season. In the second half, he effectively put the unit on his back, allowing Cousins to stay within his wheelhouse of completing short-to-medium passes.
The depth chart and schematic changes the Raiders made on offense had a direct impact on the game, especially in the second half. The second half against the Jets was arguably the most productive second half Las Vegas' offense has had this season.
The Raiders should have rested Jeanty against the New England Patriots, as it was clear early on that Jeanty had not fully recovered from the injury he suffered shortly before the start of the regular season. However, removing Jeanty completely, regardless of health, significantly hurts Las Vegas.
Las Vegas cannot sit Jeanty for a game, as it puts them at a competitive disadvantage of significant proportions, since Washington is not as effective at catching the ball out of the backfield as Jeanty is. However, the Raiders' coaching staff could effectively rest Jeanty while keeping him active.
At halftime, Jeanty had one rush, one target, and one reception. That is more of a resting than a benching. It may be framed differently by the coaching staff, but they did the right thing by giving Jeanty's body as much of a rest as possible while not hurting the team by sitting him.
Entering the season, the Raiders' defensive backfield vulnerability was well known. Las Vegas' defensive backfield has been an issue for several seasons, long before most of the players currently on the unit arrived. However, the unit itself is also subpar.
Las Vegas entered the season knowing they would need the unit to overachieve in order for the defense as a whole to be productive. Sunday was an ugly day for the unit, one week after an ugly performance against the Los Angeles Rams.
The Raiders lost Darien Porter after only one play. Yet the unit struggled so badly that the issues clearly stem from the group as a whole. The Raiders must aggressively address the unit with additional moves this offseason.
Entering Sunday, the Raiders had scored three points in their past four third quarters combined. Washington accounted for half of the unit's yards on the drive, as Las Vegas rode the young running back into the red zone, where the Raiders capitalized with a touchdown.
It was the first time Las Vegas' offense had scored on its first offensive drive after halftime this season. In seven games, the Raiders scored 26 points in the third quarter. They scored 14 points in the third quarter against the Jets.
It was the most points Las Vegas has scored in the third quarter this season. Their third-quarter success against the Jets confirmed that their third-quarter offensive woes entering Week 8 were a significant issue for the team.
Las Vegas' solid third quarter was just what the team needed, as the Jets' offense kept Las Vegas' defense on its heels for most of the game. Sunday, the Raiders' offense saved its defense. They did so largely with a productive third quarter.
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: What To Expect From Raiders’ Top Offensive Players Against Jets
full_text:
It may be only Week 8, but it feels like the Las Vegas Raiders are already entering a make-or-break game against the New York Jets.
Las Vegas has lost four consecutive games after jumping out to a 3-0 start. Winning those opening games is monumental, as just one more loss and we could be talking about surefire sellers at the trade deadline.
This week's game is a nice buffer for the Silver and Black, who have faced the Chiefs, Patriots, Bills, and Rams during their four-game skid . Meanwhile, New York is coming off an embarrassing loss to the Dolphins. With all that in mind, here are predictions for how the Raiders' top offensive players could perform in Week 8.
Cousins is averaging 36.7 pass attempts per game because Las Vegas has been playing from behind during its current losing streak. That number should drop against the Jets for multiple reasons. For one, New York has one of the slowest-paced offenses. Secondly, with T'Vondre Sweat out and David Bailey doubtful , its defensive line is exploitable. The rushing attack should be better on Sunday. Quite frankly, Cousins throwing fewer passes isn't the worst thing.
That doesn't mean the 38-year-old quarterback has been bad, but his high passing volume stems from the Raiders' poor defense and inability to establish the run. Another reason this is a favorable matchup for Cousins is that New York has forced one interception all season. Operating against a banged-up defensive line and a porous secondary, the 15-year veteran is set up for a bounce-back game.
New York's defensive line, marred by injuries heading into this game, has been well documented. That should open up rushing lanes for Jeanty to explode through. The problem is the Raiders' offensive line has been incredibly disappointing in run blocking.
If the 22-year-old running back doesn't produce on the ground, I'm not sure when he will. In the coming weeks, the Raiders face the 49ers, Seahawks, Broncos, and Browns.
Because of the lackluster run game and lack of a true WR1 on the outside, opposing defenses have doubled or bracketed Bowers essentially the entire game. The Jets will likely copy that approach, but the secondary is a weakness for this defense.
Over the last two weeks, Bowers has compiled 10 receptions for 143 yards, which feels underwhelming compared to what the superstar tight end has produced this season.

title: 3 Jets Players Raiders Defense Must Monitor on Sunday
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders are trying to stop a losing streak and will hope to do so on the road against the New York Jets.
The Jets haven't seen much success in the win column this season, but they are competitive, and this won't be an easy game for Klint Kubiak's squad. More specifically, it won't be easy for Rob Leonard's defense.
New York has been a better offensive team this season than in recent seasons, largely due to the play of former Raider quarterback Geno Smith and star receiver Garrett Wilson. Those two aren't the only players who could give the Raiders fits, though.
Who are some of the notable offensive players Las Vegas will see this afternoon? Let's break down some names to watch.
Since coming off of injured reserve, the rookie first-round pick has been dynamic.
In his last two games combined, Cooper has caught 11 passes for 218 yards and two touchdowns. The Raiders are near the bottom 10 in passing yards allowed per game, meaning Cooper could get loose and continue to be explosive.
The Jets made an effort to give their quarterback playmakers, and the rookie receiver needs to be high on Leonard's priority list. If he stretches the field and makes big plays, Las Vegas could be in trouble.
A fellow rookie first-rounder, Sadiq has flashed at times this season.
His biggest performance came against the Detroit Lions, catching seven passes for 105 yards and a touchdown. The rest of his rookie season has been quiet, but his unique pass-catching talent at tight end makes him a threat for the Raiders.
Las Vegas must be sure it is covering Sadiq and not letting him get free for receptions, because he can create explosive plays after the catch. This is a job for Raiders linebackers Nakobe Dean and Quay Walker.
While he may not catch passes or run for touchdowns, Membou is one of the most important players on the Jets' offense.
According to Pro Football Focus , Membou has only allowed 15 pressures in 254 pass-blocking snaps this season. He hasn't performed as well as he did in his rookie season, but he still looks like one of the premier tackles in the league.
The Raiders have done a good job getting pressure this season, not needing to send the blitz to get home. That will be put to the test against Membou.

title: With Trade Deadline Approaching, Raiders Direction Remains Clear
full_text:
As the Las Vegas Raiders enter Week 8, their four-game losing streak has raised questions about what the franchise could do in nine days when the NFL trade deadline strikes at 4 pm Eastern, 1 pm Pacific.
The Raiders have been in trade rumors for years with franchise edge rusher Maxx Crosby, who was infamously traded to the Baltimore Ravens in March for two first-round draft picks before a failed physical sliced the move entirely.
This time around feels different—not so much in Crosby's case, but in the way general manager John Spytek and head coach Klint Kubiak are building this team.
As a football fan, I find the trade deadline a fun part of the regular season. Two weeks before the deadline, the Indianapolis Colts traded future Hall of Fame guard Quenton Nelson and Pro Bowl defensive tackle DeForest Buckner. The Tennessee Titans traded their franchise defensive tackle Jeffrey Simmons to the red-hot Chicago Bears for two first-round picks and a late selection.
This deadline will be feisty and chaotic, but I don't expect the Raiders to be premier players in this role. It would go against what has been an incredibly disciplined approach to a rebuild; they do not and should not alter that path.
Could Spytek get a similar package for Crosby that they got from the Ravens? Absolutely, but both parties have already mended fences since that trade. Why go through another ordeal of severing ties now for a player who should be a Raider lifer?
Las Vegas could be a buyer at the trade deadline, but I would only anticipate it being for needed depth along the offensive line, defensive tackle, or edge rusher. Other than that, they would be, in theory, sellers to generate more draft capital and stay focused on the commitment to a rebuild. You do not buy significantly in the trade market if you're trying to rebuild a broken foundation that still needs touches.
Since the Raiders would be considered sellers, who would they move, excluding Crosby? The first name that pops up for me is right guard Jackson Powers-Johnson, a former second-round pick who has lost his starting job and is fighting to regain it from Caleb Rogers.
Powers-Johnson could provide aid for a team that needs desperate help along the offensive line, whether at center or either guard spot; the Carolina Panthers and Green Bay Packers make sense, and maybe the Cleveland Browns as they enter the weekend as the NFC North leader.
Another name that I don't think is mentioned enough is Darien Porter, as he and rookie Hezekiah Masses are rotating at cornerback opposite Eric Stokes. The Raiders may want to get their eyes on Jermod McCoy and get tape in that respect, and some teams could use the cornerback depth or a physical outside Cover 3 defender like Porter.
Other than those two names and the rumors that may likely persist around Crosby, the Raiders must maintain discipline in their roster construction approach. That means keeping a talent like Crosby around, but moving a lost asset from a former regime like Powers-Johnson.

title: Announcers, Referees & Jersey Combination for Raiders' Week 8 Matchup
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders will face the New York Jets on Sunday in their first of two consecutive road games. Their Week 8 matchup against the Jets is one of the four road games Las Vegas will play over the next five weeks and is undoubtedly the most winnable game in that stretch.
Las Vegas has lost four straight games, making their matchup against the Jets a quietly important game for Klint Kubiak's Raiders. The game is a true toss-up, as it is unclear which Raiders team will show up on the East Coast on Sunday.
The Raiders have plenty of things to straighten out before Sunday. Kubiak hopes a productive week of practice, combined with the proper adjustments, will help increase his team's ability to execute properly on game day.
“That’s the NFL. Every week you have to respond, and you’ve got to do it 17 weeks in a row. You can’t sit in those chairs in those team meeting rooms if you’re not an accountable human. If you’re just a talented guy who doesn’t have accountability, you don’t last very long. Those are the guys we’re looking for as we build our program,” Kubiak said earlier this week.
The Jets may be 2-5, but they are far from a pushover. New York lost to the Green Bay Packers on the road by three points in overtime. They lost to the New England Patriots by seven, giving New England a much more competitive game than Las Vegas did.
Teams are what their records say they are, but stats and records don't always tell the whole story or provide full insight. Kubiak knows the Jets are better than their record indicates. Las Vegas will have their hands full with a talented Jets team led by a former Raiders quarterback.
“I see an extremely physical team. I see a very talented team. They have our full attention. They’re very well-coached. And no matter who we’re playing each week, on these days, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday, we’d better make sure we’re focusing on ourselves and getting ourselves better," Kubiak said.
Las Vegas will wear white jerseys, silver pants, and silver helmets. John Hussey's officiating crew will referee the game. Megan Olivi will serve as the sideline reporter, while Chris Myers will serve as the play-by-play commentator, and Jonathan Vilma will serve as an analyst.
The Raiders' Week 8 slate against the Jets is a chance to get back on track after losing four straight games. However, a loss would mean the Raiders' front office and coaching staff must make significant changes or accept their fate and watch the ship sink for yet another lost season.
Las Vegas needs to improve in many areas on both sides of the ball. Despite Las Vegas' productive offseason of roster revamping, the Raiders may not be that much better than the Jets. Sunday will confirm whether the Raiders are closer to the four elite teams they have lost to or the Jets.
Earlier this week, Raiders veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins explained how critical each individual play can be in a game. Las Vegas has lost multiple winnable games because of its own mistakes. It will be on Cousins to get the offense going before the fourth quarter on Sunday.
“We can be better in the red zone. We can be better on third down. When plays are there to be made, you’ve got to make them. It’s a fine line between winning a game and losing a game. It can be one play. It can be one throw. You can say, ‘I’m playing great, having good production, things are going well,’ but if you miss one throw and you lost the game, you missed one throw , and you lost the game," Cousins said.
“You play with that tension and you prepare with that tension. I think that's where you say absolutely you can be doing better, because not playing perfect, and the only time you get away with not playing perfect is if you’re winning. Other than that, you either need to be playing perfect or you need to be winning. So, there’s plenty of room for improvement.”
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: Miami Dolphins 2026 Week 8 Snap Counts Stories: Rookie Revelations, Top Guys Emerge
full_text:
What stood out regarding play counts in the Miami Dolphins' 24-19 loss against the New England Patriots on Sunday:
We'll start with the list of inactives, which was highlighted by guard Kadyn Proctor missing the game because of a concussion.
The only Dolphins players who were active but did not play were backup quarterback Kyle McCord and offensive lineman Andrew Meyer.
Since we've been keeping track every game, the starting lineup was back to six rookies with Proctor being out. The six starters were fullback DJ Herman, Will Kacmarek at tight end, wide receiver Caleb Douglas, linebacker Jacob Rodriguez, cornerback Chris Johnson and safety Michael Taaffe.
-- There two things that stand out about the offensive snap counts, both of them involving rookies.
-- While Malik Washington missed a few plays after taking a big hit to the head on a play that resulted in a personal foul flag against New England, Caleb Douglas still looked like he emerged as the No. 1 wide receiver in this game. He played 56 of the 65 offensive snaps, compared to 48 for Washington and Chris Bell also got an elevated role with 45 snaps. That was a big jump from Bell's 31 snaps against the New York Jets in Week 7.
-- Then there was rookie tight end Will Kacmarek, who played only 20 snaps on offense, his lowest total since the season opener after he had dealt with injury issues in training camp. Kacmarek has been on the injury report in recent weeks with a hamstring problem, and if that's the reason his snap count was limited, then maybe the Dolphins need to sit him for a game to get him completely healed. If not, we'd question using him so little when the running game could have used extra blocking help against the Patriots.
-- Kacmarek's usage on offense ended up being the same as Herman, and we just don't understand that — again, barring injury complications.
-- It again was the Ollie Gordon II show at running back, as he played 53 snaps (82 percent) and Jaylen Wright got only eight offensive snaps. Given Wright's lack of production — he's averaging 1.9 yards per rushing attempt this season — it's difficult to argue against the snap distribution here, though the Dolphins might eventually want to take a look at recent waiver wire pick-up Kaytron Allen.
-- Veteran Jalen Tolbert was active but got only six offensive snaps, by far the fewest of any of the wide receivers.
-- Four players were on the field for all the team's 60 defensive snaps — LB Jordyn Brooks, LB Jacob Rodriguez, S Michael Taaffe and CB Chris Johnson. Those were the same four with 100 percent participation against the Jets in Week 7.
-- Josh Uche again led all edge defenders with 48 snaps, with Chop Robinson second with 33. Rookie seventh-round pick Max Llewellyn got only two defensive snaps and didn't play on special teams, and one can't help but wonder why the Dolphins wasted his third and final practice squad elevation for that amount of work. The Dolphins now won't be able to use in another game this season unless they sign him to the 53-man roster.
-- Also note that Llewellyn's low snap count happened even though fellow edge Malik Herring missed some game time because of an injury before returning.
-- The Dolphins went big on about a third of their defensive snaps with at least three of their interior defensive linemen. The snap counts behind Zach Sieler were pretty even between Jordan Phillips, Zeek Biggers and Kenneth Grant, with all of them getting between 27 and 37 snaps.
-- In his second game back after being on IR with a knee injury, rookie Kyle Louis played a season-high 11 snaps on defense in a nickel role.
-- Linebacker Willie Gay Jr., back after missing the Jets game because of illness, played 27 defensive snaps alongside Rodriguez and Brooks.
-- Tackle Chukwuebuka Godrick, who the Dolphins claimed off waivers from the Kansas City Chiefs after the cuts to 53, made his season debut and it consisted of four snaps on special teams.
-- Godrick and Kaytron Allen were among the six non-specialists who saw action only on special teams, along with LB Shaka Heyward, LB Jackson Woodard, CB Reese Taylor and G/T Caedan Wallace.
-- Finally with special teams, rookie Seydou Traore again led the way with 22 snaps, followed by 17 for Julius Wood, followed by 16 each for Louis, Heyward, Woodard and Allen.
