title: Eagles-Commanders SNF: Who Wins and Why in Week 8 NFC East Matchup
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA – For some reason, Eagles-Commanders round two wasn’t flexed to an afternoon game. The NFL decided to keep this matchup between a par of struggling teams, with three wind combined between them in primetime.
The 2-5 Eagles will try to snap a five-game losing streak, while the Commanders will try to win for just the second time this season. They already lost in the season-opener to the Eagles.
Here’s a closer look at the matchups:
The Eagles coach is 10-3 against Washington, including a stomping in the NFC title game two years ago. Sirianni, however, is mired in a five-game losing streak , the team’s longest in his tenure and the longest since the 2016 season when Carson Went was a rookie quarterback.
A loss on Sunday night would be their first six-game losing streak since 2012, when Andy Reid’s team lost eight in a row to finish 4-12. Reid was fired at the end of that season and replaced by Chip Kelly.
The backfield will be manned by a pair of players who signed only recently—Elijah Mitchell, who was with the Eagles in training camp until he was waived injured on Aug. 11 and brought back on Oct. 20, and Jaydon Blue.
Saquon Barkley might play, but last week his hamstring acted up, which led to a back injury, and he played 10 snaps. He was limited in the only practice he participated in this week.
“Obviously, we've been beat up in that room with injuries,” said head coach Nick Sirianni, “but I feel good about the depth and the guys that we have. I was really excited about Elijah throughout camp, and then he got dinged up in camp. Just really glad to have him back."
“Always have liked Jaydon and the things that he can do, going back to watching him coming out of Texas. Feel good about that room. Obviously, a little beat up in that room and looking forward to when we can get guys back, but I'm excited about these guys that are going to go in there and rip it.”
Britain Covey is third in the league in average yards per punt return at 12.6, but the fifth-year pro is battling a knee injury that will sideline him. Makai Lemon stepped up in a pinch last week when Covey went out in the first quarter, but special teams coordinator Michael Clay said Cooper DeJean and Jaydon Blue could also be options.
The defense has been a sieve, giving up 399 yards or more in four straight games. In last Monday’s loss to the Cowboys , they allowed 416 yards, including 204 on the ground, with Javonte Williams shredding them with a career-high 155 yards on 25 carries.
The run defense has slipped to No. 27 in the league. Washington uses a balanced running game, with Jacorey Croskey-Merrick leading the way, with Rachaad White and recently signed Austin Ekeler in the mix. Quarterback Jayden Daniels is also a threat to take off and run. That foursome has the Commanders’ rushing attack ranked No. 9 in the league.
Philly hasn’t been good at getting them, but the Commanders have. The Eagles are the only team in the league that hasn’t recovered a fumble, and they have just three interceptions.
They have turned the ball over six times, five with interceptions. That puts them at minus-3 in the takeaway/giveaway category, which is tied for 21st in the league. Washington has the second-best turnover differential at plus-6.

title: 3 Realistic Dallas Goedert Trade Destinations as Eagles Deadline Buzz Picks Up
full_text:
The Eagles have had an impressive run of homegrown tight end talent. Brent Celek's toughness stood out through 11 seasons in Philadelphia. Zach Ertz's receiving skills helped the franchise hoist its first Lombardi Trophy. Dallas Goedert's versatility has been a pillar of the offense for over eight years.
The party can't last forever, though. Ertz was traded to the Cardinals prior to the 2021 NFL trade deadline, which allowed Goedert to take on a bigger role moving forward. Could a similar move be made in 2026? Goedert is playing on a one-year deal, and rookie Eli Stowers is waiting in the wings .
The Eagles sport a disappointing 2-5 record and are expected to be at least mild sellers at the upcoming trade deadline on Nov. 10. SI's Albert Breer noted Goedert "could be had," alongside other Philadelphia contract-year pros. Here's a look at three realistic trade destinations for Goedert.
Broncos' tight ends have tallied 186 yards and three touchdowns on 19 receptions through seven games. That yardage total trails just the woeful Tennessee Titans for the lowest in the NFL. The trio of Evan Engram, Adam Trautman, and Nate Adkins is not making an impact in the passing attack.
Goedert has posted 228 yards and two touchdowns on 22 catches in five games in 2026. The 31-year-old has logged more than 500 receiving yards in six of his last seven seasons. Elite body control and an ability to rack up yards after the catch serve as the foundation of Goedert's receiving skills.
Goedert with his second TD of the night 👏 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/ytYh8raEz6
Quarterback Bo Nix could use another reliable target. He is averaging 181.6 passing yards per game, which is nowhere near his 231.2 average last season. Denver is projected to have multiple fourth-round picks in 2027. Offering one to the Eagles could sway Philly general manager Howie Roseman.
The Bears have emerged as a tight end trade destination, but it's not because of Colston Loveland's underwhelming performances. Cole Kmet suffered a season-ending knee injury in Week 7. Kmet had played 62% of the offensive snaps, as head coach Ben Johnson regularly utilizes two-tight-end sets.
Kmet's injury leaves Sam Roush as the only healthy tight end behind Loveland. The rookie out of Stanford has been playing over a dozen offensive snaps a game as a run-blocker. It'd be a lot to ask of him to take over Kmet's receiving role. That's where someone like Goedert would come in handy.
Goedert has the pace to run vertical routes and the quickness to run in-breaking routes. That's in addition to his physicality as a run-blocker. Johnson can use that flexibility to his advantage. Chicago has already been aggressive , acquiring defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. Goedert could be next.
Cincinnati tight end Mike Gesicki has been a red-zone monster in 2026, scoring a touchdown in five of six games. However, the depth behind him took a hit after Week 7. Erick All Jr. tore his ACL and joined Tanner Hudson on injured reserve. The Bengals suddenly find themselves in the TE market.
Goedert set an Eagles franchise record with 11 touchdowns in 2025. Those scores were highlighted by shovel passes, quick-flip tosses, and crisp short routes. Lining him up alongside Geiscki near the end zone would leave defenses with no easy matchups against an offense stacked with elite talent.
Acquiring Goedert would be a larger move than his expected price of a late-round pick suggests. The Super Bowl champ boasts PFF's second-highest overall grade among 30 qualified tight ends (80.0) in 2026. It'd be an all-in move that shows Cincinnati trusts quarterback Joe Burrow to lead a deep run.

title: 3 Eagles Offseason Decisions Have Come Back to Haunt Them by Halloween
full_text:
Things haven't gone the Philadelphia Eagles' way during the 2026 NFL season. The team has been completely decimated by injury issues, and they've also been plagued by some questionable decisions that were made by the organization over the offseason.
In honor of Halloween, let's look back at three offseason decisions that have already come back to haunt the Eagles this season.
Philadelphia's decision to trade for , and immediately extend, linebacker Jonathan Greenard on a four-year, $98 million deal back in April has aged like milk. Greenard has been a complete non-factor for Philadelphia so far this season, in part because of injury issues and partly because of poor play.
Greenard has appeared in four games for Philly thus far and tallied just one tackle, one QB hit and one forced fumble. That's certainly not the production that you would expect from a player making as much as Greenard.
In fairness, the entire defense has struggled throughout the season, so it's tough to single out a specific player, but the Eagles had high hopes for Greenard when they signed him, and he certainly hasn't lived up to them thus far. It's safe to say that the organization might have a bit of buyer's remorse at this point.
Linebacker Nakobe Dean is having a stellar season in his first year as a member of the Las Vegas Raiders. Here's a quick summary of Dean's productive play as of late from CBS Sports :
"Dean is in the midst of a standout season, as he's recorded double-digit stops in four of his past five games and is tied for third in the NFL with 68 tackles through seven contests."
Dean has done a bit of everything for the Raiders' defense. Meanwhile, the Eagles sorely miss Dean's production on the field, as their linebacking corps has been struggling with consistency issues all season.
As an organization, you can't pay everyone. But, Dean was a player that the Eagles drafted and developed, and then they let him leave. That decision could continue to haunt Philadelphia.
The Eagles had a ton of options, and a ton of needs, when it came to their second-round pick in the 2026 NFL Draft. They opted to use that pick on tight end Eli Stowers from Vanderbilt, and thus far that decision hasn't paid off. Stowers has appeared in just one game for Philadelphia on the current campaign and he hasn't recorded a single reception.
It remains to be seen if the Stowers pick will ultimately pay off. Perhaps he'll eventually be the team's succession plan for Dallas Goedert. But it's tough to look at all of the needs on Philadelphia's roster this season and not think that their second round pick could have been better utilized elsewhere other than on Stowers.

title: 3-Step Guide to What a Successful Eagles Trade Deadline Should Look Like for Howie Roseman
full_text:
The Philadelphia Eagles haven't been winning on the field, as they've dropped five straight games heading into their Week 8 matchup with the Washington Commanders on Sunday Night Football. But, they could still win from a strategic standpoint with some shrewd move making ahead of the NFL trade deadline next month.
Here's a look at three simple steps that Eagles general manager Howie Roseman needs to follow in order to ensure a successful trade deadline for Philadelphia.
The Eagles are a proud organization. They have been arguably the most consistently competitive team in the NFC since the turn of the century. This isn't an organization that is going to throw in the towel a single second before it has to.
But as an organization, the Eagles also pride themselves on being forward-thinking, and sometimes you just have to embrace the reality that's right in front of you. The Eagles aren't going to win the Super Bowl this year. It would take a miraculous turnaround, the likes of which has probably never been seen before in the league. It's just not their year, as injuries have ravaged the team. That happens sometimes in the NFL. Roseman has to accept this fact and prioritize the team's long-term outlook, as opposed to devoting more resources to what certainly feels like a lost season.
Prioritizing the team's long-term outlook doesn't necessarily mean having a complete fire sale, however. There are plenty of players on Philadelphia's roster that Roseman should want to hold onto moving forward. After all, the Eagles have made the playoffs in five straight seasons. They don't need a complete teardown. A retooling is probably a more apt description of what they need: Keep the core building blocks on both sides of the ball and look to better complement them next season and beyond.
When it comes to who the Eagles should label as keepers, there are some no-brainers like wide receiver DeVonta Smith, cornerback Quinyon Mitchell, quarterback Jalen Hurts and defensive tackle Jalen Carter. Other players who the team should want to continue to build with could include linebacker Zack Baun, defensive tackle Jordan Davis, running back Saquon Barkley, cornerback Cooper DeJean, offensive tackle Jordan Mailata and linebacker Nolan Smith.
With keepers identified, Roseman can now move on to the final step.
Any players that Roseman doesn't see a future for in Philadelphia beyond the current campaign, he should try to flip them for draft capital and/or young players with high upside. Guys like Riq Woolen, Hollywood Brown and potentially even guard Landon Dickerson could fit the bill there. That's not necessarily an indictment of any of those guys, but if they're not going to be back with the Eagles, the team might as well try to get something in return for them.
The Eagles have several areas that they'll need to address in upcoming drafts, and the more picks they have to address those areas, the better. In my eyes, stacking some picks in exchange for guys who won't be around long-term while holding onto key contributors on both sides of the ball would be viewed as a successful trade deadline for Roseman and the Eagles.

title: 3 Potential Riq Woolen Trade Partners Could Be on Eagles' Radar in Coming Days
full_text:
Heading into the 2026 NFL trade deadline, there are plenty of hopeful contenders across the league's landscape that could use an athletic cornerback with championship experience. As a result, Eagles cornerback Riq Woolen could be a hot commodity .
" Contract-year players like Hollywood Brown, Tariq Woolen and Dallas Goedert could be had ," Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer reported about potential deadline trades on Friday.
When the Eagles signed Woolen to a one-year deal over the offseason, they expected to be in the contender conversation themselves, but things haven't quite worked out that way this season for Philadelphia. As a result, the team could be willing to part with Woolen and other veterans who likely don't have a long-term future in Philly for the right price.
Here's a look at three potential trade partners for Woolen that could pop up on the Eagles' radar leading up to the deadline.
The Steelers traded away cornerback Joey Porter Jr. to the Cowboys last month, and they're in the market for a replacement heading into the trade deadline. Perhaps they can work out a deal with the Eagles for Woolen.
As a contending team, the Steelers are likely looking for a player with championship and playoff experience who could slide seamlessly into the secondary. Woolen fits the bill there, as he was a member of the defensive unit that helped the Seahawks win the Super Bowl earlier this year.
Woolen could fit in nicely with the Steelers, and since he's on a one-year deal, trading for him wouldn't require a long-term commitment from Pittsburgh's front office.
The Detroit Lions were interested in trading for Porter Jr. from Pittsburgh before he was ultimately shipped to Dallas at the end of September. Head coach Dan Campbell admitted as much.
"[General manager] Brad [Holmes] was—he’s been on it for a while," Campbell said of a potential Porter Jr. trade. "And it was—that’s been ongoing, and everything's got to align right and the Cowboys did what they wanted to do. But we were very much in on it."
While the Lions didn't land Porter Jr., they're presumably still in the market for a cornerback to strengthen the secondary. In fact, according to Dave Birkett of the Detroit Free Press , cornerback is Detroit's most pressing need heading into the deadline. So, perhaps the Lions will call the Eagles about Woolen, who probably has a higher ceiling than some of the other options on their roster.
Like their AFC North rival in Pittsburgh, the Ravens could also be in the market for a cornerback heading into the trade deadline. The Ravens fancy themselves as a Super Bowl contender, but the secondary has been an issue for the team, and Woolen could provide them with some size and experience at the CB spot.
The Eagles don't play the Ravens this season, and Baltimore is in the opposite conference, so they wouldn't have to worry about playing against Woolen after trading him this season, unless both the Eagles and Ravens made it all the way to the Super Bowl, which seems exceedingly unlikely at this point in time.

title: Nick Sirianni Hasn't Lost One Coach's Faith Despite Eagles' 5-Game Losing Streak
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — With the Eagles mired in a five-game losing streak and a 2-5 record that mirrors their worst start under Nick Sirianni, special teams coordinator Michael Clay offered a pointed defense of his head coach’s approach, emphasizing consistency and a return to the process that fueled a 2021 turnaround.⁠
The Eagles opened the 2026 season at 2-0 before dropping five straight, including an ugly  38-21 home loss to the Cowboys on Monday night. Star quarterback Jalen Hurts is out for the season with blood clots ; Tanner McKee has taken over under center; A.J. Brown was traded in the offseason and the roster has been further depleted by attrition and the retirement of right tackle Lane Johnson.
With the season on the precipice, Philadelphia sits third in a wide-open NFC East ahead of a Sunday night prime-time road game against the Commanders .⁠
Clay, the Eagles' well-regarded special teams coordinator, was asked what stands out about Sirianni’s leadership during the skid earlier this week, and stressed that the head coach has kept a steady hand through adversity.
“Nick is the same person each and every day, regardless of if you’re 2-5 or you’re 7-0,” Clay said. “He approaches the day the same way, approaches the meetings the same way in terms of he’s not going to waver off what he truly believes in, and we’re going to back him in those scenarios and get these guys playing to an ability they know how to play."
Staying steady is not easy in a high-pressure environment like Philadelphia, which is used to success and expects it in perpetuity.
The parallel to 2021 is hard to ignore. That season, Sirianni’s first as head coach, the Eagles also sat at 2-5 before winning seven of their final 10 games to finish 9-8 and reach the playoffs. The injury situation is far more difficult this time, making a similar turnaround even more difficult.
Clay, who returned to Philadelphia on Sirianni's first staff, was asked how the staff approached the climb in 2021.
“I think it’s just doubling down on what you really believe in and selling it to the guys that this is how our process is and how we’re going to be able to dig ourselves out of it,” Clay said. “The players take pride in what they put on tape or whatever it may be, Monday, Sunday, Thursday night, whatever it is. It’s just one of those things.
"We have a great group of guys in here that are going to take some leadership roles in terms of getting everybody out of this little rut that we’re in. The most important game is the one on Sunday, more than anything else. Can’t look forward—Can’t look behind. The results are the results; you’ve got to live with them, but now you have the opportunity to change those results into a favorable way on Sunday night.”
Sirianni has struck similar notes in his own recent comments , telling reporters after the Cowboys loss that the group talked about remaining “the same version of yourself every single day” and referenced the 2021 finish as an example of growth through process rather than panic.
Sirianni has repeatedly framed the team as “results-aware but process-driven,” stressing his core values of tough, detailed, and together over reactive changes.
“Let me say it this way: to give yourself the best chance to win each week, you have to have a great process,” Sirianni said Friday when asked about his process by Eagles On SI . “That guarantees you nothing, not one thing. It doesn't guarantee you anything, but it puts you in the best position to win each and every week. You can't completely correlate that. My thing is, if we go and do everything the right way throughout the week and we end up losing the game, I can handle that.
“When our preparation isn't the way that we want it to be, or our week isn't the way we want it to be, and it can be a lot of different things. It's not just studying tape on your own time. It's not that. It's just the focus in a meeting, the focus in a practice, or anything like that by all parties. If you don't do that, which every season there's games where that happens, then you don't give yourself the best chance to win. Let me be very clear: it's not a results-based thing.
“We are very results-aware, but we are process-driven.”
Clay’s remarks arrived amid growing external scrutiny around the Eagles.
Some analysts and former players have questioned the team’s culture and Sirianni’s job security after the longest losing streak of his tenure.
Inside the building, however, the message from Clay and others is one of continuity: the daily approach does not shift with the record; the focus stays on the next game.
Whether that formula can produce another late-season surge without Hurts remains the central question heading into the Commanders matchup.
For now, Clay’s public backing underscores the staff’s bet that the same steady presence that helped right the ship five years ago can do it again.

title: Steelers’ Michael Pittman Jr. Reveals Hopeful Return Date
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers haven't had wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. on the field since their Week 4 contest against the Cleveland Browns.
Without Pittman, the Steelers' wide receiver issues have been exacerbated. Even with the emergence of rookie Germie Bernard, there is a noticeable lack of depth at the position.
The hope is that after the bye week, the team will have a new addition via trade and possibly see some players return from injury. One possibility is the return of Pittman Jr. following the week off. Speaking to the media the day after the team's Week 8 victory, the veteran receiver shared an encouraging update and some more information on his current injury.
He wasn't able to say for sure, but he shared that he would love to return following the bye week.
"It would be great to be back after the bye week, which is what I would like," he told reporters. "But I can't go out there if I'm not effective. So, only time will tell."
As a veteran in the NFL, Pittman Jr. has experienced a lot. But this specific injury has been brand new for the former Indianapolis Colts pass-catcher. Steelers On SI publisher Noah Strackbein spoke with Pittman, who shared some more detail on this injury.
According to Strackbein, Pittman has been dealing with planter fasciitis, at least at first. Since that initial injury, it's "morphed" into something else, something that "surgery wouldn't fix."
"Yeah I mean, I've never dealt with this (injury)," he said. "So, I don't know what it's supposed to feel like or what it's going to feel like. And we got a great team here that's been helping me through it."
For Pittman, it's about doing everything he can to get back on the field and contribute with his teammates.
"Trying to get back out there as fast as possibl and prove to this team that I came to better it and not just sit on the sidelines."
While he hasn't been able to be on the field for the past four games, Pittman has had the chance to get an up-close view of the offense at work. After their latest, he offered some insights when asked for his observations.
The biggest thing Pittman noted was the impact of the team's running backs and tight ends.
"I think the offense is doing good and I think Jaylen Warren and our tight ends are really holding us up," he stated.
When Pittman Jr. returns, hopefully after the bye week, the hope is the passing game can reach that same level.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: DK Metcalf Revives Steelers' Need for WR Trade
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers absolutely dominated their Week 8 matchup, defeating the Cleveland Browns in a familiar fashion.
The 27-6 win was the Steelers' fourth consecutive victory and their sixth of the season. It was a huge win, one that could solidify this team as a contender in the AFC.
The win also solidified this team's wide receiver troubles as the biggest issue once again. Quarterback Aaron Rodgers was once again rendered less effective due to not having enough talent on the outside, and despite the team's stubbornness and defiance, they have to address this glaring hole in the lineup.
Rodgers has had four interceptions this season that came directly off the hands of his receivers. In Week 8, Metcalf dropped an easy pass. Not only that, the ball deflected off his hands and into Cleveland's possession.
When it was rookie Germie Bernard who bobbled a screen pass that resulted in an interception, it was just a moment's lapse for a first-year player. When a pass ricocheted off Roman Wilson's hands for a turnover, it was frustrating, but not a terrible mistake.
When your top pass-catcher does it, it's bad. When the player who is supposed to be your top offensive weapon and top pass-catcher makes such a costly mistake, it's a call for change.
Mistakes happen. Like many other players in Pittsburgh, it's about how you rebound from your failures. Metcalf has the chance to make up for his costly error when the team returns to the gridiron in Week 9 against the Cincinnati Bengals.
But one trend is becoming too big to describe as a one-off or a single mistake. The Steelers have been trying endlessly to make Metcalf the focal point of their red zone offense and it's been an utter disaster. Once again in Week 7, the Steelers dominated on the ground, only to turn into a passing offense when they had the goal line left to gain.
Even head coach Mike McCarthy expressed some regret about how he called a red zone trip in the first half.
"That series there, I would could have those three plays back," he said during his postgame press conference.
And that's a sentiment he probably feels about all of their red zone trips so far in 2026. It's clear that McCarthy wants to let Rodgers run the show, but Metcalf hasn't executed on the plan. The only red zone threat on this team is tight end Darnell Washington, no matter how many goal-line fades they hurl Metcalf's way unsuccessfully.
The Steelers have been involved in trade talks and the subject of many rumors as the NFL trade deadline rapidly nears. The latest rumor has tied them to Indianapolis Colts pass-catcher Josh Downs , while another report claims they're a team to watch for Jacksonville Jaguars' Brian Thomas Jr.
And after another underwhelming outing from their top wideout, it's clear that a player like Downs is essential. Downs is an explosive pass-catcher who can create separation. Those are two traits the Steelers desperately need infused into their wide receiver group immediately.
If not Downs or Thomas, any player who fits that description would upgrade this offense . As Rodgers tries to make his final season one for the history books, they need to give him as many weapons as possible.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: 7 Winners, 2 Losers From Steelers Blowout Win Over Browns
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers left no doubt about how the better team was in Week 8.
After a week filled with trash talk, specifically from Jared Verse , the Steelers dominated the Cleveland Browns in every facet of the game and got revenge for their Week 4 loss to their AFC North rival with a 27-6 blowout victory at Acrisure Stadium this time around.
With that, here are Pittsburgh's winners and losers from the contest as it heads into a Week 9 bye.
Washington continues to make his mark as a real threat in the passing game for the Steelers.
Washington went for a total of 92 yards, which led Pittsburgh on the day and is also a new career high.
The 25-year-old is now on pace for 540 yards, which would eclipse his 364-yard campaign in 2025 by a healthy margin.
It's tough to quantify how brilliant Warren has been for Pittsburgh this season.
Though he didn't log any receiving yards on his one catch for the first time this year, Warren more than made up for it by recording 143 yards and a touchdown across 17 carries.
He has now put up 100 or more yards on the ground in four games this season.
Facing a rookie left tackle in Spencer Fano, Highsmith's veteran expertise was on full display in this one.
Alongside drawing a couple of holding penalties on the first-rounder, Highsmith also posted five tackles, 0.5 sacks and three quarterback hits to go with three pressures (per SumerSports ) as part of a monster day for the Steelers' pass rush.
Pittsburgh didn't need anything from Metcalf in order to rout the Browns, but it felt like he regressed back to the level of play he showcased in the first few weeks of the season.
Metcalf hauled in just one pass from Aaron Rodgers, which went for four yards and marks his lowest single-game total since Week 17 of the 2022 campaign.
Furthermore, Metcalf was wide-open deep down the field and dropped a throw from Rodgers as he adjusted, which ended up in the hands of Denzel Ward for an interception.
Heyward hadn't done much as a pass rusher coming into this week, though that changed vs. Cleveland.
The 37-year-old posted 1.5 sacks, which more than doubled his prior total of 1 on the season, and he also had five total pressures (per SumerSports ).
Heyward was disruptive against the run per usual as well, logging two tackles for loss and being one of the main reasons why the Browns finished with 34 yards on 15 carries.
Queen, after a rough start to the season, has begun to really turn things around in a contract year.
Following what was arguably his best game as a Steeler in the team's Week 7 win over the New Orleans Saints, Queen led the black and gold with 12 total tackles while also recording 1.5 sacks, which is the most he's ever had in a single game.
Despite being under constant pressure, Deshaun Watson was still able to complete 27 of his 39 passing attempts for 324 yards.
Brisker's had an up-and-down season for Pittsburgh after signing a one-year deal with his hometown franchise in March, and he wasn't exactly playing at the top of his game against the Browns.
According to Pro Football Focus , Brisker allowed 55 yards in coverage (his most in a single contest this season) while also missing a tackle.
Watt had started cooling off just a bit after coming out of the gates hot this season, though he was back to his usual ways vs. Cleveland.
The 32-year-old paced the Steelers with two sacks, which pushes his total on the year to 7.5, and he also had a pass deflection.
In their defeat at the hands of the Browns earlier this season, Pittsburgh's offensive line allowed Rodgers to be sacked five times.
The Steelers were far more stout in pass protection in their rematch vs. Cleveland, however, as Rodgers was sacked just once.
With Spencer Anderson back in the mix as part of the team's jumbo package too, the offensive line created plenty of holes for Warren to run through as they got the better of the Browns' defense.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: Steelers Take Control of AFC North
full_text:
PITTSBURGH — The Pittsburgh Steelers are playing their best football in 2026 and it's putting them on track towards postseason success.
The Steelers dominated the Cleveland Browns 27-6 at Acrisure Stadium in Week 8 and have taken the lead of the AFC North at 6-2.
Cleveland previously held the tiebreaker, after beating Pittsburgh 27-24 in Week 4 at Huntington Bank Field, but this win gives Pittsburgh a game advantage, 6-2 compared to 5-3.
It's a big victory for the Steelers, who have won four in a row since that defeat and head into their bye week as one of the best teams in the NFL.
The Steelers are in the second-most competitive division in football in the AFC North, with only the NFC North having a better combined record.
Perhaps the next team that is most competitive in this division, aside from the Browns, is the Cincinnati Bengals, who are playing some good football too.
Cincinnati has won three straight games, 31-24 over the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium in Week 5, 35-13 over the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium in Week 7 and then a 43-36 victory in overtime against the Tennessee Titans at Paycor Stadium in Week 8.
The Bengals fended off a late comeback from the Dolphins, scored 35 unanswered points in the second half against the Ravens and erased two fourth-quarter deficits against the Titans to win it in overtime.
Pittsburgh and Cincinnati face one more time in 2026, including the first game out of the bye week at Paycor Stadium in Week 10, with Pittsburgh winning the first matchup , 30-27 at Acrisure Stadium in Week 3.
The Browns have lost two of their last four games, and all five of their wins have come within one possession.
Baltimore is in the worst position of all these teams, as they have lost their last three games, including 36-10 to the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium in Week 8.
The Ravens may also have lost quarterback Lamar Jackson for the rest of the season with a thumb injury, which he sustained on the first play from scrimmage in the loss to the Bills.
Philadelphia Phillies (Road)
Jacksonville Jaguars (Road)
The remaining nine games for the Steelers in 2026 feature some tough opponents and a few poorer ones as well.
Pittsburgh facing the Bengals out of the bye week on the road will be tough, as well as their matchups with the Denver Broncos at home in Week 12 and the AFC South-leading Jacksonville Jaguars on the road in Week 14.
The Steelers also face the Ravens twice in Week 15 and Week 18, the Philadelphia Eagles without Jalen Hurts in Week 11, the struggling Houston Texans at home in Week 13, the inconsistent Carolina Panthers in Week 16 and the terrible Tennessee Titans in Week 17.
It's a combined record of 31-35, so not the easiest of stretches for the Steelers, but certainly not the hardest.
Six wins from these nine games shouldn't be too surprising from the Steelers, barring serious injuries,  and it should spark them to back-to-back AFC North Titles out of the bye week.
Dominic writes for Pittsburgh Pirates On SI, Pittsburgh Panthers Pn SI and also, Pittsburgh Steelers On SI. A Pittsburgh native, Dominic grew up watching Pittsburgh Sports and wrote for The Pitt News as an undergraduate at the University of Pittsburgh, covering Pitt Athletics. He would write for Pittsburgh Sports Now after college and has years of experience covering sports across Pittsburgh.

title: Steelers Are Contenders, Not Trash Talkers
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers are 6-2 heading into the bye week. They just beat a Cleveland Browns team that brought plenty of attention with them because of their AFC North-leading record and trash talk heading into the game. And leaving Acrisure Stadium for the last time until Black Friday, this team is as "real" and they could be.
"He should have kept his mouth shut," Jaquan Brisker said after the game about Jared Verse's trash talk. "All that talk, and then to come out with zero tackles, that’s bad."
That was as bad as it got for the Steelers in response to Verse after the game. For those who missed it, Verse said the Browns would "own" Pittsburgh in this game. He didn't, and neither did the Browns, but the Steelers didn't really care.
For the most part, this team made it simple. "Some talk, some walk," Jaylen Warren summed it up.
That was the vibe in the locker room afterward. This team wasn't focused on revenge or shutting Verse up. They felt more disrespected that Cleveland elected to receive the ball to start the game.
Pittsburgh is focused on the big picture more than the little one. They wanted to win four in a row heading into the bye week and accomplished it. They were determined to get their defense clicking to become the dominant group they could be, and to figure out their offensive line before the midway point of the season.
"We're 6-2 going into the bye, first in the division. We're right where we want to be," Aaron Rodgers said after the game.
It's been a long time since the Steelers felt like a real contender. There have been moments and glimpses of great play, but overall, it's felt largely like Mike Tomlin was carrying them as far as he could drag them, ultimately to be eliminated from the postseason early.
This year, making the postseason isn't the goal. This team doesn't want to "get to the dance"; they want to win it. They want to be serious contenders.
"We didn't discuss it one second, what they were saying about us," T.J. Watt said about the Browns. "We just want to go about business. We have a lot of mature guys who have done it here and done it other places and had a lot of success and a lot of young guys who want to continue to grow and be great. We're just focused about what's in the building right now."
Inside the building, the Steelers have a defense that ranks top 10 in points allowed and takeaways. The team has scored over 20 points in all but one game, and is currently at the top of the division with a chance to increase that lead after the bye against the Cincinnati Bengals.
It's about Super Bowls, not trash talk in Pittsburgh.
A mindset that makes them feel bigger than their opponent. And like a real contender at the break.
"We were motivated because we wanted to get this damn win before we got to the bye," Heyward put it,"so...

title: Steelers' Jaylen Warren Roasts Jared Verse: 'Some Walk, Some Talk'
full_text:
Cleveland Browns EDGE rusher Jared Verse's comments coming into a Week 8 matchup with the Pittsburgh Steelers drew plenty of attention, as he previously stated the black and gold were "dirty" and said he wasn't "worried about nobody they got on their team."
During his postgame press conference following a blowout 27-6 win for the Steelers, however, Warren stated that the team was aware of Verse's remarks and didn't pay them much mind when asked if it was a motivator. He did offer more of an opinion on the matter at the end of his answer, though.
"Yea, but we didn't really pay attention to it," Warren said. "Some walk, some talk."
In a contentious game between a pair of AFC North rivals sitting atop the division at 5-2, the Steelers got the better of the Browns at nearly every turn.
Warren, who's emerged as one of the best running backs in the NFL this season, really helped set the tone for Pittsburgh and had yet another explosive outing en route to the black and gold's fourth-straight victory.
The 28-year-old, who celebrated his birthday on the day of the game, was unusually quiet as a receiving option out of the backfield, finishing with zero yards in that regard for the first time in 2026.
That didn't stop Warren from torching the Browns on the ground, however, as he logged 143 yards and a touchdown over 17 carries while the Steelers as a whole rushed for 200 yards on the contest.
Verse, meanwhile, recorded a single tackle and no sacks.
It sure felt like the Steelers were playing with an extra edge vs. Cleveland, which didn't come as a surprise given the gravity of the contest.
Pittsburgh flew around the field on defense and combined for a total of eight sacks with 13 quarterback hits. Additionally, it limited the Browns to 34 yards on 15 carries and recovered two fumbles.
In the locker room after the game, Jaquan Brisker stated that he believed Cleveland's decision to receive the ball after winning the opening coin toss was disrespectful and essentially motivated the Steelers from there on out while also noting that Verse's comments were far from the only reason the team was "hungry" to earn a victory.
"I think them taking the ball was kinda disrespectful," Brisker said. "Especially being at home. So it kinda turned us up, and obviously you seen how the first series went and things like that... I wouldn't say a particular player really amped us up, because I wouldn't say he motivated us. I think we were just motivated overall. Basically we didn't like how the first game went, how the first meeting went. Of course we heard the noise, so that added a little bit to it, but I wouldn't say it was just Verse. We were just hungry to win, and obviously hungry to get a win before the bye week."

title: Steelers vs. Browns Takeaways: Jared Verse Owes an Apology
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers are now 23-0 in their last 23 home games against the Cleveland Browns.
The Steelers heard the noise from Cleveland all week, and ignored it. Cam Heyward said early in the week that Jared Verse's comments about Pittsburgh playing "dirty" in their latest game would "be addressed."
It was, in the fashion of a 27-6 win at Acrisure Stadium.
Let's dive into some takeaways.
The Steelers spent all week ignoring the Jared Verse smack talk in front of cameras , but they certainly heard the noise and took it as a challenge.
Before the game, I predicted the Steelers would have five sacks (minimum) in this game. They had four at halftime. They finished with eight, and nearly took Deshaun Watson out of the game on the opening series when he was checked for a concussion.
As for Verse himself, Mason McCormick made sure to let him know they heard him talking...
Jared Verse been talking all week. Mason McCormick did his talking on this play A 15-yard penalty he will gladly take pic.twitter.com/qZT7H0HPmH
It was a welcome to the AFC North game for Cleveland's newest starting edge rusher. Everyone needs one of those games, but when you talk beforehand, it usually makes it a little bit tougher of a day for you during the game.
In this instance, it not only made life rough Verse, but made it especially difficult for his quarterback.
It's a live-and-learn situation for Verse, but one he won't get to make right until either the playoffs or next season. One thing is for certain, though, the Browns did not "own" Pittsburgh after this one.
Another week, another reminder that Jaylen Warren is a top five running back in the National Football League. This week, he finished with 17 rushes for 143 rushing yards and a touchdown.
He had 10 rushes for 102 yards at halftime.
Warren turned 28 on game day and had a little extra burst in his play to celebrate.
For another week in a row, Warren was the best player on the Steelers' roster. He continues to be the driving force for the offense and one of the most explosive players in the entire league.
Yes, he's underrated. Yes, he's arguably top five in the NFL. Yes, chances are he'll be featured in this column again next week.
5️⃣1️⃣ YARDS 🚂 @Nunless2 pic.twitter.com/3d2lNSEUfv
If it's Mike McCarthy, someone needs to tell the head coach to do some self-scouting on his red zone play-calling. If it's Aaron Rodgers, someone needs to tell him to stop trying to pad the stats. But whoever is making these red zone decisions needs to be corrected, because it's bad. Real bad.
The pointless DK Metcalf fades are where it usually begins, but it never seems to get much better from there. Jaylen Warren, who we just got done talking about being a top-five runner, is barely used inside the 20-yard line. Rico Dowdle, the two-time1,000-yard rusher behind him, doesn't get much attention, either.
Correction: the last 6 plays inside the 10. https://t.co/OcbB4Jvvga
Pittsburgh's inability to realize they need to run the ball more near the goal line will continue to hold them back. Luckily, the offense as a whole is good enough to move the ball and produce points. A few more touchdowns compared to field goals would go a long way in tight games, though.
This defense has plenty of excitement surrounding it, but every week, we're reminded that their secondary is the weak link of the entire roster. Even when the pass rush is as elite as it was this week, the corners and safeties struggled, and it made the end result look much different than it should have been.
If the Steelers could cover for just another second on average, there would be several more sacks for this team.
With the trade deadline approaching, general manager Omar Khan should at least be checking on names. Nahshon Wright, Alontae Taylor, Amik Robertson and others have been mentioned as possible trade candidates. Maybe they don't fix the problem, but if they don't cost much to acquire, it's worth taking a shot on someone.
Pittsburgh's entire defense could use the boost.
The Steelers announced an extra offensive lineman during their pregame introductions. To kick things off, they welcomed Spencer Anderson as part of the starting offense. The 200 rushing yards backed that display of appreciation well.
The jumbo package returning to the offense is a great sight to see. There were even a few moments when Riley Nowakowski was in the game at fullback.
This team may have Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy enjoying one last ride together, but this is a running football team. One with six starting offensive linemen.
Over the weekend, Alex Highsmith was mentioned as a potential name to watch at the trade deadline. The Steelers aren't interested in trading him away, but the right offer could spark a conversation.
To this point, they've told every team that has called no. That probably won't change after this game.
Highsmith was a force from start to finish, recording five tackles and a half-sack against the Browns.
His trade value went up in this one. So did the Steelers' desire to keep him for the upcoming playoff run.
The Steelers are paying DK Metcalf over $30 million for the 2026 season and then for the next three seasons afterward. He hasn't shown he's been worth that amount of money one time since he joined the roster, and that deal continues to look worse with each poor performance he has.
Against the Browns, Metcalf had one reception for four yards before Aaron Rodgers found him deep in the middle of the field, wide open. It didn't result in a completion. Instead, Metcalf bobbled the ball, which landed in the hands of Denzel Ward, instead.
So, yeah, the Steelers need to add a WR pic.twitter.com/5nwkki18rY
You could see the defeat in Metcalf as he walked off the field and was surrounded by his teammates. But the boos from the crowd were loud, and as much as this fanbase wants to embrace Metcalf as their star wide receiver, it's very difficult for them to.
The Steelers probably need a wideout at the deadline. They won't get a WR1 to replace Metcalf, but anyone helps. As long as they have options, they can probably make up for the lack of production from their $132 million wide receiver.

title: Steelers Without Veteran WR for Third Consecutive Week
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers are trending in the right direction when it comes to many of their injured players. After head coach Mike McCarthy providing an encouraging update about the list of players on the Injured Reserve, it appears that the organization might get a dose of returning players sooner rather than later.
Despite the progress, the Steelers still have to reach deep into their depth to field a full active roster, and the injuries have impacted the lineup on both sides of the ball.
One player that has gone overlooked amongst the group of injured players is wide receiver and special teams ace Ben Skowronek. The 2025 Pro Bowler has missed two consecutive games, but returned to practice in a limited capacity during the team's Week 8 preparations.
Still, he's not quite ready to return to the lineup. After the Steelers released their inactive list for Week 8 against the Cleveland Browns, Skowronek's third straight absence became official.
One area the team needs to improve the rest of the way is across the board on special teams. The early season was a tough stretch for veteran kicker Chris Boswell, but he's settled in as the season's continued. Punter Cameron Johnston has been rock-solid as well, but the rest of the units have struggled to find consistency.
That's where the Steelers miss Skowronek the most. He made the Pro Bowl last season as a gunner on the punt team, showing just how versatile he is in those situations.
The team has found an impressive new gunner to join them in safety Robert Spears-Jennings, but they still need Skowronek's presence to bring this special teams group from concern to strength. Especially after Brandin Echols and Doneiko Slaughter were previously ruled out of the Week 8 contest with injuries, this special teams group is in desperate need of upgrades.
This will be the third game that Johnson is elevated to the active roster from the practice squad. For that reason alone, this is a very important for Johnson personally. After this, the Steelers will either have to release him or sign him to a one-year contract that guarantees his spot on the active roster for the foreseeable future.
But Johnson hasn't shown much, aside from lining up in special teams situations. In two games so far, he's produced zero catches or plays on offense. The big-bodied receiver brings size and experience, that's undisputed, but he hasn't done much to move the needle on offense.
Quarterback Aaron Rodgers is still searching for depth options he can rely on. Johnson gets that shot, alongside fellow journeyman receiver Brandon Smith . Smith produced his first two NFL catches in Week 7, and the Steelers would love to get some offensive impact from another unexpected source.
In order for him to get that chance, he'll need to see the field just a bit more. According to data from Pro Football Reference, he's played in just 11 offensive snaps over the past two weeks.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Elandon Roberts' Chances of Returning to Steelers Lineup Dropping
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers surprised many when they released inside linebacker Elandon Roberts before the start of the regular season. A two-year starter with the organization once upon a time, many penciled him in to the 53-man roster without any debate during training camp and the preseason.
That wasn’t the case, as the Steelers moved on from Roberts before Week 1 of the regular season. But the divorce didn’t last too long, as the team signed Roberts back to the practice squad right after their Week 5 victory over the Indianapolis Colts.
Given the timing of Roberts’ return, there was reason to believe that the defense would make some changes at inside linebacker. Instead, the starting duo of Patrick Queen and Payton Wilson have been motivated by and improved by Roberts’s presence and experience.
The chances of Roberts getting a spot on the active roster moving forward continue to drop, especially after another week passes without being elevated. It might be a pipe dream for Roberts to get on the field with the Steelers, but that isn’t stopping him from making a huge impact on the middle linebacker group.
One of the key differences between this year’s team and last year’s version is the intangibles. The camaraderie in the locker room and the blend of youth and veteran leadership has played a part in this team’s 5-2 start.
Adding Roberts has only improved that facet of this year’s squad. Much like how Brock Hoffman has helped to steady rookie Max Iheanachor, Roberts has steadied Queen and Wilson.
That was never more evident than in Week 7, arguably Wilson’s best game in a Steelers uniform and a standout performance from Queen. That production was partly fueled by Roberts’ game film breakdown, and he explained on an appearance on the Deebo & Joe podcast what he shared with the rest of the linebackers room. Speaking about New Orleans Saints quarterback Tyler Shough, Roberts picked up on a key bad habit that the Steelers took advantage of.
“One time, he (Shough) checked, and he didn’t even look up,” Roberts explained. “The coach talked to him the whole time. So, after 15 seconds, he’s gotta make the checks himself.”
The Steelers responded by disguising coverage until there was under 15 seconds on the play clock. That confused Shough enough times to make a difference in both the running and passing game.
Roberts didn’t record a tackle, but he made one of the biggest contributions to the defense’s win over the Saints.
The Steelers are still looking for consistency in production, but there is no denying that the inside linebacker room showed elite potential in Week 7. If that is the level of play the team will get from Queen and Wilson the rest of the way, how could the Steelers possibly move away from that tandem?
Week 7 was the middle linebacker show for the Steelers. Queen finished with a team-leading 10 tackles, seven recorded individually, 1.0 sacks, a tackle for loss, a quarterback hit and a pass defended. Wilson matched that with six tackles of his own, a pass defended and an interception.
That interception was a thing of beauty, as well. Wilson perfectly played his coverage while reading and anticipating Shough. Putting himself in position to make a play on the ball, it still took an impressive feat of athleticism to catch and maintain possession of the ball.
When you are getting turnovers, tackles and a tone-setting performance from your inside linebacker duo, you ride the wave. Who knows how long it will last, but it’s forcing the team’s hand.
It’s also forcing Roberts off of the active roster. The fanbase admires him and the organization clearly values him, but don’t expect Roberts back on the field in a game setting any time soon.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Steelers May Be Team to Watch for Brian Thomas Jr.
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers are looking for a wide receiver at the NFL trade deadline. That doesn't come as a surprise, as the team has searched high and low for answers at the position for several years in a row, but this year there seem to be bigger names on the market, and Pittsburgh is interested.
The Steelers have already been linked to Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Josh Downs after the 25-year-old requested a trade from the team. According to NFL insider Jordan Schultz, the Steelers showed interest early, and they're likely still in the mix as the deadline draws closer.
Now, there's another name that has emerged. According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler, the Steelers are a team to watch for Jacksonville Jaguars' former first-round pick Brian Thomas Jr. The Jaguars haven't decided whether or not they will trade Thomas Jr., but Pittsburgh may be interested if they do.
"You have teams in the receiver market like the Kansas City Chiefs that need one, that I believe have multiple lines in the water as fas as receiver; the Pittsburgh Steelers are looking around," Fowler said on ESPN. "The Jaguars have not totally committed to trading Brian Thomas right now, but he's in and out of the lineup and would welcome a team most likely."
Reaction to latest Jonathan Taylor news…teams I’ve talked to value Taylor at a ‘2+’ clip - second-round pick and more. Plus, the latest on the receiver market and Brian Thomas Jr. pic.twitter.com/mijzgfp2r9
According to The Athletic's Jonathan Jones, the Jaguars are looking for a Day 2 NFL Draft pick in return for Thomas Jr. The Steelers currently have two third-round picks in the 2027 NFL Draft after receiving one from the Dallas Cowboys in exchange for Broderick Jones.
The upside of Thomas Jr. is still exciting for any team looking for answers as the wide receiver position. This is a former first-round pick who had over 1,200 yards and caught 10 touchdowns during his rookie season. At 24 years old, Thomas Jr. is playing in just his third season, leaving the 2027 season left on his rookie deal, and making it possible to pick up his fifth-year option this upcoming offseason.
That should intrigue the Steelers. This team has several starter-worthy options in DK Metcalf, Michael Pittman Jr., Germie Bernard and Roman Wilson, but two of those players are on Injured Reserve, and Pittsburgh is in the business of finding a solution at the position now and long-term, and Thomas Jr. may fit both of those needs.
However, he comes with a big "if." Since the arrival of Liam Coen as head coach, Thomas Jr. has fallen out with the offense. This season, he's totaled just nine receptions for 105 yards and a touchdown.
He has not caught a pass since Week 4 against the Cincinnati Bengals.
So, the Steelers would be taking a chance that Thomas Jr. just needs a change of scenery to find his production again and turn his career around before the end of his rookie deal.
Pittsburgh could take the risk and may want to depending on how the other wide receiver options look. Thomas Jr. fits what they need and comes with plenty of upside. So, it's no surprise the Steelers are a team to watch if the former first-round pick is available come the deadline.

title: 3 Matchups That Will Decide Seahawks’ Week 8 Clash vs. Bears
full_text:
On Monday night at Lumen Field, Mike Macdonald’s Seattle Seahawks look to stay above the .500 mark when they host the 5-2 Chicago Bears. It’s a battle of defending division champions and the third straight prime time contest for the defending Lombardi Trophy holders.
Macdonald’s team owns the league’s top-ranked defense in terms of fewest total yards and fewest passing yards allowed per game. Chicago’s offense has reached the end zone 21 times in seven games, while the Seahawks have allowed only 12 offensive TDs in the same number of contests.
Both teams have been in the news lately for making huge acquisitions. More importantly, both the Bears and Seahawks are looking up in their respective divisions behind a pair of 6-1 clubs. So here’s a look at some key battles that will play a big part in tonight’s result.
Talk about irony? Since 2019 and including a meeting back in Week 6 at Lucas Oil Stadium, eight-time Pro Bowl guard Quenton Nelson of the Indianapolis Colts and four-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons of the Tennessee Titans certainly had their share of battles. Last week, both found new homes last week as the former was traded to the Seahawks and the latter was dealt to the Tennessee Titans.
Now due to an amazing set of circumstances, they will renew acquaintances on Monday night in the Pacific Northwest. Nelson is currently Pro Football Focus’ second-ranked player at his position , while Simmons is PFF’s No. 10 interior defender. In seven games this season, the eight-year pro has totaled 38 tackles, four sacks, nine QB sacks, and four passes defensed.
Prepare for another epic battle.
A year ago, the 10th overall pick in the 2025 NFL draft led the Bears in catches (58) and receiving yards (713) and tied for the team lead with six touchdown grabs. Seven games into this season, tight end Colston Loveland and wideout Kalif Raymond both have 26 receptions for 244 yards, tied for the second on the club in both categories.
Loveland has two touchdowns to Raymond’s one. However, exactly half of Loveland catches (13), more than half of those yards (134) and both of those scores have come in Chicago’s last two games.
Eight-year pro Julian Love ranks sixth on the club with 24 tackles despite missing one game. He leads the Seahawks with six passes defensed and is tied for the team lead with a pair of interceptions. Can he cool off the suddenly-hot tight end?
D'Andre Swift bounces it outside for the SCORE. Bears up, 10-0. NEvsCHI on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/R75ldG3SHb
Entering Week 8, Ben Johnson’s club owned the league’s top-ranked ground attack, averaging a brisk 154.3 yards per outing. The Bears’ leading rusher is D’Andre Swift, now in his third season in the Windy City. He’s totaled team highs in carries (116), yards (476), and total touchdowns (7)—all of those scores via the ground. He comes off a season-best 22 attempts, good for 78 yards and one touchdown in Chicago’s Thursday night win over the Patriots.
Seahawks’ linebacker Drake Thomas ranks third on the team with 35 tackles, behind only Ernest Jones IV (68) and Devon Witherspoon (41). While Thomas’s 2026 grade (60.6) via Pro Football Focus is far from awe-inspiring, his number in terms of run defense (70.5) is worth mentioning. And does Aden Durde also use the former undrafted free agent from North Carolina State to spy Caleb Williams?

title: 5 Key Things to Know About Bears vs. Seahawks in Week 8
full_text:
The defending Super Bowl champions have had no choice other than to prove that they are ready for prime time. For the third consecutive week, the Seattle Seahawks will be under the lights and facing a playoff team from 2025. From a Thursday night visit to Denver (overtime loss) to a Sunday evening home game with the Chiefs (win) to this Monday night clash of defending division champions in the form of the Chicago Bears.
Yes, the ‘Hawks they’re already lost as many games as they did all of last season and are just 3-2 in their last five outings. But they sent somewhat of a physical message to Andy Reid’s team last Sunday night at Lumen Field, handing the Chiefs their first loss of 2026 via a 20-3 score.
Bears QB Caleb Williams Week 7 Highlights vs. Patriots 22/33 308 PASS YDS 2 PASS TD 0 INT Bears win 30-24. pic.twitter.com/Tw6Yxc2ioI
Meanwhile, the Bears have had some extra time to prepare for their first appearance in the Pacific Northwest since 2021. They were last seen outlasting the New England Patriots, 30-24, on a Thursday night at Soldier Field thanks to a big evening by quarterback Caleb Williams.
Of course, both of these teams made big noise late last week when it came to acquiring star players. Seahawks’ general manager John Schneider orchestrated a deal to acquire eight-time Pro Bowl guard Quenton Nelson from the Indianapolis Colts. A day later, Chicago’s Ryan Poles completed a trade with the Tennessee Titans to add four-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle Jeffrey Simmons—and paid a hefty price to do so.
As far as the rest of the NFC West, the first-place San Francisco 49ers had Week 8 off, while the Los Angeles Rams and Arizona Cardinals both came up with wins on Sunday.
Even though the Bears own a pair of postseason wins in this setting, it’s the Seahawks that have a four-game overall lead (12-8) in a series that dates back to Seattle’s inaugural campaign in 1976.
As for much more recent times, this marks the second time in three years the clubs will battle. Back on a Thursday night (the day after Christmas), the ‘Hawks managed a 6-3 triumph over the Beats in Chicago in one of the uglier games in recent years. As for the Bears’ last appearance in Seattle, the club came up with a 25-24 triumph back in 2021.
SAM DARNOLD IS PICKED IN THE END ZONE BEFORE THE HALF 😱 (via @NFL ) pic.twitter.com/QjFAJ7JRGc
Both clubs own a minus-1 turnover differential this season. Chicago has forced 10 turnovers and totaled 11 giveaways. Seattle has 12 takeaways, but has already given up the football 13 times. It's worth noting that Seahawks’ quarterback Sam Darnold has thrown at least one interception in five straight games.
Only five teams in the league, including the Bears (87.6) are allowing fewer rushing yards per game (89.4 average) than Macdonald’s team. But Aden Durde’s defense faces a very stiff challenge in the league’s top-ranked ground attack. Led by D’Andre Swift, Chicago is averaging 154.3 rushing yards per contest.
Dillion Thieneman’s sack was on green dog blitz. Green dog is when the defender has the green light to blitz if their man to man responsibility blocks. Quick recognition here by Thieneman to add on. #DaBears #Bears pic.twitter.com/h2DUSiW57q
He was the 25th overall pick in April’s draft and has come up big in his rookie season. Former University of Oregon defender Dillon Thieneman (who began his college career at Purdue) leads the Bears with 43 defensive tackles, to go along with 1.5 sacks, five passes defensed, one interception, and four special teams’ stops.
Mike Macdonald’s club has proven to be a second-half team this season. The Seahawks have been outscored a combined 72-63 in the first 30 minutes in their seven games. On the other hand, they have nearly doubled up the opposition in the second half and overtime, 105-53—allowing four offensive TDs.

title: Are the Seahawks Officially out on RB Jonathan Taylor Trade?
full_text:
For four consecutive years, the Seattle Seahawks have been a major player during the NFL Trade Deadline. Earlier this week, general manager John Schneider showed that the team remains willing to trade for high-level talent at the NFL Trade Deadline. The Seahawks traded for eight-time Pro-Bowl guard Quenton Nelson from the Indianapolis Colts . Nelson is an immediate upgrade for the offensive line.
​There was talk that the Seahawks might not be done making trades to improve the roster, especially being two weeks away from the deadline at the time. There was talk that the Seahawks might trade for Colts running back Jonathan Taylor. Despite a great fit , the Seahawks might be out on Taylor.
​On Sunday, ESPN’s NFL insiders Ian and Raport Adam Schefter reported that the Colts are open to trading Taylor. Schefter mentioned that some teams are active in trading for the three-time Pro-Bowl running back. These teams include the Denver Broncos, the Green Bay Packers, the Minnesota Vikings and the New York Giants. Seattle seems to be the biggest omission from the list of teams that haven’t reached out to Indianapolis.
​While this doesn’t mean that the Seahawks are out on Taylor, it seems they are more focused on their roster than making changes to it. The Seahawks could get veteran running back Zach Charbonnet and rookie running back Jadarian Price back from injury for Week 8’s Monday Night Football game versus the Chicago Bears. The front office and coaching staff might want to see their new rushing additions of Nelson, Charbonnet and, possibly, Price in a game before a decision.
​There is still time for the Seahawks to decide if they want to trade for Taylor, especially after their game versus the Bears. The Seahawks might be cautious of trading for an older running back and what they would have to give up. Indianapolis already reportedly turned down a trade deal that includes a second-round pick and an additional pick.  This likely means that the Colts are wanting more picks or at least one first-round pick.
​The Seahawks have multiple picks on day-two and day-three of the NFL Draft, but first-or-second-round picks. The front office might replace an early pick with Price, but that would mean giving up on the young back before he has been given several chances to show himself . Price was drafted to be a dynamic starting running back for several years in the Seahawks’ backfield.
​Seattle ranks 17th in the league in rushing yards per game (113.7), while bad offensive line play, turnovers and a lack of explosiveness have plagued the offense . If Nelson’s addition to the roster plus Charbonnet and Price’s return doesn’t improve the running game, then there are problems beyond the players. If the Seahawks trade assets for Taylor and the problems persist, then it’s not a good look for the Seahawks’ future this season.

title: Seahawks' Plans for Jadarian Price in Week 8 Being Misinterpreted
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks (4-3) will once again have another primetime game, this time on Monday at home against the Chicago Bears (5-2) . There is a lot of excitement for the Seahawks as they are set to debut newly traded left guard Quenton Nelson and running back Zach Charbonnet from injury. The running game should take a huge boost with more efficiency at the offensive line and more explosiveness at running back.
​The Seahawks could also see the return of rookie running back Jadarian Price , who is coming off a chest injury that forced him to be placed on IR. Since Price’s injury, the running game has been poor. If Price comes off IR and plays, the Seahawks’ offense should see much more improvement. Some Seahawks fans see a reason to believe that Price’s future is as early as Monday.
​During Saturday’s press conference, head coach Mike Macdonald was asked about the plans for both Charbonnet and Price. Macdonald said the coaching staff has a plan for Charbonnet, but it was different with Price. He said , “And with JD, I think if we were to make a move, I think that would happen on Monday.”
To many, this would imply that the Seahawks are waiting to see if he recovered from his injury enough to play and potentially start.  The front office can make changes to the roster in terms of who to move  up or down the 53-man roster. Price can be activated on the day of the game .
​To others, this might be the belief that the Seahawks are limiting Price to use as a trade asset. The Seahawks are among the teams that might trade for three-time Pro-Bowl running back Jonathan Taylor from the Indianapolis Colts. The Seahawks’ running game has struggled even before Price’s injury. Seattle could trade Price along with a high day-three NFL Draft pick to the Colts instead of a first-round pick.
​There is some discourse that the Seahawks should cut their losses with Price after only three games played and get a star running back for a win-now team. If the Seahawks traded for another Colts star, it would make them the team to beat.
Price, however, hasn’t gotten many chances to show his potential with Seattle’s offense. The first two games with Price were when Seattle was trying to get quarterback Drew Lock comfortable with the offense. Week 3 against the Washington Commanders was when he was benched for his fumbling issue.
​At this point in the season, Price is the only saving grace of a 2026 NFL Draft class that started rough. With safety Bud Clark and cornerback Julian Neal injured and the rest of the drafted rookies not ready,  Price is the only player who can make this draft class look somewhat successful.
​The Seahawks want to see what they have in Price, especially with one of the most elite run-blockers in Nelson leading the charge. Price showed great flashes of replacing Super Bowl LX MVP Kenneth Walker III before Sam Darnold’s injury, his turnover issues and his own injury. The trade for Nelson was a promise for Darnold to improve, but also for Price.

title: Seahawks Give Word on Jadarian Price and More Before Bears Game
full_text:
Coming a day later than typical due to the Monday Night Football tilt, the Seattle Seahawks released their third and final injury report, which will go a long way in shedding light on the likely availability of several key Seahawks. The Chicago Bears gave their own injury updates as well, so let’s have a look at what’s brewing. Starting with the Seahawks…
There’s some good news here, to be sure. Quenton Nelson (knee) , Brady Russell (wrist), Connor O’Toole (hamstring), Chazz Surratt (calf), Drake Thomas (ankle), and Leonard Williams (achilles) are locked and loaded. DeMarcus Lawrence and Jaxon Smith-Njigba , never injured in the first place, have no game status either.
But the most exciting thing for many Seahawks fans will be Zach Charbonnet (knee) and Jadarian Price (chest) having no game status and being expected to roll in full. It hasn't been a smooth ride, but it looks like we'll have our entire backfield available this week. Also massive is Byron Murphy (back) having no game status. That should be more than enough to quell concerns.
Those who are questionable going into Monday's game include Anthony Bradford (knee) , Drew Lock (right elbow), Brandon Pili (back), and Pat O’Connell (toe). Uchenna Nwosu (ankle) is doubtful, so tenatively cross him off. Charles Cross (ankle), Velus Jones (hamstring), and Rashid Shaheed (knee) are out, but that’s been assumed to be the case since the week started.
There was a lot less drama this week for the Chicago Bears, and that has held through this final practice of the week. They have one player with an out designation, and as expected, it’s Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe). Obviously, the Bears are somewhat used to not having him, but he remains a very valuable and important part of that offense as a change-of-pace back.
The questionable slate is not without concerns, of course. Malik Muhammad (toe), who has been the best cover corner in Chicago so far this year, was limited all week and is considered a 50/50 to play. D’Marco Jackson (ankle), a starting linebacker, got a full practice in but is still considered questionable. I imagine he plays, but it’s worth monitoring.
Speaking of linebacker, T.J. Edwards (hamstring) and Jack Sanborn (concussion) have no status after full practices all week. The primary relief for Bears fans, however, is Colston Loveland (neck), who was a full go today and has no status. Neck injuries are no joke, but it looks like Loveland’s issue was a very minor one and he’ll be suited up Monday.

title: Seahawks' Jarran Reed Linked to Several Teams in NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
Teams have just over a week left to improve their rosters through the NFL Trade Deadline. The Seattle Seahawks (4-3) already made moves by trading for eight-time Pro-Bowl guard Quenton Nelson from the Indianapolis Colts. This move might be the best overall trade this Trade Deadline.
There are some reports that believe the Seahawks could move some of their players to help their salary cap situation for another trade or to give Nelson a contract extension. Some reports might indicate veteran defensive tackle Jarran Reed is on another team’s radar to trade for.
​Reed is one of the top leaders on the Seahawks’ Dark Side Defense . He is also one of the most underrated players on the interior defensive line. Reed has played all 11 games, accounting for 11 total tackles, four quarterback hits, one tackle for loss and one sack. He can be the one-technique defensive tackle and the three-technique defensive tackle.
​He is a huge part of the Seahawks’ defense, and other teams understand how efficient a player he is. CBS’s Jonathan Jones notes that teams are interested in trading for Reed to to address needs of reliability in the middle of the defense. He can also be an instant veteran defensive leader for another team.
​The Seahawks weren’t likely going to trade any players before the Nelson trade, but now the front office has to start thinking about the future. Nelson is in the final year of his contract, and the Seahawks shouldn’t think twice about getting him to an extension . The biggest problem is affordability while still having room for other veterans next season.
​Moving veterans like Reed would help the front office create some salary cap space while getting some picks in return. Reed is in the second-year of a three-year, $22 million contract . If the Seahawks traded him before the deadline, the team would save  $3.26 million in cap space for the rest of this season while taking a $4.13 million dead cap hit. Next season, however, the Seahawks would save $8 million, creating $45.48 million in salary cap space and only take a $1.5 million dead cap hit.
​The downside to the move is the Seahawks lose a reliable run-stopper and underrated pass rusher from the middle of their defense. This might be the price for trading for an elite guard like Nelson, but it’s something they should consider if they want to secure one of the league’s best guards and get future capital as a result.

title: The 49ers Have 5 Trade Targets After Jauan Jennings Snub
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers reportedly called the Minnesota Vikings to make a trade for wide receiver Jauan Jennings. However, Jennings did not want to play for the 49ers, so the deal did not go through. Still, it confirms the 49ers' interest in a wide receiver.
Now that they have shown interest in a wide receiver, who are the best pivots for the 49ers?
Downs requested a trade from his current team, so he is clearly going to be an option available on the trade block. However, he is also 25 years old with an 800-yard season on his resume. So, he is going to cost a bit more than some others on the trade market.
Still, if the 49ers can trade for him and extend him, he could join De’Zhaun Stribling as a young core.
Jeudy is more of a veteran who can put the team over the top this season. The Cleveland Browns' best receivers are rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion. While they are 5-3, their best bet is to let these two develop. Trading Jeudy can open snaps for these two.
Thomas put up 1,282 yards in his rookie season. However, the team changed coaches, and the scheme does not appear to fit the former first-round pick. The Jaguars benched him in Week 6, and while he caught a touchdown in Week 8, it is not going to cool down the trade talks. The issue with Thomas is that the Jaguars are going to look for a return similar to Marvin Harrison Jr. That is a lot to trade for a player who has as many questions as Thomas.
Ridley has five catches for 81 yards this season. He is not 32 years old and has not been fully healthy this season. Still, some of that can be the player; some can be playing for a poor Titans team. Ridley is not going to cost much to acquire in a trade, and the upside is still there. The 49ers can give him a chance.
Johnston might be the best fit when you factor in age, production and cost. The Chargers are now 0-7, and Johnston is likely going to leave in free agency. Their best choice would be to trade him.
