title: The 49ers Have 3 Trade Suitors Emerging for Mac Jones
full_text:
As the weeks get closer to the NFL trade deadline , the odds of the team trading quarterback Mac Jones have once again increased. Who are three teams that are now emerging as likely candidates to trade for Mac Jones?
The Vikings are heading into Week 9 at 6-1. However, they are being carried by the best defense in the NFL and a below-average offense. An offense with Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison has enough firepower to win games. So, the issue is Kyler Murray.
The NFC North is tight, and the last-place team is sitting at 5-3. So, the Vikings could go from the last undefeated team to last place in their division in the matter of a few weeks if they do not get things together on offense.
The Vikings have the weapons and the run game for Jones to step in and compete with Murray. It would be the only chance for Minnesota to stay in contention with their elite defense. That could cause an overpay that the 49ers would have to accept.
The Ravens are going to place Lamar Jackson on the IR with a thumb injury. Their backup Tyler Huntley got hurt in Week 8. So, they are onto rookie UDFA Joey Fagano. The Ravens are sitting at 4-4, but now they are in last place in their division. They need to find a way to turn things around quickly.
What makes things interesting for Baltimore is that Jackson only has one year left on his deal and a high cap hit. The Ravens will either be looking to extend him or trade him this offseason. With a brand new coaching staff and his history of injuries, the team might look to use this year to pivot. If Jones keeps them in contention, he could be the Ravens' 2027 starter.
Philadelphia is another team that could be looking to the future. Jalen Hurts suffered blood clots and is out for the year. No one knows when he will play again. We have all seen enough of Tanner McKee to know he is not the Eagles' answer for the future.
They can trade for Jones and give him the rest of the season to prove that he deserves a chance in 2027. The division being weak only makes trading for Jones more sensible.

title: The 49ers Have Multiple Needs to Address Before the Trade Deadline
full_text:
Now that the San Francisco 49ers traded for defensive tackle DeForest Buckner, the team has taken one of their needs off the board. San Francisco made the trade early enough that they still have time to make another move before the trade deadline. If they did make a move, what would be the biggest need?
A lot of people would see this as their biggest need, but the addition of Buckner, combined with Nick Bosa and Mykel Williams starting to get healthy, has the team stronger on the edge. Williams will not slide inside nearly as much with Buckner, giving them a full-time rusher. Bosa should be back soon, and rookie Romello Height has taken steps. With Keion White as the fourth rusher, it is not a pressing need.
The team started the season playing Jack Jones in a dime role. He is now a free agent. Their backup slot option is Ashtyn Davis, who is borderline unplayable. San Francisco is going to try a rookie fifth-round pick, Ephesians Prysock or the injured Nate Hobbs . Both have potential and questions.
The good news is that adding a depth cornerback is not going to cost too much. That is a relatively big need for the 49ers.
Left guard is a big need because it is hard to see the roster getting any better naturally. Connor Colby is in his second NFL season, and his progress appears to have stalled. Carver Willis is a rookie fourth-round pick who played tackle in college. Willis could take over and hit the ground running, but the team might be best served giving him time. At the very least, looking to insert the rookie during a run into the playoffs would be a dangerous move.
Whether it be a one-season rental or someone who could push Willis next season as well, they need to figure it out.
Receiver is the toughest to gauge, but ultimately their biggest need. Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, Demarcus Robinson, and De’Zhaun Stribling could all finish the year healthy. However, all four have major injury questions, and aside from Evans, the other three do not have much proven production this season
When adding in that Jordan Watkins and Jacob Cowing did not take advantage of their snaps with those four out, it is fair to think they can add to the position. This is their biggest need.

title: Latest Report Shows 49ers Made Right Decision Moving On From Jauan Jennings
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers may need to trade for a wide receiver right now to strengthen their Super Bowl hopes this season, but a recent development has reminded them that some of their offseason decisions were spot on.
In the offseason, the 49ers had many decisions to make at wide receiver. They moved on from Kendrick Bourne after a one-year return, and they also parted ways with Jauan Jennings, who ultimately went to the Minnesota Vikings .
Jennings, in particular, was a name that raised some eyebrows. He's an intriguing character with plenty of admirable qualities, including his toughness, but he ultimately showed that he didn't make the most of his opportunity in one of the best offensive systems in the league.
This was demonstrated further after new reports from Jay Glazer revealed the 49ers and the Vikings were exploring a possible trade for Jennings, but he didn't want to hop on a FaceTime call with Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch after an agreement was in place.
Here’s Jay Glazer talking about Jauan Jennings not wanting to get on a FaceTime call with Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch to get traded back to the 49ers https://t.co/JWWNIT0zQQ pic.twitter.com/ceOmmEpLvF
Now, if true, it shows the 49ers made the right call all along with Jennings and their management of him. Don't forget that during the 2025 training camp, he missed time with a calf injury, but it was also reported that he was exploring a new deal.
It made sense for the 49ers to consider rewarding Jennings after he enjoyed a career-best 2024 season, finishing just 25 yards short of a 1,000-yard campaign. That said, handing him a lucrative new deal was understandably something the franchise was hesitant to do. Instead, the two sides eventually agreed to an incentive-based contract that also added an extra year to his deal.
However, Jennings arguably became the architect of his own downfall from that point onwards. After dealing with injuries and the consequences of missing valuable preparation time, he struggled to build on his breakout campaign. He finished the 2025 season with 55 receptions for 643 yards and a career-high nine touchdowns across 15 games. He was playing for some of those games with injuries too.
And then, during the recent offseason, reports stated that the 49ers were willing to offer $17 million a year . He declined. Then things went quiet and he joined the Vikings on a one-year, $13 million contract, with $8 million base. So far, he's only had four receptions all year.
All that can be said is that it's a massive upgrade to have a future Hall of Famer like Mike Evans on the team for less than what they were offering Jennings, despite the unique qualities Jennings brought to the receiver corps.

title: The 49ers and Vikings had a Trade in Place for Jauan Jennings and He Nixed It
full_text:
What a bad look for the 49ers.
They desperately need a wide receiver because their three big additions this offseason -- Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and De'Zhaun Stribling -- are all injured. So, of course, the 49ers called up the Vikings to inquire about trading for Jauan Jennings, who has four catches for 43 yards this season.
And, of course, the Vikings were open to trading Jennings back to the 49ers, where he spent the first five seasons of his career. The two teams even had a deal in place, a ccording to FOX's Jay Glazer.
But Jennings nixed the deal. Apparently, it was contingent upon Jennings having a FaceTime call with Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch, presumably to clear the air after their relationship became rocky during the past couple seasons.
Jennings refused to participate in the call. He wouldn't even talk to Lynch and Shanahan. Which means Brandon Aiyuk isn't the only former 49ers wide receiver who seems to hold a deep, personal grudge against them.
It's unclear why Jennings seems so upset with the 49ers. Maybe he thinks the Vikings are the better team and that he'll get his opportunities soon enough. Or, maybe he's still bitter than the 49ers never gave him the contract extension he wanted. He always saw himself as the best receiver on their roster, even better than Aiyuk, and felt the 49ers didn't appreciate him.
Did Jennings have an inflated opinion of himself? Absolutely. But that's part of what made him good. He truly believed he was the best, even though he's not. And now, the 49ers want him back, and they can't have him because they didn't show him love. Or something.
What's important to the 49ers is that they haven't figured out a solution to their wide receiver problem. Clearly, they're searching the bargain bin for a receiver they can get in exchange for a late-round draft pick, which is disappointing.
They need a true difference-maker to replace Mike Evans if he misses time with Achilles tendinitis. And they'll never draft that wide receiver at the end of Round 1, which is where they pick almost every year. They tried recently and ended up with Ricky Pearsall and Stribling, who aren't exactly as good as Evans.
The 49ers need to get serious and start offering their first-round picks to bad teams that have great wide receivers. They have 10 days to figure it out.

title: 49ers GM John Lynch Highlights Brock Purdy’s Best Qualities
full_text:
It wouldn't be unfair to suggest that San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy is the best quarterback of the Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch era.
Out of all the quarterbacks who have started since 2017, Purdy is the best. Since 2022, he's taken the 49ers to the Super Bowl, the NFC Championship Game and the Divisional Round in four seasons.
In his career so far, Purdy has completed 1,065 of 1,564 pass attempts (68.1%) for 13,433 yards, averaging 8.6 yards per attempt, with 99 touchdowns, 41 interceptions and a 104.8 passer rating.
Stats and achievements aside, Lynch highlighted multiple qualities Purdy possesses that have helped establish him as one of the league's elite quarterbacks.
"You have to be able to retain and take in a ton of information," Lynch explained to NBC Sports Bay Area . "You watch us do all those motions—Brock's handling that. He's the orchestrator, and I don't think people understand how much information [that involves]. He's got an ability to do that.
"Kyle is demanding, and Brock can take that without taking it personally, and I think that's really important. That may be one of his greatest qualities as to why he thrives with Kyle.
"And then, he's extremely talented. You see him, the way he goes and extends plays. He's done it in each and every game, aside from being able to stay in the pocket and progress.
"He's competitive. He always finds a way to get better," Lynch continued. "I think, this year, he kind of took it personally that people are saying he's a layer thrower. I'm seeing him come out with shoulder turn and driving the ball this year.
"I think that's what the great ones do. They identify things they want to work on, and they get it done. I could talk about Brock all day long, and I'm probably going too long, but he's easy to do that with."
The desire to keep improving and not letting criticism get to you is exactly what stands out. It's a small element of the exact culture Shanahan wants to embed in his team.
Purdy and Shanahan are a perfect match, and it cannot be emphasised enough how important it is for the two to remain together for as much of their careers as possible. If they can continue building on their existing partnership, a Super Bowl victory could certainly be on the cards.

title: John Lynch Sounds Off on His 10-Year Partnership With Kyle Shanahan on the 49ers
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers have had John Lynch as their general manager and Kyle Shanahan as their head coach for a decade.
Both arrived in 2017 and helped restore the organization, making it a championship contender and taking the City by the Bay to two Super Bowls, two NFC Championship Games, and, most recently, the Divisional Round last season.
Though the ultimate prize has eluded the 49ers so far, the overall commitment is to bring a sixth Lombardi back.
Reflecting on his partnership with Shanahan over the last 10 years, Lynch told NBC Sports Bay Area : "They say time flies when you're having fun, and I think that. But it doesn't feel like 10 years. Crazy that we've spent a decade here. I'm very grateful for that.
"It's been a lot of fun, and when you play football, you become very close with people because you go through really good times, you go through real hard times, and you go through everything. There's a multitude of things.
"And the most important thing is that you do it together. And whether good or bad, that you stick together and you have each other's back. That's kind of the Forty-Niner way, and we certainly do. We've had each other's back from the start and really proud of that.
"We have had a range of emotions and outcomes of getting to Super Bowls, the elation of that, the heartbreak of not winning those Super Bowls. But I think we both talk about those experiences—if you can stick together and if you are aligned, they only make you stronger. And I feel like that more than ever. We're extremely aligned.
"We're about the same thing, and how we're going to accomplish it, and how we're going to go about it, and that's really cool that after this much time, that we're as strong as ever."
Shanahan recently, rather secretly, inked a contract extension at the start of the season and is now the longest-tenured coach in franchise history. It's not known when that contract expires. Lynch, however, his contract expires after this season, so one can imagine he will have a new contract coming his way.
The next tangible goal for the duo is to win a Super Bowl. They've come close on multiple occasions, but with the 49ers off to a 6-1 start, this could finally be the year they finish the season by bringing a Super Bowl title back to San Francisco for the first time this century.

title: 4 Games 49ers Fans Should Watch in Week 8
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers will be winners this week as they're currently enjoying their crucial Bye . However, that means 49ers fans will not get to watch their favorite team.
They've been treated to some elite football every week, and now it will be empty. But just because the 49ers aren't playing doesn't mean there aren't important games to watch. That said, here are the four games 49ers fans should watch in Week 8.
This isn't an exciting matchup at all, but the Raiders are the first team the 49ers will face when they emerge from their Bye Week. Seeing how the Raiders perform will give a better idea of how Week 9 will go.
Maybe the Raiders will surprise everyone in this game. Or it will more likely be the usual from them this season. In any case, it's always good to preview an upcoming opponent to see how difficult or easy it will be for the 49ers.
In a few weeks, the 49ers will head to Mexico City to play the Vikings. Minnesota arguably has the best defense in the league, which is going to be tested against the Lions' electric offense.
The Vikings are the last undefeated team, so they're a strong force that mustn't be overlooked despite their weak offense. This matchup will give 49ers fans a better understanding of what's in store for the 49ers down the road.
Plus, the Lions might be a playoff opponent for the 49ers. This is the most insightful game of Week 8 to show where the 49ers stand in the NFC.
Another upcoming opponent for the 49ers is the Cowboys. They'll face them in Week 10 after the Raiders, which is always a premier matchup.
49ers fans can key in on the Cowboys' offense, which has a bunch of firepower, but also bear witness to the mediocrity of their defense. Facing the Cardinals is a minor bonus, as there's not much to learn about them.
Last but not least is the battle on Monday night between the Bears and the Seahawks. This is the most exciting matchup of Week 8, which is part of why 49ers fans should watch.
But most importantly, they're two of the top NFC teams. The 49ers will obviously play the Seahawks again, and they might play Chicago in the playoffs, making this a must-watch game.

title: Predicting the 49ers' Wins and Losses After the Bye Week
full_text:
The Bye Week arrived at the perfect time for the San Francisco 49ers .
After starting the season 6-1 , they receive crucial rest. That will be extremely beneficial as they begin their second- half season push with the playoffs ahead.
They'll surely love to replicate their run as they did in their first seven games, but their schedule will be much tougher. Let's dive into which games the 49ers will win and lose when they emerge from their Bye.
This is about as easy a matchup that the 49ers could've asked for emerging from the Bye. They get to open up at home against the Raiders, who have been in freefall since Week 4.
The Raiders have a putrid defense and cannot run the ball. Aside from Brock Bowers, they don't have a lethal threat to worry about. The 49ers should have no problem defeating them.
It shouldn't be too difficult to beat the Cowboys either. Although they will be a step up in competition from the Raiders. Dallas has some ballers on offense.
But the 49ers have dogs on defense that will exploit how soft the Cowboys are. This should be a fairly easy win for the 49ers to get on the road.
For their second international game of the season, the 49ers will host the Vikings in Mexico City. Minnesota's defense has arguably been the best in the NFL.
Brock Purdy and Kyle Shanahan have also struggled heavily against Brian Flores. That alone will be why the 49ers lose, despite the Vikings' offense being incredibly average at best.
As great as the 49ers were against Seattle in the first matchup, I don't believe they'll have their number this time. The Seahawks will make the proper adjustments and be more motivated than last time. A season split seems fitting between these two juggernauts.
This game has a sloppy outing for the 49ers written all over it. They'll be coming off a war against the Seahawks and will travel to the East Coast, which is always tough, to play a fairly solid Giants team. They might lose this game, but I don't think the Giants are good enough to pull it off.
The Rams may be more motivated in this game than in Week 1, but they're not good. They bought into their offseason hype, and it shows. It'll be a closer matchup than in Australia, but the results will remain the same as they were then.
This doesn't deserve much of an explanation. The Chargers are the worst team in the NFL. There's no way they will salvage their season or have the ability to play well against the 49ers.
This is the premier game on the 49ers' second-half schedule. Not only will it be a good measuring-stick game against a good team, but the 49ers need to finally prove they can beat the Chiefs, and I think they will. What better way to do it than at Arrowhead?
It's over for the Eagles. They won't have Jalen Hurts, and none of their star players are performing up to their ability. This might be an easier outing for the 49ers than against the Chargers.
This game screams "throw away" for the 49ers. Either a bunch of their starters won't play, or they will only play for a time. It has nothing to do with how the Cardinals are.

title: The 5 Best-Performing 49ers at the Bye Week
full_text:
Achieving a 6-1 record at the Bye Week has the San Francisco 49ers in excellent standing.
They couldn't have asked for a better start. A significant reason for their awesome start is thanks to five players who have been their best performers this season. Let's dive into who these five players are.
No stats are needed to explain this. Fred Warner has been a monster this season. Ball carriers hate to see Warner coming because they know he's going to lay a massive hit on them.
Or he's going to punch the ball out, which I am convinced is because his hands have a magnet that is attracted to the material of a football. It's the only way to explain why he's so insanely accurate with those peanut punches.
Warner has been so elite this season that he will have a strong case to be the Defensive Player of the Year if he keeps it up. He leaves everyone in awe with every performance. At this point, I'm out of words.
Aside from his performance in Week 6 against the Washington Commanders, Renardo Green has been on a tear this season. He's easily been the 49ers' best defensive back.
Green is currently tied for the most interceptions (3) in the league, and of the 195 qualified defensive backs, he has the 17th-lowest passer rating allowed (55.1).
He's always had the talent. All Green needed was the right coach to unlock him, which is what makes defensive coordinator Raheem Morris a match made in heaven for him.
It's probably safe to say that Mike Evans has been the best free agent signing by the 49ers under Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch. He's been sensational.
Similar to Warner, you don't need to look at the stats to know or see the impact Evans has made. He's been exactly what the 49ers wanted and more.
Look no further than what he did against the Seattle Seahawks. He said in the offseason that he thinks he's their missing piece and has proven it so far.
I'd argue he's been the 49ers' MVP this season. The 49ers' offense has been elite with him on the field, but in the six quarters without him, it's fallen off significantly.
The 49ers will need to hope and pray that Evans can overcome his Achilles tendinitis quickly. They will have no shot at winning the Super Bowl without him.
It's undeniable that Brock Purdy is playing at a different level this season. He's been sharper than he's ever been, with how accurate his throws have been, the limited mistakes he's made, and his overall playmaking ability.
It's why he's been referenced as the NFL MVP so early in the season. With how sharp Purdy has been playing, he's become a driving force behind the 49ers' offensive success after Evans.
Trent Williams is always a top-five performer on the 49ers, but rather than obviously pointing him out, the entire offensive line deserves recognition. They've been amazing through seven games this season.
They're allowing the lowest pressure rate (26.7%) in the league. Purdy has only been sacked seven times and pressured 62 times on 232 dropbacks.
Pass protection aside, they've done a fine job of opening up rushing lanes for Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black. They're easily the best-performing unit of the 49ers entering the Bye Week.

title: Every Record the Buccaneers Set in Historic Win Over Falcons
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers beat the Atlanta Falcons in Week 8. With that win, they moved within half a game of the NFC South lead and picked up their second win in a row for the first time in 385 days.
It isn't the fact that Tampa Bay won that has people talking, though — it's how Tampa Bay won. A rainy day brought a big change to the offensive game plan, and it resulted in a historic, record-breaking performance in Tampa Bay's 16-0 win.
Here's every record the Bucs became a part of when they beat the Falcons without completing a single pass:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers — and, by extension, quarterback Baker Mayfield — did not complete a pass against the Atlanta Falcons. That's an astonishing feat in itself, and it created a windfall that led to breaking more records.
The Bucs became the first NFL team since 1974 to win an NFL game without completing a pass. That game was on Sept. 9, 1974, when the Buffalo Bills defeated the New York Jets 16-12 in similarly rainy conditions.
The Falcons also set a new record on Sunday, though it's probably not one they're very proud of. Atlanta got shut out by the Bucs on Sunday, and with that, the Falcons became the first team to be shut out by a team that didn't complete a pass since 1942. Mayfield didn't complete a pass, but his passer rating (39.6) was higher than Falcons quarterback Michael Penix's (12.0).
With the conditions as they were, the Bucs had to run the football a lot, and oh, did they. The Bucs toted the rock to the tune of 324 rushing yards, which broke the franchise record for most rushing yards in a game — that record was previously set in 2015 against the Philadelphia Eagles, when the Bucs had 283 rushing yards that day.
Tampa Bay may not have passed much at all on Sunday, but it didn't last Sunday, either. Over the last two games the Bucs have played, they've completed just seven passes on 14 attempts — despite that, they've won both of those games by a combined 59-13.
The Bucs are set to play the Chicago Bears on Sunday Night Football in Week 9 on Nov. 8. They probably won't be able to win that game by completing fewer than 10 passes, but at this point, we're open to believing.

title: The Good, Bad and Ugly From Buccaneers' 16-0 Shutout Victory Over The Falcons
full_text:
That's how many days had passed since the Tampa Bay Buccaneers last won back-to-back football games.
Thankfully, that dreadful drought has officially reached its conclusion after the Buccaneers secured a much-needed victory on Sunday, defeating the Falcons 16-0 for their second victory in as many weeks. With the win, the Bucs have now improved their overall record on the year to 3-5 while going 2-0 against NFC South teams.
Not only does this victory represent the first time the Bucs have won back-to-back games in well over a year, but it also provides some optimism for a team that was getting dangerously close to eliminating itself from playoff contention before the halfway mark of the 2026 NFL season.
Now, let's break down the good, the bad and the ugly we saw in this crucial Week 8 NFC South showdown between the Buccaneers and Falcons.
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers' rushing attack entered a new tier of domination on Sunday.
Following last week's 258-yard explosion, I don't think anybody expected the Bucs to surpass that mark again this season, let alone the very next week. The Bucs didn't just surpass that mark, though; they absolutely obliterated it by rushing for an absurd 324 total yards on the ground against the Falcons, a top-five rushing defense in the entire league heading into this game.
As has been the case for the majority of this season, Bucky Irving was electric running the football in this contest. When it was all said and done, Irving had ducked and weaved his way to 170 yards on the ground and 1 TD while averaging 6.3 yards per rush on 27 carries. Had he not fumbled the ball through the end zone early in the game, he'd have had another TD added to his resume.
As the game went on, Irving got some rest while Kenneth Gainwell took the majority of snaps, and boy did he take advantage of that opportunity. Gainwell rushed 25 times for a career-high 140 yards, and his relentless and slippery style of running was reminiscent of his partner in crime, Irving.
After a surprisingly disappointing start to the year, the Buccaneers' offensive line has officially re-established itself as one of the league's best. As a group, they deserve a ton of credit for the team's dominant rushing performance over the past two weeks.
The 324 total rushing yards achieved by the Buccaneers today vs. the Falcons is the most in franchise history.
Oh, how things can change quickly in the NFL. Just a few short weeks ago, the fans in Tampa were calling for Todd Bowles' job. Now? They would be wise to praise him for the job he's done with his young defense, which all of a sudden looks like one of the best all-around units in the entire NFL.
The Bucs' defense has been operating on all cylinders over their past four games, and they've produced some pretty astounding numbers in the process. Dating back to their Week 5 win over the Cowboys, the Bucs' defense has come up with 10 sacks, nine interceptions, two forced fumbles and two fumble recoveries with their opponents averaging just 13.8 points per game over that stretch.
For the first time all season, Alex Anzalone made a big impact on this football game. Not only did the veteran linebacker have two interceptions (in the rain) in the first half, but he also did a much better job fitting the run. Anzalone finished the game with six total tackles and, more importantly, appeared to be much quicker at diagnosing plays and reacting accordingly.
The Bucs don't need Anzalone to lead the team in interceptions this season (which he currently is) for him to meet the expectations he had coming into this year — they just need him to play sound, disciplined football without making costly errors. If Anzalone can do that, the Bucs' defense will be much better off.
Jacob Parrish and Zyon McCollum continue to impress. Not only did each player record an interception today, but they've both been incredibly consistent in all phases of coverage while also providing exceptional run support this entire season.
If the Bucs' defense continues to perform as it has been, the play of their two starting corners will be a big reason why. If the Buccaneers continue to churn out victories, don't be surprised to see one, if not both, players named to an All-Pro team by season's end.
Although it didn't matter in the end, Irving fumbled a ball through the end zone in the first quarter. Mistakes happen, sure, but this one was completely avoidable. Irving was far too cavalier carrying the football with a defender in close proximity and pursuit, and he got burned for it.
The play happened right in the middle of a torrential downpour at Raymond James Stadium, which should have been added motivation for Irving to keep the ball high and tight.
The Buccaneers became the first team since the Bills in 1974 to win a game without completing a single pass. It's an impressive feat, really, and a testament to just how dominant the Buccaneers were at running the football. That being said, it's likely not an achievement that Baker Mayfield is very proud of.
The Bucs become the first NFL team since the 1974 Buffalo Bills to win a game without completing a pass 😳 pic.twitter.com/kQQJ3S9fqr
All that matters, though, is that the Buccaneers won this football game, and Mayfield finished the contest without any setbacks to his injured thumb.
It goes without saying that the weather played a big role in the lack of success for both the Falcons and Buccaneers on Sunday. Especially in the first half, the rain was as relentless through the air as Irving and Gainwell were on the ground, and credit to the fans who stuck around to cheer on the home team — if only the grass at Raymond James Stadium were so resilient.
Even though he passed for more yards than Mayfield, there's no question that Michael Penix struggled more than any other player in this football game. Penix was 8/24 and threw for 125 yards and 0 TDs to go along with his four interceptions.
He should have had another interception on the opening drive when a pass intended for Drake London hit Jacob Parrish square in the hands, but the Bucs' talented young corner was caught off guard and couldn't secure it.

title: Grading Each Position Group in Buccaneers' Shutout Win Over Falcons
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers dominated in an absolute monsoon in Week 8 against the Atlanta Falcons. Everything went right for the team on all three sides of the ball, and the Falcons looked like they couldn't play football in certain situations.
Let's go over the grades for each position group in another Buccaneers win.
Baker Mayfield did not complete a pass today, and it really didn't matter. Given the conditions of the pouring rain, Mayfield did a great job of staying on top of the football and handing the football off well.
Yes, there were a couple of fumbled snaps between Mayfield and center Graham Barton, but that was mainly due to the conditions of the game. Mayfield did what he needed to do in this matchup.
When you set a new franchise record for team rushing yards in a game, you get the highest grade possible. Both Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell set career highs in rushing yards today with 170 yards and 140 yards, respectively. We didn't see any of Sean Tucker in this matchup, but overall, Irving and Gainwell were phenomenal in this game.
The receiver's main role was blocking on the day, and they did that job well. Chris Godwin Jr., Tez Johnson and Ted Hurst III did a good job of helping extend runs for the Bucs' backs and contributed in the way they needed to for this matchup.
Cade Otton has really transformed into a great blocking tight end this season. It is also important to note that Bauer Sharp has essentially become this team's second tight end on the roster, and it makes sense due to his great blocking ability in recent weeks.
This group has been one of the top reasons why the Bucs have had rushing success the past two weeks and should have a big role going forward.
This group has dominated in the past two weeks regarding the rushing offense. The Falcons knew that the Bucs' game plan was to run the football all day today, and it didn't matter because the offensive line simply executed at a higher level than the Falcons could handle.
The Bucs have found their identity as a rushing team and the offensive line is the biggest reason as to why.
This unit really did a good job of containing one of the best running backs in the league, Bijan Robinson. The pressure was there on quarterback Michael Penix Jr., especially from rookie Rueben Bain Jr. This defense continues to make plays, and the pass rush looks to finally take form.
Alex Anzalone had two interceptions on the day and was far and away in his best game as a Tampa Bay Buccaneer. Josiah Trotter also did a very good job making tackles today and continues to have a great rookie season for this team. There were some missed opportunities given the rain, but overall this unit seems to be getting better every week.
Starting corners Jacob Parrish and Zyon McCollum both had interceptions today and continue to look like one of the best duos in the entire NFL. The only negative was that Antoine Winfield Jr. took a very bad angle on a Jahan Dotson reception that resulted in a big completion.
However, this has been one of the best surprises of the season so far, and Todd Bowles and cornerbacks coach Rashad Johnson deserve a lot of credit.
Chase McLaughlin led the way with three field goals and helped the Bucs keep the lead throughout the day. Riley Dixon had a great day punting the football given the conditions and put the Falcons in field position that they simply couldn't deal with.

title: Overreactions From Buccaneers' Run-Heavy Win Over Falcons
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have won two games in a row. They've done it off the back of some seriously impressive rushing performances.
Tampa Bay defeated the Atlanta Falcons 16-0 in a game where they did not complete a single pass. They're now 3-5 and just a half-game back of the NFC South lead, and they have an excellent ground game and a chainsaw of a defense to back it up.
Here are our three overreactions to Tampa Bay's crazy win against the Falcons without a passing game to be seen:
This might seem crazy to say, and it doesn't mean that the Bucs are necessarily a good team. But let's look at the facts.
They certainly have the best defense — it's a top-five unit in the league. They definitely have the best running game, too, as it's come alive over the last two weeks behind Bucky Irving. They also have the best kicker in football, and that kicker largely won the game for them on Sunday.
The Buccaneers are just half a game out of the NFC South lead. They might drop some games coming up against teams like the Chicago Bears or Detroit Lions, but even then, they seem to be better than every other team in the NFC South at this point.
That could win them the division and get them in the ballroom.
Running back Bucky Irving had over 100 yards by halftime, and the Bucs put up nine points without completing a pass. This brand of football seems unsustainable, but the Bucs have done it two weeks in a row now.
Zac Robinson's switch to a gap and counter run scheme has opened up the run game in a big way. The Bucs will eventually have to pass at some point, but if the run game is this dominant, Tampa Bay may be able to lean on it in a way that no one thought they would be able to.
Is it entirely sustainable? No, but it's proven that the Bucs can win games solely off the back of the run game.
My goodness, have the Bucs been on a heater on defense this last few weeks.
The Bucs had four interceptions off Michael Penix on Sunday. They continue to take the ball, and the linebacking corps and the secondary continue to swarm. The Bucs defense has been suffocating, and it's clear now that this is legitimately a top defensive unit in the NFL.
Todd Bowles has been calling excellent games over the past few weeks, and his players are executing at every level. This Bucs offense may need some work in a few areas, but this Bucs defense? They're absolutely lethal.

title: Buccaneers Lose Starter to Knee Injury
full_text:
It's football weather in Tampa Bay as the Buccaneers take on the Atlanta Falcons.
Since kickoff, the rain has been coming down nonstop and has led to some sloppy play by both teams.
The Bucs have had a botched snap or fumble four times, while Michael Penix Jr. has thrown three interceptions for Atlanta.
The Buccaneers' running game and defensive ability to take the ball away have been at the forefront of the game
Even with how well those two aspects are playing, the defense took a bullet in this one as outside linebacker Yaya Diaby has been ruled out for the rest of the game with a knee injury.
According to our boots on the ground in Tampa, Falcons tight end Nick Muse fell into Diaby. And despite trying to work through the injury on the side, he will be unable to go the rest of the way.
Diaby is now OUT for the remainder of the game. https://t.co/dSf5RrQhME
Diaby had been extremely underwhelming to begin his contract year, but exploded last week against the Carolina Panthers for three sacks. He also has 11 tackles and one interception.
He finally looked to be turning his own personal season around, and the hope is that nothing serious is going on inside his knee that could cause him to miss an extended period of time.
We will hear from head coach Todd Bowles following the game on Diaby's status, but likely won't have a true understanding of the seriousness of it until further tests are done on Monday.
With Diaby now out for the rest of the game, the Bucs will rotate the likes of Anthony Nelson and David Walker.
Walker has been extremely useful against the pass, but with the weather, Nelson might be better suited to stop the run game led by Bijan Robinson.
The good news is that the Bucs haven't had to generate much pressure due to the weather and field conditions, so being down one player won't necessarily have a huge impact on the game.

title: Buccaneers Reveal Good News Right Before Falcons Matchup
full_text:
Every game is a must-win game for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at this point, but this game on Sunday vs. the Atlanta Falcons could very well make or break Tampa Bay's season.
The Bucs are 1.5 games out of first place in the NFC South. The Carolina Panthers lost their Thursday Night Football game to the Green Bay Packers (and fired a good number of their defensive staff as a result), so if the Bucs beat the Falcons, they'll be just 1.5 games back from the NFC South lead.
Naturally, Tampa Bay will want every starter it can have to try and win this game. And it looks like one questionable key offensive player will indeed play today against the Falcons.
Right tackle Luke Goedeke has been dealing with a calf injury for the last two weeks. He didn't play against the Panthers and did not practice on Wednesday and Thursday this week, but he did practice Friday — and now, he's slated to play.
Goedeke is active against the Falcons today. With no practice squad elevations, he'll almost certainly play against Atlanta, giving the offensive line a big boost against a Falcons front that can get a lot of good pressure with four players.
Swing tackle Ben Chukwuma played in Goedeke's stead last week. He won't have to do so again this week, as Goedeke will anchor down the right side while All-Pro Tristan Wirfs holds down the left side.
Goedeke will be a crucial player. The Bucs may need to establish the run in inclement weather, and Atlanta boasts the fourth-best run defense in the NFL by rushing yards per game. If running back Bucky Irving is going to get going, he'll need Goedeke's help to do it, and that could be the key to controlling the clock and beating an Atlanta team that just knocked off the San Francisco 49ers the week prior.
The Bucs play the Falcons at 1 p.m. at Raymond James Stadium.

title: 2 Position Groups That Need to Step Up for Buccaneers to Beat Falcons
full_text:
After a brutal start to the 2026 NFL season for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , there's all of a sudden a slight glimmer of hope.
After pummeling the Panthers in Carolina last weekend 43-13, the Bucs are now looking to string together back-to-back regular season victories for the first time in over a year. More importantly, with the Atlanta Falcons coming to town on Sunday, the Buccaneers will have a chance to make up even more ground in the division with the Panthers having already lost this week's matchup to the Green Bay Packers on Thursday.
Even though the Falcons and Panthers both sit at 3-4 atop the NFC South standings, the Falcons have a -2 point differential on the season compared to Carolina's -15. Interestingly enough, the Buccaneers, who are looking up at both teams with their 2-5 record, are +11 in the point differential category.
A win against Atlanta this week would be massive for the Buccaneers to close the gap in the NFC South standings. And with four divisional games still to be played, Tampa Bay would all of a sudden have a very realistic path to push for the top seed in the South by season's end.
Conversely, a loss to Atlanta would not only put the Bucs even further behind these teams in the standings, but it could signify the end of their competitive window this year and potentially turn the Bucs into sellers ahead of the Nov. 10th trade deadline.
In other words, even though we aren't quite at the halfway mark, the result of this Sunday's game against the Falcons could very well determine the fate of the 2026 Buccaneers.
Let's take a look at two key position groups that will need to step up in order for the Buccaneers to get a much-needed victory this weekend.
Although Todd Bowles' defense has really established itself as one of the league's better all-around units, there are still flaws to be found.
Most obvious among them is veteran LB Alex Anzalone who, despite signing a substantial contract to become a key leader of this defense in the offseason, has struggled mightily in all facets. Far too often, Anzalone loses his footing, fails to shed blocks, takes poor angles and misses tackles. Even more concerning is that he's been more of a liability in pass coverage than the asset that he was advertised to be coming over from Detroit.
Thankfully, his rookie running mate, Josiah Trotter, has been superb . That being said the Buccaneers have struggled as a unit when it comes to defending opposing tight ends. Meanwhile, Falcons tight end Kyle Pitts, though inconsistent, always seems to be a problem for the Buccaneers.
Trotter needs to keep playing how he has been, but Anzalone must step up in order to contain Pitts, who remains one of the most gifted pass-catching tight ends in the game. Throw in the challenge of defending the best running back in football, Bijan Robinson, and the importance of the Buccaneers' linebacker duo stepping up on Sunday becomes that much more obvious.
Even after Mike Evans surprised everyone by leaving Tampa Bay in the offseason, the Buccaneers remained confident in their WR room because of the quality depth they'd assembled leading up to that moment. Unfortunately, though, the Bucs' talented collection of pass catchers hasn't come close to producing the results everyone expected.
Although Chris Godwin has proven in the past to be a game changer, we've yet to see that version of the Bucs' veteran this season. The team's supposed number one WR, Emeka Egbuka, is unlikely to suit up in this game due to a foot injury and Jalen McMillan remains without a timetable for return.
Young receivers like Tez Johnson and Ted Hurst have both performed well in limited opportunities, but they'll need to be targeted more in this game in order to take the top off the defense and open up other opportunities for Zac Robinson's offense .
Although the Buccaneers managed to dominate the Panthers last weekend while passing for just 64 yards in the game, that's unlikely to be replicated against the Falcons, who present a much stouter run defense. As a result, the Bucs will need to attack the Falcons through the air in order to keep them honest. With Mayfield still nursing a thumb injury on his throwing hand, even more of that responsibility will fall on the Bucs' pass catchers.
In order for the Bucs to be effective through the air against Atlanta, they'll need to take some shots downfield to both Johnson and Hurst while utilizing Chris Godwin at all levels of the field. If those players are able to create separation against the Falcons' defensive backs, it will make life that much easier on Mayfield and significantly increase the Bucs' chances of winning this critical game.

title: How Buccaneers' Bucky Irving Seperated Himself in the NFL This Month
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have won two games. In those two games they won, there was a common denominator.
Running back Bucky Irving didn't get to do much in 2025, as he was injured early in the season and came back late while he was recovering. This year, though, he's played in every game, and he's made his presence known in more ways than one.
The Bucs have won twice in October, and during this month, Irving has been the reason why. He's had some huge games, and as it turns out, he's separated himself from the rest of the NFL in a big way.
Irving put up 378 rushing yards in the month of October. That's the most in the league among any player in that same time frame.
OK, Bucky pic.twitter.com/UBuSl8fr5T
Irving has 21 more rushing yards than the next-highest player, New York Jets running back Braelon Allen, at 357. Rounding out the list are Carolina Panthers running back Chubba Hubbard (356), Atlanta Falcons running back Bijan Robinson (355), Pittsburgh Steelers running back Jaylen Warren (345) and Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker (341).
The brunt of these rushing yards came in two games for Irving. Irving exploded against the Dallas Cowboys, running for 165 yards on 21 attempts. He also went wild against the Panthers, scampering for 106 yards on 24 attempts.
So far this season, Irving has put up 558 rushing yards for 4.7 yards per carry. He also has four touchdowns on the ground this year.
The Bucs paired Irving up with Kenny Gainwell this offseason in free agency with the expectation that Gainwell would get some significant looks, but so far, Irving has gotten the brunt of the work in Zac Robinson's offense. Given that he's been one of the best running backs in football this year, it's unlikely that Irving will see some reduced carries anytime soon.
The Bucs play the Falcons at 1 p.m. on Sunday in Raymond James Stadium. The Falcons have one of the best rushing defenses in the NFL, so it will be hard for Irving to get going — but he's proven this year that he can make it happen at any moment.

title: Buccaneers Will Face This Falcons Star at Home For the First Time on Sunday
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are no strangers to playing the Atlanta Falcons. The two teams have been locked in a divisional rivalry for years in the NFC South, and they've had plenty of notable battles in that time frame.
They are mostly strangers, however, to Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. The Falcons drafted Penix in the first round of the 2024 NFL Draft, but ever since then, he's played the Buccaneers just one time — he was the quarterback for the Falcons last year when the Bucs beat them 23-20 in Atlanta to open the season.
Now, Penix is set to start against the Bucs for just the second time on Sunday. And that start is a milestone for both him and the Buccaneers.
The Buccaneers will host Penix and the Falcons on Sunday, and it will mark the first time that Tampa Bay has played Penix at Raymond James Stadium. The Bucs haven't beaten the Falcons in Raymond James Stadium since Oct. 9, 2022, but the Bucs have generally faced Kirk Cousins or Desmond Ridder in that time span.
This will also be Penix's first time at Raymond James Stadium, which means it will be the first time he's had an NFL homecoming. Penix grew up in the Tampa Bay area in Dade City, so this will be his first NFL game in his home region despite being drafted by the Falcons three seasons ago.
Penix may have grown up in the Tampa Bay area, but he insinuated at a press conference earlier this week that, because of Tampa Bay's lack of success during most of his life, he did not grow up a Bucs fan.
"Nah, I was never a Bucs fan," Penix said this week in the lead-up to the game. "I think the year I was born was the year they won the Super Bowl. And after that, as I was growing up... I wasn't a fan of the Bucs."
Michael Penix Jr. when asked if he was a Bucs fan growing up in Dade City, just north of Tampa “Nahhhh I was never a Bucs fan” pic.twitter.com/W11ZlVY6jO
The Bucs, however, seem to be fans of his. Head coach Todd Bowles had a lot of good things to say about Penix, and he's certainly keeping Penix's skill set in mind as he game plans to defeat him for the second time in his career.
"He can throw the ball. He's got great zip on the ball and great timing on the football – [a] strong arm," Bowles said. "He can get out of the pocket. He runs a lot better than you think he can run. He's really not giving the ball away. They're doing a great job taking care of the football, which is going to be critical in this game. We’ve been getting [interceptions], but they're a hard team to get them off of, and he's playing winning football."
The Bucs will face off against Penix and the Falcons at 1 p.m. on Sunday in Tampa.

title: Buccaneers' Rookie Already Establishing Himself As Major NFL Draft Steal
full_text:
Regardless of where they went to college, who coached them, or what position they played, the NFL is a massive adjustment for every first-year player.
The intensity, speed, physicality, intelligence and technique of NFL players are world-class, and even if a particular player was utterly dominant at the collegiate level, that doesn't necessarily mean it will translate to the next level. In fact, it often doesn't.
This is largely why the NFL Draft is so unpredictable. Not just in terms of predicting what positions or players teams will select, but also for NFL GMs and front office executives trying to forecast which prospects will continue to ascend at the NFL level and which will not.
With the 2026 NFL season just about at the halfway point, we've now got enough of a sample size to begin reflecting on this year's rookie class, assess how the prospects selected are making out as NFL players, and give credit where it's due.
This is exactly what ESPN sought to do this week when they ranked the top 10 rookies in the NFL so far.
Located within the ranking behind former Ohio State defenders Arvell Reese and Sonny Styles, both of whom occupy the top two spots, and just behind Browns' WR Denzel Boston, who was listed third, you'll find impressive Buccaneers rookie LB Josiah Trotter ranked as the fourth-best rookie of the 2026 draft class, according to ESPN.
With 62 tackles, one sack, and one interception, Trotter has made his impact felt early and often this season, outplaying his veteran LB partner, Alex Anzalone, by a massive margin.
Here's what NFL expert Matt Bowen had to say about the decision to rank Trotter as the fourth-best rookie so far.
"Trotter's play recognition stands out on the tape," Bowen wrote. "He is quick to diagnose against the run, getting eyes on formation keys and pulling guards to make tackles. His 43% run-stop win rate ranks 10th among all linebackers, and he has the physical play style to drop the hammer on contact."
The article also mentioned Trotter's impressive performance in coverage, which is something that was considered a potential knock on him coming out of Missouri as a prospect.
"Plus, Trotter has created some on-the-ball production in coverage, which includes a pick-six on quarterback Joe Burrow and the Bengals," Bowen wrote. "He's an ascending player who can also be schemed as a blitzer in Todd Bowles' defense."
For prospects taken outside of the first 32 picks, it usually takes a little extra time to earn the respect of those around the league. These players aren't given the benefit of the doubt or viewed with a biased lens in the same way first-rounders are. This makes Trotter's ranking in the top five all the more impressive, as he was taken with the 46th overall pick.
Some valuable context that should be viewed in a very positive light by Bucs fans is the fact that every other player listed in ESPN's ranking of the top-10 rookies was drafted ahead of Trotter. This means that not only did the Buccaneers draft themselves an exceptional player at a key position, but they got incredible value on that selection.
Considering this is the first season in 15 years where the Buccaneers are playing without Lavonte David manning the middle of their defense, they should count their lucky stars, because it appears as though they may have found a player to take his place.

title: Titans’ Veteran DE Emerging as a Blue Chip Trade Candidate With Deadline Looming Large
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans fell to 1-7 in the 2026 NFL season on Sunday after a 43-36 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals on the road in overtime.
Despite not doing enough to pull off a victory in overtime , the Titans showed promise on both sides of the ball and received standout performances from multiple players, including edge rusher Jacob Martin. The 30-year-old signed a two-year deal with Tennessee in March and has established himself as one of the franchise's best offseason additions.
Martin had his best game of the season against the Bengals, posting three sacks and nine quarterback pressures with four defensive stops, and it couldn't have come at a better time.
Though Martin has exceeded expectations so far in 2026 and is under contract for another year, it would make sense for the Titans to move him before the 4 p.m. ET deadline on November 10 . The Temple product is tied for fifth in the NFL in sacks (6.5) and should attract interest from contenders in need of pass-rushing support.
Trading Martin would allow Tennessee to take a closer look at the younger talent in the edge rusher group, especially Femi Oladejo and rookie first-round pick Keldric Faulk. Additionally, the Titans are still in a rebuild, so acquiring picks for a veteran piece like Martin would be a savvy move by general manager Mike Borgonzi.
Contenders such as the Detroit Lions, San Francisco 49ers, Cleveland Browns, and Buffalo Bills could be interested in Martin's services. The veteran journeyman is on an affordable deal and is providing quality pass-rushing production this season, so plenty of other teams should be in the running.
As for what Tennessee could get back for Martin, a fourth-round pick seems like a realistic return. A third-round pick is possible, but unlikely, given that Martin will turn 31 in December and isn't a consistent game-wrecker.
By trading All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears last week, the Titans signaled that they are willing to discuss trades for their veteran contributors and are looking ahead to the future. It would be a surprise if the team doesn't make another move by November 10, and dealing Martin would be a logical course of action.
The Titans will enjoy a bye in Week 9 before hosting the Jacksonville Jaguars at Nissan Stadium in Week 10. We'll see whether Martin is still on the roster by then or instead playing valuable snaps for a playoff contender.
Dharya Sharma is a sportswriter from Nebraska who has been covering the Tennessee Titans through his website, SharmSports, since 2023. He is also an NFL and NBA writer for The Sporting News and had a previous stop with Sportsnaut. Follow him on X @SharmSports

title: Titans' Trade Stock Hits a New High With Multiple Players After Loss to Bengals in Week 8
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans dropped another close game, losing 43-36 to the Cincinnati Bengals in an overtime thriller.
The Titans are now 1-5 in one-score games this season, and 1-7 on the year. Despite the loss, the Titans played arguably their best game of the year on a day where QB Cam Ward overcame not having WR Carnell Tate to produce the first 300-yard game of his career.
That development is gonna make the upcoming trade deadline more interesting. Ward obviously needs all the help he can get, but we’ve also reached a point where the stock of some of the Titans’ likeliest trade candidates has never been higher.
It creates an internal dilemma where the team has to weigh the pros and cons of trading a key piece, especially offensively. Is the capital being offered more valuable than having someone who can help Ward develop?
That’s the answer Tennessee will have to answer when teams inevitably come calling ahead of next Tuesday’s deadline. I don’t believe the Titans will just give players away for the sake of getting something in return, but as we saw last week, everyone has a price.
With that said, let’s dive into which players we should be keeping our eyes on as the trade deadline draws near.
The Titans’ veteran running back is one of the more complicated trade candidates. Pollard has undoubtedly increased his value over the last two weeks, totaling 246 rushing yards and five touchdowns while averaging over five yards per carry.
That type of consistency out of the ground game makes life easier on the Titans’ young quarterback. Trading away someone like Pollard could make the Titans incredibly one-dimensional, especially with RB Tyjae Spears’ inability to stay on the field.
However, if the Titans can get an early day-three pick (round four or five) in return for a running back on an expiring contract, they absolutely have to consider it.
Before the recent breakout, I thought maybe Tennessee could get a late day-three pick (sixth or seventh round) in return. But with how the Memphis product is playing, it wouldn’t shock me if someone offered a fifth-round pick to secure a consistent ball carrier for an offense with championship aspirations.
I personally don’t think someone would realistically go to a fourth-round pick for a rental, but if someone does offer that, then that’s something that Tennessee should take without hesitation. Even if it requires sending something like a future sixth or seventh-round pick in return to seal the deal.
But considering how important Pollard is for Ward, I think it’ll take at least a fifth round pick to lure him away.
Few have increased their stock as much as Hooker has of late. The veteran safety has already tied his career high of five interceptions through eight games ( most in NFL ), including three on Sunday against the Bengals. Hooker has also had a couple of close calls that could’ve increased that total even further.
Most INT this season Amani Hooker         5 10 players tied        3 pic.twitter.com/JHq91I4PXm
The former Iowa standout still has two years left on his contract and could be someone teams consider a real investment rather than a rental.
At this rate, Hooker would likely fetch a fourth-round pick in return, and if it turns into a bidding war between multiple teams, you could even see a team possibly go as far as offering a conditional third-rounder to secure his services.
If that’s the case, again, Tennessee should jump all over it.
CB Alontae Taylor is one of the Titans’ prized offseason additions that hasn’t panned out the way anybody hoped it would. But with CB Marcus Harris’ status unknown going forward after exiting with an ankle injury in Week 8, I believe Taylor ends up becoming more likely to stay than not.
Staying on defense, Titans' veteran pass rusher Jacob Martin has already set a new career high with 6.5 sacks through the team’s first eight games, including three against the Bengals today.
Pass rushers are a premium come playoff time, so with his value being as high as it is, it wouldn’t shock me to see a team offer a mid-to-late day three pick to try to take him away.
Lastly, WR Calvin Ridley makes sense for everyone involved. Ridley has fallen down the depth chart in Tennessee, so he may be better suited trying to help a playoff-caliber team that needs a veteran receiver to help stabilize their room.
I don’t think this one would take much; a late day-three pick could probably get it done. If someone does offer that, Tennessee would be wise to take it.

title: Robert Saleh Postgame: 1 Offensive Tendency That Fueled Cam Ward's Career Game Despite Loss to Bengals
full_text:
No Tennessee Titans fan is going to feel "good" after a loss. At the same time, at a certain point in the middle of a 1-7 campaign, you have to be happy about signs of progress that are geared toward a team's future. The Titans got a sign like that today from Cam Ward.
In spite of a 43-36 loss - with plenty to complain about therein - Ward answered the call and kept Tennessee in the game in the second half. His 304 passing yards were a career high. Ward also threw two touchdowns and avoided a pick for the first time in five weeks, passing 26-40 on the day.
The second-year QB is still 4-21 as a starter. He took a brutal sack at the end of regulation, and sailed a pass past Elic Ayomanor that ended overtime. But something clicked for Ward today, and a performance like this one could be seen as a turning point if he keeps it up.
What clicked, exactly? Well, in his expectedly dejected postgame-presser, head coach Robert Saleh noted one aspect of the offense in passing. When the Titans went tempo, Ward balled out.
"He looked awesome today," Saleh said of Ward after the game. "I thought the offense was outstanding today... the tempo really does help Cam."
Brian Daboll has been continuously criticized for calling inconsistent plays and not trusting Ward to get into a rhythm under center. Ward has had plenty of his own issues, but his OC not even trying to move the ball downfield at times hasn't helped the QB's case.
Today, however, Daboll and Ward worked together to generate numerous chunk plays. This was particularly impressive in the absence of premier WR Carnell Tate; when Tennessee sped things up in Cincinnati, Ward's often-questioned decision-making faded into the background.
Entering today ( per TeamRankings ), Tennessee had by far and away the lowest time of possession in the NFL with an average of 24:41, as well as the second highest no-huddle rate at 16.1%, according to Sharp Football Analysis. The Titans finished just one second shy of the Bengals' TOP today, with 32:11.
Their predictable, short-field passing game had a lot to do with the low TOP prior to Week 8. Retaining and even upping the tempo, combined with giving Ward looks downfield in Cincy, fully opened the game up for the second-year QB.
A loss is a loss, absolutely. Ward won't be excused for all of his mistakes either. But the Titans' passer didn't achieve the first 300-yard game of his career by any accident. Daboll's faster, more aggressive play-calling fueled Ward's improvement.
In what looks like a trial run for the Titans the rest of this season, Tennessee should fully commit to seeing what Ward has as a game-changer, rather than hoping he fits the mold of game manager in week after losing week. That starts and ends with trusting him beyond the sticks.
Lane covers the Tennessee Titans, where he brings an evolving team's journey to fans on a daily basis. A longtime sports fanatic and recent baby blue jersey aficionado.

title: Titans Fall to Bengals in Overtime Thriller: 3 Major Takeaways From the Painful Defeat
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans entered today coming off a heartbreaking, last-second defeat at the hands of the Cleveland Browns last week. The Titans blew that game after jumping out to a dominant 14-0 start, fueled by a breakout run from Tony Pollard.
Today, Tennessee got out to a 13-0 lead in the first quarter fueled by - you guessed it - a breakout run from Pollard. What followed was an overtime thriller that nobody expected between 1-6 and 4-2 teams; one that ended in the same old way for Tennessee.
The Titans ultimately lost 43-36, failing to make good on a golden opportunity late to win this thing. Here are three takeaways from a game that should've cast a positive shadow over this franchise.
Tennessee trading away DT Jeffery Simmons earlier this week called the defense into question in a huge way. Today's game both helped and hurt their overall case.
That unit showed flashes today. Amani Hooker led the way with a mind-boggling three interceptions, doubling QB Joe Burrow's season-long INT total prior to today. On top of Hooker's leading efforts, Alontae Taylor forced a second-half fumble.
Taylor's move to nickel has clearly benefitted the CB, and may even save his role in this defense. But you can't allow 462 yards passing to the opposing team and expect to win. The takeaways are brilliant, but this incomplete defense still can't do enough to be commended consistently.
Cam Ward deserves a tip of the hat today. On the heels of a wave of doubts landing on Ward's shoulders following his showing last week and the Simmons trade, the QB had arguably the best game of his career.
Ward's 304 yards represent a new career high. He finally broke his five-game INT streak and, even considering a lost fumble in the third quarter, played a solid game. Taking a sack that led to an overtime loss is a serious negative mark, though. Ward would finish passing 26/40.
The QB still isn't entirely out of the woods at this point, especially with that aforementioned sack signaling Ward's decision-making issues remain (see also a crucial fourth-down ball that didn't come close to Elic Ayomanor in OT), but this is still a net positive performance that turns the dial in the right direction for him.
Coming off a career, three-touchdown game in last week's loss to the Browns, Pollard continues to build on his value as a veteran out of the backfield today.
The 29-year old RB posted 117 yards on 21 carries today, including two more touchdowns to add to his tally. Pollard is at six scores on the year now.
These past two weeks have been huge not only for Tennessee's offense, but for the trade value that Pollard could have ahead of the looming November 10 deadline. He's effectively the best player in this offense right now (sans Carnell Tate) and poses as either a reliable back or rising trade asset.
Lane covers the Tennessee Titans, where he brings an evolving team's journey to fans on a daily basis. A longtime sports fanatic and recent baby blue jersey aficionado.

title: How New-Look Titans Can Build on Promising First Half and Upset Bengals
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans are in a competitive game with the Cincinnati Bengals through one half, as the team trails the Bengals 14-13, but has shown plenty of promise on both sides of the ball.
Despite facing heavy scrutiny on a weekly basis this season, the Titans' offense has come to play on Sunday. Quarterback Cam Ward has been solid, completing 14 of 22 passes for 166 yards with a 86.6 passer rating. Ward has completed passes to seven different receivers and is keeping the ball out of harm's way.
Running back Tony Pollard has been one of the most productive players at his position in recent weeks, and that has continued into Week 8. Pollard currently has 67 rushing yards on nine carries, and scored a 40-yard touchdown in the first quarter .
As for the defense, head coach Robert Saleh's unit has struggled at times to contain the Bengals' dynamic passing attack, but the group forced a turnover in the first quarter, an interception by safety Amani Hooker off quarterback Joe Burrow. A sack by edge rusher Jacob Martin also led to a key goal-line stand for the defense in the second quarter on fourth down inside the 5-yard line.
The Titans arguably played their best half of football all year against the Bengals, and if Saleh's squad can keep it up, an upset could be on the way.
Tennessee must continue to play clean football. A turnover by the offense or a surplus of penalties will kill the Titans' chances of winning, as they don't have enough talent to enter a shootout with the Bengals.
However, Tennessee also won't be able to tally its second win of the year if they play scared, conservative football. The offense must keep its foot on the gas, and the defense should continue to make Burrow uncomfortable, while also stepping up against the run. Bengals running back Chase Brown is averaging 6.8 yards per carry, which isn't going to cut it for the Titans' defense.
Despite trading defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons on Thursday and signaling that the rebuild is still ongoing, Tennessee is showing signs of life, and an upset over a playoff-contending team like the Bengals is just what the Titans need right now to get back on track as a franchise.

title: Titans' Road Duel vs. Bengals: 2 Ways Tennessee Can Spark Hope... Even in a Loss
full_text:
We'll say it over and over again: Moral victories don't count for much. At the same time, the Tennessee Titans have counted few actual victories this season. At 1-6, and now having traded away their best player, it's about taking what you can if you're Tennessee at this point.
What's exciting about the guys that remain? What can Robert Saleh and Mike Borgonzi build on alongside their newly-acquired draft assets? Are the young players still developing as needed? These are the questions Tennessee should be asking right now.
Of course, an actual win is the ultimate positive - but without the shorthanded Titans surprising a 4-2 playoff team on the road, here are two ways Tennessee can generate some positivity even if they do fall short today.
In the absence of Simmons, the Titans desperately need other members of the defensive line to step up. This is a unit that looked weak enough with Simmons as-was; without him, the outlook is bleak for the forseeable future.
Still, with Jonah Laulu being picked up off waivers and Nazir Stackhouse seeing a recent uptick in snaps ( and production ), there are pieces here that have the opportunity to prove themselves.
Between now and the offseason, guys on the d-line are essentially auditioning to keep their spots post-draft and however else Saleh decides to shake things up prior to his second year. Few players are safe (outside of veterans like John Franklin-Myers and Jermaine Johnson II).
That makes for shifting sands in the future, but a massive window for multiple players right now. Seeing Laulu, Stackhouse, or someone else produce would be a solid sign of progress in Week 8.
To say that the stove is boiling under Cam Ward right now would be an understatement. Not only has his recent play caused doubt about his future as the team's leader, but the Simmons trade opened the door to worry about how this franchise actually feels about him.
It's no longer unfair to say that Ward could soon be short on time as the undisputed starter in Nashville. He's thrown for 200+ yards only one time this season. His 4-5 touchdown-to-interception ratio is the simplest way to show he's fallen behind in year two.
But with a solid showing at Paycor Stadium fresh off a roster-shaking move? Ward could buy himself a bit of faith amidst a sea of unanswered questions for Tennessee.
The climb is tough with his favorite target, rookie WR Carnell Tate, confirmed to sit for the contest. All the same, the gate remains open for Ward to re-earn the hope that he gave this franchise when he was taken first overall last year. That hope would go a long way for the Titans right now.

title: Predicting Titans' Starters vs. Bengals: Who replaces Jeffery Simmons at DT?
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans have had a tumultuous week that included shipping off the face of the franchise for some much needed future draft picks. And despite that gut punch, the team somehow has to turn around just a few days later and try to beat one of the best teams in the NFL.
To say the Titans have their work cut out for them on Sunday would be an understatement. The Bengals enter this game looking like a like legitimate Super Bowl contender in all three phases. As for the Titans, well, let’s just say they do not.
With all of that said, let’s take a look at who the projected starters are for the Titans ahead of their Week 8 matchup with the Bengals.
With RB Tyjae Spears out once again, look for another heavy dose of Pollard with possibly some Nick Singleton carries sprinkled in for the first time in a few weeks.
With rookie WR Carnell Tate out, this passing attack could be in for a long afternoon unless one of these guys steps up.
This would be a great time for one of Tennessee’s prized free agent signings to make his presence felt, but considering the current trajectory offensively, It’s probably best not to get your hopes up.
The loss of DT Jeffery Simmons will be palpable at least for the rest of the season. The Titans will have to hope that Franklin-Myers is capable of becoming a dominant three-tech once again to help fill the massive void left by Simmons. While Thomas is the likeliest candidate to start in the short term, don’t be surprised to see rookie DL Keldric Faulk get some playing time inside now that Simmons is gone.
Robert Saleh has expressed his continued confidence in Faulk, and I’d imagine we start to see more packages with the rookie kicked inside as the season unfolds.
Faulk definitely needs another offseason in an NFL program to add the necessary size and strength to be successful, especially along the interior, but these inevitable reps will be critical for Faulk as he tries to figure out where he’s most comfortable heading into next season.
Williams and Flott have sneakily been a solid tandem along the boundary, but they have a massive test waiting for them this week. If the Titans are gonna have any shot of pulling off the upset, they’ll need this group to limit the impact made by Bengals star WRs Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins.
Unfortunately, that’s much easier said than done.
With P Tommy Townsend also sitting, the Titans will have to rely on the newly acquired Thomas Morstead to flip the field for them.

title: 1 Titans WR Has the Perfect Window to Audition for a Trade in Week 8 vs. Bengals
full_text:
Few people, if anyone, expected Jeffery Simmons to be the first Titan that Tennessee would trade this season. It could probably be safely argued that few people expected the team to move their longtime cornerstone at all. Yet, here they stand short of Simmons heading into Week 8.
In a seriously shorthanded matchup with the Cincinnati Bengals - as both WR Carnell Tate and RB Tyjae Spears are out with injuries - this road duel feels most important as it relates to the November 10 trade deadline. Who is realistically next on the chopping block for Tennessee?
The big names seem to be Tony Pollard, Amani Hooker, and even Alontae Taylor. However, nobody has a better opportunity on paper to audition for their potential next team than Calvin Ridley.
Ridley entered this season as a starter in the Titans' offense on the outside, though he's quickly faded out of relevancy in favor of second-year WR Elic Ayomanor. Ridley now remains involved in a limited fashion, boasting little more than his veteran presence.
He's technically questionable for tomorrow's contest, but was a full participant in Friday's practice. The stars are aligning for Ridley to take the field.
With only five receptions for 81 yards on the year, it's clear that Ridley's role with the Titans has almost totally waned. But at 31 years old and operating on a restructured contract, the value of Ridley may not be lost on a more competitive team in need of complimentary minutes at WR.
Tate being on the bench is obviously bad news for the Titans, but it almost certainly means more clock for Ridley. If Tennessee starts playing from behind (as is unfortunately expected), Ridley will have perhaps his best chance of the year to get going.
It could not come at a better time for either party. Tennessee appears to be on the brink of a full-on fire sale, and a "look what I can do" outing from Ridley would help light that fuse.
Ridley did eclipse 1,000 yards just two years ago in his first (and only) 17-game season with the Titans. Staying healthy has been a problem, with his most recent injury being hip-related, but the vet is paced well to surpass the mere seven games he played last season. He's only missed one game in 2026 up to now.
If Ridley does play in Week 8, an increase in snaps poses him well for a near-future trade. The former Alabama sensation simply doesn't fit the system in Nashville anymore. We'll watch closely to see if this comes to fruition as the trade deadline puts pressure on every possibility.
